body:
## What does this PR do?

Treat malformed CoinGecko response payloads as unavailable instead of attempting mapping operations on scalar values.

## Why is this change needed?

The API can return a successful HTTP response with an unexpected top-level or per-coin JSON value. The client now skips those values consistently in both single-coin and batch lookups.

## Testing

Focused malformed-payload tests pass. The complete legacy test module still has pre-existing live-network and stale batching assumptions unrelated to this change.

Drafted with Zo Bot; reviewed by HrachShah.

## Summary by Sourcery

Treat CoinGecko API responses with unexpected JSON shapes as unavailable to avoid processing malformed data.

Bug Fixes:
- Handle non-mapping top-level CoinGecko responses by returning no results in batch price lookups.
- Skip individual coins whose CoinGecko payloads are not JSON objects in single and batch lookups instead of attempting to read price fields.

Tests:
- Add tests covering malformed per-coin payloads and malformed top-level API responses for the crypto price checker.

author: aaronontheweb
body:
Follow-up to #8400. That fix widened node1's shutdown-delivery window (Identify 25s -> 45s) but left node3's receive window at 30s, inverting the invariant that the sender must out-wait the receiver. On build 129150 node3 gave up at exactly its 30s mark and node1 delivered ~2s later — node3 failed, node1 passed.

This widens node3's receive and teardown windows to 45s so they out-last the sender's deadline, resends the fire-and-forget shutdown message to cover a lost first delivery, and removes the spec's outer Within entirely: barriers now run outside any Within so their timeouts cannot be starved by earlier slow steps (Akka.NET Within does not dilate, and EnterBarrier's timeout is the Within remainder), with every wait carrying its own explicit bound. #8400's fresh-probe loop and fail-fast transport config are untouched.

author: joshcoyne
body:
## What

On mobile, opening the Scene inspector (or any kruddgui console — log/board/scene/assets) had it fill the entire remaining dock area with no height cap, so it covered the whole screen and hid the live 3D viewport behind it. You couldn't see the entity or gizmo while editing its transform. The native tests' isolated `*-draw-panel` entry points already assumed a `vh * 0.72` cap with a `160px` floor, but the live per-tick `kruddgui-draw` path never applied it — this wires the live path up to the same cap (factored into shared `kruddgui-console-max-vh-frac` / `kruddgui-console-min-h` constants).

Also reduced how far you have to scroll to reach Bindings: the Position/Rotation/Scale rows each burned a whole line just for their label; they now sit inline in a fixed-width column to the left of the fields, matching the style already used by the Info block's `label: value` rows.

## Related issues

Follow-up from user feedback on the mobile editor view (screenshot showed the Scene inspector covering the whole screen with the transform fields eating most of the visible scroll area before reaching Bindings).

author: ewhauser
body:
## Summary

- add opt-in, non-interactive Unix support for `bazel run` with an explicit target/program-argument boundary
- keep program arguments out of durable and model-visible projections while classifying build, launch, and program outcomes from bounded BEP evidence
- enforce a configurable combined stdout/stderr ceiling and document the security and configuration model
- add policy, reducer, server, storage, and fake-Bazel process coverage

## Why

`bazel.run` previously rejected `command = "run"`, forcing clients outside the MCP execution, cancellation, evidence, and inspection lifecycle. This adds the feature without expanding the three-tool surface or allowing interactive execution.

## Impact

`run` remains denied by default and must be explicitly allowlisted. The runner forces non-interactive stdin, disables argument residue in terminal/BEP output, preserves raw local evidence, and exposes a typed `RunSummary` with build/program phase outcomes.

## Validation

- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
- `make check`

The live Bazel matrix was not run locally because this Codex environment did not expose a Bazel MCP tool; CI remains the live Bazel validation path.

author: jaredledvina
body:
On Azure, the operator issued a CiliumNode `/status` update on essentially every 60s IPAM sync tick for every node, even when nothing changed (~333:1 status:spec write ratio on Azure vs ~2:1 on AWS/ENI). Two things defeated the operator's `DeepEqual` write-skip gate:

- `AzureInterface.DeepEqual` compared three `json:"-"` fields (`vmssName`, `vmID`, `resourceGroup`) that are never serialized to the apiserver, so a freshly rebuilt in-memory interface always differed from the round-tripped `origNode` copy.
- `Status.Azure.Interfaces` was built from non-deterministic Go map iteration, so its order changed every call and the index-by-index `AzureStatus.DeepEqual` saw a change even when the interface set was identical.

Changes:
- Exclude the three non-serialized fields from the generated `AzureInterface.DeepEqual` (`+deepequal-gen=false` markers + regeneration).
- Populate `Status.Azure.Interfaces` in a deterministic, ID-sorted order via a new `AzureStatus.SetInterfaces`, with the ordering invariant documented on the field.
- Rework Azure native-routing CIDR derivation (`deriveVpcCIDRs`) to select from the interfaces actually backing the node's IPAM pool allocations (multi-subnet aware), with a pinned-interface preference, a deterministic smallest-ID fallback, and explicit logging of skipped/unparseable CIDRs.

Adds unit tests for the deterministic ordering, the DeepEqual field exclusion (round-trip), and the CIDR selection paths. Azure-only; AWS/ENI is unaffected.

author: romneyda
body:
Closes #97938

Related: #97939

Supersedes #101564 without closing it. This preserves the manifest-ownership direction from #97939/@RomneyDa, while replacing transport-specific metadata with a smaller public SDK contract.

## What Problem This Solves

Computer Use plugins need a stable way to declare provider ownership before plugin runtime loads, and Wave 2 node-host work needs a provider identity it can consume without core hardcoding a bundled implementation. The existing draft contract mixed discovery with Codex/MCP transport, platform, and permission details that are not generic provider identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `contracts.computerUseProviders` for static ownership and `api.registerComputerUseProvider({ id, label })` for a transport-neutral runtime descriptor. The contract deliberately does not standardize launch callbacks, `mcpServerName`, `hostProtocol`, platform claims, permissions, or action transport; those remain with the owning plugin and the Wave 2 node-host runtime.

Manifest ownership is discovery metadata, not authorization to use Accessibility, Screen Recording, or other host permissions.

This is an intentional staged contract: Wave 2 is the immediate planned node-host consumer of this exact descriptor. Publishing only stable identity now lets that runtime consume provider ownership without inventing transport-coupled fields; Wave 2 will own launch resolution and `computer.act` fulfillment outside this API.

## Accepted Product Risk

ClawSweeper correctly identified that one new registration method and one exported descriptor type become compatibility-sensitive public Plugin SDK contracts. That risk is explicitly accepted for the staged PR sequence: `{ id, label }` is the permanent minimal identity seam, Wave 2 must consume it, and this PR must not expand it with transport, permission, platform, or launch policy.

## User Impact

Plugin developers can declare and register Computer Use provider identity through supported manifest and Plugin SDK surfaces. Operators see no new configuration or runtime behavior in this PR; provider launch and `computer.act` fulfillment remain follow-up runtime work.

## Evidence

- Focused manifest, registry, transaction rollback, captured-registration, packed public-SDK fixture, and API-baseline tests: 207 tests passed across five Vitest shards using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, package export, and 8,154-export surface budget checks passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm check:changed` passed the scoped core/extensions/scripts/docs/tooling lanes, including all required typecheck, lint, boundary, import-cycle, and policy gates.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm build` passed, including the published Plugin SDK declaration graph and export verification.
- Two fresh uncommitted Codex autoreviews reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Direct upstream Codex inspection confirmed Computer Use is currently a discoverable plugin with MCP configuration, not a generic host provider protocol; this is why MCP server naming is outside this contract.

AI-assisted: implementation and validation were completed with Codex; the final diff and dependency contract were reviewed directly.

body:
The next two lean-OSS commands. Follows the merged #165/#167/#168.

## `qm test` — run YOUR collection file
Same engine as `run`, but against a **collection file you provide** (`--collection <file.json>`), defaulting to `--mode both` → a native-vs-prompt **scoreboard**. Loads via the existing `persistence::evals::read_capped` (1 MB cap, schema-validated), auto-detecting the two JSON shapes it supports (a v2 collection object or a raw `ToolTask[]`). Other formats (CSV/JSONL/BFCL/…) are documented as not-parsed, not faked. `qm run --collection <file>` now accepts a file too.

## `qm report` — offline re-assessment
Score **one saved run against many bars**, no backend. `run`/`test --save-report <path>` persist the raw `BatchReport`; `qm report --report <path> --profile <id|file>` reloads it and re-assesses via the existing no-hardware `assess_report`. `--profile` accepts a `ReadinessProfile` `.json` or a built-in id (shared by run/test/report).

## Verification (live on Ollama)
- **test:** a custom 2-task file under `--mode both` → scoreboard showing the 3B's native FC reporting-in-prose (0/2) vs prompt (2/2), exit 20. Bad/missing/malformed/non-collection files → exit 2 `[QM-BAD-COLLECTION]`.
- **report:** `run --save-report` → valid BatchReport; offline re-assess → Ready @ 0.6 bar; the **same run** against a stricter custom profile (min_pass_k 0.9) → **NotReady, "pass^k 0.80 < 0.90 required", exit 20**; `--fail-on never` → 0. Bad report/profile → exit 2.
- **A rule-7f leak fixed by reading the live output:** the verdict line was printing the full absolute collection path → now basename only (`display_collection`, unit-tested); error paths redacted via `redact_path`.

Full lib suite: **1245 passed, 0 failed** (+2 unit tests).

author: m-jerez
body:
## Problem

Pure-fn entry tuples shipped **both** the `code` string **and** the live `createPureFn` literal regardless of the build's `emitMode`. So a `code`-mode build (which drops the live closure for every *type* fn to save bytes) still shipped every pure-fn body **twice**, and the on-demand built-in bodies (`rt::findCycle`, the format validators, …) were unconditionally live rather than following the mode's CSP contract. `emitMode` predates the pure-fn lane and was never revisited.

Implements [`docs/todos/purefn-cache-respect-emitmode.md`](https://github.com/MionKit/ts-run-types/blob/claude/purefn-cache-emitmode-iuzkpz/docs/done/purefn-cache-respect-emitmode.md) (moved to `docs/done/`).

## Change

Pure-fn entries now honor `emitMode` exactly like type-fn entries:

| mode | pure-fn `code` slot | pure-fn `createPureFn` slot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` (default) | body string | dropped (hole); runtime rebuilds via `new Function` |
| `functions` | dropped (hole) | live `function(<params>){<code>}` |
| `both` | body string | live literal (prior unconditional behavior) |

**Go** — `purefunctions.CollectEntries(entries, emitMode)` gates the two slots via `EmitsCode()` / `EmitsFactory()`, symmetric with the type-fn `codeArg`/`createRTFnArg`. A trailing `createPureFn` hole is trimmed; the interior `code` hole (functions mode) stays in place. Threaded at all three call sites (`render.go` + `dispatch.go`'s `serveBuiltinPureFns` and the scanFiles path). The built-in table needs no change — delivery flows through `CollectEntries`, so built-ins inherit the gating for free.

**Runtime** — `initPureFunction` rebuilds the factory from `code` + `paramNames` via the new `buildPureFnFactoryFromCode` (`new Function(...paramNames, code)`, strict mode) when `createPureFn` is absent, caching it on the entry. `CompiledPureFunction.code` and `.createPureFn` are now both optional; the pure-fn tuple type models the trimmed `createPureFn` tail.

No change to emitted body bytes within a slot, no public API change, and transform-wire byte-parity (`transform-modes.test.ts`) preserved.

## CSP note

A `code`-mode pure fn (built-ins included) now uses `new Function` exactly like a `code`-mode type fn, so it is NOT CSP-safe without `unsafe-eval` in `code` mode. A CSP consumer already on `functions`/`both` keeps working unchanged. `rt::findCycle` is no longer unconditionally CSP-safe — documented in `ARCHITECTURE.md` + `CLAUDE.md`.

## Tests

- **Go** — `TestCollectEntries_EmitMode*` in `module_test.go`: mode gating, trailing-trim / in-place-hole shapes, byte-stability.
- **JS runtime** — `entryTuplePureFn.test.ts`: full materialization across all three modes incl. the code-mode `new Function` reconstruction, `paramNames` `[]` and `['utl']` (composing factory), round-trip identical, strict-mode; plus direct `buildPureFnFactoryFromCode` coverage.
- **FE end-to-end** (spawns the real binary) — `pure-fns-cache.test.ts`: a user `registerPureFnFactory` **and** the table-served built-in `rt::findCycle` (demanded by a circular `createValidate`) honor each mode; the code slot alone reconstructs a working fn.
- Two override tests now assert the escaping-neutral `code`-string cfn body (the production-default form) instead of the live literal.

Full JS suite: **8044 passed, 35 skipped**. Go internal suite: **all green**.

## Also filed (out of scope)

While running the full Go suite I found a **pre-existing, non-gating** bug: `cmd/gen-run-type-kind`'s `TestRunTypeKindFileInSync` resolves `runTypeKind.ts` under the Go module root (`ts-go-runtypes/packages/…`) instead of the monorepo root, so it can never pass when run. CI only runs `go test ./internal/...`, so it never surfaces there. Recorded in `docs/todos/gen-run-type-kind-sync-test-wrong-path.md`; not fixed here.

author: brennanb2025
body:
Fixes #9165.

## Problem

The remote Node/npm toolchain gate added in the upgrade is stricter than the deploy it guards:

- **Deploy** (`ssh-remote-commands.ts`, `commandWithNodePath`) prepends `nodeBinDir` to PATH and runs **bare** `npm` — so npm can resolve from anywhere on PATH.
- **The gate** (`ssh-remote-node-toolchain-probe.ts`) invoked npm by absolute path `<nodeBinDir>/npm` (POSIX) / `<nodeBinDir>/npm.cmd` (Windows, behind a `Test-Path` colocation check).

A host whose only resolvable node has npm elsewhere on PATH (e.g. node symlinked into a dir without npm) resolved and deployed fine on v1.4.144, but after upgrade the candidate is rejected with **no fallback** → SSH/relay connection fails to establish. Failure is loud (not data loss) and the population is narrow — standard nvm/fnm/volta/apt/brew installs all colocate node+npm — hence P1.

## Fix

Make the probe resolve npm exactly the way deploy does — bare `npm --version` under the same prepended PATH — so it still confirms npm is runnable (the #8450 concern that motivated the gate) without demanding colocation:

- **POSIX** probe now runs `PATH=<nodeBinDir>:$PATH npm --version`.
- **Windows** probe drops the `Test-Path` colocation gate, prepends the dir to PATH (backslash form, matching deploy, so bare-command PATH lookup resolves reliably), and runs `& npm --version`.
- Updated the resolution contract comment to cite both #8450 (why the gate exists) and #9165 (why it must not require colocation).

## Verification

- `ssh-remote-node-toolchain-probe.test.ts` + `ssh-remote-node-resolution.test.ts`: **38 passed**.
- Typecheck (`tsconfig.node.json`) and oxlint on the touched files: clean.

The change only relaxes the probe toward deploy's real behavior, so it cannot accept a toolchain deploy would then fail on.

author: molaoshi
body:
## What broke
`new URL("/rate", "https://exolix.com/api/v2")` resolves to `https://exolix.com/rate` — a leading-slash path is treated as absolute, silently dropping the base's `/api/v2` prefix. Every proxied Exolix call (`/api/exolix/*`) therefore 404'd in production after #55. Chainflip was unaffected (its base URL has no path prefix). Verified live: direct Exolix call with the server key returns 200; the proxy returned Exolix's `{}` 404.

## Fix
- New shared `joinApiUrl(base, path, params)` helper that concatenates instead of resolving, preserving the base path prefix and tolerating slash mismatches.
- `lib/server/exolix.ts` and `lib/server/chainflip.ts` both use it.
- 5 regression tests, incl. the exact Exolix case.

## Verification
13/13 unit tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean.

author: vmhq
body:
## What

- New `adguard2` service: enabled by `ADGUARD2_BASE_URL` with its own `ADGUARD2_USERNAME`/`ADGUARD2_PASSWORD` Basic Auth credentials. Exposes the standard `adguard2_api_reference`, `adguard2_operation`, `adguard2_request` tools and shows up in `vmhq_status` / `vmhq_find_operation`.
- New `adguard_combined_stats` tool, registered only when **both** AdGuard instances are enabled. It fetches `/stats` from each in parallel and returns per-instance stats plus an aggregated total.

## How aggregation works

- Numeric counters (`num_dns_queries`, `num_blocked_filtering`, …) are summed.
- Per-time-unit series (`dns_queries`, …) are summed element-wise, aligned at the most recent value (shorter histories are zero-padded at the start).
- `top_*` lists are merged (shared entries summed) and re-sorted by count.
- `avg_processing_time` is weighted by each instance's query count, falling back to a simple mean when there are no queries.
- If one instance fails the response is flagged `partial: true`; if all fail, a normalized error with per-instance detail is returned.

## Implementation notes

- `adguardAuth` in `serviceRegistry.ts` now takes an env prefix (`ADGUARD` / `ADGUARD2`) so both instances build Basic Auth independently; mismatched credential pairs still throw at startup.
- `apiCatalog.ts`: `adguard2` reuses the same endpoints array as `adguard` (no duplication of the ~50 endpoints), overriding only `service`, `title`, and the auth note. The catalog record is now built from a `BASE_CATALOGS` literal validated with `satisfies`.
- `combineAdguardStats()` is exported from `mcp.ts` and unit-tested.

## Reviewer notes

- `defaultPathPrefix` is informational only (nothing prepends it to request paths); the combined-stats tool calls the catalog's `stats` endpoint through the same code path as `adguard_operation`, so behavior matches existing production usage.
- Tests: 69 pass, `bun run typecheck` clean. New coverage: registry enablement/credential handling for `adguard2` and the stats aggregation rules.

author: ruannilton
body:
## Summary

Terceira task da Fase J2 do Marco J (`.claude/specs/infra-providers/`) — **J2.3**, `DurableOutbox` + o relay de entrega.

- **`runtime.OutboxStore`** (`codegen/rtsrc/outbox.go.txt`, novo, ao lado de `memoryOutbox`): interface `ProcessBatch(ctx, batch, deliver func(OutboxRow) error) (processed int, err error)` — dialeto-agnóstica de propósito, para o núcleo `runtime` nunca importar `database/sql` (NFR-12/21). `EventFactory` (alias `func() Event`, mesma forma de `sqlruntime.EventFactory`).
- **`DurableOutbox`** implementa `Subscribe` (mesmo formato de `memoryOutbox`) + `Start(ctx)` (loop ticker/select, mesma forma de um worker periódico gerado, ex. `StartIdempotencyCleanup`) + `Tick(ctx)` (exportado — o gancho de teste que processa um lote sem esperar o ticker). `deliver` trata tipo de evento desconhecido ou payload malformado como condição **permanente** (marca entregue mesmo assim — nunca entra num retry infinito por uma linha que nenhum `ProcessBatch` futuro decodificaria diferente, mesmo espírito do poison-pill do RabbitMQ); uma falha de **handler** é retentável (propaga, `ProcessBatch` incrementa `attempts`).
- **`codegen/sqlrt/outbox.go.txt`** (novo): `outboxStore`/`NewOutboxStore(db, dialect)` implementa `ProcessBatch` de verdade — abre **uma** `*sql.Tx` para o lote inteiro (Scan + todo Mark/Increment + Commit), porque a trava `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` do Postgres (J2.2) só vale enquanto essa transação está aberta.
- **Achado sutil, documentado no arquivo:** `Dialect.MarkDelivered(idPlaceholder, timePlaceholder)` monta o texto sempre com `timePlaceholder` aparecendo **primeiro**, apesar de vir depois na lista de parâmetros — para bater com isso nos dois esquemas de binding (Postgres numerado por `$N`, sqlite posicional por ordem textual de `?`), o chamador precisa passar `Placeholder(1)` como `timePlaceholder` e `Placeholder(2)` como `idPlaceholder`, executando com os argumentos na mesma ordem (`now, id`) — inverter essa ordem quebraria silenciosamente o sqlite.
- `.claude/specs/infra-providers/tasks.md`/`.claude/state.md` atualizados (J2.3 concluída; próxima: **J2.4** — o relay alimenta o canal cross-service, R9).

## Test plan

- [x] `codegen/sql_outbox_relay_test.go` (novo, via `gentest.WriteFiles`/`RunTests` sobre sqlite real): `TestDurableOutboxDeliversAndMarks` (entrega ao handler, `delivered_at` deixa de ser NULL, um 2º `Tick` não re-entrega a linha já marcada) e `TestDurableOutboxRetriesOnHandlerFailure` (**crash simulado**: handler falha na 1ª tentativa ⇒ `attempts` sobe, `delivered_at` continua NULL; a MESMA linha é re-escaneada no próximo `Tick` ⇒ handler sucede na 2ª tentativa ⇒ entrega — at-least-once cumprido)

body:
## What
Adds automated secret scanning to catch hardcoded credentials — the core problem called out in #288 ("secrets currently hardcoded in CI and env files"). The repo already scans dependencies with Trivy, but nothing scans for committed secrets.

## Changes
- **`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml`** — runs gitleaks on every push and PR in **report-only** mode (exit code `0`), mirroring how the existing Trivy job reports without failing the build. It uses the gitleaks Docker image directly, so no organization license is required.
- **`.gitleaks.toml`** — extends the default gitleaks ruleset and allowlists documented `.env.example` placeholders and the public test address so the scan stays low-noise.
- **`docs/security/secrets-management.md`** — documents the current guardrails plus a proposed design for the remaining acceptance criteria (managed vault, CI secret injection, rotation policy of 90 days for API keys / 30 days for DB credentials, and audit logging).

## Notes
- Scoped to what a contributor can land without infrastructure access. The vault, CI secret injection, and audit logging need cloud accounts/infra, so they're captured as a documented proposal for maintainers rather than implemented here.
- Report-only by design: since the issue notes secrets already exist in the repo, the scan surfaces them without breaking CI. It can be made blocking (exit code `1`) once the repo is confirmed clean.

closes #288

author: tcstulio
body:
Closes #1205

## Bug (achado na triagem de backlog)
O loop de entrega (`create`) marcava `deliveredTo` a menos que `deliver()` **lançasse**. Mas `deliverWhatsApp`/`deliverEmail` faziam `await channelRouter.sendWhatsApp/sendEmail(...)` **ignorando o retorno** `{ success, error }` — e o `channelRouter` **não lança** em falha (sessão caída, destino recusado, SMTP negado): devolve `{ success: false }`. Resultado: **falha silenciosa era contada como entrega** (`deliveredTo`), mascarando não-entregas reais.

## Correção
Os dois `deliver*` checam `result.success` e **lançam** em falha → o loop joga o canal em `failedChannels`, não em `deliveredTo`.

## Testes
- WhatsApp/e-mail com `success=false` → `failedChannels` (não `deliveredTo`); `success=true` → `deliveredTo` (caminho feliz preservado).
- Suíte do `notificationService` verde.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Fixes #2011.

## The bug

On a cross-filesystem worktree relocate, `relocateWorktreeTo`
(`session/git/worktree_archive.go`) takes a fallback path that copies the bytes
to `dest` **and** repairs/registers the worktree with git — both user-critical
steps succeed. If only the source-directory removal then failed, it returned a
non-nil error. That error return is what corrupts state:

- It triggers the daemon's archive-rollback / restore-retry logic even though a
  **valid worktree already exists at `dest`**. On retry, collision handling
  picks a fresh dest (`dest-2`), copies + registers a **second** worktree, and
  the first is left registered/orphaned — corrupting `git worktree list` and
  breaking branch exclusivity.
- The `"remove the original manually"` advice is worse than useless: instance
  state can still point at `src`, so following it breaks recovery.

## The fix

When copy **and** git-registration both succeeded and only the source cleanup
failed, emit a **WARNING** (naming the leftover dir + an `rm -rf` reclamation
command through the `shellsuggest` seam) and return **nil**. The worktree is
valid and usable at `dest`; the leftover source is a disk-reclamation nuisance,
not a move failure. The cleanup failure stays visible in the log.

The neighboring **repair-failure** branch (git registration genuinely did *not*
succeed) still returns an error — that is a real failure and out of scope for
#2011.

## Fail-first evidence

Added `TestRelocate_CopySucceedsCleanupFails_NoErrorNoRetryOrphan`, which drives
the **real** `MoveWorktree` → `relocateWorktreeTo` engine (not `moveDirCrossDevice`
directly — that would skip the repair/registration gate that must have SUCCEEDED
for this bug to apply) and models the caller's retry-on-error loop.

**Observed failing at `083c586`** (origin/master HEAD, pre-fix). The failure
output reproduces the reported orphan-on-retry directly — the loop advanced into
a **second** worktree at `…/arch-2` after the first move to `…/arch` returned an
error:

```
Received unexpected error:
  worktree copied and registered at …/archived/repoid/arch-2, but failed to
  remove original …/archived/repoid/arch; remove the original manually: copied
  worktree to …/arch-2 but failed to remove original …/arch: forced source
  cleanup failure
Messages: copy+register success with a failed source cleanup must return nil,
  not error (else the caller retries into a second worktree)
```

With the fix the loop stops after one attempt (`attempts == 1`), no `dest-2`
directory is created, exactly one worktree is registered on the branch, and the
cleanup failure surfaces as a warning. The pre-existing
`TestMoveWorktree_CrossDeviceCopyCleanupFailureCommitsCopiedLocation` was updated
from the old error contract to the new nil+warn contract while keeping its #1475
invariant (worktreePath commits to `dest`).

## Adjacent-caller audit

Grepped `session/git/` and every worktree move/relocate path for the same
"user-critical work succeeded but cleanup failed → hard error" anti-pattern:

- **`relocateWorktreeTo` line 190** — the reported bug. **Fixed.**
- **`relocateWorktreeTo` repair-failure branch (line ~172)** — returns an error
  when `git worktree repair` fails, i.e. registration did **not** succeed. This
  is a genuine failure (retry is appropriate); **left as-is**, out of scope.
- **`moveDirCrossDevice`** — returns the typed `copiedWorktreeSourceCleanupError`
  when `removeAll(src)` fails after a successful copy. This is the **signal
  channel** `relocateWorktreeTo` inspects via `errors.As` to distinguish
  "copy succeeded, cleanup failed" from "copy failed"; it does not make the
  hard-error decision. **Left as-is** — the fix relies on this signal.
- **Callers of `relocateWorktreeTo`** — `MoveWorktree` (archive teardown) and
  `RestoreWorktreeTo` (restore) both share this single engine and simply
  propagate its return, so both are fixed by the one change. No caller-side
  handling of the cleanup case remains.

## Retry path confirmed

With the nil return, `ArchiveSession` proceeds to `CommitArchive` (no
`AbortArchiveToLost`, no Lost-restore retry) and `RestoreArchived` proceeds to
`RestoreFromArchive` (no `RestoreWorktreePath` collision suffix, no second copy).
The new test models this loop and asserts a single attempt with no second
worktree.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l .` — clean
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `golangci-lint run --timeout=3m --fast` — clean (full repo)
- `go test ./session/git/...` — pass (host-safe; no daemon spawn)

author: simon-yhkim
body:
## What changed

- Detects the RNFirebase v25.1 native analytics module before evaluating `@react-native-firebase/analytics`.
- Fails closed on older 0.0.8 preview binaries that do not contain RNFirebase.
- Preserves native analytics on rebuilt binaries and composes with the runtime analytics kill-switch from #1062.
- Adds regression coverage for missing, throwing, and correctly linked native-module registries.

## Why

The 0.0.8 preview APK was built before RNFirebase was added, while later OTA updates kept the same `runtimeVersion: 0.0.8`. The resulting native fingerprint drift allowed JavaScript that referenced a native SDK absent from the installed binary to reach cold start. This could terminate Android immediately after the OTA was applied.

An emergency recovery OTA has already restored the last known-good preview update (`ffafbe72`). This PR makes current `main` safe to publish to those older 0.0.8 binaries.

## Impact

- Existing 0.0.8 users skip native Firebase analytics and can launch safely.
- Newer rebuilt binaries continue to use native analytics when the module is linked and the consent/runtime gates allow it.
- Analytics remains fail-closed for missing modules, unresolved capability, consent denial, minors, and runtime kill-switch failures.

## Vision axis

- Axis 2: 개인 비서 기반

## Validation

- `npm run verify`
- 368 test suites passed
- 2,827 tests passed
- Targeted analytics suite: 36 tests passed
- Targeted ESLint and TypeScript checks passed
- RNFirebase v25.1 official source confirms the native module name is `RNFBAnalyticsModule`

- **観測点GeoJSONの遅延ロード**: 観測点(最深積雪 / 累計降雪量、計 約900KB)は既定オフなのに毎回ロード時に取得していました。空ソースで追加し、**初回選択時に `fetch`→`setData`** で取得するよう変更。初期表示のクリティカルパスから約900KBを除外。
- **preconnect / dns-prefetch**: 外部オリジン(`unpkg.com` / `cyberjapandata.gsi.go.jp`)への接続を前倒し。

### 読込UX・堅牢性
- **ローディングをスピナー化**し、取得失敗時に**再読み込みボタン**を提示(`loadGosetsuData` のリトライ設計と接続)。
- **観測点データの取得失敗をトーストで通知**し、選択を自動的に「なし」へ戻す。

### 共有性
- 地図に **`hash: true`** を付与し、位置・ズームを共有リンク(`#z/lat/lng`)で再現可能に。
- 選択中の観測点レイヤーを **`localStorage`** に保存し、再訪時に復元。
- **`<meta name="description">` / Open Graph / Twitter カード / canonical** を追加(共有時のリンクプレビュー改善)。

### アクセシビリティ
- **`:focus-visible`** のフォーカスリングを追加(WCAG 2.4.7)。
- viewport の **`maximum-scale=1.0` を撤廃**しページ拡大を許可(WCAG 1.4.4)。
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`** を尊重(CSSトランジション/アニメーション、および県移動の `fitBounds` の duration)。
- **`<noscript>`** によるJS無効時の案内(日本語 / 英語)を追加。

### i18n
- 追加キー `loading.retry` と `layers.stationLoadError` を4言語(ja / en / zh-Hans / ko)に追加。

## 検証

ヘッドレスChromium(Playwright)で実挙動を確認済み:

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 観測点データが初期ロードで取得されない | ✅ 0件 |
| 観測点選択時のみ該当データを取得(他方は0のまま) | ✅ maxdepth=1 / snowfall=0 |
| 地図データ取得失敗→エラー表示+再読み込みボタン | ✅ `is-error` / ボタン表示 |
| 再読み込みで復帰(県別リスト24件描画) | ✅ 復帰確認 |
| 観測点取得失敗→トースト通知+「なし」へ復帰 | ✅ 確認 |
| URLハッシュに位置反映 / localStorage保存 | ✅ `#4.5/39/138` / `maxdepth` |
| OGP・description メタタグ | ✅ 出力確認 |

author: vectorpeak
body:
Fix JS client embedding validation so malformed embedding rows are rejected before requests are prepared.

## What Problem This Solves

`validateEmbeddings` is intended to reject embedding payloads whose rows are not arrays of numeric values before the JS client prepares a write or query request. The current check uses the result of `Array.prototype.filter()` as the condition:

```ts
!embeddings.filter(...)
```

That condition does not behave like a validation predicate. `filter()` always returns an array object, and array objects are truthy in JavaScript, even when the filtered result is empty. Because of that, malformed embedding rows like this can pass the JS client validator instead of producing the existing `ChromaValueError`:

```ts
[[1, "bad"]]
```

There is a second diagnostic issue in the same branch: a non-array inner row can reach `.every()` directly and raise a raw `TypeError` instead of the validator's intended Chroma error. Both cases are SDK runtime validation / developer-experience bugs. This PR does not claim a server-side integrity or security fix.

## Change

The fix changes the validator from "build a filtered array and test whether the array object is falsy" to "require every embedding row to satisfy the row predicate":

```diff
-  if (!embeddings.filter((e) => e.every((n: any) => typeof n === "number"))) {
+  if (
+    !embeddings.every(
+      (embedding) =>
+        Array.isArray(embedding) &&
+        embedding.every((n: any) => typeof n === "number"),
+    )
+  ) {
```

This keeps the change narrow:

- `every()` makes the validation result a real boolean decision across all rows.
- `Array.isArray(embedding)` ensures malformed inner rows use the existing `ChromaValueError` path instead of falling through to a `TypeError`.
- The element contract intentionally stays the same: values are accepted when `typeof n === "number"`.

In particular, this PR does not add `Number.isFinite()` or otherwise change the JS client's existing NaN / Infinity policy.

## Evidence

The failing payload is a normal SDK input shape with one invalid element inside an embedding row:

```ts
await collection.add({
  ids: ["id1"],
  embeddings: [[1, "bad"] as unknown as number[]],
});
```

Before this change, the `filter()` truthiness check did not reject that row at the JS validator boundary. After this change, the same shape is rejected with the validator's existing message:

```text
Expected each embedding to be an array of numbers
```

The test coverage checks both affected validator surfaces:

- `add.collections.test.ts` rejects non-numeric embedding values for `collection.add()`.
- `add.collections.test.ts` rejects a non-array embedding row, covering the previous raw-`TypeError` path.
- `query.collection.test.ts` rejects non-numeric `queryEmbeddings` for `collection.query()`.

No screenshot or media evidence is included because this is a JS SDK validation path; the focused unit tests are the relevant behavior proof.

## Possible call chain / impact

```text
collection.add/update/upsert
  -> prepareRecords
  -> validateBaseRecordSet
  -> validateEmbeddings

collection.query
  -> prepareQuery
  -> validateBaseRecordSet
  -> validateEmbeddings
```

The change is limited to JS SDK runtime validation. It does not change server-side embedding validation or embedding generation behavior.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` passed (with local CRLF conversion warnings only).
- `cd clients/new-js && pnpm --filter chromadb test -- add.collections.test.ts query.collection.test.ts` passed.
- `cd clients/new-js && pnpm --filter chromadb build` was attempted; JS/CJS bundles built, but local DTS generation failed resolving `@chroma-core/default-embed` after the Windows pnpm install hit symlink `EPERM` issues.

author: sahilsapra391
body:
## Why

The L3 Stripe webhook (#124) grants credits on `checkout.session.completed` but has **no reversal path**. A buyer could purchase 50 credits for \$10, spend them, then file a card dispute or request a Stripe refund and keep both the credits and the money. This was the top money exposure flagged in the L3 review (rated MEDIUM), deferred because it needs charge→user linkage plumbing. This PR builds that plumbing and automates the interim manual process (owner posting a negative `admin_adjust` via `scripts/grant_credits.py` on each Stripe dispute email).

## ⚠️ Base branch

Targets `claude/launch-l3-stripe` (**PR #124, still OPEN**), not `main` — the code it extends (`billing.py`, `billing_routes.py`, the `ext_ref` ledger column) lives only on that branch. **Merge #124 first**, then this. When #124 merges and its branch is deleted, GitHub auto-retargets this PR to `main`. The diff shown here is only my changes.

## What

1. **Charge→purchase linkage.** `grant_purchase` now stamps the Stripe `payment_intent` on the purchase ledger row (new `payment_ref` column). A later refund/dispute event carries that `payment_intent` (not our checkout event id), so a pure DB lookup maps it back to the grant — no Stripe API call, deterministic in tests.
2. **Reversal.** New `db.reverse_purchase()` appends a **negative `chargeback` row** reversing the *exact* credits that payment granted (append-only ledger — the grant is never mutated). The webhook handles `charge.refunded` **and** `charge.dispute.created` (`billing.REVERSAL_EVENTS`).
3. **Idempotency — per PAYMENT, not per event.** New partial-unique index `uq_credit_ledger_chargeback` on `payment_ref where reason='chargeback'`. This is a deliberate strengthening of the "per event id" ask: the money leaves our account only once, so a redelivered event **and** a refund arriving alongside a dispute on the same charge (two event ids, one payment) both reverse only once. The DB index also settles the concurrent-insert race.
4. **Negative balances are correct.** If the buyer already spent the credits, the balance goes negative — they can't run again until they re-buy.

## Tests (8 new, 968 pass, ruff + mypy clean)

Refund reverses once + redelivery no-op · dispute reverses · refund+dispute on one charge don't double-reverse · unrelated dispute is a no-op · balance goes negative after spend-then-chargeback · reversal matches exact credits (promo-sized grant) + idempotent per payment.

## Known limitations (out of scope, documented)

- **Partial refund** → full clawback (unconditional; fine for a fixed-price \$10 one-time product — partial refunds shouldn't occur). A `log.warning` fires if a grant ever lands with no `payment_intent` (un-auto-reversible → manual `admin_adjust`).
- **Merchant-won dispute** → no auto re-grant (no `charge.dispute.closed` handler; owner re-grants manually). A natural L3 follow-up.

author: mahirkhan0828
body:
## The recurring OG build failure

Every lettersprite deploy, 1–3 phantom sites failed their production build with:

```
Error occurred prerendering page "/opengraph-image"
Error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')
```

…hitting a *different* set of sites each time and clearing on a manual redeploy.

## Root cause (reproduced)

The generated OG card (`src/lib/og.tsx`) fetches its brand fonts from Google Fonts **at build time**, best-effort. When that fetch flakes (transient network failure during the static export), `displayFamily`/`bodyFamily` come back `undefined`, and the card elements were rendered with `fontFamily: undefined`.

Reproduced directly against `next/og`:

| style | result |
|-------|--------|
| `fontFamily: undefined` | **throws `undefined … 'split'`** |
| `fontFamily: "Oswald"` (unloaded) | OK |
| key omitted | OK |

Satori splits `fontFamily` on `,`; a bare `undefined` crashes it and aborts the whole export. The flaky fetch is why it was transient and site-random.

## Fix

A small `fam()` helper includes `fontFamily` **only when the face actually loaded**; a failed font load now degrades to `next/og`'s bundled default font instead of crashing the build.

```ts
const fam = (name?: string) => (name ? { fontFamily: name } : {});
// …style={{ …fam(bodyFamily) }}
```

## Verification

- Reproduced the exact error and the fix against `next/og` locally.
- `eslint` + `tsc --noEmit`: clean.

body:
## Summary
A raw control-character byte inside a quoted string in the function-call DSL surfaced the bare
`serde_json` message ("control character ... found while parsing a string"), which teaches nothing
and sends callers toward the wrong workaround. This wraps the `serde_json` string-decode error at the
`parse_value` call site so the message names the offending character and position, states that DSL
string escapes follow JSON (`\n`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\`), and notes that callers passing `ops` through a
JSON transport (every MCP client) must double-escape (`\\n` in the wire form, because the transport
decodes one level before the parser runs). Grammar unchanged (ADR-016 / ADR-084 §3c basis).

## Scope note
PR #957 already normalizes raw `\n`/`\r`/`\t` bytes before they reach `serde_json`, so those no
longer error at all. The bare-serde-message problem remained for the other raw control bytes (NUL,
form feed, ESC, ...); this addresses the error message for that remaining path.

## Tests
`control_char_error_teaches_escape_syntax_and_mcp_double_escape` feeds a raw form-feed byte in a
quoted value and asserts the error is `DslError::InvalidValue` with a message carrying the escape
grammar and the double-escape guidance. Non-control-character parse errors pass through unchanged.

Gates: `cargo test -p khive-request` (122 passed), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo clippy -p khive-request --all-targets -- -D warnings` all clean.

author: hugocorreia90
body:
## Consistent state snapshot for the remote-`[state]` uploader

Part of the remote-state hardening series (follows the typed-authority + `RemoteStateSession` spine and the add-wins freeze markers). This PR removes the torn read from the mid-run state upload and is the prerequisite for the upcoming CAS work.

### Problem

The mid-run periodic uploader snapshotted the live ledger with an **unlocked `std::fs::copy`** while the run's `StateStore` held the file open and kept committing write transactions. On the Linux pods where this bites, a byte copy can smear across a commit — the uploaded blob is a torn read (an internally inconsistent redb file, or one that won't reopen). redb 2.6.3 offers no `Database::backup` and no untyped row iteration, so a plain copy was the only tool in reach.

### Change

- **`StateStore::snapshot_to_excluding`** — a consistent logical export under one `begin_read` (MVCC) snapshot: every row is drawn from a single committed state, so no concurrent writer can tear a correlated pair. The live store keeps taking writers throughout (the method holds only a read txn), so the run is never blocked. Tables are opened via a **closed static registry** (the state schema is exactly two key/value shapes); a table present on disk but absent from the registry is a hard error, never a silent drop.
- **`write_epoch` dirty signal** — an in-memory `AtomicU64` bumped by a single `commit_write` chokepoint that every production write transaction routes through. The periodic uploader captures the epoch *before* its read and re-uploads only when it has advanced, so a clean tick costs zero I/O. (In-memory only — the local-backend blob stays byte-identical.)
- **Periodic uploader over a `Weak` handle** — the uploader holds a `Weak<StateStore>`, never a strong clone, so the run tail's `Arc::try_unwrap` (which recovers the owned store for the terminal writes) is never blocked. Shutdown is **cooperative** (signal + join) rather than a bare `abort()`: an aborted task would detach the in-flight `spawn_blocking` snapshot, leaking its scratch file and holding its store upgrade past `try_unwrap`. The snapshot runs on the blocking pool and its scratch file is removed by a Drop guard.
- **End-of-run finalize is now lock-free** — the owned `StateStore` is dropped before `session.finalize()` at every finalize site, so its copy runs against a quiescent, unlocked file (the redb `Database` and its advisory writer lock are released first).
- Snapshots larger than 128 MiB `warn!` (documented; streaming is deferred to keep the CAS put path single-shot).

### Tests

- MVCC snapshot never tears a correlated pair under concurrent writer load, with a **RED demo** proving a non-atomic byte copy *does* tear (the test fails if it can't observe a tear).
- Registry matches the on-disk table set and pins the closed two-shape split; an unregistered table errors.
- `write_epoch` bumps on every production write method (both shapes, insert + delete); epoch is captured in the safe direction (recorded value never overstates snapshot content).
- Periodic uploader uploads on a dirty epoch and skips clean ticks (put-count instrumented); cooperative stop drains with no late upload and no leaked scratch.
- Drop-before-finalize is a genuine RED→GREEN discriminator (the writer lock is held while the store is open, free after the drop); terminal writes still persist with the periodic wired.

### Compatibility

No `rocky.toml` surface change, no redb bump, no remote-key change, no `*Output`/schema change (no codegen or fixture cascade). Local-backend blob byte-identical; short runs (no periodic) unchanged.

Gates green locally: `cargo nextest run -p rocky-core -p rocky-cli` (2968 passed), `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

body:
## Objective

Create the durable, tenant-isolated database and ORM foundation for future AI processing without executing AI or exposing any new application capability.

## Implementation summary

- Added `AIJob` with `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` lifecycle states.
- Added immutable/versioned `AIArtifact` storage for the initial `infrastructure_test` type.
- Pinned jobs and artefacts to an exact organisation, meeting, transcript, and transcript version.
- Added integer minor-unit cost storage, bounded safe error metadata, token and duration telemetry fields.
- Added tenant-safe idempotency and logical artefact-version uniqueness.
- Added ORM navigation without eager-loading JSON content.
- Added database, migration, rollback, drift, cross-tenant, and PostgreSQL RLS coverage.
- Added the WO-004A1 sprint record, schema documentation, architecture/security updates, and ADR 0005.

## Database migration

Alembic revision: `0004_ai_database_foundation`

The migration:

1. adds composite transcript uniqueness needed for tenant-safe trace foreign keys;
2. creates `ai_jobs` with lifecycle, numeric, length, currency, idempotency, requester, trace, and lookup controls;
3. creates `ai_artifacts` with confidence, version, exact-job-trace, logical-version, and lookup controls;
4. validates the current transcript version on job insertion and prevents later job trace changes;
5. prevents artefact content/trace overwrite while allowing a one-way `superseded_at` marker; and
6. enables and forces PostgreSQL RLS on both tables.

Downgrade removes artefacts before jobs and removes the added transcript composite uniqueness while preserving Sprint 3 tables. Rollback destroys AI foundation rows and therefore requires an environment-appropriate backup.

## Security and tenant isolation

- Both new tables have non-null `organisation_id`.
- Composite foreign keys reject cross-tenant meeting, transcript, requester, job, and artefact relationships.
- Artefact organisation/meeting/transcript/version must exactly match its job.
- PostgreSQL RLS uses the existing transaction-local trusted organisation context and is both enabled and forced.
- Tests cover tenant A read/write denial against tenant B for both tables and verify forced RLS flags.
- Jobs store only bounded safe error metadata; no secrets, raw prompts, transcript copies, or full provider responses were added to audit data.
- No production customer data was used or should be used.

## Validation

Passed locally:

- Ruff lint and formatting
- mypy strict
- Pytest: 69 passed; the PostgreSQL-only RLS test skipped locally and runs in CI against PostgreSQL 16
- Migration upgrade, downgrade, re-upgrade, and drift
- PostgreSQL offline DDL generation
- Repository secret/scope audit
- Prettier, ESLint, and TypeScript
- Vitest: 21 passed
- Playwright Chromium: 6 passed
- Next.js production build
- API source distribution and wheel build

The external npm advisory scan reports one pre-existing moderate transitive PostCSS advisory (`GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93`, via Next.js, patched in PostCSS 8.5.10). The web dependency graph is unchanged because remediation is outside this database-only work order.

## Known limitations

- Sprint 3 transcript versions are counters on one mutable row; historical transcript bodies are not preserved.
- Null idempotency keys remain distinct at the database layer; a future service must require a non-null key.
- `content_json` is persistence only; a future authorised service must validate typed content before insert.
- No production identity, retention/export/erasure, or operational control is completed by this work.
- The new tables are not exposed through repositories, services, APIs, or UI.

## Explicitly out of scope

No repository, service, lifecycle transition service, worker, job claiming, retry execution, provider abstraction, mock provider, OpenAI integration, prompt registry, output parser, API endpoint, frontend, polling, summary, decision, action, risk, question, follow-up email, CRM feature, integration, recording, transcription, embedding, memory, automation, billing, or autonomous agent was added.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Confirm migration upgrade/downgrade ordering and PostgreSQL 16 compatibility.
- [ ] Confirm exact transcript trace and job/artefact composite foreign keys.
- [ ] Confirm idempotency and logical artefact-version uniqueness.
- [ ] Confirm job trace and artefact overwrite guards.
- [ ] Confirm enabled/forced RLS and cross-tenant tests.
- [ ] Confirm indexes match the approved lookup and future scheduling shapes.
- [ ] Confirm documentation accurately states the mutable transcript-history limitation.
- [ ] Confirm no WO-004A1 out-of-scope implementation is present.
- [ ] Confirm all required GitHub Actions checks pass.

This PR is intentionally a draft and must not be merged as part of WO-004A1.

author: mckoss
body:
## New Playwright coverage

Five new specs (14 tests total, all green) driving the production build in a real browser:

| Spec | Targets |
|------|---------|
| **shows.spec** | Public `/shows` — the security-critical privacy allowlist: hidden gigs, addresses, and band-only notes must never render; canceled marking; subscribe links carry the `webcal://` feed; copy-to-clipboard |
| **calendar-feed.spec** | `/shows/calendar.ics` hit cookieless like a calendar client: content type, CANCELLED projection, hidden-gig/notes leak guard, ETag 304 fast path |
| **gigs.spec** | Band-only gig list shows every gig (incl. hidden) and navigates to the packet with band-only detail |
| **rsvp.spec** | RSVP Yes persists to `rsvps.db` across a reload; Clear removes it |
| **navigation.spec** | App nav links; unknown gig id renders a clean 404 |

Fixtures gain three gigs to exercise these: a canceled show, a hidden gig with fake secrets the leak tests assert on, and an RSVP rehearsal.

## Harness fix: flaky "attempt to write a readonly database"

The RSVP spec exposed a real ordering race in the harness. Playwright's webServer readiness probe boots the server — opening `members`/`rsvps`/`activity.db` — **concurrently with `globalSetup`**, whose `rmSync` of the data dir unlinked those files under the server's open connections. Every later sqlite write then failed with `SQLITE_READONLY_DBMOVED`, surfaced as *"attempt to write a readonly database"* (reproduced deterministically: open dbs → wipe dir → write fails).

Fix: the wipe/seed now runs as the **first step of the webServer command** (`node e2e/seed.mjs && npm run build && node build`), strictly before the server boots, so nothing ever unlinks the stores after they're open. `globalSetup` and the `warmup.setup.ts` project — which worked around a misdiagnosed "first-time creation race" (concurrent creation of a new sqlite file is actually fine) — are removed.

No application code changed.

## Verification
- e2e: **14/14 passed**, stable across 5 consecutive full-suite runs (was flaky before)
- unit: **356/356 passed**

**READY FOR REVIEW — awaiting Warwick's merge.** Head `0efc9fa`. **CI green** (unit + integration + secret-scan). **105/105 tests.** Frozen reactor branches untouched. **No live watcher started. Nothing merged.**

author: nb11b
body:
Adds the v3 grammar front end for deterministic exact expression discovery.

## Core pipeline

```text
checked grammar
→ bounded canonical expression enumeration
→ exact blade-wise integer polynomial classification
→ exact and primitive equivalence classes
→ deterministic relation ranking
→ scoped symbolic certificates
→ automatic near-miss controls
→ exact prime-field corpus
→ generated host/CUDA evaluators
→ exact witness search and reduction
```

## Implemented

- checked JSON grammars for dimension, signature, variable grades, operators, expression cost, semantic-class limits, and corpus limits
- deterministic canonical expression enumeration
- exact polynomial hashes for identical expression semantics
- primitive hashes after removing integer content and overall sign
- recovery of integer-multiple relations
- bounded relation selection with stable identifiers
- exact certificate emission
- automatic one-edit controls admitted only with nonzero polynomials and exact deterministic witnesses
- prime-matrix expansion into the existing v1-compatible host/CUDA manifest format
- deterministic unit tests, host workflow, and a Windows CUDA evidence runner
- task, component, README, wiki, and knowledge-graph records

## Initial grammars

- vector products in `Cl(4,0)`
- unrestricted multivector reversion/product relations in signature `(2,2)`
- nested commutator and cyclic Jacobi relations in `Cl(3,0)`

Representative baseline equivalence classes include:

- `[a,b] = 2(a ∧ b)` for vectors
- `reverse(a b) = reverse(b) reverse(a)`
- `[a,b] = -[b,a]`
- the cyclic commutator Jacobi expression has a zero polynomial

These are validation controls for the discovery machinery, not claims of previously unknown results.

## Validation architecture

- grammar parser rejection tests
- exact polynomial and integer-multiplier checks
- enumeration and relation-selection determinism
- repeated corpus-build byte equality
- generated v1 specification compatibility
- exact near-miss precheck witnesses
- host evaluator compilation and execution
- physical CUDA identity/control matrix with host witness reproduction and reduction

Hosted GitHub Actions attempts currently terminate before executing any job steps, including the pre-existing exact-host workflow. The workflows and local gates remain checked in, while local exact-host and physical CUDA validation are the active acceptance path.

## Physical smoke gate

```powershell
& .\benchmarks\geo_identity_search\scripts\run_identity_grammar_discovery.ps1 `
    -Assignments 131072 `
    -CpuChecks 512 `
    -Primes @(65521,65519) `
    -PrecheckAssignments 1024 `
    -MaxRelations 8 `
    -MaxControls 2 `
    -Archive
```

## Full gate

```powershell
& .\benchmarks\geo_identity_search\scripts\run_identity_grammar_discovery.ps1 `
    -Assignments 262144 `
    -CpuChecks 1024 `
    -Primes @(65521,65519,65497,32749) `
    -PrecheckAssignments 2048 `
    -MaxRelations 12 `
    -MaxControls 4 `
    -Archive
```

## Interpretation boundary

An exact zero blade-wise integer difference polynomial establishes a relation only for its declared dimension, diagonal signature, variable grade supports, and commutative scalar-coefficient model. A finite-field witness is exact in its field. Relation ranking is a search heuristic, not a measure of mathematical importance.

The PR remains draft until the local exact-host and physical CUDA gates pass.

author: adamlabadorf
body:
Fixes #127 — a single-valued reference whose range is a **polymorphic base** (abstract, or concrete with concrete subclasses) had **zero referential integrity**: a dangling id was silently accepted on both `put` and `ingest` (`created=1, errors=0`, no exception), while a non-polymorphic reference (a real FK) still caught it.

## Root cause

Such references get no SQL foreign key — subtype instances are dispatched to their own per-class tables, so no single table can be the FK target (#93), and `ddl_generator._post_process_create_table` strips the constraint. The integrity *check* was dropped along with the constraint rather than replaced.

## Fix

Referential integrity for these slots is enforced in the application layer, reusing the existing `_entity_registry` cross-class index (the `resolve_type` machinery from #116) — no per-descendant-table probing needed:

- **Deferred to commit.** Written references are queued during `create` / `update` and verified just before `conn.commit()`, in both the single-write `_transaction` and the ingest `staged_transaction`. Because the check reads the committing connection, staged-but-uncommitted registrations are visible — so **forward references within a bundle resolve**, exactly as SQLite's deferred FKs do (#95). A per-row eager check would have broken legitimate out-of-order ingest.
- **Validation.** The target id must be registered under a class within the reference's declared base subtree (`concrete_subclasses(base)` ∪ base). A missing id → dangling; an id under an unrelated class → wrong-type. Either raises the new **`DanglingReferenceError`** (a `ValidationError` subclass, so REST 422 / GraphQL `VALIDATION_FAILED` apply) and rolls the write back.
- Scoped to **single-valued** references (the ones stored as a bare TEXT id). Multivalued references persist as relationship rows (#79) and are out of scope.

In the Brain Bank schema this closes the gap on `Dataset.produced_by → Activity`, `Diagnosis.sample → Sample`, and `Measurement.sample → Sample`.

## Verification

Confirmed against the issue's scenario (abstract `Activity` base, concrete `Assay` subtype):
```
valid produced_by      -> ACT-1            (accepted)
dangling (single put)  -> DanglingReferenceError
forward-ref in bundle  -> ACT-2            (resolves — created later in same staged txn)
dangling in bundle     -> DanglingReferenceError (whole bundle rolled back)
```

## Tests

`tests/core/test_polymorphic_reference_integrity.py` — abstract- and concrete-base valid/dangling cases, wrong-type rejection, forward-reference resolution and dangling rollback within a staged bundle, the update path, the null-reference no-op, and the non-polymorphic-FK control.

Full `tests/core` suite green locally — **1286 passed**. No regression from the added commit-time hook: for schemas without polymorphic-base references nothing is queued and the check is a no-op.

Closes #127

author: jakechampion
body:
Follow-up to #5077 — the next slice of making the self-host compiler cheaper to compile.

## What

A function's lowered IR is dead the moment `emitFunc` returns, but both native backends held the whole `ip.Funcs` slice until the last byte of output was written — tens of millions of ~160 B ops staying live exactly when the output buffer is at its largest. Both emit loops (x86-64 + arm64) now nil each entry as they advance, so the GC reclaims the IR incrementally (nothing after the loop reads `ip.Funcs`; the walk is forward-only).

With the live set now *shrinking* through emission (ends ~1.1 GB vs ~3.9 GB), the harness caps tighten to bank the win:

- `FERN_EMIT_MEMLIMIT_MB` default 5120 → **4300** (still ~900 MB above the ~3.4 GB live peak at emission start)
- `FERN_BUILD_HEAVY_MB` default 6500 → **5800** — more concurrent-build admission on large hosts

## Measured (asm_ir_run driver emit, 4-core / 16 GB host)

| | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| original (pre-#5077) | 134 s | 9.0 GB |
| soft cap only (#5077) | 111 s | 6.25 GB |
| cap + IR release (this PR) | **74 s** | **5.2 GB** |

The speedup comes from GC cycles getting progressively cheaper as emitted functions' IR dies.

## Verification

- **x86-64 output byte-identical**: the full 470 MB driver emit compared against the pre-change emit, twice (at both cap values).
- **arm64 output byte-identical**: stash-compare on `parser.fern` before/after the change.
- Unit suites pass (`e2eharness`, `native/x86_64`, `codegen/x86_64`).
- Cold e2e driver builds through the new caps pass: `TestSelfHostIRF64Eligible`, `TestSelfHostReuseDifferentialX86_64` (covers the env-dependent driver path fixed in #5077).

author: walight999
body:
## Why

The Week Ahead card (and every other LINE push) went silent for ~a week from Jul 11. Root cause: LINE's free-tier **monthly quota was exhausted** → every push returned 429. The one alert that fires for this (`line_push_failing`, CRITICAL) is itself **pushed over LINE** — so the dead channel swallowed its own alarm. The 80% quota early-warning (`line_quota_high`) is ROUTINE (surfaces only in the EoD digest, also LINE), so it never reached anyone either. Workflows kept reporting success the whole time.

## What

- **`src/ops_alert.py`** — a direct Telegram Bot API DM to the operator, the only delivery path that does **not** depend on LINE. Env-gated (`OPS_TG_BOT_TOKEN` + `OPS_TG_CHAT_ID`), best-effort, never raises. Kept separate from `telegram_news.py` (whose webhooks fan out to public subscribers) — ops alarms stay private.
- Critical health warnings + the `line_quota_high` early-warning now **mirror to the ops channel** from both `run_watchdog` and `run_once`'s health pass.
- `line_client._send` now **preserves the real HTTP status** on failure (was a blind status-0). `record_line_outcome` stamps `last_status`; `check_pipeline_health` uses it so the alert says **why** LINE is down: `429` = quota exhausted (resets on the 1st, self-heals) vs `401/403` = token/channel broken (needs a human). Also feeds the upcoming quota-aware sender gate.
- `store.py`: `+last_status` column on `source_state` (additive — `_ensure_tab` rewrites the header, existing rows get `""`).
- Wired `OPS_TG_*` env into `news_cron` / `event_mode` / `watchdog`.

Deliberately did **not** touch the cooldown backoff (immediate → 4h → 12h): it is correct anti-spam for a genuine multi-day outage; the bug was the delivery *channel*, not the frequency.

## Operator step (to activate)

Set two GitHub secrets: `OPS_TG_BOT_TOKEN` (may reuse @FinisitNews_bot's token) and `OPS_TG_CHAT_ID` (the operator's private DM chat id). Until set, the ops channel is a graceful no-op.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/ -q` → **294 passed** (+9)
- New tests cover: no-op when unconfigured, `should_mirror` taxonomy (critical + quota yes, routine no), send never raises, mirror drops routine warnings, and 429-vs-401 alert messaging.

author: ozand
body:
## Problem (live, 2026-07-18 01:03–01:16Z)

The first self-fix attempt after the #789 tamper repair mis-targeted: the loop proposed removing the `operator-confirmed` state-writing from **error_pattern_audit.py**, but the hack lives in **approval_truth.py**. The tamper-defect item's "likely writer" hint derived from the tampered entry's `files_changed` — which names the entry's own integrated artifact (the VICTIM), not the script that wrote the foreign signal (the perpetrator). The subagent honestly found nothing to remove → outcome partial, one wasted cycle.

## Fix

- New bounded helper `_tamper_suspect_scripts(selfevo_repo, signal)`: text-searches the instance repo's `scripts/*.py` (each file read once, 200KB size cap, fail-open) for either the foreign signal literal (from `tamper_signal`) or the sidecar filename (`completed.json`). Matching scripts (bounded 3, sorted) become named suspects in the defect evidence: `signal 'operator-confirmed' written by non-harness code into demand/completed.json — found in scripts/approval_truth.py; remove its state-writing`. No match / no repo → the generic wording, never a fabricated attribution.
- The `files_changed` victim hint is removed entirely.
- With named suspects the item id is keyed on **entry_id + perpetrator set**, so a corrected attribution mints a FRESH demand id that reaches the loop even if the mis-attributed item was already exhausted by the wasted attempts. Without suspects the stable per-entry id is unchanged.
- `collect_demand` now passes `selfevo_repo` into `_tamper_defect_items`.

## Tests

`tests/test_demand.py::TestTamperPerpetratorAttribution` (new) + updated `TestTamperDefectDemand`:
- live fixture (victim `error_pattern_audit.py` in `files_changed`, signal literal in `approval_truth.py`) → evidence names `approval_truth.py` and NOT `error_pattern_audit.py`; `affected_path` = perpetrator
- sidecar-filename (`completed.json`) match alone is a suspect
- no-match → generic wording, id identical to the repo-less item
- 5 matching scripts → exactly 3 named (bounded)
- >200KB file skipped (bounded read)
- exhaustion interplay: generic (mis-attributed) id exhausted under current head/release → corrected perpetrator-keyed item has a fresh id and still surfaces via `collect_demand`

Full suite: 1724 passed, 2 failed (known systemd-dependent noise in `tests/test_cycle_health_summary.py`). Ruff clean on touched files.

Closes #792

author: d-takeuchi
body:
Fixes #799.

#785 added the `APP_USER` environment variable so that Sail commands run as a
custom user (`docker compose exec -u "$APP_USER"`). However, nothing actually
creates that user inside the container, so with the stock runtimes any value
other than `sail` breaks every command:

    unable to find user test: no matching entries in passwd file

This PR makes `start-container` create the user on startup when it does not
already exist, using the same approach as the existing `sail` user and sharing
the `sail` group so file permissions behave the same. The compose stub now also
passes `APP_USER` into the container, since `bin/sail` already exports it.

When `APP_USER` is unset or left at its default (`sail`), the script does
nothing, so existing projects are unaffected. I verified this by building the
8.4 runtime: with `APP_USER=test`, the user is created and
`docker compose exec -u test` works; without it, the container's passwd entries
are identical to before the change.

author: tyler-r-kendrick
body:
Implements **SLM-128 / LDI3-01** — a shared, **architecture-neutral** objective library adding three OpenUI-native structured local-preference objectives over the exact grammar-legal action sets. One implementation (pure functions of a 1-D logit row + materialized action sets) that both the causal and TwoTower trainers call — the trainer extracts the row, this module owns the math, nothing duplicated in architecture-specific files. Builds on the SLM-116/117 materializers + objective-support admission now on `main`.

## What landed
`src/slm_training/harnesses/preference/structured_objectives.py`:
- **`StructuredObjectiveConfig`** — typed, versioned, fail-closed-on-unknown-fields config with a deterministic `content_sha` fingerprint (part of run/adapter identity).
- **`StructuredObjectiveInput`** — logits + legal/good/bad/ambiguous/unobserved sets + per-action evidence weights, roles, criticality, optional same-state reference; rejects empty good/bad, out-of-legal ids, overlapping partitions.
- **Objective A — Legal-Set FTPO** (two variants): explicitly pair-weighted `G × B` set margin normalized per state, and a legal probability-mass margin `softplus(margin + log P_B − log P_G)` reporting good/bad/ambiguous/unobserved mass separately.
- **Objective B — TAB-PO-inspired barrier**: additive, separately-metered SFT anchor `−log p_legal(g)` for verifier-critical, under-confident good actions (zero for confident; structural roles default low) + a `token_erosion_rate` metric.
- **Objective C — TBPO-inspired ratio control**: bounded good-vs-bad log-ratio control against a same-state reference, advantage-centered or centered by a serializable `StateBaseline` fit only from train states; disabled + reported without a reference.
- **Composition**: preference + optional barrier + target/non-target locality tethers, each separately metered (no double-counting); per-state-normalized batch loss so large action sets can't dominate (un-normalized mode kept for ablation); a no-model-update fixture report generator.

Existing `ce_margin`/`unlikelihood`/`ftpo_*` are **untouched** (new names) — historical behavior and the **68 existing preference tests are unchanged**.

## Tests
`tests/test_harnesses/preference/test_structured_objectives.py` (16, green): both Legal-Set FTPO variants match hand-computed values, state normalization prevents large-set dominance, legal mass sums over only the legal set, barrier selectivity + structural-role weighting, erosion detection, ambiguous/unobserved normalized-but-never-targets, ratio control compares at identical states and disables without a reference, state-baseline fit + round-trip, mass-margin gradients match finite differences, tiny-probability numeric stability, config round-trip/fingerprint/fail-closed validation, architecture-neutral call over "causal"/"TwoTower" mock logits, and input validation. `ruff`, `python -m scripts.repo_policy`, `git diff --check` clean.

## Evidence artifact
`docs/design/iter-ldi3-01-structured-objectives-20260718.md` + a deterministic fixture report. author: junjihashimoto
body:
## Route the framework's outbound HTTPS through the native TLS client

Follow-up to #13 (the OpenSSL `TlsClient`). Makes the existing serving exes
actually speak HTTPS natively instead of shelling out to curl.

- **`LeanTea.Llm.Openai`** — `chat` / `chatRaw` now call
  `LeanTea.Net.postJsonText` (the scheme dispatcher) instead of the
  http-only `HttpClient`. `http://` (LM Studio) still uses the socket
  client; `https://` (OpenAI proper) now uses the OpenSSL `TlsClient`. Every
  serving exe that talks to an LLM gets HTTPS for free. `chatStream` stays
  curl-backed (streaming SSE).
- **lakefile** — package-wide `moreLinkArgs := tlsLinkArgs`, which is
  `sslLinkArgs` **only** when `LEANTEA_TLS=1` (read via `run_io` at configure
  time) and empty otherwise. So with the flag every exe links
  libssl/libcrypto (HTTPS-capable); the default portable build never touches
  OpenSSL. `https_smoke` drops its own `weakLinkArgs` (covered package-wide).

### Toggle note
Link args are read at configure time, so switching `LEANTEA_TLS` on an
existing build dir needs one reconfigure to re-read them (and match the
build-time C backend):
```
LEANTEA_TLS=1 lake build -R <exe>
```
A fresh checkout built with the flag from the start needs no `-R`.

### Verified
- `LEANTEA_TLS=1 lake build -R llm_chat_cli` → links openssl (2 ssl libs);
- default build → 0 ssl libs (portable);
- `https_smoke` still GETs `https://example.com`;
- default lib + downstream `lean-tea-chuhan` still build.

author: ben-gy
body:
## Summary
**What:** A top-down, two-team capture-the-flag tank arena. Drive, aim, and bank ricochet shots off the walls; steal the enemy flag and race it home. First team to 3 captures wins. Bullets take two hits (a graze cracks you); grabbing a flag grants a brief adrenaline invuln so a run is a real race; nobody is ever eliminated (respawn). Power-ups: spread, rapid, speed, shield, extra ricochet.
**Genre:** arcade
**Multiplayer:** live P2P (2–4 humans, always a 2v2 with bots backfilling empty seats), host-authoritative snapshot star, versus.
**Stack:** Vite + TypeScript, Canvas 2D, Trystero P2P.

🎮 **Play:** https://tiny-tanks.benrichardson.dev

## Features
- Ricochet bullets you bank around corners — and your own rebound can kill you
- Capture-the-flag objective with two-hit tanks, respawns, and a grab-invuln so runs complete
- Twin floating analog sticks on touch (left drives, right aims + auto-fires); WASD + mouse on desktop
- Three modes that change the SPATIAL problem: Clash (open), Labyrinth (dense cover), Rampart (structured chokes)
- Bots fill empty seats and play the objective; solo is a full 2v2 (you + a bot ally vs two bots)
- Portrait arena that fills a phone screen; installable PWA; procedural art + audio, no assets

## Balance (principle 18)
The sim is **provably point-symmetric** — a mirror-input fairness test keeps seat 0 and seat 1 exactly mirrored for a whole game, so team fairness is true by construction (not luck). `tests/balance.test.ts` plays 160 AI-vs-AI 2v2 games per mode and asserts the shape:
- Team win rate **48–55%** (all three modes)
- P(leader-at-first-capture wins) **66–72%** (< 82 — comebacks happen)
- ~0–1 timeouts of 160 (games reach the cap), blowouts 13–19%, ~50–70s games

The sim referee OVERRULED the design repeatedly (documented in `src/game/arena.ts` / `bot.ts`): with one-shot kills bots scored **zero** captures; the fixes measured, not argued, were two-hit tanks, a grab-invuln, cover on the return path, and — the fairness bug the sim caught — a self-symmetric centre pickup that the lower seat always won (removed).

## Test Results
- [x] `npm test` — 122 tests pass, incl. P2P-sync determinism, **point-symmetry fairness**, snapshot round-trip, host-transfer takeover, room-code normalization, host-election, no-deadlock rematch, one-join net-lifecycle, Trystero-rejoin characterization, source-hygiene, per-mode layout invariant, and the balance sim
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds
- [x] Bug fixes mutation-verified (checkOver tiebreak → red; self-symmetric pickup → fairness + layout tests red)
- [x] Verified in-browser at ~375px — **every mode** (Clash, Labyrinth, Rampart) fills the portrait phone screen, zero horizontal overflow, twin-stick zones on-screen, overlay correctly hidden, zero console errors

author: aidantemple
body:
## Summary

Fixes a set of correctness bugs and dead code found during a code review of the initial commit, plus follow-up cleanup:

- **Crash fix**: `WaveManager.CurrentWave` called `Queue.Peek()` unguarded, throwing `InvalidOperationException` once the player cleared the last wave. `Update()`, `Draw()`, `Enemies`, and `WaveNumber` now handle an empty wave queue safely.
- **Double missile hit**: `GameScene.HandleCollisions()` could apply a missile hit to an enemy that another missile had already killed in the same frame, double-counting score and spawning a duplicate death effect. `Enemy.CurrentHealth`'s setter now synchronously flips `IsAlive` to `false` at zero health, and the collision check now guards on `enemy.IsAlive`.
- **Unclamped player movement**: `Player.Update()` only clamped `Position.X` to the viewport; vertical drags could push the ship off-screen. `Position.Y` is now clamped the same way.
- **Enemy laser slot bug**: `Enemy.FireLaser()` only ever searched 2 of the 6 allocated laser slots, and skipped resetting its cooldown timer on a successful fire, producing an unintended burst-then-silence firing pattern. It now cycles through all slots and resets the cooldown on every fire.
- **Dead code in `Wave.cs`**: the off-screen enemy re-lane check could never run because `Enemy.UpdateMovement()` already wrapped `Position.Y` at the same threshold one step earlier. The re-lane randomization now lives in `Enemy.UpdateMovement()` (the place that actually owns the wrap). Also removed a `HasReachedEnd` branch nested inside an `IsDead` check that required a condition `IsDead` already excludes, so it could never fire.
- **Game-over transition**: the scene transition to `StatScene` on player death was commented out with a `TODO`; `StatScene` was already fully implemented and used elsewhere via the same pattern, so it's now wired up.
- **Redundant draws**: `Player`, `Enemy`, `Laser`, `Weapons/Missile.cs`, and `Weapons/Torpedo.cs` each drew their sprite manually and then also called the inherited `base.Draw()`, issuing a wasted second `SpriteBatch.Draw` per entity every frame. Removed.
- **Cleanup**: named the enemy spawn-lane bounds (`GameVariables.EnemySpawnMinX/MaxX/MinY/MaxY`) instead of duplicating magic numbers in `Enemy.cs` and `Wave.cs`; derived the enemy wrap threshold from the real viewport (`m_ViewportRect.Height`) instead of a hardcoded `800`; deleted the orphaned, unbuilt duplicate `Missile.cs`/`Torpedo.cs` at the project root (only the `Weapons/` copies were ever compiled).

## Test plan

This is a WP8/XNA/MonoGame project targeting an SDK not available in this environment, so changes could not be compiled or run here.

- [ ] Build in Visual Studio with the Windows Phone 8 / MonoGame SDK
- [ ] Play through to clear all 24 waves and confirm no crash on the final wave
- [ ] Rapidly tap-fire missiles into a single enemy and confirm only one kill/score increment/explosion occurs
- [ ] Drag the ship to the top and bottom edges of the screen and confirm it stays on-screen
- [ ] Observe enemy fire rate/laser count over an extended play session
- [ ] Let the player die and confirm the game transitions to the stat screen

author: alexgleason
body:
## Problem

OpenCode ≥ 1.17 passes `agent` to the `chat.headers` plugin hook as the agent **name** (a string), not the `{ name, mode }` object the plugin expects. The plugin's string branch hardcodes `x-opencode-agent-mode: primary`, so **subagent detection silently never fires** on current OpenCode.

Field data (OpenCode 1.17.20, Meridian 1.52.0): **2280/2280** requests in my journal ran as `agent=primary` — every explore/task subagent went out at the primary 1M tier, burning rate-limit budget. Verified empirically by dumping the hook input:

```json
{"keys":["sessionID","agent","model","provider","message"],"agent":"explore","agentType":"string","providerID":"anthropic"}
```

## Fix

Resolve the mode for string agents from the plugin's `config` hook (merged OpenCode config, which carries `agent.<name>.mode` for user-defined agents and built-in overrides), layered over a built-in agent mode map (`build`/`plan` primary, `general`/`explore` subagent). The legacy object shape keeps working unchanged. `mode: "all"` normalizes to primary (can't tell per-request; preserves capability).

Live-verified on my deployment: subagent requests now log `agent=subagent` and route to the 200k tier, primaries keep `[1m]`.

## Tests

- New `src/__tests__/plugin-agent-mode.test.ts` — 11 direct unit tests of the plugin covering both runtime shapes, config-hook resolution, built-in overrides, `all` normalization, provider filtering, name sanitization, and per-instance state isolation.
- Full suite: 2010+ pass / 0 fail; `bun run typecheck` clean.

author: n3fariox
body:
On Linux, reading from the PTY master after the slave closes returns -1/EIO rather than 0/EOF. The reader thread was silently dropping this error without sending PtyEvent::Exited, so the server never learned the child died until the 3-second keepalive timer fired try_wait().

- Treat PTY read errors the same as EOF (matches stock mosh mosh#264)
- Drop pair.master on Unix so the reader thread holds the sole master FD, ensuring EOF/EIO is delivered reliably
- Use ioctl(TIOCSWINSZ) for resize on Unix, keep pair.master.resize() on Windows for ConPTY compatibility

Additionally, it refactors system health checks into a dedicated service. The most important changes are:

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1b87523352213b3e6c7750c1986dc07c965da8517087afde54af520f978b6fccR164-R196) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cd60dd103eb00bb41b3b062b4b646640d90ae29a9e0430f56922797183e232c5R14-R15) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cd60dd103eb00bb41b3b062b4b646640d90ae29a9e0430f56922797183e232c5R1197-R1245)

**Event Dispatching**

* Modified the import flow to dispatch a notification when a library import completes successfully. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5157e2bcc8d783cdc1d4e923112dcb74c8458f3967a4a7db37c3dbb9aec07016R3-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5157e2bcc8d783cdc1d4e923112dcb74c8458f3967a4a7db37c3dbb9aec07016R69-R76)
