author: huyd0
body:
## Root cause of the `TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND` dashboards

The deploy run's log (run #26, step *Provision dashboard helper objects*) shows:

```
"[dbx-platform] dashboards-setup"  TERMINATED SUCCESS
error: Statement failed (StatementState.FAILED): [NO_SUCH_CATALOG_EXCEPTION]
Catalog 'main' was not found. SQLSTATE: 42704
```

Two stacked bugs:

1. **The workspace has no `main` catalog** (auto-enabled Unity Catalog workspaces get a workspace-named catalog instead), so `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS main.dbx_platform` — the first setup statement — fails, and none of the `main.dbx_platform.*` tables/functions the dashboards query were ever created. `azure-cost-pull` and the forecast jobs fail the same way, so `azure_costs` / `cost_forecasts` have no data path at all.
2. **The failure was invisible**: Databricks `python_wheel_task` calls the entry point function directly and ignores its return value — a task only fails if the function *raises*. `cli.main()` catches the `RuntimeError` and `return 1`s, so every failed job terminates `SUCCESS` and the deploy stays green.

## Fixes

- `pyproject.toml` now points the `dbx-platform` console script at `cli.entry()`, which raises `SystemExit(code)` for non-zero exits — a failed check now fails its scheduled job on both surfaces (CLI exit codes unchanged).
- `dashboards setup` runs `CREATE CATALOG IF NOT EXISTS` before `CREATE SCHEMA`. The catalog statement is best-effort (an identity may lack metastore-level rights even when the catalog exists); if the schema create then fails because the catalog is truly absent, the error now names the remediation (create the catalog, or re-render the dashboards against an existing one).
- Tests cover all three behaviours: catalog-before-schema ordering, tolerated catalog-create failure, loud failure with remediation text, and the entry-point/`pyproject` contract.

## New: Platform Command Center (tabs instead of five separate dashboards)

`dashboards/templates/platform_command_center.lvdash.json` consolidates the five standalone dashboards into **one AI/BI dashboard whose six pages render as tabs**: Overview, Azure Bill & Forecast, Databricks Cost, Jobs, SQL Warehouses, Governance & Lineage.

Design changes vs the community-suite originals (which are single pages named "New Page" with 13–43 widgets stacked ~100 grid rows deep):

- Every tab leads with a **KPI counter row** (currency-formatted via serialized `format` specs, with prior-30d comparison `target`s), then one full-width trend, then breakdowns, then action tables.
- **Filters are honest**: the date-range/workspace/compute-type filters on the Databricks Cost tab are bound to every dataset they claim to filter (the originals bound their "global" date filter to 2–5 of 9–21 datasets, silently ignoring the rest). Fixed-window counters say so in their titles instead of pretending to react.
- **All dataset SQL is time-bounded** (30/90d / 26w) — the originals ran unbounded scans over all of `system.billing.usage` / `system.query.history` / `system.access.table_lineage` history.
- **Datasets are shared across widgets** (26 datasets / 47 widgets), which is what makes AI/BI cross-filtering span widgets and keeps most interaction client-side.
- Skinny unreadable pies replaced with counters/horizontal bars; the dual-axis WoW combo now plots weekly $ (bars, left axis) against growth % (line, right axis) instead of two same-unit series on two axes.
- Only references `main.dbx_platform` objects that `dashboards setup` provisions (enforced by the existing structural test, now covering the new template).

The five original dashboards stay deployed; `resources/dashboards.yml` notes to drop them once the Command Center covers your needs. The new dashboard will render once the catalog issue is resolved (next deploy self-heals it if the CI principal can create catalogs — otherwise create the catalog once or re-render to an existing one).

author: giladresisi
body:
## What this fixes

Confirmed production incident: TikTok's ~24h access token expired during `postSocial`'s status polling — after the publish init + video upload had already succeeded. The workflow's token-refresh loop re-ran `postSocial` from scratch → second init → **two identical TikTok posts**, green workflow, success email. TikTok completes a publish server-side once init + bytes are in; our polling is pure observation, so a re-run must resume observing the in-flight publish, never initiate a new one.

The TikTok provider now reports the `publish_id` via an `'in-progress'` progress status the moment init returns (before the byte upload). A re-run picks it up and polls that publish to completion instead of re-initing; `FAILED` falls through to a clean fresh init (nothing was published), and token/network errors propagate so the next re-run resumes again.

## Why Redis, not the DB (supersedes #1682)

#1682 (closed) implemented this with two nullable `Post` columns. The `publish_id` is only needed **within the scope of publishing the post** — transient de-duplication state, not a long-term record — so it shouldn't be DB-persisted. It lives in Redis under `post:inflight:<postId>` with a **2h TTL**, deleted eagerly on success and TTL-expired otherwise, following the existing ioRedis analytics-cache pattern (5cca81e0). (The marker is deliberately NOT cleared on ERROR: the workflow keeps retrying after marking ERROR for timeout/generic failures, and a re-run must still resume — caught by the Sentry review below, fixed in the second commit.) The TTL aligns with the project's other Redis retention (OAuth connect state and analytics caches: 1h) and comfortably exceeds any single publish saga (~9-min poll window plus retries). **No schema change, no migration, no deploy ordering.**

## Verification (real TikTok test channel)

Injected `access_token_invalid` after init+upload: the re-run resumed the **same** `publish_id` (marker value never changed — no second init) → exactly one TikTok post, state `PUBLISHED`, `releaseId` equal to the crashed attempt's publish_id, marker cleared. author: currentsuspect
body:
## What

The flagship Muse adapter: a **localhost JSONL socket inside the running app**, speaking the exact MuseRepl protocol against the session the user has open. Agent edits execute on the main thread through the same command system as UI edits — **one shared undo stack**, one History panel. The user can Ctrl+Z anything the agent does.

```bash
AESTRA_MUSE_PORT=41952 ./Aestra
# from anywhere local:
echo '{"id":1,"verb":"set_steps","args":{"pattern":1,"unit":1,"pitch":60,"steps":"x---x---x---x---"}}' | nc 127.0.0.1 41952
```

## How

- **`MuseSocketServer`** (AestraAudio, headless-testable): binds **127.0.0.1 only** — a local control surface, never a network service. One IO thread runs a select loop (accept + read + write for N clients) with line framing (1 MiB runaway-line guard, CRLF tolerated). `processPending(service)` is the **only** place requests execute — by contract on the caller's thread.
- **App integration**: opt-in via `AESTRA_MUSE_PORT` (off by default). `AestraApp` starts the server after full init, pumps it once per frame in the `UI_Update` block, marks the root dirty after processed requests (so idle frame elision doesn't hide agent edits), and stops it first in shutdown.
- `ws2_32` linked on Windows; ephemeral-port support keeps tests parallel-safe.

**Known v1 limit** (documented in code): panels that refresh only on user interaction (e.g. the Arsenal unit list) may lag visually until the next interaction; model-observer refresh is follow-up work.

## Validation

- **New `MuseSocketServerTest`** drives a real loopback TCP connection: two requests in one packet split correctly, responses correlate by id, socket edits land in the shared undo history, a garbage line is answered with `parse_error` without dropping the connection, a second client is served independently, clean stop. 14/14.
- Full commands suite 11/11; app target builds.
- **Live proof**: the real GUI app was driven over the socket while its window ran — session state read back (the 50 demo tracks), BPM set to 140, a unit added, and a four-hit kick row written into the live pattern, all visible to the running session's undo history.

author: shaiku
body:
## Problem

Databases open with `run_auto_analysis=False` by default, which defines only entry/export functions. There was no client-reachable way to complete auto-analysis on an already-open database short of closing and reopening it.

The root cause is a name collision. The worker tool that actually runs full auto-analysis (`enable_auto(True); auto_wait()` for IDA, `GhidraProject.analyze()` for Ghidra) was named `wait_for_analysis` — the same name as the supervisor management tool — so the bootstrap filter (`worker_provider.py`) excluded it from the client tool list. The client-visible management `wait_for_analysis` only awaited a background analysis task, which exists solely when `run_auto_analysis=True` at open time. On a database opened with analysis off, it therefore returned immediately **without analyzing anything**, contradicting its name.

## Changes

- **Rename** the worker-side `wait_for_analysis` → **`analyze_database`** (IDA and Ghidra). It no longer collides, so it becomes a client-visible `ANNO_MUTATE` tool. Pinned in both backends' `PINNED_TOOLS` for discoverability.
- **Make `wait_for_analysis` honest:** `wait_for_ready()` now triggers a one-time `analyze_database` pass via `_ensure_analysis_started()` when no analysis has run, is running, or has failed for the worker. A new `Worker._analyzed` flag prevents redundant re-analysis; an explicit `analyze_database` call sets it too (via `RoutingTool.run()`).
- `_background_analysis` proxies `analyze_database` and marks the worker analyzed on success. Dropped the now-dead `wait_for_analysis` exception in the analysis-block guard.
- Updated `docs/architecture.md` and added/adjusted supervisor tests.

## Trade-off

Since the server instructions tell clients to always call `wait_for_analysis` after `open_database`, every database (including already-analyzed `.i64`/`.gpr` files) now gets one idempotent analysis pass on first wait. For IDA this is effectively instant when nothing is queued; for Ghidra `GhidraProject.analyze()` on a fully-analyzed program is cheap but non-zero.

## Testing

- New/updated supervisor tests pass (on-demand trigger fires, already-analyzed skips, prior error not retried).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean; idalib threading lint passes.
- Pre-existing platform-specific test failures (POSIX signals, symlinks, fat Mach-O, darwin/linux paths) are unrelated to this change (confirmed identical on the base tree in a Windows dev environment).

author: samaybar
body:
## Why

The landing page is the first thing a template deployer sees, and it had three problems for a newcomer:

1. **The two-tab split ("I'm new" / "I know what I'm doing") hid content behind a self-assessment.** Someone who clicked the wrong tab never saw the other half. The "pro" tab in particular buried the paid-plan requirement in a grey note at the bottom.
2. **ChatGPT was invisible.** The server has dedicated `search`/`fetch` tools for ChatGPT connector compatibility and both READMEs cover it, but the landing page said "Claude" throughout — a ChatGPT user would assume it doesn't work for them.
3. **Heavy duplication.** The `/mcp` URL appeared twice, the connect steps twice, GitHub instructions in two variants, and "custom connectors require a paid plan" three times — none of them prominent.

## What changed

- **Removed the tabs.** One linear page: requirement banner → what this is → connect it → add GitHub → try this first. Nothing hidden.
- **Added a requirement banner at the top**, visually distinct (amber) rather than the muted grey note. Keeps plan naming deliberately non-specific and points people at their provider's current plans, since tier names and entitlements change.
- **Client-neutral copy throughout** — "your assistant" instead of "Claude", with explicit Claude *and* ChatGPT steps in the connect instructions (ChatGPT needs developer mode enabled).
- **Collapsed `ghPro`/`ghNew` into one `githubBlock`**, with the manual-token path demoted to an "Advanced" line so the `github-connect` flow is the obvious path.
- Dropped the now-dead `showTab` handler and `.tabs`/`.tab` CSS; added `.banner`/`.gh`/`.advanced`.

Net ~1KB smaller and roughly 40% less copy for the same information.

## Verification

- `node --check` passes on the patched file.
- Grepped for dangling references to `showTab`, `ghPro`, `ghNew`, `.pane`, `id="pro"`, `id="new"` — all clear.
- Rendered the template literal to static HTML and confirmed the banner is present, the three section labels are in order, and the URL block now appears once (was twice).

Not verified: how it looks in a real browser at mobile widths. Worth a quick look before merge.

## Not included

Two things discussed but deliberately left out of this PR:

- **`ALLOWED_RAILWAY_EMAILS` required/optional contradiction.** The template marks it required; the code and READMEs describe it as optional with trust-on-first-use. The safe behavior is already what the template does — this just needs a docs wording fix ("required when deploying from the template, optional for manual deploys"). Separate PR.
- **`GITHUB_TOKEN` scope mismatch.** The landing page's manual-token link pre-selects classic `repo`, while `combined/README.md` recommends fine-grained with Administration=R/W for repo creation. These disagree and the classic `repo` scope may not cover repo creation in all cases. Worth resolving separately.

author: djwaldo
body:
## What

Moves the `ts-convert-to-databricks-mv` conversion from **agentic (LLM-emitted) DDL** to a **deterministic Python pipeline**, running from **one source of truth in both runtimes** — the CLI and the Databricks Genie agent. This is the reverse of the from-direction BL-063 pattern.

## Both runtimes, one source of truth

- **CLI:** new `ts databricks build-mv` command (emit-only; reads exported Model/Table TML JSON, writes `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW … WITH METRICS` `.sql` files; no profile, never executes DDL).
- **Databricks Genie agent:** the same pure modules are vendored into `notebooks/databricks_mv_lib.py` via `build_mv_lib.py`'s CLOSURE; the Genie SKILL calls `build_metric_view`/`build_view_ddl` directly. A single canonical `UntranslatableError` (hoisted to `formula_common`) is identity-tested across both directions.

## The reverse translator (new pure modules in `ts_cli/databricks/`)

- `mv_emit_expr.py` — TS-formula tokenizer + recursive-descent parser → dict-AST
- `mv_emit_sql.py` — AST → Databricks SQL (aggregates, `*_if`→FILTER, safe_divide, CASE, null-compare, IN/BETWEEN, pass-through, precedence-aware parenthesization)
- `mv_emit.py` — orchestrator: classify/route columns, joins, cross-measure `MEASURE()/ANY_VALUE()`, cascade-skip of dangling refs, `build_metric_view`, `detect_fact_tables`
- `mv_emit_window.py` — LOD→`OVER(PARTITION BY)`, moving/cumulative/semi-additive/period-offset windows
- `mv_build_view.py` — YAML→DDL wrapper (`$$` guard), view-name, summary

## Summary

Specification and planning artifacts for **003 — First-Visit Product Tour**: an optional, skippable overlay that walks a first-time visitor through FoxMapper's core contribute-and-share loop, then leaves them on a live hunt view ready to file a real report.

The tour is a thin, client-only layer over surfaces that already exist — each step anchors to an existing `data-testid`, state lives in the device-scoped IndexedDB `meta` store, and nothing touches the report log or the network.

## What's in the tour

- Ordered walkthrough: what you're hunting → the map and its **credible-region estimate** → the three ways any radio can report (bearing, signal-strength, "I hear nothing here") → how to bring a team in.
- Fully offline, keyboard-accessible, reduced-motion aware; relaunchable from settings.
- A maintainer-facing **drift safeguard** (a Vitest drift test as source of truth, a Claude Code `PostToolUse` hook to surface it in-session, and a scope doc) so the tour cannot silently rot when a control is renamed or a report kind is added.

## Constitution check

All five principles pass: honest uncertainty (the estimate is shown as a region, never a point — including the empty-map sample), every radio contributes (stock-handheld paths are explicit), offline is normal, plain language (no NRQ/DFS/PHG), and zero cost of entry (device-local state, no account). No new backend; no location-estimate math touched.

## Contents

Spec (with clarifications), plan, research, data model, contracts, quickstart, and a dependency-ordered task list (27 tasks; MVP = User Story 1).

This PR is documentation only — no product code changes yet.

author: myrison
body:
## What changed

The gitleaks secret-scan workflow installed org-wide for SOC2 had two defects present identically in every repo:

1. **Full-history scan on every PR/push.** Every `pull_request` and `push` event re-scanned the entire git history with gitleaks instead of just the new commits — slow, and scales poorly as history grows.
2. **Blanket `continue-on-error: true` around the whole scan step.** This made a scanner crash or a malformed/missing SARIF report indistinguishable from "no secrets found." Only actual secret *findings* are supposed to be report-only; operational failures should fail the job.

This PR ports the exact, already-validated fix for both defects into `homebrew-tap`. The fix already shipped in:

- `hypercurrent` PR #5479 (PE-422)
- `isotope` PR #1816 (PE-423)

Both merged after full local review plus bot review (tessie, greptile). This PR is a mechanical, byte-for-byte port of the same final files from isotope's `main` branch:

- **`scripts/ci/select-gitleaks-range.sh`** — determines the scan range per trigger event. `pull_request` scans `base..head`; `push` scans `before..after` (falling back to a full-history scan with a warning on forced pushes, missing/zero SHAs, or unrelated histories); `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` still do a full-history scan, as intended for the weekly SOC2 sweep. Only ever builds ranges from validated commit object IDs — event-derived values are never evaluated as shell source, since they get forwarded into `run-gitleaks.sh`'s `git log --log-opts`.
- **`scripts/ci/select-gitleaks-range.test.sh`** — self-contained unit tests for the above (builds its own throwaway git fixtures internally; does not touch this repo's history).
- **`scripts/ci/run-gitleaks.sh`** — runs gitleaks with the selected range, validates the SARIF report is well-formed and non-empty, and now fails the job on scanner/report operational failures. Findings themselves remain report-only (warns and exits 0) — unchanged from current behavior.
- **`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml`** — wires the scripts in and removes the blanket `continue-on-error`. The push trigger's `branches: [...]` targets `['main']`, matching this repo's actual default branch (this is the same literal value as isotope's canonical file, since both repos default to `main` — no divergence needed, confirmed explicitly below).

## Why bots are skipped (`[SKIP-BOTS]`)

This is a mechanical, identical port of a diff that has already been:
- Reviewed and merged in hypercurrent (PR #5479 / PE-422)
- Reviewed and merged in isotope (PR #1816 / PE-423)
- Bot-reviewed by both tessie and greptile in both of the above

Re-running tessie/greptile on an unmodified copy of already-approved code would be pure noise. Every repo's `greptile.json` has `{"ignoreKeywords": "[SKIP-BOTS]"}`, and revvie-sdlc's webhook gateway checks PR titles for this marker to skip auto-triggering bot review — that's why it's in the title.

Original review trail:
- hypercurrent PR #5479: https://github.com/revenium/hypercurrent/pull/5479
- isotope PR #1816: https://github.com/revenium/isotope/pull/1816

## Test plan

Local verification performed before pushing (all passed):

- [x] `bash -n` syntax check on all 3 scripts (`select-gitleaks-range.sh`, `select-gitleaks-range.test.sh`, `run-gitleaks.sh`) — all OK
- [x] Ran `scripts/ci/select-gitleaks-range.test.sh` from the repo root — printed `All Gitleaks range-selection tests passed.` and exited 0
- [x] Validated the workflow YAML: `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml')); print('YAML OK')"` → `YAML OK`
- [x] Confirmed the push-branch target: `grep -A2 "^  push:" .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` → `branches: ['main']`
- [x] Verified the 3 committed script blobs are byte-identical to isotope's canonical git blob SHAs (`git ls-tree HEAD scripts/ci/`)

body:
## Usage

```bash
uv run pytest tests/sim/test_conditional_snapshot.py -q
INT14_OUT="$(mktemp -d)"
uv run python experiments/runners/run_belief_conditioned_ablation.py --frozen --out-dir "$INT14_OUT"
```

The first exercises the immutable conditional shard/manifest contract: freeze → verify → load fail-closed, plus atomic writes and identity digests. The second runs the smallest matched ablation (`policy_only`/`policy_value` vs `belief_conditioned_*`) from one frozen conditional fixture through the existing `train_search_supervised` + `_matchup`/`_student_vs_random` arena. Both are honest plumbing/measurement receipts; `CLAIM_BOUNDARY.strength_claim` is `False` because the toy condition is an uninformative uniform determinization with a pre-registered ~0 strength-gap prediction.

## Summary

This lands INT-14 in the intelligence wave: the immutable on-disk shard/manifest contract that sits between a conditional search (INT-13, not yet shipped) and a conditioned student, plus the smallest belief-conditioned policy/value student ablation against the existing Teacher-0 arena path. It pins the frozen, digest-bound shape that INT-13's `ConditionalStrategyResult` must conform to and proves the conditioning path does not break the arena, using a synthetic uniform-determinization toy producer that conforms to the same shape. No learned belief head, no Rust, no arena/rating, no Study/protocol changes — conditioning is a Python obs-field + shard-key extension, and the arena is reused as-is.

## Changes

- New `manabot/sim/conditional_distill.py`: `schema_version: 2` conditional snapshot mirroring Teacher-0's `CLAIM_BOUNDARY`/`SnapshotError`/atomic-write/`snapshot_identity_sha256`/freeze-verify-fail-closed shape, extended with a condition axis in the NPZ and a `condition_schema` block in the manifest; shard ingestion adapter pinning the `ConditionalStrategyResult` row shape.
- New `experiments/runners/run_belief_conditioned_snapshot.py`: freezes the small synthetic uniform-determinization conditional fixture (two shards + `snapshot.json`) used by both the contract tests and the ablation.
- New `experiments/runners/run_belief_conditioned_ablation.py`: matched four-arm ablation runner (`policy_only`/`policy_value`/`belief_conditioned_policy_only`/`belief_conditioned_policy_value`) reusing `train_search_supervised` and the existing arena.
- `manabot/model/agent.py`: conditioning channel threaded through the student so a provided condition label is carried in the observation field and gated on/off per arm.
- `manabot/infra/hypers.py` + `manabot/sim/search_supervised.py`: minimal config and ingest hooks to accept the condition axis without changing the unconditioned path.
- `tests/sim/test_conditional_snapshot.py`: contract proof for freeze/verify/load round-trip, identity digest, atomic write, condition-schema validation, and fail-closed behavior on tamper/drift.
- Frozen fixture: `experiments/runners/_fixtures/belief_conditioned_toy/shard_0000{0,1}.{json,npz}` + `snapshot.json`, generated by the snapshot runner and committed as the immutable ablation input.

author: mohameddy
body:
### Fixes Issue #25: Adversarial-ordering audit of the last-recipient-absorbs-remainder split design

**Overview**
Resolved the order-dependency vulnerability in the `compute_split` logic across the `escrow` and `milestones` contracts by enforcing a strict deterministic tie-breaker.

**Adversarial-Ordering Exploit Analysis**
*   **Single-call maximum extractable value:** In the worst-case scenario, the maximum rounding dust generated in a single transaction is `recipients.len() - 1` minor units. If an attacker consistently places themselves at the targeted index, they absorb this entirety.
*   **Cumulative exposure:** While the single-call value might seem mathematically negligible, a colluding maintainer processing hundreds or thousands of bounty splits over time creates a systematic extraction mechanism at the direct expense of proportional fairness.
*   **Resolution:** By implementing an `Address`-based tie-breaker (`current_addr < best_addr`), we have completely removed vector-position bias. The dust distribution is now strictly deterministic and order-independent, rendering adversarial vector ordering mathematically useless.

**Acceptance Criteria Met:**
*   [x] Refactored `compute_split` in `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs` to use Address-based tie-breaking.
*   [x] Refactored `compute_split` in `contracts/milestones/src/lib.rs` to mirror the same order-independent logic.
*   [x] Verified that `maintenance-pool` does not utilize array-based proportional splits (`withdraw` targets a single recipient), rendering it immune to this specific vector.
*   [x] Added `test_adversarial_ordering_resistance` to explicitly prove that an attacker manipulating their position in the vector yields zero economic advantage.
*   [x] `cargo test --workspace` passes cleanly.

body:
## What

Agent- and script-launched dev servers (`zsh -c ...`) were bypassing the shims entirely: `devhost setup` wrote the PATH export only to `~/.zshrc`, which non-interactive zsh never reads. The parallel-agent workloads devhost is built for were exactly the ones running without isolation.

- **`devhost setup` (zsh) now writes to both `~/.zshenv` and `~/.zshrc`** — for the PATH export *and* the guarded `DOCKER_HOST` line (same gap for container isolation). `.zshenv` covers every zsh invocation; the `.zshrc` copy still re-prepends past version managers and macOS `path_helper` in interactive shells. fish was already safe (`config.fish` loads in both modes); non-interactive bash reads no rc file by design — documented gap, mitigated on Linux by the PATH-independent `ld.so.preload`/eBPF tiers.
- **`devhost doctor` gains a dedicated check**: it spawns a fresh non-interactive `$SHELL`, reads its PATH, and flags a missing shim dir with the fix hint — turning silently un-isolated agent servers into a named finding.
- Agent skill updated to point at the new check.

## Verification

- On a machine reproducing the real incident (shim export only in `.zshrc`): doctor's new check reports ✗; running the patched `devhost setup` adds the line to `.zshenv` (idempotent, `.zshrc` untouched); doctor flips to ✓.
- `profilePaths` unit tests for zsh/bash/fish file sets; multi-file append round-trips for PATH and DOCKER_HOST lines; `go build` / `vet` / full `go test` green.

## Intent

Make RKA's governed knowledge/ directory a conformant OKF v0.1 bundle without weakening RKA's governance model. OKF v0.1 is an interchange layer (only 'type' required; consumers SHOULD-not-MUST preserve unknown keys); RKA is the governance layer; they compose. Added 'type' as a required frontmatter field (validator checks non-empty only, matching OKF; recommended vocabulary rfc/adr/constitution/prd/spec/instruction/context documented in RFC-003, deliberately NOT a closed enum). Reserved index.md/log.md as ungoverned bundle structure; created knowledge/index.md (bundle-root, okf_version, enumerated entries) but deliberately did NOT create log.md (deletion test). Kept 'date' as the SOLE freshness field mapped to OKF 'timestamp'; deliberately NO duplicate timestamp field (the sync obligation RFC-003 s7 used to reject 'owner'). The bundle index is OPTIONAL (adversarial review corrected an earlier hard-require contradicting RFC-003 s4); integrity checked only when index.md present. Moved LICENSE docs/->root and renamed CONTRIBUTOR_GUIDE->CONTRIBUTING for GitHub detection; historical/decision-record mentions left untouched. The OKF zoom-out report in docs/reviews/ had its governed frontmatter stripped to match its ungoverned siblings. Recorded in ADR-0011 + RFC-003 v0.6.0. NOTE: test step skipped - the repo's only test command (bats .devcontainer/tests/) targets a devcontainer path absent on this host (pre-existing infra gap); the frontmatter validator is exercised by lint-frontmatter in the lint step.

body:
## Summary

Fixes Bug #1 from PR #145: token classification for compress-as-anchor (v1.12.9+).

**Problem**: Since v1.12.9 (PR #153 compress-as-anchor), compression summaries live inside `compress` tool calls' `summary` parameter. However, `estimateContextComposition` classified ALL tool part tokens as `toolTokens` — including the summary content. This caused:

- **Inflated `tool%`**: compress summary text (~1-5K tokens each) counted as tool overhead
- **Deflated `summary%`**: summary tokens not tracked
- **Misleading context breakdown**: nudge shows e.g. `12.3K tool (90%) | 0.1K summaries (1%)` when the real distribution has significant summary content
- **Suboptimal compression decisions**: model sees wrong category distribution

**Fix**: In `estimateContextComposition` (`lib/messages/inject/utils.ts`), when `toolName === "compress"`, extract `summary` text from `part.state.input.content[].summary` and classify it as `summaryTokens`. Structural overhead (tool name, topic, startId, endId, state output) remains `toolTokens`.

Before:
```
Breakdown: 12.3K tool (90%) | 0.1K summaries (1%) | 0.5K text (9%)
```

After:
```
Breakdown: 8.1K tool (59%) | 4.3K summaries (31%) | 0.5K text (10%)
```

## Files Changed

- `lib/messages/inject/utils.ts` — `estimateContextComposition` tool part branch (+17/-3)
- `tests/inject-utils-pure.test.ts` — 5 new tests + `mkCompress` helper (+85)
- `devlog/2026-07-18_compress-token-classification/REQ.md` + `WORKLOG.md`

## Verification

- TypeScript: 0 errors
- Tests: 730/730 pass (5 new)

## Test Coverage

| Test | What it asserts |
|------|----------------|
| compress tool summary counted in summaryTokens not toolTokens | summary text classified correctly |
| compress tool structural overhead counted in toolTokens | split is correct (structural → tool, content → summary) |
| compress with multiple content entries sums all summaries | batch compression with N content entries |
| compress tool without state.input falls back to toolTokens | malformed input doesn't crash |
| non-compress tools unaffected by summary classification | regression guard |

author: copilot
body:
Several GitHub Actions workflows were relying on implicit `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions. This change makes workflow permissions explicit so the repository default can be reduced to read-only without breaking automation.

- **Workflow permission hardening**
  - Added top-level `permissions:` to workflows that previously had none.
  - Restricted each workflow to the minimum scope it needs instead of inheriting broad defaults.

- **Write access only where required**
  - Kept comment-writing automation functional with targeted write scopes (for example, `auto-cc.yml`).
  - Preserved cache behavior in `pretest.yml` by granting `actions: write` only to the jobs that use `actions/cache`.

- **Publish workflow completeness**
  - Added the missing explicit permission on the `postcheck` job in `publish.yml` so the workflow is fully annotated.

Example of the pattern applied:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  static-checks:
    permissions:
      actions: write
```

author: villanch
body:
## Summary

- make cachebench join dumps and usage by correlation ID without allowing a missing callback to shift every later sample
- attribute model tier from the model recorded in each dump and expose exact/legacy/missing/cancelled coverage in JSON and Markdown
- add a deterministic cachebench self-test for dropped callbacks, legacy fallback, orphan usage, cancellation, and high-quality aggregation
- fix structured ReAct task lifecycle events containing boolean or numeric metadata being rejected by map[string]string decoding
- make YAKC cache keys include the resolved transitive include graph so changed benchmark libraries cannot silently execute stale bytecode
- move the changing RecentToolsCache block after the final cache boundary so Skills and Schema remain reusable

## Measurement

Ran aim.InvokeReAct with 进行主机体检 for the full 1200-second window on aibalance and evaluated only memfit-standard-free records joined by exact correlation ID.

- post-change: 80 calls, 3,831,814 prompt tokens, 2,197,408 cached tokens, 57.35% exact token hit
- baseline reconstructed with the same exact join and dump-model truth: 64 calls, 3,126,472 prompt tokens, 1,958,272 cached tokens, 62.64%
- semi-dynamic-1 variants fell from 4 to 2; the stable variant covered 76/80 high-quality calls
- cold calls fell proportionally from 25.00% to 23.75%, and their share of misses fell from 56.11% to 47.27%
- 14 of 19 post-change cold calls occurred after the same semi-dynamic-2 hash had already been seen, indicating that upstream cache namespace/routing affinity is now a larger bottleneck than prompt byte drift

The total hit rate did not improve in this longer and different task trajectory, so this PR does not claim the 90% target. It makes the metric trustworthy, removes one early-prefix invalidator, and identifies sticky upstream routing/cache namespace plus timeline-tail growth as the next optimization targets.

A short post-fix smoke run verified that the report now emits alignment, modelAttribution, modelMetadata, and exact coverage; cancelled/nil-usage calls were excluded instead of shifting later records.

## Verification

- go test ./common/aiengine ./common/yak/antlr4yak ./common/ai/aid/aicache
- go test ./common/ai/aid/aireact -count=1
- targeted prompt boundary tests after the final template adjustment
- go run common/yak/cmd/yak.go common/ai/aid/aicache/cachebench/selftest.yak

- full 1200-second aim.InvokeReAct benchmark plus a post-fix short smoke run

author: acmis1
pengw0048
body:
## Why

Across recent PRs (#453, #455, #457, #459) the core logic landed correct, but green-locally runs kept passing while CI blocked on mechanical misses a *targeted* local subset hides: a >32-char Alembic revision id (PostgreSQL-only), model↔migration schema drift, an OpenAPI snapshot not regenerated, a cross-file regression the full suite would catch, ruff/basedpyright, and runtime artifacts swept in by a stray `git add -A`. `make preflight` is the single "what CI gates on" command to run before opening a PR.

## What

`scripts/preflight.sh` runs, fast-fail, cheap→expensive:

1. **artifact hygiene** — fails if a gitignored runtime artifact (`__result_*.lock`, `outputs/`, `*.db`, `*.migrate.lock`, …) is in the git index (the class of mistake CI never catches because it runs on a clean checkout).
2. **ruff** + **basedpyright** — the `python-quality` gates.
3. **openapi --check** — the committed HTTP contract.
4. **core-contract** (graph + sqlpolicy + migrations) — fast fail-first, catches migration/fresh-baseline drift in ~30s.
5. **full kernel pytest** — the net for cross-file regressions (fresh `DP_DATA_DIR`, swept lock artifacts).
6. **web** (typecheck + vitest) — when `web/node_modules` is present.
7. **PostgreSQL contracts** — when `DP_TEST_DATABASE_URL` points at a reachable PostgreSQL; otherwise clearly skipped with a note that CI runs it.

`make preflight` runs the full gate; `make preflight-fast` runs steps 1–4 (~1 min) for iteration. AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md point at it as the before-you-open-a-PR step, and the stale AGENTS.md "no linters are configured" note is corrected (ruff + basedpyright have been the `python-quality` gates for a while).

## Note

The artifact-hygiene check immediately caught a real pre-existing miss: a 0-byte `kernel/dataplay.db.migrate.lock` committed before its `*.migrate.lock` gitignore rule existed. Removed here.

Verified: `make preflight` passes end-to-end locally (full kernel suite + static gates), `make preflight-fast` passes.

author: anarkiwi
body:
## Summary

Adds an **exact** render-cost backend by running the real `plot_world` in py65 and memoizing it — instead of hand-reimplementing the self-modifying rasteriser (which the fill-emulator passes showed is "multi-day" work to reproduce what py65 already does byte-exact). The exact cost is a memoized function call, not a reimplementation.

Exactness by construction: py65 executes the ROM code that generated `golden_render_cost.json`, so `render_cost_exact` reproduces it — **15/15 sweep views, worst abs diff 0.0 frames** (`test_exact_backend_matches_golden`).

## Design (ROM-free invariant preserved)
The `sentinel/` model stays standalone/ROM-free: CI and `python -m sentinel.player` run **without** the ROM. So:
- The pure-Python proxy `render_cost` stays the **default**, byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The exact backend is **optional and ROM-gated**: `RENDER_COST_BACKEND=py65` uses it only when the ROM is present; ROM/py65 absent → warns once, falls back to the proxy (never crashes). Importing the model never imports py65.
- `sentinel/rendercost_py65.py`: `render_cost_exact(state,h,v)` builds a py65 machine from the live `State.mem` image (`oracle.machine_from_image`), runs `plot_world $2625` with the `$245B` occlusion table active, returns `processorCycles`/19656. Memoized (blake2b over terrain grid + object arrays + observer + view; LRU-bounded).
- Selection hook in `projector.render_cost`; both settle call sites (`player._settle`, `actioncost.action_rounds`) inherit it.

RE note: the golden setup inherits the play-view raster clip `$0051/$0052 = $F0/$30`; setting it explicitly took the backend from 3/15 → 15/15 exact.

## Measured
- **Exact == golden:** 15/15, 0.0-frame diff.
- **Performance (in-loop is viable):** exact ls0 player run 92.7s, only **10 `plot_world` evals** for the whole run (memo collapses repeats; `render_cost` is only hit on the transfer-settle path). ~2.2s/uncached call.
- **ls0 under exact cost: WON, 0 breaches** (46 actions) — same outcome as proxy (WON, 49). No regression.
- **ROM-free intact:** `import sentinel.player` works with ROM absent; non-oracle suite green; default proxy output unchanged.

## Validation
`test_rendercost_py65.py` 6 passed (incl. oracle exact==golden, memoization, ROM-free fallback). black + pylint clean. ROM image not committed.

author: ys-ll
body:
Closes #310.

The broadcast button used to be all-or-nothing per workspace, so users
could not exclude a specific terminal from the broadcast group. This
adds a Ctrl/Cmd+Click modifier that toggles a single panel's
participation, while a plain click keeps the existing "toggle the whole
workspace" behaviour.

## Behaviour
- **Plain click** on the broadcast icon: if any panel in the workspace is
  broadcasting, turn all off; otherwise turn every ssh/local panel on.
  (Same as before.)
- **Ctrl/⌘ + Click**: toggle only the current panel — lets the user
  hand-pick a subset that broadcasts between themselves.
- The icon now lights up per-panel, so the broadcast group is visible at
  a glance.
- Tooltip is a two-liner: the original label plus a `Ctrl+Click` hint.
  All 9 locales updated.

## Implementation
- Replace `tabStore.broadcastWorkspaceId: string | null` with
  `broadcastPanelIds: Set<string>`.
- New store API: `isPanelBroadcasting`, `toggleBroadcastPanel`,
  `getBroadcastPanelIdsInWorkspace`. `isBroadcasting(workspaceId)` is
  now derived from the set.
- All dispatch call sites (typing, suggestions, right-click paste,
  history run, quick commands) filter by the broadcast set instead of
  the whole workspace.
- Clean up `broadcastPanelIds` on `closeTab` / `removePanelFromWorkspaceTab`.

## Verified
- `npm run build` clean.
- `wails dev` manual test: plain click / Ctrl+click toggle correctly,
  tooltip shows both lines, typing / paste / history / quick command
  all respect the selected subset.

---

关联 #310。

原来广播按钮是「一个工作区整体开/关」，无法排除个别终端。本 PR 增加 Ctrl/⌘+点击 修饰键：普通点击维持原「工作区全开/全关」行为，Ctrl+点击 则只切换当前面板的广播开关，用户可以自由挑选参与广播的终端子集。

## 交互
- **普通左键点击** 广播按钮：工作区里有任一面板广播中 → 全灭；否则把所有 ssh/local 面板全部加入广播组。（同原来）
- **Ctrl/⌘ + 左键点击**：只切换当前面板 —— 用户可以手动挑选一个子集互相广播。
- 按钮高亮改成「本面板是否在广播中」，广播组一眼看清。
- Tooltip 双行显示：原文案 + `Ctrl+点击：单独切换此终端`，9 种语言都补上。

## 实现
- `tabStore.broadcastWorkspaceId: string | null` → `broadcastPanelIds: Set<string>`。
- 新增 API：`isPanelBroadcasting`、`toggleBroadcastPanel`、`getBroadcastPanelIdsInWorkspace`；`isBroadcasting(workspaceId)` 改为从集合派生。
- 所有分发点（输入、建议、右键粘贴、历史命令、快捷命令）改为按广播集合过滤，而不是遍历整个工作区。

author: quantumexplorer
body:
## Issue being fixed or feature implemented

DPNS usernames could not change hands: even though the DPNS `domain` document type has declared `transferable: 1` and `tradeMode: 1` (direct purchase) since genesis, data triggers unconditionally rejected `Transfer`, `Purchase` and `UpdatePrice` on domain documents. On top of that, a username resolves through `records.identity` — not through the document's `$ownerId` — and domain documents are immutable, so even if a transfer had been allowed, the name would have kept resolving to the previous owner with no way for the new owner to repoint it.

This PR enables username transfers and sales as of protocol version 13.

## What was done?

- **Data trigger bindings list v1** (`rs-drive-abci`): drops the reject bindings for `Transfer`, `Purchase` and `UpdatePrice` on DPNS `domain` documents, letting the generic document validation paths (which already honor `transferable`/`tradeMode`) accept these transitions. `Replace` and `Delete` stay rejected — name records remain immutable and permanent.
- **`records.identity` rewrite** (`rs-drive`): v1 of the document transfer and purchase high-level operation conversions rewrites a transferred or purchased domain document's `records.identity` to the new owner as part of the same batch operation, so the username resolves to the buyer atomically. All other document types are unaffected.
- **Platform version wiring** (`rs-platform-version`): new `DRIVE_ABCI_VALIDATION_VERSIONS_V9` (bindings: 1), `DRIVE_STATE_TRANSITION_METHOD_VERSIONS_V3` (transfer/purchase conversion: 1) and `DRIVE_VERSION_V8`, consumed by `PLATFORM_V13`. Protocol versions ≤ 12 keep the old structs for chain replay.
- **DPNS contract**: added the `identity` property-name constant used by the rewrite.

## How Has This Been Tested?

New drive-abci execution tests in `batch/tests/document/dpns.rs` (`dpns_username_transfer_tests`):

- `test_dpns_username_transfer` — registers a name, transfers the domain document to a second identity under PV13, and asserts the processed document's owner **and** `records.identity` both point to the recipient.
- `test_dpns_username_sale` — sets a price with `UpdatePrice`, purchases with a second identity, and asserts ownership, `records.identity` rewrite, and the seller's balance credit.
- `test_dpns_username_transfer_protocol_version_12_rejected` / `test_dpns_username_sale_protocol_version_12_rejected` — the same flows under PV12 still hit the reject data trigger, proving activation is gated on PV13.

All 9 DPNS-related drive-abci tests pass; `cargo clippy` on the touched crates and `cargo fmt --all` are clean.

## Breaking Changes

Consensus-breaking at protocol version 13 activation: nodes without this change would reject DPNS domain transfer/purchase/update-price transitions (and would not perform the `records.identity` rewrite) that nodes with this change accept once PV13 activates. No behavior change for protocol versions ≤ 12.

- [x] I have added "!" to the title and described breaking changes in the corresponding section if my code contains any

## Ce face NX-176a
Clarify conversațional pentru cereri sub-specificate (general, orice vertical) — schimbarea de fond
trăiește în promptul nano de triaj (vezi `tasks/NX-176a.md`).

## Fix-uri din review-ul Codex (adresate în commit-ul acestui branch)
- **P0 — excepția de siguranță trăia DOAR în prompt.** Guard-ul NX-116 (`confidence low → clarify`)
  putea downgrada la clarify orice `sales`, inclusiv o cerere cu **sarcină/alăptare**, ratând
  gate-ul determinist de contraindicații (NX-173). Fix: `_safety_sensitive` reutilizează
  `detect_contexts_in_turn` (registrul NX-173, **fail-safe** pe `RegistryError`) → pe context de
  sănătate NU downgradăm; rămâne `sales` ca gate-ul să filtreze + avertizeze. Determinist, nu prompt.
- **Teste** — sarcină low-confidence rămâne `sales` (assert pe rută + event `triage_safety_kept_sales`
  + absența `triage_low_confidence`) și contrast non-safety care downgradă corect la clarify. Plus
  cazul „laptop" rulează pe DomainPack `electronics`, nu `beauty` (onestitatea contract-testului).

Rebased onto current `main` **`f10498cd`** (was `197d946`). ---

## Summary

Replaces the profile's IntersectionObserver **scroll-spy** (all 8 sections stacked) with **true section navigation** driven by `?section=`, plus a client-side unsaved-edit navigation guard. **Frontend only** — no backend API, profile schema, database, migration, Gmail card, warning logic, or billing change.

Canonical slugs: `about, career, skills, documents, goals, integrations, security, billing` (section 05 slug `preferences` → `goals`; label "Career goals" unchanged).

## Routing
- **Renders only the selected section.**
- Deep links, back/forward (rail items are real `<Link>` → push), and refresh all resolve from the URL.
- Missing → `about` (URL left clean). Invalid → `about`, canonicalized with **`replace`** (never `push`). Explicit valid section always wins.
- **Preserves every unrelated query param** when switching. A **Gmail callback** (`?gmail=`) opens **Integrations** (unless an explicit valid section is present) and keeps `gmail` for the #1159 card, whose cleaner uses `window.location.pathname` (route-agnostic — stays on `/profile`).

## Unsaved-edit contract
Editable state lives in the parent `draft` (controlled inputs) — **unsaved values survive section switches**, no refetch. Guarded on leaving:
- **Refresh / close / hard nav:** `beforeunload`.
- **Client-side `<Link>` nav away from `/profile`** (e.g. sidebar route): a **profile-scoped, capture-phase click interceptor** (active only while dirty) prompts; cancel blocks, confirm allows. Same-route section changes are never prompted.

## Known residual gap — browser Back route-exit (documented, deliberately out of scope)

This PR does **not** claim complete route-exit protection.

- Browser **Back that exits `/profile`** may discard unsaved profile edits **without an in-app confirmation**.
- **Protected** in this PR: refresh / tab-close (`beforeunload`), and internal sidebar/`<Link>` navigation away from `/profile` (capture-phase interceptor).
- **Preserved** in this PR: section Back/forward **inside** `/profile` keeps the draft (draft lives in component state; section changes never refetch or discard).
- Safe cross-route **browser-history** interception requires shared **WorkspaceShell/navigation** ownership; it is **not implemented here** to avoid a history trap that would break required in-profile section back/forward.
- Tracked as a **separate P1 follow-up**: *Profile cross-route dirty-state protection* (user data-loss prevention), owned at the WorkspaceShell/navigation layer.

## Accessibility
Semantic `<nav>`, `aria-current="page"`, focus moves to the section heading after an *intentional* change (never on initial load), desktop sticky rail + accessible mobile `<select>`, RTL mirrored. Obsolete `IntersectionObserver`/`scrollIntoView` removed (no dual nav). `/profile` shell wraps `ProfileEditorial` in `<Suspense>` (Next 14 `useSearchParams`).

## Tests / build (re-verified on rebased head `b688cdc8`)
- `profile-editorial.test.tsx` (stateful `next/navigation` mock): only-one-section, every-valid-section, deep link, missing/invalid fallback + canonicalization, param preservation, Gmail callback, explicit-section-wins, scroll-doesn't-navigate, unsaved-survives-switch, `beforeunload` guard, and the **internal-nav guard** (cancel blocks / confirm allows / section-change no-prompt / clean no-intercept) — **32/32 pass** on `b688cdc8`.
- `next build` clean (`/profile` 11 kB). Full frontend vitest (**686 pass**, 66 files) and lint green; CI green on `b688cdc8`.

4 files, +467/−80, all `apps/web` (`ProfileEditorial.tsx`, `app/profile/page.tsx`, `lib/translations.ts` (+2 keys), `profile-editorial.test.tsx`). No backend/schema/API/migration/Gmail/warning/billing change.

author: markm00n
body:
## Summary

Real failure observed just now, not a hypothetical: PR #11 and #12 merged about 15 seconds apart. The `deploy-storybook` run triggered by #12's merge got as far as committing the regenerated `dashboard-data.generated.json`, then had its `git push origin HEAD:main` rejected because #11 had merged in the meantime and moved `main` out from under it:

```
! [rejected]        HEAD -> main (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs
```

The job failed (red X), even though nothing was actually broken — the *next* run (triggered by #11's own merge) picked up both sets of changes and pushed successfully on its own. So `main` ended up correct either way, but the first run still shows a failure for no real reason, and there's no guarantee the self-heal always happens depending on merge timing.

## Fix

Retry the push up to 5 times, rebasing onto the latest `origin/main` between attempts. This is safe to do blindly here — unlike a general-purpose auto-commit, this step's commit only ever touches one generated file (`dashboard-data.generated.json`), so there's nothing else in the diff that could produce a real merge conflict; a rebase is always clean in practice.

## Test plan
- Can't fully simulate the race locally (it requires two concurrent GitHub Actions runs racing a real push), so this is reviewed logic rather than a reproduced-and-fixed test.
- The retry loop only activates on push rejection — normal single-merge runs (the common case, already verified working across PRs #9–#12) are unaffected.

author: zgover
body:
The Billing page's monthly/annual toggle appeared dead — and mostly was:

1. **Plan cards ignored it**: `BillingPlanCardsComponent` had no `interval` prop, so cards always showed the monthly price. Toggling produced zero visible change.
2. **Plan switches ignored it**: the subscription route only knew monthly `PRICE_ENV` (and was missing the `advanced` entry entirely), so orgs with a live subscription always landed on monthly prices — an annual org switching plans silently dropped to monthly billing.
3. **It never reflected reality**: the org doc didn't store the subscription's interval, so the toggle always started on "month" even for annual customers.

Fixes: cards render the annual headline price ("$16/mo billed yearly") when toggled; `preview`/`switch` accept `interval` (defaulting to the subscription's current interval) and re-price per-plan add-on items at the same interval (AGL-528 follow-through — Stripe allows one interval per subscription); the webhook + switch mirror `subscription.interval` and the page initializes the toggle from it.

**Verification**: typecheck 135/135, 21 affected projects' tests green, and the local emulator e2e suite (14/14) — the billing spec now actively flips the toggle via a new `interact` hook and asserts Starter goes $25 → $16/mo billed yearly, which fails without this fix.

Also done this session (no repo change): ran `setup-stripe.mjs` in test mode — 44 price envs now populated in the console dev env, including all new add-on monthly+yearly pairs.

author: gesslar
body:
## Problem

`the_file_name()` (`src/compiler/internal/compiler.cc`) builds the leading-slash, extension-less object name that is passed as the `file` argument to the `valid_override` master apply. It stripped a **fixed two trailing bytes**:

```c
tmp[0] = '/';
strncpy(tmp + 1, name, len - 2);
tmp[len - 1] = '\0';
```

That was only correct while `.c` was the sole source extension. With `.lpc` (or any extension that isn't two characters), it chops the wrong number of bytes and leaves a mangled tail. For example, compiling `/adm/simul_efun/object.lpc`, `valid_override` receives:

```
file "/adm/simul_efun/object.l"   (expected "/adm/simul_efun/object")
```

The `valid_override` docs specify `file` as the extension-less object name (the example compares `file == "/adm/obj/simul_efun"`), so any master that matches on `file` silently fails to match under `.lpc`.

## Fix

Strip the *actual* extension by scanning back to the last dot in the basename, so both `.c` and `.lpc` (and anything else) resolve to the documented extension-less form:

- `/adm/simul_efun/object.lpc` → `/adm/simul_efun/object`
- `/adm/foo.c` → `/adm/foo` (unchanged)

A dot is only treated as an extension when it appears in the basename (after the last `/`), so dotted directory names don't get truncated. Allocation is sized to `base + 1` (`/` + kept bytes), matching `int_new_string`'s `size + 1` contract.

`the_file_name()`'s only callers are the two `valid_override` argument pushes in `grammar_rules_exprs.cc`, so the blast radius is contained to that apply.

author: ssaattww
body:
## 概要

Issue #21 に対応し、実行中の Step 名とネストした実行階層を Text / JSON ログから確認できるようにします。

`ILogger.BeginScope` の scope chain を実行位置の正本とし、root Entry、通常 Step、nested `CompositeStep`、`If` / `Switch` の選択 branch、retry の attempt を一貫して扱います。

Closes #21

## 変更内容

### Engine

- root workflow の Entry scope と Step scope を整理
- Step 本体ログへ現在の `StepName` と `Attempt` を伝播
- nested `CompositeStep` に `CompositeName` scope と lifecycle ログを追加
- simple execution に Step の開始、成功、skip、失敗ログを追加
- `If` に `then` / `else`、`Switch` に `case=<value>` / `default` の branch scope を追加
- retry、timeout、cancellation、producer、trace の既存結果契約を維持
- Switch case 値の文字列化に失敗しても、ログでは `case=<unavailable>` を使用してworkflowを継続
- branch定義時の重複case検査と空branch検査ではcase値を文字列化しない

### CLI logger provider

- `AsyncLocal` の scope chain からログ出力時点の snapshot を構築
- Text ログへ execution path と attempt を追加
- JSON ログへ次のフィールドを追加
  - `EntryName`
  - `StepName`
  - `BranchName`
  - `Attempt`
  - `ExecutionPath`
- ログファイル名の `{RootStepName}` は最外側の Entry 名を使う既存契約を維持

### 文書・サンプル

- `doc/issue-21-hierarchical-logging-design.md` を追加
- 複数フォルダサンプル README に階層ログ例を追加
- `tasks-status.md` と `phases-status.md` を T73-T77 / P31 へ同期
- 実装報告と最終レビュー報告を `reports/` に追加

## ログ例

```text
[12:00:00] [Information] Devo6.WorkFlow.Step [Main > RunTextPipelineStep > TextPipeline > LoadTextStep] Loading source text
[12:00:01] [Warning] Devo6.WorkFlow.Engine [Main > FetchStep] [attempt=2] Step started for attempt 2
```

```json
{
  "EntryName": "Main",
  "StepName": "LoadTextStep",
  "BranchName": null,
  "Attempt": 1,
  "ExecutionPath": [
    "Main",
    "RunTextPipelineStep",
    "TextPipeline",
    "LoadTextStep"
  ]
}
```

## TDD・検証証跡

### Red

GitHub Actions run `29635422686`、artifact `8426932606` で先行テストを実行しました。

- 43件中40件成功
- 既存skip 1件
- 未実装だったnested `CompositeStep`の階層と選択branch名について、意図した2件の失敗を確認

### Green

GitHub Actions run `29635559813`、artifact `8426981336` で実装後の結果を確認しました。

- 階層ログfocused test: 10/10成功
- 関連回帰: 32件成功、既存skip 1件、失敗0件
- format成功
- `git diff --check`成功

コード規約修正後のrun `29636057186`、artifact `8427137522`では、階層ログ、関連回帰、`CodingStandardsContractTests`を合わせて45件成功、既存skip 1件、失敗0件でした。

### Final

最新head `75c67a77b3ede7b201aba37fd40766f35a6bcdb7` に対するGitHub Actions run `29637264438`が成功しました。artifactは`8427507904`（`test-results-29637264438`）です。

- Restore: 成功
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`: 成功
- solution test: 303件中300件成功、既存skip 3件、失敗0件
- `git diff --check`: 成功
- `SwitchBranchLoggingSafetyTests`: 定義時から `ToString()` が例外を送出するcase値で登録・実行・`case=<unavailable>`表示をend-to-end検証
- artifact: `restore.log`、`format.log`、`test-results.log`、`test-results.trx`、`diff-check.log`
- artifact保持期間: 14日

PR xUnit workflowは`contents: read`の検証専用です。ソースを変更・commit・pushせず、ログとTRXをartifactへ保存します。artifact確認後の修正はGitHubコネクタ経由で明示的にcommitします。

## 互換性

次の公開契約は変更しません。

- `IStep<TOut>` / `IAsyncStep<TOut>`
- `StepInput` / `StepContext`
- `CompositeStep` の公開API
- `WorkflowResult`
- `ExecutionTrace` / `ExecutionTraceStep`

Textログの1行形式にはexecution pathが追加されます。機械処理ではJSON形式またはstructured logging providerの利用を推奨します。

body:
## What

Follow-up ① of #1032. [PR #1050](https://github.com/yukimemi/kanade/pull/1050) made dynamic groups resolvable **backend-side** (a schedule's `target.groups` expands them at dispatch), but the **agent-side** consumers never saw them:

- `kanade exec --groups <dynamic>` — the agent isn't subscribed to `commands.group.<name>` (it doesn't know it's a member).
- Group-scoped notifications (`notifications.group.<name>`).
- `client.visible_to: {groups:[<dynamic>]}` on the client app.
- `runs_on: agent` schedules targeting a dynamic group.

All of these decide membership from the `agent_groups.<pc_id>` KV each agent watches, and a dynamic group is never written there. This PR closes that gap by **materializing** derived membership to the agent side.

## How

**New bucket `agent_groups_derived`** (history:1, bootstrapped + in `ALL_KV_BUCKETS`) — per-PC *derived* membership, machine-owned. Kept **separate** from the operator-owned `agent_groups`: the materializer is the sole writer here, the operator the sole writer there, so the two never clobber each other (no provenance metadata, no CAS contention on one hot key). Readers **union** the two.

**`projector/group_materializer.rs`** — on a 60s tick (and immediately on any `GroupDef` change, via a `group_defs` watch) it resolves every `GroupDef` (static `members:` or dynamic `query:`, via the cache-backed `resolve_group_members` from #1050), inverts to a per-PC map, and **reconciles** the derived bucket:
- changed-gated upsert of each desired PC, plus
- **delete** of PCs that left every declared group — so a PC reimaged out of a dynamic group stops subscribing to its old `commands.group.<name>` (reconcile, not append).

Cache-backed + changed-gated ⇒ an unchanged tick does **no SQL and no KV writes**, waking no agent.

**Agent `groups.rs`** — `manage()` now watches **both** `agent_groups` and `agent_groups_derived` (`tokio::select` over two key-watches), unions them, and drives the existing subscribe/diff/`groups_tx` path off the union. This one producer fix covers **every** `groups_tx` consumer (notify_bus, command_replay, local_scheduler / `Target::matches`).

**Three cold KV-read paths** that bypass `groups_tx` each union the derived bucket themselves:
| Path | File | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `pc_groups` | agent `klp/handlers/jobs.rs` | `client.visible_to` |
| `read_my_groups` | agent `klp/handlers/notifications.rs` | notification history replay |
| `membership_map` + `list_all_groups` | backend `api/agent_groups.rs` | notification audience + SPA Groups page |

## Why a separate bucket (not metadata in `agent_groups`)

The reconcile must **delete** membership a PC no longer has. If derived membership lived in `agent_groups.<pc_id>` alongside manual entries, removing a derived group would have to rewrite that key while preserving the operator's manual entries — but a flat `Vec<String>` can't tell them apart, forcing either a clobber or a full wire-type + all-readers/writers rework. Separate buckets make each side a single writer that reconciles freely; a materializer bug can't touch operator-set membership.

## Agent load

One extra **single-key** watch (`agent_groups_derived.<pc_id>`, not a `watch_all`) that only delivers when *that* PC's derived set actually changes (changed-gated writes). Steady state = zero extra traffic; `history:1` = no reconnect replay churn. The 60s reconcile runs on the **backend** and doesn't scale with fleet size.

## Scope

One PR — the feature only works end-to-end with all of it. No SPA changes (Groups-page display correctness rides the `membership_map` / `list_all_groups` union). Event-driven fine-grained invalidation (recompute the instant inventory changes) is a future optimization, out of scope. Remaining #1032 item ② (stale `check_status` rows for out-of-scope PCs) is still separate.

## Test

- `cargo make check` green (fmt + clippy + tests + lock).
- New unit tests: materializer `build_desired` (invert, multi-group-per-PC union, empty); agent `union_groups` (dedup/sort, empty sides).
- Existing `diff_groups` tests unchanged (the union feeds the same diff).

Next: real-machine verify on minipc (backend first, then agent) — create `clients`, confirm the materializer writes `agent_groups_derived`, `exec --groups clients` runs on clients only, a group notification reaches a dynamic member, `visible_to` shows the job, and a manual `kanade group add` coexists untouched.

## Summary

Reforge **THE MOON** into a discovery sweep (like SPACEZ), and give the autopilot the smarts to actually play — and be watched playing — it. Along the way the map visualizer learned to draw spawners, and the bot got a fog-of-war explorer and a debug read-out.

## Linked issue

<!-- none -->

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` — 1754 tests pass (moon content test + two loot tests re-pinned to the new moon RNG; level snapshot updated)
- [x] `make lint` + `make fmt-check` clean; engine + website typecheck
- [x] `node scripts/leveling-curve.mjs --targets` — every rung OK, moon stays on the XP ladder
- [x] `node scripts/simulate-run.mjs --difficulty easy --level moon --start-level 8 --gear-tier magic` — victory, boss down, 1 death (was timeout / 11 deaths before the rock-avoidance fix)
- [x] `map-preview moon --heatmap` — coverage rose ~18% → ~28% (on par with SPACEZ); both detours on the sweep
- [x] Playtest screenshot — the bot's decision ("EXPLORE FOG") renders over the hero's head under `?debug`

## What changed

**Level — the moon reforged.** Four basins behind three ridges whose gaps alternate low/high/low, so the climb from the lander to the flag is a full down-up-down-up serpentine. Both off-path detour caches (the CRASHED LANDER, THE THIRTEENTH GRAVE) now sit on the sweep's low turns. XP stays on target.

**Bot — a smarter, watchable autopilot.**
- Fight-steering (give-ground / drift / hold-off) now routes through the obstacle-aware nav, so the hero rounds scattered moonrocks instead of grinding into them.
- The survivor UNCOVERS THE MAP's fog — dipping into nearby line-of-sight pockets, then clearing remaining fog — before committing to the boss (gated so a boss-ready hero still rushes).
- Each decision is tagged (`MARCH PATH`, `EXPLORE FOG`, `GIVE GROUND`, …) for the debug overlay.

**BOT VIEW — a new DEVELOPER-menu mode.** Pick a difficulty + mission and watch the autopilot play it with a realistic leveled, rolled-gear arrival hero, its live decision printed over its head. Arrival levels are floored so no map past SPACEZ ever starts at level 1 and nightmare/jesus never start at 1. Reuses the warp pickers and the existing `?bot=` plumbing.

**Visualizer.** The map-preview design view now renders spawner knots + an authored mob-density heatmap read straight off the YAML (already merged as a prior commit on this branch).

author: rbaumier
body:
Closes #7753

## Root cause
`mutex-over-atomic` text-matched the bare token `Mutex` and never resolved *which* `Mutex` it was. `tokio::sync::Mutex`, `futures::lock::Mutex`, `async_std::sync::Mutex`, and `async_lock::Mutex` all render as the bare token `Mutex`, indistinguishable from `std::sync::Mutex` under a text match — so an async mutex (which holds a lock across `.await` and has **no** `AtomicX` drop-in equivalent) was falsely flagged with "prefer AtomicBool".

## Fix (import-graph provenance)
Disambiguate the `Mutex` identifier by its resolved **module path**, an accepted structural signal:
- New shared lever in `rust_helpers.rs`: `is_async_mutex_type(name_node, source)` + a single auditable `ASYNC_MUTEX_MODULES` const (`tokio::sync`, `futures::lock`, `async_std::sync`, `async_lock`).
- Qualified type paths (`tokio::sync::Mutex<bool>`) resolve off the path segments; unqualified `Mutex<…>` resolves through the file's `use` graph — grouped (`use tokio::sync::{Mutex, …}`), aliased (`as`), and glob (`use tokio::sync::*`) forms handled.
- The rule skips only the resolved async modules; `std::sync::Mutex` / `parking_lot::Mutex` (via `use` or qualified) and an unqualified `Mutex` that resolves to no known async path keep flagging. The rule now also handles qualified paths and extracts the single primitive type argument.

## Glob-import decision
A glob from a known async-mutex module (`use tokio::sync::*`) is treated as async-provenance for a bare `Mutex`, since it genuinely brings `tokio::sync::Mutex` into scope. An explicit `use std::sync::Mutex` binding always wins over a co-present async glob (regression-tested).

## Conscious tradeoff
Qualified `X::Mutex<prim>` for a module not in the async set now flags (it previously fell through unflagged) — symmetric with the bare-unresolved→flag policy and required so `std::sync::Mutex<bool>` flags. A project-local async re-export (`crate::sync::Mutex<bool>`) would flag, same as its bare-`use` form already does.

## Reviews
- Anti-exemption auditor: **ROOT_CAUSE_OK** — gate resolves module-path provenance, not any user-chosen name; std/parking_lot/bare-unresolved all still flag.
- Quality review: no blockers/majors. Minors dispositioned: added explicit-wins-over-glob and aliased-to-Mutex regression tests; kept positional `use_as_clause` parsing to mirror the existing `collect_rust_use_leaves` idiom; documented the qualified-path tradeoff above.

## Tests
33 rule tests pass (15 new: tokio/futures/async_std/async_lock via use/grouped/aliased/qualified/glob skip; std/parking_lot/qualified-std/bare-no-import still flag). All existing carve-outs (Condvar sibling, `#[allow(clippy::mutex_atomic)]`, test dirs) preserved.

Note: clippy was not run (compiler-budget constraint for this change).

author: rlsn
body:
## Problem

The "Available Tools" section of the root-agent system prompt listed every registered tool regardless of whether the principal had the corresponding `tool:<name>` grant. Two symptoms followed:

1. **Revoked tools still visible.** After `peko capability revoke`, the prompt kept listing `Read`, `Write`, `Agent`, etc., so the LLM claimed to have tools it could not invoke.
2. **Raw `<tool_call>` text instead of native tool calling.** After revocation, the runtime tool catalog was correctly empty (the execution-time gate worked), but the prompt still listed the tools, so the LLM hallucinated a textual `<tool_call>` block from training data instead of using native tool calling.

## Root cause

`AutoPromptHandler::handle` (the per-tool handler auto-installed by `ExtensionCore::register_tool` for `PromptSystemSection { section: "tools" }`) ignored the hook context's capability state and unconditionally emitted `### {tool}\n\n{description}`. The skill and agent prompt sections already filtered correctly via `invoke_hook_text_with_principal`; the tool section was the only one that did not.

A second contributing issue: `build_fresh_with_session_context` (the per-iteration prompt rebuild path used by `agentic_loop` so the prompt picks up `SYSTEM.md` and tool changes mid-session) did not forward `principal_capabilities` to the builder. Even if the section had filtered, the rebuilt prompt would have re-emitted the original tool list.

## Fix

Three small, focused changes:

1. **`AutoPromptHandler::handle`** — read `ToolRuntimeContext` from `ctx.state["tool_context"]` (seeded by the builder) and return `HookResult::PassThrough` when `tool:<name>` is not granted. Match is case-insensitive (capability comparison lowercases on construction; `self.tool_name` is already canonical lowercase from `ToolMetadata::new`).

2. **`build_tools_section`** — switch from `core.invoke_hook_text(...)` to `core.invoke_hook_text_with_principal(...)`, forwarding `principal_id`, `capabilities`, `active_extensions`, and `workspace`. Matches what the skills and agents sections already do.

3. **`build_fresh_with_session_context`** — forward `principal_capabilities` and `principal_active_extensions` to the builder. Mirrors what `build_with_session_context` already does.

## Tests

Three new regression tests in `src/extensions/framework/core/tool_registration.rs`:

- `auto_prompt_suppressed_when_capability_not_granted` — `tool:Write` granted, `Read` → `PassThrough`
- `auto_prompt_emitted_when_capability_granted` — `tool:Read` granted → `Continue(Text("### read\n\n..."))`
- `auto_prompt_wildcard_capability_covers_tool` — `tool:*` covers `Bash`

Full test suite: 1894 passed, 0 failed. Clippy clean on touched files (the 27 pre-existing clippy errors are in untouched code from prior work).

## Scope

3 files changed, 153 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-). No new modules, no API changes, no behavior change for callers that already gate on `principal_capabilities` at the LLM-call site (`build_tool_definitions` was already correct).

- `expo prebuild --platform android --no-install` → exit 0 (all config plugins resolve)

Merge once the native map + SPV are device-verified (or land the maplibre v11 migration first).

author: scottjarvie
body:
## Outcome

Unifies the legacy public `/extension` surface with the shared marketing shell and introduces the smallest reusable Research Spine foundation:

**Capture → Vault → Research → Story**

The slice calmly distinguishes private-by-default handling, source provenance, human review, and publish readiness without changing any private workflow or policy.

## Scope

- Rewrite `app/extension/page.tsx` onto `MarketingNav` + `Footer`
- Add reusable server-rendered `ResearchSpine` primitive
- Add a durable Design/IA Foundation vNext specification
- Add a direct behavior-lock script
- Give the mobile brand/home link an accessible name after the 390px snapshot exposed the gap

Exactly five files changed. This does not edit files owned by open PRs #12-#18, including `package.json`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `docs/README.md`, private app/API routes, Convex, auth, or story publishing code.

Linear: [GEN-111](https://linear.app/jarvie/issue/GEN-111/unify-the-public-capture-entry-with-the-research-spine-foundation)

## Foundation decisions

Accepted:
- One Research Spine: Capture → Vault → Research → Story
- Public capture promise bridges into a private workspace
- Privacy, provenance, review state, and publish readiness remain distinct meanings
- The extension remains user-mediated and does not publish

Deferred:
- Private workspace shell/nav changes
- Shared status-chip semantics
- Global CTA vocabulary
- `/features` vocabulary alignment
- Mobile-menu Escape/`aria-controls`
- Broad token/theme cleanup

Rejected:
- Inventing public routes for private workflow stages
- Immediate dark private-app restyling
- Collapsing all trust states into one generic badge
- Changes to auth, FamilySearch access, security policy, or production data

## Proof

Behavior locks were written before the structural change and observed failing for the missing primitive; the later accessibility assertion also failed before the nav-label correction.

- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/check-public-research-spine.ts` — pass
- `pnpm check:extension` — pass
- `pnpm check:protected-routes` — pass
- `pnpm typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm lint` — pass, 0 errors; one pre-existing Convex export warning
- `pnpm build` — pass
- `pnpm verify` — **38 passed, 0 failed**
- `git diff --check` — pass
- Local route smoke for `/`, `/features`, `/extension`, `/privacy`, `/roadmap`, `/updates` — all 200

Browser/accessibility proof at 390, 768, 1024, and 1440:
- no horizontal overflow
- one main landmark and one H1
- four ordered Research Spine stages
- exactly one current stage: Capture
- shared footer present
- zero console errors or warnings
- 390px menu open/close and accessible brand link verified

## Independent review

A fresh Fable 5 High read-only review returned **accept with fixes**. Corrected:
1. recorded the existing `/features` vocabulary fork as deferred;
2. replaced brittle source-format checks with rendered, order-independent assertions;
3. removed drift-prone version/timing/limit numbers from public marketing copy.

The optional mobile-menu keyboard contract remains explicitly deferred because it would widen this conflict-free slice.

## Release boundary

Draft only. No deployment or release was attempted: the seven-PR trust-boundary/bug stack (#12-#18) is still open, so release ordering is not unambiguous. Revalidate the authenticated shell with synthetic/empty state only after that stack drains.

Closes #1126

## BO: DASH-022 — Render accessible current-run summary

Adds a live, responsive, accessible Aiur current-run summary to the Units page. Every fact comes from the daemon-owned DASH-014 `Aiur.CurrentRunSummary` snapshot — the UI performs no aggregate math.

### What's here

- **`RunSummaryPresenter`** (pure): formats truthful counts (live / remaining / succeeded / non-work terminal / unknown-state / total), weighted progress (exact percentage only when DASH-014 provides one, otherwise a named lower bound with coverage), defaulted/excluded weight, wall-clock elapsed, and formula-qualified ETA or an explicit unavailable reason. Keeps unknown, partial, stale, unavailable, zero, and exact values distinct. Holds the last-known-good `reconcile/2` logic and a single bounded screen-reader `announcement/1`.
- **`RunSummary` component**: renders the summary region with native/ARIA progress semantics **only when an exact value is known** (`role="progressbar"` + `aria-valuenow`); unknown progress omits `aria-valuenow` and names coverage/unavailability instead. All counts, coverage, health, freshness, and reasons are named and non-color-dependent.
- **`DashboardLive` wiring**: reads the snapshot on mount/reconnect, subscribes to `current-run-summary:changed`, and coalesces high-frequency renders/announcements through a bounded debounce.
- **Last-known-good**: a same-run summary is retained (labelled stale, with the failed-refresh health/freshness) across an unavailable update; a new run generation or an unconfirmable run window never displays the prior run as current, and it never falls back to zeros or summed agent time.
- **CSS**: namespaced, additive `.run-summary-*` styles reusing the existing theme custom properties (light/dark) and reflow, so the shared summary container/CSS can serialize with DASH-015 without semantic reorder.

Nonfinancial only: no token, cost, provider, account, plan, quota, or credit facts — those remain DASH-015's behind DASH-021.

### Tests

- Presenter: every count class, exact/lower-bound/zero/defaulted progress, elapsed, ETA availability + unavailable reasons, loading/empty/unavailable states, LKG reconcile + generation transition, announcement bounds.
- Component: exact vs. lower-bound ARIA semantics, stale/unavailable/empty/loading rendering, absence of protected fields.
- LiveView: pushed-snapshot render, burst coalescing into a single scheduled flush, LKG retention, run-generation transition.

Scoped local gate green (compile `--warnings-as-errors`, format, presenter + component + full `dashboard_live_test.exs` 54/54). Full CI runs the authoritative suite.

### Lane note

L2 lane follower under BO-018 (#1105). Shared `DashboardLive`/OCC-CSS/summary-container changes serialize with DASH-015 at the lane integration head; CSS is additive/namespaced to minimize conflict. Base is `develop` per configured `tracker.base_branch`.

A divisão interna deixaria invocações diretas sem o gate. Nenhuma instalação ocorreu. O rollback é reverter os dois commits desta branch ou abandonar a PR draft; a branch arquivada `archive/renova-aura-agent-os-monolith-943306b` preserva o snapshot remoto original e não deve ser alterada.

`8f22a69b741aa51a904f11d1f2dfa13216c61838`

A decisão reutiliza, sem apresentar nova auditoria, as conclusões `PR2_PREVIOUS_TECHNICAL_AUDIT_STILL_VALID` e `PR2_HUMAN_REVIEW_PASS_WITH_NON_BLOCKING_FINDINGS`. body:
## Dependencia y orden de merge

Este es el **PR B** y debe mergearse **SEGUNDO**, después de #96 (PR A: normalización de Ficha Médico) y antes de #97 (PR C: Turno/Scores).

Permanece en borrador porque #96 todavía no está mergeado en `main`. Antes de marcarlo listo se debe:

1. rebasar esta rama sobre el `main` que contenga #96;
2. resolver cualquier conflicto sin ampliar el alcance;
3. repetir tests focalizados, suite completa `src/tests/rayen-import`, typecheck, release gate, `node --check` y autoreview.

## Qué cambia

- Extrae desde `extension/background.js` la coordinación transversal de escrituras clínicas a un owner UMD clásico, `extension/clinical-write-runtime.js`.
- El owner recibe explícitamente Chrome/storage, Web Crypto, reloj y callbacks de autorización/lectura clínica.
- Mantiene en `background.js` los handlers de Turno y Scores, endpoints, autorización clínica y normalización de las lecturas de recuperación.
- Carga el owner durante la evaluación inicial del service worker y falla de forma cerrada si no está disponible.

El cambio es de ownership; no cambia mensajes, timeouts, protección antiduplcado ni semántica de ACK/recuperación.

## Cobertura

- Exclusión mutua por clave clínica.
- Persistencia del marcador antes del POST y persistencia tras resultado incierto.
- Generación obsoleta y ACK correcto/incorrecto.
- Recuperación en dos fases con doble lectura fresca y conservación del bloqueo ante cambios.
- Prueba estructural para impedir que `background.js` vuelva a apropiarse de la coordinación y presupuestos razonables de tamaño.
