author: cadari2
body:
## Summary

Implements the v0.5.7 design spec (`docs/specs/v0.5.7-econ-spec.md`), replacing the fixed-year scripted economic arcs with an endogenous, partly-randomized economy, plus two bug fixes and three new player-facing features.

- **Randomized macro events** — a hazard deck (pandemics, financial panics, land bubbles) follows the same per-year-chance / per-playthrough-cap / refractory-gap grammar as the existing war/quake system, replacing the old fixed-year scripted arcs (1904/1918/1955/…/2023). All draws are deterministic (`st.evRng`).
- **Endogenous economy** — a new city-attractiveness engine (transit reach & quality, housing slack & affordability, reachable jobs), damped by congestion and land prices, drives migration and couples into the business cycle. Replaces the scripted era demographic tide.
- **Building vintage & filtering** — buildings now carry a construction year; they lose tenants to newer stock nearby ("filtering") and out-of-code buildings cost more to maintain, climbing faster than inflation (capped). A **Renovate** action resets the clock.
- **Bug fix — organic growth on owned land**: company-owned parcels no longer spawn or densify buildings on their own.
- **Bug fix/feature — trackage rights overhaul**: the gauge-compatibility gate now checks in-service gauge overlap instead of default construction gauge; lines can terminate/stop at partner stations; revenue splits as true through-fares (each company's own rate on its own km) plus a per-company flat service charge paid once per operator a journey uses.
- **Feature — negotiable deals**: name your own price for a rival's hex, whole company, network-wide trackage rights, or per-hex trackage rights over just a stretch of their track — one counter-offer, rejection cooldowns, insult penalties. AIs make offers to the player too. Per-hex rights include a map interaction: click a rival's track hex, drag along **connected track only** to extend the selection (bare land, a gap, or a third company's track is silently skipped), then submit an offer.
- **Feature — NYC eras**: display-only era table now shows the sitting US president instead of period names (same mechanism as London's real-monarch eras).
- **Save v13** migrates all of the above cleanly from older saves (vintage seeded at the grace boundary so no upkeep shock on load).

## Test plan

- [x] `node tools/smoke.js` — 358/358 checks pass, including new coverage for the growth freeze, aging upkeep, negotiation protocol (accept/reject+counter/insult), per-hex trackage-rights pathing, save round-trip of every new field, and a full 1872–2028 AI-only run asserting econ fields stay finite and deck caps hold.
- [x] `node tools/domsmoke.js` — full DOM/UI smoke passes, including three new steps driving the real mouse/touch event handlers: entering per-hex-rights selection mode from the Companies panel, a drag that starts on a rival's track and correctly skips a bare-land hex mid-drag before extending onto the adjacent connected hex, and the full offer-and-accept flow granting rights and clearing selection state.
- [x] Manual review of the balance rails from the spec (opening-years pinch, office_l gamble, rail-first→property-later arc) — preserved by construction (no new demand channels; every shock effect flows through existing `st.econ.*` fields).

author: alexlopashev
body:
## Summary

This PR redesigns the BHCP v0 kernel around one behavior-neutral composition primitive: a finite `kernel-network` containing only structural identity, output type, typed child goal calls, and one total, pure BHCP reducer symbol.

The standard orchestration vocabulary—`all`, `any`, `none`, `chain`, unary `gate`, and persistent retention—is no longer privileged IR behavior. These forms are specified as versioned, self-hosted BHCP prelude definitions that lower completely to the minimal network before checking and semantic hashing.

It also factors semantic truth from operational execution:

- execution states: `Completed | Faulted`
- verdict states: `Satisfied | Refuted | Unresolved`
- reducer states: `Pending | Concluded`

Every state family uses adjectival variants consistently. `Pending` avoids importing language-level concurrency expectations, while gate outputs use `Excluded | Included<T>` so they do not collide with execution's `Completed` state.

## Why this design

The previous combinator-shaped kernel made each orchestration behavior part of the trusted semantic base. That prevents the language from defining and evolving its own composition algebra.

The new trusted boundary is deliberately narrow:

1. validate a finite, typed network;
2. invoke a total, deterministic, pure BHCP reducer over parent input and sealed child results;
3. accept either a non-empty set of known, unobserved children or a terminal result with a checked derivation;
4. generically re-evaluate the reducer and validate its sealed premises;
5. prevent reducers from manufacturing evidence or traces, inspecting operational trace contents, or selecting behavior-specific proof rules.

A network contains no behavior kind, quantifier family, guard, dependency list, budget, scheduling order, parallelism hint, or policy decision. Those concerns either lower away or belong to clauses and analysis/execution artifacts.

Parallelism and sequencing emerge from the reducer's requested child sets. Multiple requested children express horizontal eligibility; successive singleton sets express chaining; immediate conclusion expresses a closed gate. Effects, ownership, state, policy, and budget analysis still determine what an execution graph may schedule.

Separating `Completed(verdict)` from `Faulted(fault)` prevents infrastructure failure, timeout, missing evidence, and genuine counter-evidence from collapsing into one ambiguous result category.

## Representable semantic self-hosting

Self-hosting is now a concrete language boundary rather than an opaque compiler callback.

Every lowerer has the compile-time BHCP signature:

```text
Meta<DerivedForm,I,O> -> Meta<NetworkShape,I,O>
```

`DerivedForm` contains source-independent parent and child type information plus an optional typed condition. `NetworkShape` contains only output type, child shapes, and reducer symbol; it has no network or child IDs. Lowerers cannot inspect tokens, comments, diagnostic labels, spans, profiles, ambient state, planner data, or ID allocation.

The compiler validates the returned core shape and assigns deterministic structural IDs. Compile-time meta values and executed lowerer definitions disappear before executable semantic IR and hashing; every reachable runtime reducer definition remains in IR and semantic identity.

The canonical profile binds `§all`, `§any`, `§none`, `§chain`, and `§gate` to explicit versioned lowerer and reducer symbols. `§compose using f` is the sole core source form and produces the same network shape directly.

Composition quantifiers are intentionally stricter than logical quantifiers: only elaboration-time finite domains expand into explicit children. Verifier-backed or runtime-only collections use bounded or well-founded recursive goals instead of introducing a hidden dynamic-family kernel primitive.

## Normative changes

- Rewrites S2 around factored execution results and three semantic verdicts.
- Replaces privileged composition kinds with the minimal `kernel-network` in S8.
- Defines the compile-time `DerivedForm`/`NetworkShape` metamodel and standard-prelude symbol bindings.
- Specifies the exact monomorphized reducer ABI: parent input plus one optional execution-result field per child, returning `Reduction<ParentOutput>`.
- Specifies standard-prelude laws for `all`, `any`, `none`, `chain`, and unary `gate`.
- Makes pure gate conditions Boolean-or-fault; evidence-dependent judgments must be explicit child goals.
- Removes latch as a composition primitive; retention derives from ordinary capability-controlled state-read and compare-and-swap child goals.
- Moves recursion bounds to recursive child calls and all budget/concurrency decisions to execution artifacts.
- Requires derived forms and static composition quantifiers to lower completely before semantic hashing.
- Makes operational traces opaque to reducer choice.
- Adds the grammatical-family convention for categorical variants.
- Makes derivations generic: they contain only structural identity and sealed premises, not behavior-specific proof-rule tags.
- Lets a checked premise-free derivation supply evidence for empty logical identities without synthetic child evidence.

## Schema and artifact changes

- Replaces `composition-node`, `composition-kind`, and `latch-spec` with `kernel-network`, `kernel-child`, `child-observation`, `reduction`, and `derivation`.
- Adds `function-definition` and required semantic-IR `functions` for BHCP reducers.
- Adds `Verdict<T>`, `ExecutionResult<T>`, `Reduction<T>`, and compile-time `Meta<...>` type forms.
- Adds `derived-form-shape` and ID-free `network-shape` CDDL rules.
- Removes quantified-family, network-wide recursion, budget, and planner-hint fields from `kernel-network`; recursion is per child.
- Splits extension descriptors into disjoint shapes: derived extensions require a BHCP lowerer and no payload schema; native extensions require a payload schema, remain must-understand, and cannot masquerade as lowerings.
- Renames the `runtime-outcome` root to `execution-result` while retaining all 17 root fixtures.
- Updates planner/evidence vocabulary from `indeterminate` to `unresolved` and keeps categorical edge names grammatically consistent.
- Regenerates canonical IR expectations after the required `functions` field is introduced.

## Rust foundation

The executable slice now includes strongly typed models and validation for:

- semantic verdicts and operational faults;
- factored execution results;
- kernel children and argument modes;
- sealed child observations;
- pending and concluded reductions;
- generic proof-carrying derivations;
- kernel networks and reducer-symbol resolution;
- exact monomorphized reducer signatures;
- BHCP function definitions and `Option` types in semantic IR;
- disjoint derived/native extension descriptor boundaries; and
- rejection of non-minimal kernel schema fields.

Stable `BHCP4101` diagnostics reject malformed network/reduction values. Stable `BHCP4001` diagnostics reject missing reducers and invalid reducer signatures. Stable `BHCP5002` diagnostics reject mixed execution/verdict states, invalid extension descriptors, missing lowering metamodel rules, and schema attempts to restore behavior or planner metadata to the kernel.

## Intentionally deferred

This PR establishes and validates the semantic/kernel representation; it does not pretend that the current clause-only source compiler executes it.

Still deferred:

- parsing network, metamodel, and prelude function source;
- the complete total-expression, structural-recursion, and termination checker;
- checked-in standard-prelude lowerer/reducer definitions;
- executing derived lowerers;
- reducer evaluation and scheduling;
- the runtime generic proof checker and evidence-graph integration;
- planner/runtime/state-persistence behavior.

Unsupported source syntax continues to fail explicitly. The next executable boundary is the total expression checker plus checked-in standard-prelude l

author: 0frankie
body:
## The trap

`serve_penn.py --brain llm` only checked that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` **exists**, not that it works. An invalid key (typo, placeholder, revoked) booted fine — and past boot it was invisible by design:

1. `AnthropicClient.chat` catches every API error and returns `None` (printed only under a `verbose` flag serve_penn never sets).
2. `_result_or_none` turns any raised decide exception into `None`.
3. A `None` decision is the brain-outage degrade: idle this tick, re-ask next tick — forever.

Failed calls never reach the usage ledger, so the run monitor and `/usage` stayed at $0 with zero rows. Net effect (hit in the field tonight): a sim that ticks normally while the whole cast sits frozen on **"waking up"** at $0 spend, with nothing in the terminal. Symptom fingerprint: ~0.7 s/step instead of 0.1 s (one failed API round trip per tick).

## The fix

`check_anthropic_key()` runs once at `--brain llm` boot, after `resolve_llm`:

- **GET /v1/models** with the key — free, no tokens billed, one round trip.
- **401/403** → `SystemExit` with a one-line fix (matching the existing missing-key/wrong-provider gates).
- **Network trouble / 5xx** → warn and continue; transient failures belong to the run's own retry path, not a boot blocker.

The `urlopen` seam is injectable, so the four new tests stay fully offline like the rest of `test_penn_live_llm.py`. The README's key-hygiene paragraph now documents the check and the frozen-cast symptom for older checkouts.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest godot-generative-agents/tests/` — 277 passed (4 new).
- End-to-end against the real API: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-definitely-invalid … --brain llm` now aborts at boot with the new message (exit 1) instead of serving the frozen sim.
- `black --check` clean. Engine (`text_adventure_games/`) untouched.

author: teng-lin
body:
Closes #1960.

## Summary
`source_add` accepted a `title` for YouTube / Google-Drive / web-page imports but silently dropped it — these types re-derive the display title server-side, and the YouTube path didn't even forward it. An agent setting a deliberate title for citation stability got the upstream title with no signal.

This **honors the title via a best-effort post-add `rename`**:
- `SourcesAPI.add_url` gains an optional `title=`; `add_url`/`add_drive` apply the requested title through `honor_requested_title` after the add.
- **Non-fatal:** a rename failure (`RPCError`/`NetworkError`) keeps the added source with its upstream title and logs a warning — the add never fails because the retitle did.
- The MCP `source_add` tool flags a miss with `title_override_applied: false` + a `warning` (caller re-issues `source_rename`).

## Live-verified behavior
The whole design hinges on *when* the backend derives the title. I tested it against the live API (profile with real auth):
- **URL (Wikipedia)** and **YouTube** both return `READY` immediately with the title already re-derived, and a follow-up rename **holds (80–96s, no revert).** So the rename reliably sticks for these types — the title is derived synchronously, not asynchronously after the add.

## Review notes (this PR was taken over from a stalled implementation and run through simplifier + claude/codex/agy review + ultrathink)
- **Fixed (codex Important):** `honor_requested_title` returned the `UPDATE_SOURCE` echo wholesale, which can be sparse (id+title) and drop `url`/`kind`/`status`. Now uses `replace(source, title=…)` — preserves full metadata, swaps only the title (the `_source/upload.py` pattern). Test added.
- **Confirmed non-issue:** the `(RPCError, NetworkError)` catch is correct/sufficient (`SourceNotFoundError` etc. all subclass `RPCError` → non-fatal).
- **API-compat:** additive keyword-only `title=`; `audit_public_api_compat` clean, no allowlist entry.

## Known limitations / follow-ups (deferred)
- **`wait=True` miss-flag:** the MCP `title_override_applied` flag is only emitted on the `wait=False` path (the `wait=True` tail returns the `source_wait` aggregate). I prototyped surfacing it on the wait path too (checking the final ready title — a safety net if Drive *does* revert async), but it pushed `mcp/tools/sources.py` past the ADR-0008 1000-line ceiling, so it's deferred rather than breach the guardrail for a scenario live-testing suggests doesn't occur. Worth a follow-up with a proper sibling extraction if Drive is confirmed to revert.
- **Drive not live-verified:** I couldn't test a Drive import (no Drive file id to hand). URL + YouTube confirm the rename sticks; Drive is very likely the same (same backend), but worth a live check.

## Test plan
- [x] mypy · ruff · ruff format — clean
- [x] `uv run pytest` (full suite) — **12371 passed**, 77 skipped, 1 xfailed
- [x] ADR-0008 module-size ratchet green (`sources.py` = 998 ≤ 1000)
- [x] Coverage: title honored (rename called), rename-failure non-fatal, sparse-echo metadata preserved, MCP miss-flag (wait=False), drive+youtube+url paths, title-less add keeps historical call shape
- [x] **Live-verified** rename-survival for URL + YouTube

T52 r4「剩余全部缺陷 Workflow 批修」战役 **Tier 3 收官（低危/eval/descriptions）**：9 个并行文件互斥代理修完 9 簇——**23 项修复**（20 代理 + 3 集成完成）+ 其余诚实存档/文档化/待裁。**本批闭合 r4 backlog：205 项全部处置完毕**（修复或附精确理由归档）。silver-core-sdk 0.67.1 → 0.67.2。

body:
Publishers' og:images sometimes paste a dark graphic onto a white 1200x628 canvas; the white side bars read as broken card edges on both themes (seen on the BQP SpaceWERX item, 2026-07-17, fixed by hand that day).

**What this does**
- New `trimWhiteBorders` in `scripts/fetch-thumbs.ts`: shaves uniform near-white borders ONLY when it is provably a border shave, never a content crop. Guards: all four corners must be near-white (each RGB channel >= 235), the trim must keep at least half the pixels, the result must still pass the 200px minimum-dimension gate, and it must actually be smaller.
- Applied inside `reencodeForStorage`, so the scheduled sweep pipeline and `set-item-image.ts` both get it automatically.
- `set-item-image.ts` grows a `--no-trim` flag to keep an image exactly as the source serves it.

**Verified**
- The original letterboxed BQP og:image (1200x628) trims to 842x628.
- A dark-cornered photograph is untouched; a small subject on a white canvas is rejected as a content crop; an all-white image returns null.
- 5 new tests in `scripts/__tests__/fetch-thumbs.test.ts`; full `bun run build` (typecheck, 528 tests, feed/registry/signals/orbits checks, prerender) passes.

The FundingChoices block in `root.html.heex` (AdSense CMP + Google's full-page ad-block-recovery message) was gated only by the production host, while the AdSense loader right below it was already gated by `show_ads?/1`. So a **paying patron running an ad blocker could still get Google's full-page "please allow ads" recovery overlay** — nagging exactly the people who paid to be ad-free.

Patrons load no ads, so they need neither the AdSense consent surface nor the recovery nag. This gates the whole FundingChoices block the same way as the ad loader.

- `root.html.heex`: added `show_ads?/1` to the FundingChoices conditional, comment updated with the rationale

  - anonymous visitor on prod host → FC scripts present
  - patron on prod host → FC scripts absent
  - non-prod host → FC scripts absent

## Not in this PR

The other half of the report — whether to disable/limit the AdSense auto-ads **vignette** format (the full-screen interstitial the July 14 session most likely hit) — is an AdSense dashboard decision Steven is evaluating against the format-level earnings split. No code change involved.

## Test plan

author: kishiguro
body:
## Summary
Fixes review finding #4 of `docs/design/bgp-code-review-findings.md` (dual-homed L3VPN withdraw blackholes the survivor).

- `handle_import_v4/v6` stored every VPN import under one `(remote_id 0, ORIGINATED_PEER)` Loc-RIB identity, ignoring the origin RD, and `handle_withdraw_import` ignored its `rd` argument — a prefix imported from two PEs (two RDs) aliased to one row, so either PE's withdraw removed the row holding the OTHER PE's still-valid route (CE-side blackhole). The per-prefix transport maps aliased the same way, destroying the survivor's labelled tunnel.
- Fix: per-origin-RD synthetic candidate ids (`import_ids`, base 16 — clear of the redistribute identities 1..=5 that already share the `ORIGINATED_PEER` ident). Imports from different RDs coexist as separate candidates; a withdraw removes exactly the withdrawing RD's row (no-op for an RD never imported from) and best-path promotes the survivor. Transports move to a per-`(prefix, RD)` store; the winner-only maps `fib_install` reads are refreshed after every import/withdraw so the survivor's tunnel is restored.

## Test plan
- New `bgp_vrf_dual_home.feature` (z1/z3 export `10.9.0.0/24` under RDs 65001:1/65001:3, z2 imports both), red/green-verified live: on the pre-fix binary PE1's withdraw removed the prefix from z2's VRF while RD 65001:3 was still advertised (the exact finding); with the fix the survivor stays, the second withdraw empties the row, and a re-add re-imports. Teardown clean.
- Full workspace suite (`--exclude bdd`) 39/39 green; 619 BGP unit tests; workspace clippy clean.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Linux Quick Chat (#110285) sends by spawning the CLI per message: no delivery acks, a fresh process per send, agent identity via a CLI field instead of the gateway's own contract, and no connectivity awareness. This PR gives the Linux app a real native gateway connection — the same trust class the macOS app has — and routes Quick Chat through it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three gateway security contracts shaped the design, each verified in source before building (none were relaxed):

1. Browser-origin token-only sockets get their scopes cleared by design (`connect-auth.ts`), so a webview WebSocket client was rejected.
2. A native client id alone does not grant operator scopes either — device-less shared-token auth collapses `operator.read` to `[]` (proven by the existing `server.auth.default-token.suite.ts`). The macOS app's real trust class is a persistent device identity with nonce-bound challenge signing.
3. Self-signed gateway TLS (`gateway.tls.autoGenerate`) cannot be verified by system roots, and mDNS fingerprints are not an authoritative trust source.

What ships, accordingly:

- **Native WebSocket client** (`gateway_ws.rs`, tokio-tungstenite): connect/hello handshake, request/response correlation with timeouts, `agents.list` + `chat.send` with ack classification, 1–30s capped reconnect backoff, heartbeat watchdog. Auth material never reaches the webview; the invoke API surface for `quickchat.js` is unchanged in shape.
- **Persistent device identity** (`gateway_device_identity.rs`, ed25519-dalek): Ed25519 keypair + endpoint-bound reusable device token, atomic 0600 storage in the app config dir, zeroized credential buffers, v3 nonce-bound signature byte-identical to the macOS/OpenClawKit layout (fixture-bytes test).
- **Auth surface (flagged for maintainer review)**: additive `openclaw-linux` entry in the closed client-id set; the native-app UI predicate extracted to one shared helper (`isNativeAppUiClient`) that admission now uses, with Linux added alongside macOS/iOS/Android; new dedicated test file proving direct-local pairing auto-approves and remote pairing stays explicit.
- **TLS trust handoff**: `dashboard --json` additively emits the gateway's authoritative leaf-cert SHA-256 (same canonical format as `src/infra/tls/fingerprint.ts` and the discovery `gatewayTlsSha256` field) only when TLS is enabled; the Rust connector pins it with a constant-time compare (custom rustls verifier that still enforces handshake-signature validity), uses system roots when no pin is handed off, and rejects a pin on plain `ws://`. Trust failures surface distinctly from downtime.
- **Quick Chat integration**: identity/agents/switcher served from the gateway list (render-ready `identity.avatarUrl`), sends via `chat.send` with UUID idempotency keys and macOS-identical routing (global scope ⇒ `global` + agentId), a connectivity strip driven by connection-state events, and the entire CLI spawn path (`spawn_agent_turn`, message temp files, CLI list structs) deleted.

Known limitations, deliberate: SecretRef-configured tokens are withheld from the handoff (already-paired installs keep working via device token; first-run documented), ack-only send classification (terminal turn outcome stays in the session), streamed replies are the named follow-up.

## User Impact

Linux Quick Chat sends now get real accepted/failed acks from the gateway, agent identities and avatars come straight from the gateway contract, a slim strip shows when the gateway is unreachable (with automatic reconnect), and the app pairs itself as a first-class local device — visible and manageable like the macOS app. Docs updated (`docs/platforms/linux.md`).

## Evidence

Live end-to-end in an Ubuntu 24.04 container running a real repo-built gateway (token auth, three seeded agents):

| Paired + gateway-served avatar | Message staged |
| --- | --- |
| ![bar](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/9f94a9420f2dec783c4ce3bb9e8a5f61/raw/gw-bar.png) | ![typed](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/9f94a9420f2dec783c4ce3bb9e8a5f61/raw/gw-typed.png) |

| Gateway killed → strip | Gateway restarted → auto-recovery |
| --- | --- |
| ![strip](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/9f94a9420f2dec783c4ce3bb9e8a5f61/raw/gw-strip2.png) | ![recovered](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/9f94a9420f2dec783c4ce3bb9e8a5f61/raw/gw-recovered.png) |

The live run exercised the full new path: dashboard handoff (`wsUrl` + fragment token) → connect/hello → device pairing (direct-local auto-approve; `quickchat-gateway-device.json` persisted mode 0600) → `agents.list` with avatar → send → gateway kill → "Gateway unreachable — retrying" → restart → reconnect via reused device token.

Validation:

- `cargo +1.93 fmt --check` and `cargo test --locked`: 69/69 (Blacksmith Testbox run 29633282403, and re-verified in the Linux container on the final head).
- Focused Vitest across every touched TS surface: 43/43, plus the relocated Linux admission test (33/33 in the shared suite unchanged).
- `pnpm build` clean in the container; `node --check` on the JS; `git diff --check` clean.
- Dependency health checks recorded for `tokio-tungstenite` 0.30.0, `ed25519-dalek` 3.0.0, `rustls` 0.23.42, `subtle` 2.6.1.
- Structured second-model review: multiple rounds during the build (accepted findings fixed); the final round's two P1 deserialization claims were verified false against source — both structs carry `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` (`gateway.rs:104`, `gateway_ws.rs:188`) — and are additionally disproven by the live container run above, which decodes both payloads on that exact code.

author: davion-knight
body:
## What

Adds a **Total Network Value (TNV)** rollup to the `/api/v1/economics` summary — a single top-line economic figure splitting root TAO value vs. alpha value across the whole network, which none of the existing economics fields expose.

- `total_alpha_value_tao` — Σ each alpha subnet's (netuid > 0) `alpha_market_cap_tao` (`alpha_price_tao × total_stake_tao`, the market-cap proxy each row already carries).
- `total_root_value_tao` — the root subnet's (netuid 0) staked TAO, valued 1:1 (root has no AMM); `0` when the root subnet has no economics row.
- `total_network_value_tao` — the two summed.

## Why

Backprop surfaces TNV as its headline number (#5968 competitive survey). metagraphed already captures per-subnet `alpha_price_tao` + `total_stake_tao` everywhere, so this is **pure aggregation over existing data — no new ingestion, no new route**.

## How

- New pure `computeNetworkValue(rows)` in `scripts/lib/economics-artifacts.mjs`, summed in **exact rao-integer BigInt space** and emitted as fixed 9-decimal strings — matching `total_stake_tao`'s own documented past-2³ ceiling handling (the network-wide total is ~328M TAO, well over the ~9,007,199 TAO exact-double limit).
- Wired into `buildEconomicsArtifact`'s `summary`. That single builder feeds **both** the live economics tier (`scripts/refresh-economics.mjs`) **and** the built artifact (`scripts/build-artifacts.mjs`), so `GET /api/v1/economics` and the `get_economics` MCP tool (whose output schema treats `summary` as an opaque object) both carry the new fields with no separate wiring.
- Schema (`schemas/components/05-subnets.schema.json` → `EconomicsArtifact.summary`) + OpenAPI/types regenerated.

**GraphQL parity:** the GraphQL `EconomicsList` type intentionally exposes only `subnets`/`total`/`next_cursor` (no `summary` block), so there is no summary field there to mirror — REST + MCP are the surfaces that expose the summary, and both now carry TNV.

## Tests

`computeNetworkValue` unit-tested: alpha-only, root split, null/non-finite → 0, empty, exact-rao summation, and large past-2³ magnitudes. All validators green locally: `contract-drift`, `schemas`, `openapi` (162 routes), `openapi-examples` (162/162), `api`.

Closes #6641

author: jlperla
body:
## Summary

- add `linear_solver="augmented_qr"` as an explicit algorithm on `UnderdeterminedLevenbergMarquardt`
- solve the damped least-squares subproblem directly through the augmented matrix `[J S; sqrt(lambda) I]`
- preserve the existing `qr` algorithm as a separate choice
- remove the duplicate square-only solver, result type, tests, and documentation
- migrate coverage for metrics, rank-deficient systems, JIT, AD, float64, and GPU paths

## Why

Square systems do not define a different nonlinear problem here. The augmented-QR factorization is useful as its own linear-solver algorithm, but a separate square LM implementation duplicated the surrounding nonlinear method and API.

## Compatibility

This removes `SquareLevenbergMarquardt` and `SquareSolveResult`. Existing square-system users should use:

```python
UnderdeterminedLevenbergMarquardt(
    residual,
    linear_solver="augmented_qr",
    geodesic_acceleration=False,
    cache_jacobian=False,
)
```

## Validation

- nlls-gram: 325 passed, 8 skipped
- strict MkDocs build passed
- Ruff formatting and lint passed
- tinydiffeq full suite against this branch: 257 passed
- all documented tinydiffeq ODE/DAE/SDAE and differentiation examples passed
- tinydiffeq full-suite time: 481.50 s vs 482.27 s before
- direct solver microbenchmarks improved from 81.80/229.61/344.69 µs to 79.17/220.62/317.08 µs for n=1/4/8

author: richardmhope
body:
Picks up the CI/test-efficiency work from `claude/ci-test-suite-efficiency-ywq4te`, rebased onto current main, reviewed, and extended.

## What's here

### Test suite: cache the fixture bcrypt hash (the big win)
`bcrypt` at the production work factor (`BCRYPT_ROUNDS=12`) is ~250ms of pure CPU per call, and the `admin_user` fixture re-hashed the same literal password on **every** test that uses `client` — which is most of the suite. `conftest.cached_password_hash()` computes one real, production-work-factor hash **per distinct password per session** (the salt lives inside the hash, so it verifies identically everywhere, login tests included) and the fixtures + setup-only users switch to it.

**Measured locally: full suite 158s → 64s (~60% faster), 743 passed.** The hashing-*specific* tests (`test_offload`, `test_auth_hardening`, `test_code_review_low/medium`) deliberately keep the real `hash_password`/`_hash_password_sync` so the offload, timing, and work-factor behaviour stays under test.

### CI waste
- **`concurrency` cancel on PRs only** — a new push supersedes the previous run instead of letting its six jobs finish; pushes to `main` still run to completion (no commit left without a green record).
- **`timeout-minutes` on every job** — a hung step can't burn the 6h default.
- **Playwright/Chromium install overlaps stack boot** — the ~2 min of pip + browser download now runs while Postgres init + migrations + Caddy come up, instead of adding to it.
- **`pytest --durations=10`** so a suite-runtime regression is visible in the log.

### Added in review
- `CLAUDE.md` CI-gates note documenting the concurrency-cancel + per-job timeouts (the original commit documented only the test helper).

## Reviewed and deliberately *not* bundled (higher-risk, better as their own PRs)
- **`pytest-xdist` (`-n auto`)** — the biggest remaining lever, but the session-scoped single Postgres + autouse `TRUNCATE` isolation means workers would need **per-worker databases** (derive the DB name from `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER`, `CREATE DATABASE` per worker) and a **capped pool / worker count** to avoid exhausting Postgres `max_connections` (esp. on high-core dev machines). Real flakiness surface — deserves a focused, separately-verified PR.
- **Docker layer cache for the `ui` build** (`buildx` + `type=gha`) — would cut the per-run image build, but is fiddly with compose and a known cache-corruption footgun; separate PR.
- **Playwright browser cache** — skipped: the download is already fully hidden by the boot/readiness overlap, so caching adds a new SHA-pinned action + maintenance for ~0 wall-clock.

## Validation
- Full suite green locally (743 passed, 63.8s) against real Postgres 18.
- ruff check + `ruff format --check app tests alembic e2e` clean; `ci.yml` parses.

author: davideast
body:
```ts
// serve-init.ts invoked the injected boot fetch as a member call:
env.fetch('/__pyric/init-events.json')   // this === env → browsers throw
                                         // TypeError: Illegal invocation
// …inside catch/fire-and-forget paths, so nothing ever surfaced.
```

Fixes #364 — but the bug was never where the symptom pointed. Studio's feed layer is sound (now pinned by a test that renders the worker backlog before any live event). The defect is in the worker boot: browser `fetch` is this-sensitive, and every member-call site (`hydrateEventHistory`, capture flush, `--persist` prime/mirror/clear, auth flush) threw `Illegal invocation` into swallowed catches. Verified against real Chromium via Playwright.

## What that actually broke

- A rebooted SharedWorker (tab close/reload gap — routine under vite dev) answered Studio's first event subscription with an **empty history** → the field report's "Activity initially empty, then backfills."
- The capture flush died before its `.catch` attached → `.pyric/last-session.json` was **never written** on the default worker path — silently breaking the `pyric verify` loop too.
- Only `fetchInitPayload(env.fetch)` passed fetch as a value (plain call), which is why rules/seed always worked and the bug looked Studio-shaped.

## Fix

One file: `buildWorkerCtx` detaches fetch before any use (`const ambientFetch = bootEnv.fetch; fetch: (...args) => ambientFetch(...args)`). `entry.ts` is the sole production caller, so every path is covered.

## Risk

Minimal by construction — a call-convention fix with no behavior change for test stubs (already this-insensitive). End-to-end re-verified in a real browser: worker death → Studio first open renders the full pre-open history; capture file written.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- Characterization (failing-first): `serve-init.test.ts` boots the real `buildWorkerCtx` through a `browserishFetch` that replays the browser's `this` contract — pre-fix: hydration primes 0 of 4 events, capture never POSTs (32 pass / 2 fail); post-fix green.
- Studio seam exonerated and pinned: `studio-events-hydration.test.tsx` — real `useStudioEvents` + `workerEventFeed` shows the backlog before any live event.
- Gates: cli `test/serve` 563 / 0 fail; studio 338 / 0; typechecks clean. (cli full suite has 11 pre-existing environment failures with no import edge to the changed module.)
- Real-browser probes (temporary, not committed) reproduced the exact field symptom pre-fix and its absence post-fix, on both `pyric dev --ui` and the vite plugin.

</details>

author: p2sqrd
body:
## The problem

On a 390px phone (iPhone width), **every page had a 300px horizontal scroll** — the same amount everywhere, pointing to one shared culprit rather than scattered issues: the nav bar. The logo, seven links, the 🔔, the "?" tour button, the nameplate, and "Sign out" were all crammed onto one non-wrapping row that needed ~690px, forcing the whole document to 690px wide.

The page *content* (tables, the budget tower, stacked cards) already behaved on mobile — the nav was the only thing breaking the layout.

## The fix

Below the `lg` breakpoint, the link row and the desktop-only right-side controls collapse into a hamburger sheet:

- **Top bar on phones:** just the logo, the 🔔, and a ☰ button.
- **The sheet (new `MobileMenu` component):** every link stacked (Archive's sub-pages indented), plus the tour launcher, the nameplate, and Sign out. Closes on link tap, backdrop tap, or Escape; locks body scroll while open. Portaled to `document.body` so the sticky header's `backdrop-blur` doesn't trap it.
- **Desktop is untouched** — the inline nav renders exactly as before at `lg`+.
- The first-login onboarding auto-open still fires on phones, because its launcher stays mounted (just visually hidden) below `lg`.

Also enlarged the keeper **"Keep" checkbox** into a full-cell ~44px tap target so it's comfortable to hit on a phone (was a 16px box).

## Files
- `src/components/MobileMenu.tsx` — new hamburger button + slide-down sheet.
- `src/components/Nav.tsx` — wire in `MobileMenu`; hide desktop-only controls below `lg`.
- `src/components/NavLinks.tsx` — hide the inline link row below `lg`.
- `src/components/KeeperSelectionForm.tsx` — 44px keeper checkbox tap target.

## Verification
- Horizontal overflow measured at **0px on all six main pages** at 390px (was 300px each).
- Confirmed by screenshot: collapsed bar, open sheet, and the keeper page.
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `vitest` (14 passing), and `next build` all green.

## Note
Wide tables (Budget, Standings) now scroll sideways *inside their own container* on phones rather than breaking the page — standard responsive behavior. Reflowing them into stacked cards on mobile is a larger, separate piece of work if we want it later.

### Motivation

- Améliorer le référencement local et la cohérence des balises SEO de la page d’accueil sans toucher au contenu visible ni aux images fournies.
- Remplacer un JSON-LD existant incomplet/brisant par un balisage Schema.org valide et limité aux seules informations vérifiées.

- Harmonisation des balises principales dans `index.html` : remplacement de `title` et de la `meta description`, et alignement des balises Open Graph (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`) et Twitter Card (`twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`) pour refléter Clair&Net, Évreux et l’Eure (27).

author: jenner-analytics
body:
[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) provides an API that runs SAS code, with support for more than 200 SAS procedures. You can also use it with AI assistants in a collaborative workspace. It's available for Mac on the Apple App Store, and by license for Windows and Linux.

We support the larger community by
(1) increasing access to SAS-compatible systems,
(2) by providing test coverage and a test coverage framework to public SAS repos in order to encourage the use of best practices in software engineering.

Your utl-worst-case-median-survival-...-censoring.sas runs on Jenner unmodified — this PR adds a small compatibility bundle so you can see for yourself. It's the test we wrote for your project, shared in case it's useful, and was assembled with AI assistance as is most code in modern businesses today. The bundle pins the SAS side of your SAS-vs-R comparison: the exponential survival simulation, PROC QUANTLIFE at the 0.50 quantile, and reading medians.csv back in to re-derive the input census — all captured as small, self-contained runs.

What made this one worth reproducing carefully was the design of the simulation itself: drawing the event time and an independent exponential censoring time and keeping `min(time_event, time_censor)` with `status = (time_event <= time_censor)` is a compact way to manufacture a trial that lands at ~74% censoring, and it's a deliberately unkind stress test for a median estimator. The soapbox note about the upper CI on the median difference diverging between SAS quantlife and R quantreg near the 0.5 quantile is the honest observation most write-ups skip, and the side-by-side quantile table makes exactly where the two engines part ways easy to read.

The `jenner-check/` directory is self-contained and nothing runs on merge — no workflows, no hooks, nothing outside that folder is touched. It holds three bundles, each a byte-for-byte copy of the SAS it runs, the captured log and listing, plus a small runner:

```
jenner-check/
├── run_jenner.sh
├── README.md
├── t001_survival_data_export/      # the make-data DATA step + PROC EXPORT dbms=csv
├── t002_quantlife_median_survival/ # PROC QUANTLIFE, quantile=0.50, method=km
└── t003_medians_census/            # medians.csv read back -> PROC FREQ + PROC MEANS
```

To run one against the hosted API, check out this PR's branch and run from the repo root:

```bash
# check out this PR (puts you on its branch), then run from the repo root:
gh pr checkout 1
curl -sS --data-binary @jenner-check/t002_quantlife_median_survival/script.sas https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

Or `cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all` re-runs every bundle and verifies the pinned fields in each `expected.json`. It's free to try, no signup — full API reference: [the docs](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/).

On data: the runner uploads only the SAS source text of the script it runs (plus a two-line autoexec) to api.jenneranalytics.com, which runs it and returns the log and listing. It does not read or upload any data files — anything sitting next to a script stays on your machine — and nothing is sent unless you run one of these commands yourself. Only the code you run is transmitted, as with pasting a snippet into any hosted tool; since a script's own source is what's sent, you can review it first if it ever embeds values inline.

Merge it, close it, or ignore it — all fine, and no response is expected. We won't open further PRs in this repo. To opt out for good, put `no-more-prs` in any comment or open an issue titled `jenner-check: opt out`.

author: gabrielvilabracho
body:
## Summary

Replaces a previous, since-reverted standalone `/demo` UI (separate reducer-driven views, never merged) with demo data injected through the app's existing adapter seam — the real dashboard, invoice tables, review flow, client analytics, and audit pages render deterministic demo data unchanged, with simulated actions going through the same ports as live traffic.

- `generateDemoDataset(seed, { baseClock })` — pure, mulberry32-seeded generator producing ~600 invoices across 12 months plus clients/suppliers/staff/batches, anchored to the existing marketing fixture personas. No `Date.now`/`Math.random`.
- Three demo port adapters (`PortalBackendPort`, `ProtectedPageDataPort`, `SessionPort`) sharing one in-memory store, selected in `runtime.ts` as `mock -> demo -> bff` when `DEMO_MODE === 'true'` (exact match, fail-closed).
- Mutations (`decideInvoice`, `createBatch`/`finalizeBatch`, client/supplier/staff/settings/catalog writes) go through the real port, guarded by the invoice lifecycle's `canTransition` rules.
- `middleware.ts` bypasses Clerk entirely when `DEMO_MODE === 'true'`; `/demo` and `/login` redirect to `/dashboard`. Any other value of `DEMO_MODE` behaves byte-identically to today.
- `decideInvoiceAction` gets a demo-only schema variant that relaxes id validation (non-UUID demo ids) — live validation is untouched.
- `getPortalNow()` freezes "now" to the dataset's base clock in demo mode so dashboard/client/audit KPIs don't drift from the generated data as wall time passes (found and fixed during adversarial review — see below).
- The old bespoke `/demo` UI and its `useReducer` runtime are deleted; `reducer.ts`'s lifecycle guard is reused by the new adapter instead.
- 7 e2e tests under a dedicated `playwright.demo.config.ts`, wired into CI.
- `openspec/changes/interactive-demo-mode/` rewritten to document the shipped design instead of the rejected one.

This branch is based on `main` plus a cherry-pick of `8c8d900` (env-gated marketing dataset foundation, already on `feat/landing-v2`), since the demo generator depends on those fixtures and neither `main` nor a clean checkout had them yet.

## Review

Ran an adversarial dual review (risk + reliability, fresh context) before opening this PR:
- **Risk**: no blockers. Fail-closed bypass verified (exact match, spoofed headers scrubbed, no path reaches the real BFF under `DEMO_MODE=true`). Two hardening suggestions left as follow-ups (see below).
- **Reliability**: one CRITICAL finding — dashboard/client/audit pages mixed the frozen dataset clock with the real wall clock, causing KPIs to drift over time. Fixed via `getPortalNow()`. Also fixed an incidental invoice-id collision guard in `finalizeBatch`, and added edge-case tests (pagination past the end, `nextCursor` contract, month-boundary generation).

## Deferred (not in scope of this PR)
- Boot-time assertion refusing `DEMO_MODE=true` combined with real backend credentials.
- e2e assertion for the double-approve honest-error toast.
- Generator quirk: at a midnight month-start base clock, a few current-day rows get timestamps just after the base clock (documented in the test, not a crash).

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter @inv-platform/web exec vitest run` — 1006 passing, only 2 known pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (`bff/mappers/__tests__/export-fixture.test.ts`, `bff/__tests__/protected-pages.test.ts`)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @inv-platform/web exec tsc --noEmit` — zero errors
- [x] `pnpm --filter @inv-platform/web build` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @inv-platform/web e2e:demo` — 7/7 passing, executed against real dev servers
- [ ] Manual: `DEMO_MODE=true pnpm --filter @inv-platform/web dev`, browse `/dashboard`, approve an invoice from the review flow, confirm the KPI updates

author: cgasgarth
body:
Closes #24

## Why

RustTable now has a deterministic performance contract for the real photo and processing APIs without putting timing work into pre-commit, pre-push, or PR validation. The benchmark is explicit, stable-Rust, manifest-isolated, and runs only from merge-only main validation.

## How

- add a stable custom benchmark target with `harness = false`, `bench = false`, and `test = false`
- add strict versioned TSV parsing, nearest-rank statistics, integer normalization, checked arithmetic, and exact CLI validation
- measure deterministic 128-asset photo construction/iteration and 256x256 exposure-plus-offset rendering
- add 300-second hard-deadline execution with result evidence uploaded by merge-only GHA
- add five non-timing contract tests and keep the full workspace test path free of measured benchmark output

## Calibration

After one discarded warm-cache run, five independent release-mode runs on the local documented Rust 1.95 host produced normalized p95 observations:

- photo: 64,756,016; 59,191,176; 62,667,112; 56,400,401; 61,317,144 ppm. Limit = ceil(max(64,756,016 x 1.5)) = 97,134,024 ppm.
- render: 3,691,458; 3,504,465; 3,400,265; 4,045,348; 3,422,022 ppm. Limit = ceil(max(4,045,348 x 1.5)) = 6,068,022 ppm.

## Summary

This PR expands the checkout example into a detailed, local-first reference
microservice for Go developers learning Restate.

The completed system demonstrates durable workflows, virtual objects,
replay-safe side effects, Kafka-compatible event ingestion, service discovery,
contract testing, integration testing, compensation, and AWS Lambda packaging.
It runs locally without an AWS account.

## What changed

- Added a Redpanda single-broker development environment.
- Configured Restate to consume `orders.submitted.v1` directly from Kafka.
- Added the keyed `OrderEvents` virtual object for ordered, idempotent event processing.
- Added a CloudEvents-shaped `order-submitted.v1` contract.
- Added JSON Schema, example events, strict decoding, and semantic validation.
- Added a standard-library Kafka REST event publisher.
- Added idempotent Restate deployment discovery and Kafka subscription setup.
- Added durable event-processing receipts for asynchronous status queries.
- Updated the local and Lambda entrypoints to expose the event handler.
- Added unit, contract, synchronous integration, and Kafka integration tests.
- Added a Docker-backed integration-test command and CI job.
- Added a stable Restate node identity so persisted state survives container recreation.
- Added architecture, testing, service-discovery, contract, and AWS documentation.
- Added a separate gamified onboarding course under `exercises/`.

## Local development

Start Restate and Redpanda:

```bash
make infra-up
```

Start the Go service in another terminal:

```bash
make run
```

Register the services and configure the Kafka subscription:

```bash
make setup-local
```

Publish the example order event:

```bash
make publish-event
```

The Restate UI is available at http://localhost:9070/.

## Testing

The following checks were completed successfully:

```bash
make test
make build
make build-lambdas
make test-integration
docker compose config --quiet
git diff --check
```

The integration suite verifies both:

HTTP ingress → workflow → inventory and payment
Kafka REST → Redpanda → Restate subscription → event object → workflow

Container recreation was also tested with persisted Restate and Redpanda volumes.

## Documentation

Key entry points:

- README.md
- exercises/README.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/testing.md
- docs/service-discovery.md
- docs/aws-deployment.md
- contracts/README.md

AWS impact

No AWS account is required for local development.
The existing SAM deployment remains available, and the order Lambda now also
hosts OrderEvents. In an AWS environment, the local Redpanda broker can be
replaced with Amazon MSK or Confluent Cloud without changing the event contract
or Restate handler.

author: 0nlynet
body:
## Root cause

The checked-in legacy SQL creates `users.tenant_id` and `users.password_hash`, but the current TypeORM entities query `users."tenantId"`, `users."passwordHash"`, and newer account-status columns. A database initialized from that legacy SQL therefore throws during the very first login lookup, including for an unknown email, which surfaces as HTTP 500.

The same drift exists between legacy snake_case tenant timestamps/settings and the current tenant entity, and legacy `slug`/`name` constraints block current workspace and invite writes.

## What changed

- adds the project’s first registered TypeORM migration and transactional migration table
- automatically runs registered migrations in production before Nest starts
- detects the real legacy columns, adds only missing current columns, backfills account/tenant values, and preserves legacy data
- marks password-backed legacy accounts verified so pre-verification customers are not locked out
- relaxes only obsolete legacy NOT NULL fields that block new workspace/member writes
- refuses an unsafe identity repair if an existing table is missing its primary identifier
- adds TypeORM CLI `migration:run` and `migration:show` commands
- removes the unused `ormconfig.ts` that still enabled unsafe production synchronization

## Validation

- reproduces the stale checked-in SQL schema in PostgreSQL-compatible memory
- proves an existing broker can be loaded after migration
- proves a new agent can be inserted after migration
- `npm test -- --runInBand` — 11 suites, 28 tests passed

author: docasheesh-png
body:
## P0 — the *real* iOS login root cause (from build 27's on-screen trail)

Build 27 (with the previous bound-the-wait fix) let Google finally open, and the sign-in trail revealed the deeper bug:
```
07:44:23 clearing any old session…
07:44:27 opening Google sign-in…          ← 4s gap = the bounded clear TIMED OUT (signOut hung)
07:44:37 Google returned — token: YES     ← native Google auth succeeded
07:44:37 verifying with Firebase…         ← signInWithCredential starts
07:44:55 failed: sign-in did not complete ← 18s later → timeout
```

**Root cause:** on the iOS WKWebView the web-SDK `signOut()` persistence write can **hang**, and a hung signOut **holds Firebase Auth's internal operation queue** — so the `signInWithCredential` that follows is stuck behind it forever and login never completes. The earlier fix let Google *open*, but the still-pending hung signOut then **poisoned the actual sign-in**. In other words, the pre-login force-logout is *itself* what breaks native login (and was the original "infinite loading on return from Google" too).

## Fix (root cause)
- New pure `preLoginWebSignOutAllowed(isNative)` → **false on native**. `forceLogoutBeforeLogin()` now no-ops on the app.
- The native sign-in (`signInWithCredential` / email / phone credential) **replaces the old session on its own**, so the pre-logout is unnecessary *and* harmful there.
- **Web keeps** the bounded clear (a stale session can wedge `signInWithPopup`, and `signOut` is safe on a real browser).
- The `clearing any old session…` trail line is web-gated so it never lies on the app.

## Honest note (rule 3)
The old session was never the blocker — the *attempt to log it out* was. Removing it on native is what lets the new login complete; the successful sign-in then replaces the old session, which is the outcome you actually wanted.

## Tests
`nativeAuthGuard.test.ts` +2: `preLoginWebSignOutAllowed(true)=false`, `(false)=true`. Full gate green: `tsc` clean, **7325 pass** (only the 2 pre-existing Sonic `@aws-sdk` env-gap files fail, unrelated).

## Next
On merge → build **build 28 (`.ipa` → TestFlight)** so you can re-test Google login end-to-end.

- CI: extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `l3build-regression` and `ctan-smoke` jobs that install a LaTeX toolchain, run `l3build check` / `l3build ctan`, and upload diagnostics/archives on failure. 
- l3build/tooling: make `build.lua` the authoritative l3build configuration (and `l3build.lua` a compatibility shim), read `insr-version.json` for version/metadata, and add detailed `uploadconfig`, `tdslocations`, `testfiledir`, `tagfiles` and file categories. 
- Registries & runtime API: add `config/theme-registry.tex`, `config/fontset-registry.tex`, and `config/plugin-registry.tex` and extend `tex/latex/insr/insr-core.sty` and `insr-config.sty` with registration/activation APIs for themes, fontsets and plugins plus plugin dependency/conflict handling and public commands `\INSRUsePlugin` and `\INSRUseTheme`. 
- Versioning & schema: add `insr-version.json` as the canonical version/metadata source and `schema/insr-project.schema.json` to define a strict JSON configuration contract. 
- Developer tools: add `tools/insr_cli.py` (CLI to validate/generate deterministic TeX from JSON) and `tools/insr_version.py` (load/version helpers). 
- Tests & fixtures: add a large set of deterministic l3build regression fixtures under `testfiles/` (`*.lvt` and `*.tlg`) and several new unit tests under `tests/` (including `test_professionalization_static.py`, `test_stabilization_static.py`, modifications to existing tests in `tests/*_static.py`), and minor test-related changes (support dir and cleanup calls). 
- Docs & config: add multiple authoring and process guides under `docs/` (l3build/CTAN/OVERLEAF/PLUGIN/THEME guides, audit notes) and update configuration files such as `config/project-config.tex` and `config/active-target.tex` to the new canonical keys. 
- Small behavioral/compatibility changes: remove reliance on `\input@path` in the bootstrap (enforced by static tests) and update CTAN upload metadata to be manual-only until uploader contact is finalized.

- Ran the repository static checks via the existing static test harness with `bash scripts/test.sh --static-only`, which completed successfully. 
- Executed the unit test suite with `python -m pytest -q` which ran the updated and newly-added tests under `tests/` (including `test_professionalization_static.py`, `test_stabilization_static.py`, and modified `test_config_static.py` / `test_publication_layer_static.py` / `test_release_metadata_static.py`) and passed.

body:
Reverts the D-lane disable (#245). Safe now because the root cause it guarded against is **fixed in production**:

- **#246** made `cancelVoucher` append a `voucher.cancelled` event (`ensureVoucherCancelEvent`) — so cancelling a voucher no longer leaves a live posting in the journal. Future cancellations stay synced.
- The **reconcile backfill ran** on the founder's society: **2 healed, 0 drifted**. (My "~6 / 168 / ₹51 lakh" estimates were all wrong; the actual drift was 2, found by the reconcile script — investigation beat every guess again.)

With the journal reconciled (0 drifted), `ledgerTrialBalance(journal)` now equals the state-based `getTrialBalance`, so the D-lane's figure should match the Trial Balance page (**₹1,80,60,318.00**).

Re-enables both tools (cash + trial balance) and restores the answer-expecting tests: `test:ask-core` 74/74, `test:tool-trial-balance` 11/11 (bundle route answers again), `test:tool-cash-balance` 18/18, `test:dlane-parity` 21/21, `tsc` clean. `ask-core.mjs` rebuilt.

### ⚠️ Honest caveat — a robustness gap remains

The seam still reads the **raw journal with no parity gate** (unlike the app's `getTrialBalance`, which uses `ledgerParity` and falls back to voucher state). It is correct **only because** the journal is now synced and #246 keeps it synced. If a future code path drifts the journal, the D-lane would over-count silently again. The robust fix — the seam fetches vouchers and runs the same parity gate — is a tracked follow-up.

### 🔴 The real acceptance test (RULE 2)

Do NOT call this done on green tests. After deploy, ask `/ask` **मेरा ट्रायल बैलेंस मिलता है?** and confirm it shows **₹1,80,60,318.00** — the Trial Balance page's own total. If it matches, verified. If not, re-disable and investigate.

Bundle changed → **`npx supabase functions deploy ai-ask`**, not Vercel alone.

author: chayuto
body:
## Why

Dependabot bumps of `@playwright/test` could never merge on their own: the lockstep guard failed the e2e job by design and someone had to push the matching container-tag edit (first hit: #221, `1.59.1 → 1.60.0`).

## What

- New `playwright-version` job in `ci.yml` and `deploy.yml` reads the `@playwright/test` version from `packages/app/package.json` and exposes it as an output.
- The e2e and post-deploy smoke jobs set `container.image` to `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v${{ needs.playwright-version.outputs.version }}-noble` instead of a hardcoded tag.
- `scripts/check-playwright-lockstep.mjs` deleted — with a derived tag there is no mismatch to guard against.
- ADR-0004 amended; CLAUDE.md, copilot-instructions and a change note updated.

## Failure mode

If extraction ever breaks, the tag is malformed and the job fails loudly at image pull — the silent browser-download fallback ADR-0004 protects against cannot occur.

After this lands, #221 only needs a `@dependabot rebase` to go green.

## What changed

- restores a working **Cancel order** action for the current `pending_merchant` order schema
- shows cancellation on both **Orders** and **Track**
- asks for confirmation and cancels through a Firestore transaction

## Root causes

## Cancellation rule

Customers can cancel only while the order is still `pending_merchant` and no rider is assigned. Once the merchant accepts or starts processing, the option disappears.

- `node --check customer-mvp-hardening.js`

author: baronjensen
body:
## What

Ports the desktop app to macOS, closing the "GTK app pending" gap from the platform-support table. macOS now gets the same split-view experience as Linux: dashboard on the left, terminal tabs on the right.

## How

- **`bin/cc-app-mac` (new, ~1000 lines)** — native Cocoa app via PyObjC. `NSSplitView` with a dashboard `WKWebView` (`127.0.0.1:4777`) and a slim custom tab strip of terminal tabs, each a `WKWebView` loading `dash/term.html` (xterm.js) over the shared ttyd instance on `4779`.
- **Zero dashboard JS changes** — WKWebView natively exposes `window.webkit.messageHandlers.centro`, so the existing openInApp / rename / theme bridge in `dash/index.html` works as-is.
- **Full interop with the GTK app's state**: same `app-tabs.json` / `app-tabs-history.json` schema, same `app-{focus,tab-open,tab-close}.json` IPC files (consumed via a 500 ms poll), same `/ensure` + plain-tmux `select-window` open/focus semantics. Native title bar, dark appearance, real `NSMenu` with Cmd shortcuts (the GTK custom chrome is a Linux/WSLg workaround and was intentionally not ported).
- **`bin/cc-app`** — 5-line Darwin dispatch (`os.execv` to sibling `cc-app-mac`) inserted before any `gi` import; Linux path byte-identical.
- **`bin/cc-webterm` fix** — the no-systemd fallback assumed `setsid`, which stock macOS does not ship (only keg-only `util-linux` has it), so terminal tabs were dead out of the box. Now feature-detects `setsid` and falls back to `nohup`; behavior on Linux unchanged.
- **`install.sh` / READMEs** — darwin branch message and platform table updated: native app available via `cc-app`; deps are `pip install pyobjc-framework-Cocoa pyobjc-framework-WebKit` + `brew install ttyd` (not auto-installed). Popups remain pending.

## v1 scope (deliberate)

Deferred for follow-ups, code structured to add them: fuzzy tab switcher, tabs overview, snippets modal, copy/export Claude reply, drag & drop, ligature config. Web Notifications inside WKWebView are not implemented by WebKit, so the dashboard's browser-notification toggle no-ops in-app (macOS notifications still flow via `osascript`/`say` as today).

## Testing

On macOS 26 (Apple Silicon):
- Full suite: **319 passed, 1 skipped** — including the text-match tests pinned to `bin/cc-app` and `bin/cc-webterm`.
- Live end-to-end: app launch via `cc-app` shim → tab open via `app-tab-open.json` IPC → `ESTABLISHED` websocket from the app's WebKit process to ttyd (`lsof`) → `tmux send-keys` output confirmed reaching the app over the socket (`nettop` byte counters) → tab persisted in `app-tabs.json` and restored after app restart.
- `bin/cc-webterm` verified to start ttyd cleanly on a machine with no `setsid` (`/token` → HTTP 200, pidfile alive).
- Query-string preservation through `loadFileURL:allowingReadAccessToURL:` (the risky WebKit detail) was probed directly and confirmed: `arg`/`ws`/`theme` all reach `term.html` from a `file://` origin.

## Summary

Implements the follow-up noted in #137: the .ghx optimization setup dialog previously started from hard-coded defaults every session, so the rhino.compute EXE path, port, and sampler settings had to be re-entered each time. They now persist across app sessions and pre-fill the dialog.

Captured from the dialog when a run starts, applied as defaults the next time a .ghx is opened. Per-file values (study name, journal path, objective directions) stay derived from the dropped file.

author: bucky-local[bot]
body:
## Diagnosis
The `subtract` function in `calculator.py` uses the `+` operator instead of `-`, causing `subtract(7, 4)` to return `11` instead of `3`. This was introduced in PR #1 as a deliberate bug. The test `test_subtracts_two_numbers` correctly asserts that `subtract(7, 4) == 3`, which fails because the implementation adds the operands rather than subtracting them.

## Fix
Change the `subtract` function in `calculator.py` to use the `-` operator instead of `+`, so that `return left + right` becomes `return left - right`.

body:
## The bug

Three audits of the same repo at the same commit (identical `file_count=243`, code unchanged) scored **8.9, 9.9, 9.9** within one hour in prod. Re-auditing the same code returns a different number, which undermines trust in the score.

## Where the instability actually is

I traced the full scoring pipeline. It is **not** the score math and **not** a missing `temperature=0`:

- **The score formula is pure and deterministic** — `app/scan/scoring.py` `_score()` / `compute_scores()`: per-category subscore = `10 − Σ(severity_weight × confidence)`, total = fixed weighted mean. No LLM call, no randomness. Same findings in → same number out (now guarded by a test that shuffles the finding order 100× and asserts a stable result).
- **Temperature is already 0** for both providers — `app/llm/client.py` (anthropic and openai_compat paths both send `temperature: 0`).
- **Root cause: the LLM scan is non-deterministic even at `temperature=0`.** This is documented in `app/scan/llm_scan.py` (`run_llm_scan`): critical findings reproduce ~100%, but `high`-severity ones only ~50–70% by coordinates run to run. A different findings *set* feeds the deterministic formula, producing a different score. The variance is in the **input to** the score, not the score computation.

Because the number is a faithful function of the findings, the fix is to stop producing a *new* findings set for content we've already audited.

## The fix — content-hash caching

- `app/scan/pipeline.py` `content_digest()`: canonical SHA-256 over sorted `(path, per-file-sha256)` of the archive. Stable across zip packaging (member order, compression, timestamps); sensitive to any file-content change.
- `migrations/0008_audits_content_hash.sql`: adds `audits.content_hash` + index.
- `app/db.py`: `AuditRepository.create(...)` persists `content_hash`; new `get_by_content_hash()` returns the most recent completed audit for that digest (None when DB not configured).
- `app/main.py` `create_audit`: before scanning, look up the digest — on a hit, return the stored audit verbatim (`reused: true`) instead of re-running the non-deterministic scan.

I deliberately did **not** strip the LLM out of the score. The LLM findings are real signal; the score correctly reflects them. Removing them to chase a stable number would be a large product regression, not a fix. Caching pins the result while keeping the LLM's value.

## Tests

- `tests/test_checks_scoring.py::test_score_is_deterministic_regardless_of_finding_order` — the core invariant: same findings → same score, order-independent (100 shuffles).
- `tests/test_audit_determinism.py` (new):
  - `content_digest` stable across repackaging; changes when a file changes.
  - `test_identical_content_returns_identical_score_via_cache` — posts a byte-identical zip twice with a **scripted LLM that returns different findings on the second call**; asserts the second response is `reused`, same `audit_id`/`score`/`findings`, and only one row persisted. Proves the cache (not luck) pins the result.
  - `test_different_content_is_not_served_from_cache` — different content bypasses the cache.

`350 passed` locally.

## Test plan
- [ ] `python -m pytest -q` green
- [ ] Apply migration `0008` before deploy
- [ ] Verify a repeat audit of an unchanged repo returns `reused: true` with an identical score

## 🚀 Overview

This PR integrates an LLM-powered explanation pipeline into the MONCO backend using Ollama.

The backend now generates patient-friendly explanations for brain MRI classification results while maintaining a clean, modular architecture.

---

## ✨ Features Added

- Integrated Ollama with the FastAPI backend
- Added prompt engineering for structured medical explanations
- Implemented LLMService for communication with Ollama
- Added PredictionService to orchestrate the prediction pipeline

- Improved backend architecture using a service-oriented design

```
Client
   │
   ▼
FastAPI Route

   ▼
PredictionService

            AI-generated Explanation
```

author: luke20001024
body:
## What changed

- makes cached records visible before background directory traversal and point-reads today outside the history lock
- sorts newest records first and updates today without rebuilding the whole dashboard
- lazy-loads nearby daily photos, generates bounded WebP thumbnails, and reuses them across tabs
- makes archive metadata cache-first, progressively hydrates titles, and reuses same-tab state
- adds v0.8.8 documentation, installation guidance, design contracts, and regression coverage

## Why

The previous implementation placed optional full-cycle scans, image reads, and archive title reads on visible interaction paths. A single slow Chrome File System Access request could therefore make a small local dataset feel blocked even when usable cached content already existed.

The new boundary is experience-first: render trusted existing content immediately, read only the smallest freshness-critical item on the foreground path, and perform bounded optional work progressively in the background.

## Impact

- warm tabs show existing records immediately
- new today entries appear without waiting for historical traversal
- daily-summary text appears before photos, with photos loaded near the viewport
- archive reopen is zero-scan in the same tab; new tabs use metadata-only cache
- directory identity, permission, complete-only cache, and mutation safety remain enforced

## Validation

- all Node regression suites
- capture lifecycle, daily snapshot, Daily Review recovery, photo drawer, record dashboard, and installation contract suites
- `git diff --check`
- v0.8.8 release ZIP full extraction and SHA-256 verification

author: samchon
body:
## Issue

Closes #2195.

`typia.json.application<T>()` silently **dropped** any function property that was optional, nullable, or a union-of-functions. The three diagnostics written for exactly those shapes never ran.

```ts
interface App {
  good(): number;
  bad?(): number; // silently omitted from `functions`, no error
}
typia.json.application<App>(); // -> functions: ["good"]
```

## Root cause

In `JsonApplicationProgrammer.Validate` the per-function `union / required / nullable` checks were wrapped in `if valid == false`. `valid` is computed from the **top** metadata alone (is the application itself a single required non-nullable object). For a normal, otherwise-valid application `valid == true`, so those three checks were **dead code**. `WriteApplication` then silently `continue`d over any property that was not a sole-literal, single, required, non-nullable, single function — so the malformed member vanished with no diagnostic.

## Fix

Remove the inner `if valid == false` gate so the per-function shape checks run for **every** function property, independent of the top-level `valid`. A malformed function property now fails validation with a clear message instead of being silently dropped. The top-level "must be a class/interface type" gate is untouched. The now-unreachable silent `continue` in `WriteApplication` is left as defense in depth.

### Sibling: `LlmApplicationProgrammer`

`LlmApplicationProgrammer.Validate` carried the byte-identical `if isValidType == false` gate. It was **reproduced** (via `test-error` probes) to silently drop a malformed function property with no diagnostic too, so the same unwrap is applied there.

## Tests

Six new `tests/test-error` fixtures (optional / nullable / union-of-functions, for both `json.application` and `llm.application`). Each produced **no** diagnostic before the fix (silent drop, red) and now asserts its exact message.

- `test-error`: green — 72 files, 867 typia diagnostics (all 6 new fixtures named)
- native Go `json` + `llm` programmer/transformer tests: pass
- `test-typia-schema` (171 cases) and `test-mcp` (20 cases): pass — no valid application regressed

No version bump. No `@typia/interface` shape edits.

## What

A professional UX pass across desktop and iPhone, keeping the brand (teal / navy / Barlow). Replaces the flat, 0-radius / hard-border look with a real **elevation + radius + type system**, and collapses the app-action cluster behind a **hamburger** on small screens.

## Design system (`ui-tokens/tokens.css`)
- Navy **elevation ramp** (`navy-500…900`), **hairline** borders + soft **shadows** (`shadow-sm/md/lg`).
- **Radius** scale (`sm/md/lg/pill`), **type** scale (`text-xs…xl`), **control-height** tokens (32 px / 44 px touch), teal-bright accent + focus ring, transitions.
- All colours stay token-only (stylelint `no-hardcoded-color`); the 2D-canvas geometry overlay colours are untouched.

## Surfaces & controls
- Every floating panel — sketch toolbar, timeline, browser tree, numeric HUD, dialogs, help, onboarding, plane picker, New Project, measure — becomes a rounded, shadowed, hairline-bordered navy surface with real depth. The header is an elevated app-bar.
- One button language: rounded, raised, hover = teal border, active/primary = filled teal on cream, `:active` press, comfortable min-height, and a single `:focus-visible` ring in `global.css`.

## Mobile hamburger
- ≤700px: the app actions (New Sketch, Measure, New Project, Save, Open, Export STL, Shortcuts) collapse into a dropdown toggled by a hamburger (`app-menu-toggle`); controls grow to 44 px touch targets; the sketch tool row stays a scroller. Desktop keeps the inline corner-anchored layout (hamburger hidden).

## Perf
Solid raised surfaces + `box-shadow`, **not** `backdrop-filter` blur, to hold the 100-body ≥30 fps floor (blur over the WebGL canvas is costly on mobile).

## Docs
ADR-0044, MASTER_DOCUMENT §12, README.

## Tests
- `mobile-menu.spec`: hamburger collapsed by default, opens on tap, every action reachable, closes on choose; hidden inline on desktop.
- `responsive.spec` updated for the hamburger; still asserts zero horizontal page overflow in both modes.
- Verified with desktop (1280) + iPhone-12 (390×844) screenshots.

body:
## 问题

北邮人 (byr.pt) 等站点将登录页改为前端框架渲染的 SPA 后，站点卡片「更新 Cookie&UA」始终失败，报错依次为：

1. **未找到用户名输入框**：SPA 登录页的用户名输入框无 `name`/`id` 属性（仅有 placeholder），现有候选 XPATH 均无法匹配；且 `domcontentloaded` 时表单可能尚未渲染。
2. **登录失败**（误报）：登录 API 成功后，前端脚本延迟 1 秒才执行 `window.location.href` 跳转。而现有逻辑在 `networkidle` 后立即抓取页面判定登录态——此时页面仍停留在 /login（含密码输入框），`is_logged_in` 误判为未登录。实际上此刻 Cookie 已写入浏览器上下文。

## 修改

- `_SITE_LOGIN_XPATH["username"]` 末尾追加 `//input[contains(@placeholder,"用户名")]`（置于末位，经典站点仍优先按 name/id 匹配，无回归影响）
- 首次未找到用户名输入框时，`wait_for_selector("input", 5s)` 等待渲染后重取源码重试一次（仅失败路径触发）
- 登录成功判定改为最多 3 次、间隔 2 秒的重试，覆盖前端延迟跳转窗口（首次判定不等待，经典站点无额外延迟）

## 测试

- 北邮人 (byr.pt) 实测：修改前两处报错均复现；修改后「更新 Cookie&UA」成功，Cookie（auth_token/refresh_token/session_id 三件套）正确写入，站点连通性、用户数据解析、索引搜索均正常
- 假凭据提交实测：客户端表单校验与服务端错误响应路径不受影响
- 经典 NexusPHP 站点路径不受影响（新增 XPATH 在候选末位、重试仅在原失败路径触发）

Each handled action (create/update/delete/photo/voice) logs one run; a 15-min **unref'd** heartbeat refreshes `status.json` so an idle-but-alive bot reads healthy (cadence semantics differ from cron agents, per the ticket).

`runLog.ts` writes `agents/telegram-bot/{runs.jsonl,status.json}` via the bot's **existing** `vaultTransport` — no new git plumbing. `router.ts` gains one **optional** `onAction` callback fired after a successful action (never on `not yet supported`); every pre-S51 caller omits it and is unaffected. `index.ts` subscribes it + starts the heartbeat.

**DoD evidence** (vs `docs/slices/slice-S51-bot-run-logging.md`):

1. Handled create writes one `runs.jsonl` line + refreshed `status.json`; note carries the action — `runLog.test.ts`
2. Heartbeat writes `status.json` only; logging failures swallowed + `console.warn`, never break handling — `runLog.test.ts` (never-throws + heartbeat cases); `emitAction()` also guards a synchronous throw
3. `status.json` cross-parses through the PWA's real `agentStatus.ts` (`parseStatus` + `healthOf`) — `runLog.test.ts`
4. All existing bot tests pass unmodified — **147/147 green** (141 prior + 6 new)
5. Diff confined to `services/bot/`; tests green
