author: justapig9020
body:
## Summary
Add `qemu_cortex_a53_aarch32` as a verification platform for the Armv8-A AArch32 architecture.

The board starts at AArch64 EL3, uses a minimal boot shim to transition
to AArch32, and runs Zephyr at Non-secure EL1 in AArch32 Supervisor (SVC) mode.

This PR focuses on uniprocessor support only. SMP support will be added
in a follow-up PR.

## Motivation
A reproducible Armv8-A AArch32 platform is needed to develop and verify the SMP support proposed in #105804.

## Changes
Add Cortex-A53 AArch32 support at the CPU, SoC, and board levels, including:
- the `CPU_CORTEX_A53_AARCH32` CPU option and its compiler mapping;
- the `qemu_cortex_a53_aarch32` SoC and devicetree description;
- MMU regions for the QEMU virt platform;
- the `qemu_cortex_a53_aarch32` board configuration; and
- a minimal AArch64 EL3 boot shim.

With the QEMU virt machine the primary Cortex-A53 starts at AArch64 EL3. The boot shim prepares the required EL3, timer, and GIC state, configures the lower Exception Level to use AArch32, and enters Zephyr at Non-secure EL1 in SVC mode.

The shim is integrated into the board build. It is built with the AArch64 Zephyr SDK toolchain as a post-build step and passed to QEMU through `-bios`, while the Zephyr binary is loaded separately at its configured entry address. As a result, the board can be built and run directly using the standard `west` commands.

## Testing

The following test suites were run on `qemu_cortex_a53_aarch32`:
- `tests/kernel/timer`
- `tests/kernel/sched`
- `tests/kernel/threads`
- `tests/arch/common`

```shell
west twister -p qemu_cortex_a53_aarch32 \
  -T tests/kernel/timer \
  -T tests/kernel/sched \
  -T tests/kernel/threads \
  -T tests/arch/common
```

Results:
- 35 executed test configurations passed
- 1 configuration was build-only
- 349 of 349 executed test cases passed
- 0 failures, and 0 errors

## Related work
Depends on #113783.
This is part of the Armv8-A AArch32 SMP work proposed in #105804.

author: dgageot
body:
When a terminal reports a degenerate size (0×0 or 1×1), the resize handle in `pkg/tui/tui.go` computed a negative repeat count for `strings.Repeat`, crashing the TUI with `panic: strings: negative Repeat count`. The existing `width <= 0` guard did not account for the horizontal padding subtracted afterwards, so any width narrower than `appPaddingHorizontal` slipped through and produced a negative inner width.

The fix adds a guard on the padded inner width itself. A follow-up commit also handles the status suffix: `lipgloss` ignores non-positive `MaxWidth`, so a paused/working suffix wider than the terminal could overflow the row on very narrow terminals. The suffix logic is extracted into a `lineWithSuffix` helper that truncates the suffix when the terminal is too narrow to accommodate it.

Both fixes are covered by a unit test over tiny widths (`pkg/tui/tui_resize_handle_test.go`), a full-TUI e2e resize cycle through degenerate sizes (`e2e/tui/degenerate_resize_test.go`), and a board-TUI render sweep across degenerate sizes × all dialogs (`pkg/board/tui/degenerate_size_test.go`). All three tests were verified to panic on main without the fix.

author: lklyne
body:
## Summary

Four items from PR 4a (HTML iframe fixes), in priority order:

**1. Live-update watcher fix.** `fs.watch` on the file itself silently stops reporting changes once an editor/agent does an atomic save (write-temp-then-rename replaces the watched inode). Fixed by watching the parent directory and filtering events by filename — the directory's inode survives renames inside it, so no re-arming logic is needed. The existing `fileReloadVersion` → cache-busting `?v=` query param → iframe `key` remount plumbing was already correct; only the watcher itself was broken.

**2. Refresh button.** Added a "Refresh" item to the html file entity's right-click context menu (`src/renderer/above-view/FileBodyLayer.tsx`) that force-reloads the iframe via a new `refreshFileEntity` IPC action, independent of the watcher.

**3. Border on html file entities.** Root cause: `fileKind.update()` (`src/main/entities/builtin/file.ts`) only wired `file`/`subpath`/`objectFit`/`width`/`height`/`canvasX`/`canvasY` — a `showDeviceFrame`/`presetIndex`/`orientation` patch on a file entity was silently dropped on the headless mutation path (CLI `specular update`, MCP `upsert_entities`, `POST /canvas/apply`), even though the exact same field already works for pages and the human-facing inspector's "Show device page" checkbox (which calls the IPC path directly, bypassing the registry). Wired the same mutators `pageKind.update()` already uses, and added the missing `--device-frame` CLI flag (only `--no-device-frame` existed before).

**4. Agent-editing indicator — done, lightweight.** The watcher fix made this nearly free: `HtmlInlineRenderer` now shows a brief pulse (900ms fade, inset ring) whenever the entity's reload version advances, whether from a disk change or a manual refresh. No presence infrastructure, no new state — just a one-shot CSS keyframe keyed off a value the renderer already receives.

## Manual test steps

1. Create an html file and add it to the canvas: `specular add file /path/to/test.html --at 100,100`.
2. With an editor or agent, edit the file **using an atomic save** (most editors default to this — write-temp-then-rename). Verify the canvas iframe refreshes automatically within ~1s, with a brief blue pulse around the entity.
3. Right-click the html entity → click "Refresh". Verify the iframe reloads (and the pulse fires) even without an on-disk change.
4. Toggle the border: `specular update <fileId> --device-frame` — verify a device-frame border appears around the html entity on canvas. Then `specular update <fileId> --no-device-frame` to confirm it can be removed again. (The inspector's "Show device page" checkbox under the file's device section does the same thing and already worked pre-fix.)
5. Delete the html entity and confirm no `FSWatcher` leak / no crash on a subsequent disk write to the now-orphaned path.

## Test results

- `pnpm typecheck` — pass
- `pnpm test:unit` — 1027/1027 pass
- `pnpm test:integration` — 199/199 pass (includes a new atomic-save regression test in `tests/integration/file-watcher.test.ts`, mutation-verified against the old file-watch behavior, and a new `tests/integration/file-entity-device-frame.test.ts` covering the border patch path, mutation-verified)

author: sedlardavid
body:
## What

- **Drop the unused ~37 MB local CanvasKit dir from deploys.** The app loads CanvasKit from Google's gstatic CDN at runtime (`buildConfig` sets `engineRevision`, does not set `useLocalCanvasKit`), where it's already brotli-compressed (~2.3 MB). The local `build/web/canvaskit/` is an offline fallback the app never fetches and the service worker never precaches.
  - Add `scripts/deploy.sh` — builds, strips `canvaskit/` (**42 MB → 4.9 MB upload**), deploys via SWA CLI.
  - Verified the app still renders with the dir stripped (canvaskit served from CDN).
- **Trim `staticwebapp.config.json`** — remove the now-dead `/canvaskit/*` route and the `.wasm` MIME map (SWA doesn't brotli `application/wasm` anyway).
- **Remove internal working docs** from the public repo (`docs/plan/`, `docs/seo/` audit + action plan) and gitignore those paths.
- **README** caching notes updated to match.

## Why it matters

Corrects an earlier assumption: the SEO audit's "10.6 MB payload" overcounted by including the unused local wasm. Real initial payload ≈ `main.dart.js` (985 KB br) + CDN canvaskit (2.3 MB br) ≈ **3.3 MB**. The "wasm brotli didn't work" follow-up is moot — the wasm on the critical path comes compressed from the CDN.

## Note

To self-host CanvasKit instead (privacy / true offline): set `useLocalCanvasKit: true`, remove the strip step in `scripts/deploy.sh`, and pre-compress `canvaskit.wasm` → `.wasm.br`.

author: 0xgosu
body:
Fixes #175.

## Problem

A single LLM-answered `@noop` on an idle signature (reasonable in the moment — the declared task source had just run dry):

1. **Parked the refill feature forever** — idle resolution honored the learned-noop plurality BEFORE declared-source resolution, and the plurality was source-blind, so `task_source_exhausted` → generation (`llm.task_generate_command`) was never reached again. The agent produced `[shadow_mode]` "do nothing" escalations indefinitely.
2. **Was CLI-unreachable** — no `signatures` state row was created, so `hap signatures list` omitted the rule and `signatures delete/reset` failed with `no signature matches`.
3. **Hid its provenance** — escalations showed `rule=[none yet]` while the decision-table plurality actually drove the suggestion.

## Fix

- **`internal/domain`**: `ConfidenceResult.TopActionOperatorBacked` — true when an operator- or rule-sourced decision backs the top action (a `SourceRule` row implies past operator confirmation). The idle noop precedence now requires `TopActionOperatorBacked || DeclaredTask == nil`:
  - operator-taught noops still outrank declared tasks (unchanged behavior, now provenance-scoped);
  - a pure-LLM noop yields to a pending declared task, and to `task_source_exhausted` → `ActionGenerateTask` (the #175 repro);
  - with no declared source an LLM noop still silences a chatty idle agent (the original nudge-loop case);
  - approval/choice/error noop handling is untouched.
- **`internal/daemon`**: new atomic `Store.EnsureSignature` (single `INSERT OR IGNORE`, never touches an existing row) called after all four LLM `RecordDecision` sites (noop promotion, action send, multi-tab series, remote-env picker), so every LLM-learned rule is listable/deletable/resettable. Companion: `applyCorrection`'s clean-slate `DecisionFloorID` stamp is re-keyed from "no state row" to "no operator/rule evidence in the pre-existing history" (`domain.HasOperatorEvidence`), preserving the guarantee that the first operator correction floors out prior LLM guesses now that a row exists by then.
- **`internal/store`**: idempotent `migrate()` backfill creates shadow rows for decisions-only signatures in existing databases (type fields from each signature's newest decision by id).
- **Display**: no code change needed — with the row present, escalations render the real rule summary (`rule=[shadow — 0/N confirmations, … top action "@noop" …]`); `rule=[none yet]` remains only for truly-unseen signatures.

## Testing

- New/updated unit tests across `internal/domain` (provenance matrix, the #175 repro, exhausted-without-generation escalation, nudge-loop preservation, non-idle noop unchanged), `internal/daemon` (row creation on the noop/send/series/picker paths; first-operator-correction flooring with a pre-existing LLM-created row), `internal/store` (`EnsureSignature` contract, migration backfill end-to-end incl. delete + re-migrate), `internal/cli` (LLM-learned signature list/reset/delete + escalation rule rendering).
- Full suite `go test -tags "vectors cpu" ./... -count=1` green; `go vet` and `golangci-lint run --build-tags "vectors,cpu"` clean.

author: suchethac
body:
## Summary

Three defects on `docs/api/predicting-properties.md`, the prediction API reference. Each
was verified by **running** the snippet, not reading it.

### 1. The spectrum example raised — and contradicted the page

```python
obs_wave = obs_wave_rest * (1 + model.redshift)   # AttributeError: no .redshift
```

`SEDModel` has no `.redshift` attribute. Worse, **line 195 of this same page** says:

> **The SED array does not carry its axis.** … Never reconstruct the observed axis by hand
> as `wave * (1 + params["redshift"])`.

…and line 226 did exactly that, twenty lines later. `wave_obs` is *already* observer-frame,
so the example now passes the grid you actually observed on, and the page stops arguing
with itself.

### 2. "configurable via `model.approx`" — right noun, wrong verb

`model.approx` **now exists** (added in #1237, after #1214 was filed — the doc was
prescient). But it is **read-only**: assigning to it raises `AttributeError`. Configuration
happens at build via `approx=`, or through `with_approx()` which returns a clone. Now says
how to set it *and* how to read it back.

### 3. Title and example disagreed — and both were right

The section titled itself *"KeyError on unknown properties"* while its example caught
`AttributeError`. Measured:

| Access style | Raises |
|---|---|
| `pred.nonexistent_property` (attribute sugar) | `AttributeError` |
| `pred.properties["nonexistent"]` (catalog) | `KeyError` |

So the doc wasn't wrong about either exception — it paired the wrong title with the wrong
example. It now shows both, and leads with the property that actually matters: **unknown
properties raise, never return `NaN`**.

## Verification

- All four constructs executed against a real spectroscopic model (the fixed spectrum
  snippet returns a spectrum; both error styles raise as documented; `model.approx` reads
  back `ApproxState(exact)`).
- All 13 python blocks on the page parse under `ast.parse`.
- Full lint suite green — all 8 gates, not just ruff.

Item 1 of #1214 (`predict_photometry(filters=...)`) was already fixed by #1218; line 37 now
correctly reads `model.predict_photometry(params)`.

Closes #1214

author: djben
body: ## Summary Solar Orbit Origin Configurations and Presets A batch of planning-workflow upgrades for the launch windows panel: one-click destination presets from the game's own body groups, a new Return-trip section, per-window fuel estimates, configurable section visibility with on-demand computation, and a smarter alarm system. ## Features ### Presets & list management - **Presets ▼ dropdown** (replaces the My Bases button): *My Bases* plus one entry per in-game celestial body group (`ObjectInfoGroups` — Near-Earth Objects, Inner/Middle/Outer Belt, Jupiter Trojans, Kuiper Belt, …), labeled with the game's localized names and listed sunward-out. Built dynamically at open time, so it tracks whatever groups the scene has. - **Clear** button removes all destinations at once. - Destroyed bodies (`ObjectInfo.IsInGameDestroy`) are hidden from presets, search, and origins, and auto-removed from the table. - **Solar Orbit** is a selectable origin: the game models it virtually (pinned to the Sun, conventional 0.01 AU), so the mod synthesizes a circular 0.01 AU heliocentric orbit in Earth's orbital plane for the transfer math. ### Table - Columns per section: **Departs | Arrives | Δv | Fuel (E/F)**, dates in `yy/MM/dd`. Every column header is a sort toggle. - **Fuel (E/F)**: propellant estimate per window via the rocket equation, as Empty/Full-cargo load (`23.8/31.2t`, ≥1000t as `kt`). Uses `SpacecraftType.GetExhaustV(player)`, which already applies the company's researched exhaust-velocity bonuses, so the figure always reflects the current engine variant. Figures exceeding the craft's tank capacity render red. - **Return section** (shown by default, in place of Fastest): the first optimal window from the destination back to the origin departing after arrival, with the same columns and its own next-window row. ### Options ▼ (persisted in BepInEx config) - *Show Δv column* (default off), *Show Fastest* (default off), *Show Return trip* (default on), *Show next transfer window* (default off). - Hidden data is **computed on demand**: the next-synodic and return-trip Lambert searches are skipped entirely while hidden (the defaults roughly halve refresh cost) and are backfilled automatically when re-enabled, reusing the cached outbound windows. The panel resizes to the visible sections. - *Alert [N] day(s) before*: editable lead time for alarms (default 0). ### Alarms - Notify checkboxes on every window — Optimal, Fastest, and Return (return notifications read dest → origin). - Alarms are day-precise and fire N days before departure; the message is `Launch Window (Optimal) 26/11/12` style. Old sidecar alarms keep firing under the legacy month rule — the sidecar format is backward compatible. ### UI - Whole UI enlarged ~1.5×; table numerals use Orbitron (the game ships no monospace font; a `*Mono*` font is auto-preferred if one ever appears); mouse-wheel scrolling works anywhere over the list; per-row delete moved to the trailing edge. ## Testing - `dotnet test src/tests` — 48/48 pass, including new coverage for the day-precise/lead-time alarm firing rules. - Game-API claims (body groups, destroyed flag, exhaust-velocity research bonuses, Solar Orbit convention) verified against the decompiled game code and exercised in-game. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: sachiniyer
body:
Closes #2036.

Two high-severity `go/allocation-size-overflow` alerts have been open on
the security tab since #2033, both on `ghostTmuxNames`:

    names := make([]string, 0, len(data.Tabs)+1)
    seen  := make(map[string]struct{}, len(data.Tabs)+1)

Both are FALSE POSITIVES. `data.Tabs` is a persisted session's tab list —
an agent tab plus a handful of shell/process/web tabs — so overflowing
`len+1` would need ~2^63 tabs, which cannot exist.

Fixed the way #1988 fixed the identical false positive on shellsuggest's
`make([]string, 0, len(args)+1)`: restructure so there is no allocation-size
arithmetic left to flag, rather than blanket-dismissing the rule. A
dismissal would bury a future REAL alert of the same class; this does not.

The `+1` was slack anyway. On any post-#953 record the legacy name is
already one of the tabs, so the exact cap is `len(data.Tabs)`. The one
input that can exceed it — a pre-#953 record, which has no Tabs at all —
grows the slice once, for a single string, on a path that runs once per
ghost record during cleanup.

Behaviour is unchanged by construction: same names, same order, same
dedupe, for every input.

## Verification

`ghostTmuxNames` had no direct test, so this adds
`TestGhostTmuxNames_OrderDedupeAndEmptySkip` over the contract ghostCleanup
depends on — legacy name first, persisted order, deduped, empty names
skipped.

To be explicit about what that test is and is not: it is a regression
guard, NOT a fail-first repro. The change is behaviour-neutral, so no test
can fail on the old code — the failing signal here is the CodeQL alert
itself (alerts #20 and #21, both open at the time of writing). The test
was checked for teeth by mutation instead: removing the dedupe, dropping
the legacy name, and removing the empty-name skip each turn it red.

`TestGhostCleanup_KillsEveryTabTmux` already covered this function end to
end against a real tmux server, but it asserts the outcome (every tab's
session is dead), which is order- and dedupe-blind.

## Adjacent sites

Audited every `make(..., len(x)+N)` in the tree. Three others exist —
`session/tmux/clientless.go:93`, `ui/task_pane.go:226`,
`app/home_model.go:561` — and CodeQL flags none of them; the open alert
list is exactly these two lines. Left them alone rather than churn
unflagged code: `clientless.go`'s `+4` is an exact arg-count pre-size that
would lose meaning if trimmed.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Closes #2027.

The 12h grace window for an external PR with an unanswered change request
was enforced against `hoursBetween(...)`, which rounds to tenths of an
hour:

    const ageHours = hoursBetween(reviewMs, nowMs);
    if (ageHours < STALE_HOURS) { ... }

A change request aged [11.95h, 12h) rounds to 12.0, which is not < 12, so
the PR was closed up to ~3 minutes before its grace window was actually
up. Immaterial in effect — it can never pick a wrong target, only clip the
tail of a window — but the threshold we publish should be the threshold we
enforce.

The decision now compares exact milliseconds. `hoursBetween` stays, for
the log and reason lines only.

It also now truncates rather than rounds, because rounding made the grace
message argue with itself: at 11h57m it read "only 12h old (< 12h grace)",
quoting an age that is not less than the threshold it was granting grace
against. Truncation makes the reported number a lower bound on the real
age, so a message granting grace can never quote an age at or past the
threshold. The three call sites are all descriptive, and none can see a
negative duration (contributor responses are filtered to strictly after
the review; `nowMs` is always later).

## Verification

Watched the new tests fail on the old code and pass on the new (the JS
tests run in pr.yml's Lint job, so they gate):

  - 11h57m → KEEP — fails on old code, which closes it. This is the
    reported bug.
  - the grace message never reports an age >= the threshold — fails on old
    code at 11h57m / 11.99h / 11.999h.
  - 12h01m → CLOSE — passes both ways. Not a repro; it pins that the exact
    comparison did not drift the window the other way.

The existing boundary test (exactly 12h → CLOSE, inclusive) still passes,
so the fix moved the tail of the window without moving the boundary
itself. Full file: 24 tests, all green.

## Summary

- parse ISO-8601 forecast timestamps that include fractional seconds
- preserve support for timestamps without fractional seconds
- add a regression test using the live forecast API timestamp format

## Root cause

The public forecast endpoint returns timestamps such as `2026-07-18T07:32:08.628Z`. The default JSON decoder ISO-8601 strategy rejected those fractional seconds, so the forecast reader returned no value and the probability row stayed hidden.

## User impact

QuotaPeek can display the Codex reset probability again when the forecast endpoint returns its current timestamp format.

- `make verify`
- 10 tests passed
- universal app verified for `arm64` and `x86_64`

author: samoswald270800-spec
body:
## The bug

On the candidate profile, the **Permissions** card showed a single **"Turbo engine"** row bound to `canTurbo` and **omitted Reasoning entirely**. For a user whose admin locked **Reasoning** (`canReasoning = false`) while Turbo stayed enabled, the card couldn't show the real lock — it only ever talked about Turbo, so the locked feature was mislabeled/hidden (e.g. user 1234: "profile says Turbo, but Reasoning is the locked one").

## The fix

`Reasoning` (`canReasoning`) and `Turbo` (`canTurbo`) are **two distinct engine permissions**. The profile now shows them as **separate rows**, each bound to its own key, using the **same names as the rest of the app** — `AdminDashboard`, `SettingsPopover`, and `SuperAdminDashboard` already label these `Reasoning` / `Turbo`.

```
Expand answers   — canExpand
Screen analysis  — canAnalyze
Reasoning        — canReasoning   ← added (was missing)
Turbo            — canTurbo       ← was mislabeled "Turbo engine"
```

## Scope of the naming audit

I checked every place these features are named to make sure the fix is consistent "everywhere":

| Surface | Mapping | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `AdminDashboard` | `canReasoning`→Reasoning, `canTurbo`→Turbo | already correct |
| `SuperAdminDashboard` | same | already correct |
| `SettingsPopover` | same | already correct |
| backend `interview.js` enforcement + error text | keyed off `canTurbo` / `canReasoning`, message uses the live `architecture` name | already correct |
| **`ProfilePage`** | collapsed both into one `canTurbo` "Turbo engine" row | **fixed here** |

The profile was the only mismatch — no other surface needed changes.

## Verification

Headless Chromium against the built app, modeling user 1234 (`canReasoning=false`, `canTurbo=true`) — **36/36 checks, 0 runtime errors**:
- Permissions card now renders 4 rows;
- **Reasoning → Locked** (the real lock);
- **Turbo → Enabled** (no longer mislabeled as locked);
- assertion that no Turbo row reads "Locked" while Turbo is on.

`vite build` passes.

## Summary

Part of the notification-system PRD (`docs/prd-notifications.md` §11, issue 4 of 6). Adds the "Notifications" panel from PRD §4: a standard `PANEL_REGISTRY` entry that renders the session's fired-alert log (issue #218's `FiredAlertStore`) so a missed banner/ping can be reviewed later.

- New `notifications` entry in `PANEL_REGISTRY` (sm 220×150 / md 300×240 / lg 380×320) rendering the store's session log newest-first: timestamp, payload icon (`ItemSprite` when set), title/body, and the matched catalog kind ids (hidden at `sm`). Empty state uses the existing `EmptyState`.
- Added to `defaultLayout()`; existing users get it on upgrade via `mergeWithDefaults` — covered by `test/panelCanvas-notifications.test.ts`. `mergeWithDefaults`/`defaultLayout`/`isPersistablePanel` moved out of `PanelCanvas.tsx` into a new `panels/panelLayout.ts` (a component file can't also export plain functions under `react-refresh/only-export-components` — same reason `dps/dpsDetailContext.ts` is split from its provider).
- New `alerts/alertStoreContext.ts` (`AlertStoreContext`/`useAlertStore()`) exposes the App-level `AlertEngine.store` to `NotificationsPanel`, which is mounted by registry lookup deep under `PanelCanvas` with no direct parent/child relationship to `App.tsx`. `App.tsx` provides it around `AppShell` using the same store instance already passed to `AlertToastHost`.
- The panel imports only the store contract (`FiredAlertStore`/`FiredAlert`) + existing UI primitives (`ItemSprite`, `EmptyState`) — no `AlertEngine`/`catalog`/`dispatcher` internals, no packet types (PRD §1 layering contract).
- Persistence-across-map-change / clear-on-detach are store semantics (already covered by `alerts-store.test.ts`); `test/notificationsPanel.test.ts` asserts them through the identical `getAll`/`subscribe`/`reset` calls the panel's own data-source effect makes.
- Panel gallery shots regenerated (picked up automatically by `npm run shots`'s per-`PANEL_REGISTRY`-entry loop): `harness/PanelMount.tsx` now seeds a `FiredAlertStore` for `type === 'notifications'` via the same `alertGallerySeed.ts` the toast-host gallery uses (extracted from `AlertToastGalleryMount.tsx` so both share one seed). `docs/notifications.md` and `docs/overlay-renderer.md` (+ `docs/overlay-harness.md`) updated.

- The settings gear on this panel (issue 5 of the plan, #221).
- Filtering/search/grouping in the list.

author: sauldhernandez
body:
## Intent

Add the first identity-instance mutation on top of the reviewed identity metadata, encrypted-document, manifest-fingerprint, and exact-spec crypto layers. User-owned fixed-token identities must be persisted without reintroducing surface-level identity semantics or allowing metadata and secret material to diverge.

## What it enables

- Creates or replaces a user-owned fixed-token identity from one exact global identity spec.
- Parses the stored spec, requires `fixed_token`, and records its semantic manifest fingerprint, issuer, and exact global key.
- Encrypts the trimmed `TOKEN` value outside the database transaction using owner, identity name, and exact spec revision as authenticated context.
- Revalidates the complete spec record in a serializable transaction, then atomically upserts identity metadata and encrypted material. A spec drift or retryable conflict causes a fresh selection and fresh encryption.
- Shares the same success, failure, replacement, key-rotation, and rollback contract across SQLite and Postgres.

## Usage examples

This is an internal manager layer; transport wiring lands later in the stack. Its intended call shape is:

```rust
let identity = IdentityManager::new(db, key_provider)
    .create_or_replace_user_fixed_token(
        &principal,
        "github_personal",
        "github",
        token,
    )
    .await?;
```

The `github` spec lookup is exact-global for a user identity. The returned record contains only safe metadata; the token is stored only in the encrypted identity document.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p coral-app state::db::repositories::identities_contract_tests::identity_repository_contract_holds_against_sqlite --lib -- --exact --nocapture`
- `make postgres-tests`
- `make rust-checks` (1,972 passed, 7 skipped; rustdoc passed)
- 572 changed lines (543 additions, 29 deletions)

author: jenarvaezg
body:
Slice **S1** of PRD #1103 (CRUD de holdings manuales vía asistente). The domain core of the reconcile — a pure, I/O-free module that decides, per candidate row, whether to create a new holding, update an existing one, or leave it alone.

## What

`packages/domain/src/holding-matcher.ts` — `matchHoldings(rows, holdings) → RowMatch[]`, given candidate rows (extracted from a document or typed) and the current portfolio:

- **Strong key — ISIN / provider symbol**: an exact hit resolves the row on its own at `strong` confidence. Generalizes the ISIN `matched`/`new` bucketing of `propose_statement_import` (`statement-import-plan.ts`), keeping its `ISIN_SHAPE` rule and the #695 lowercase provider-symbol index (so `Bitcoin` finds `bitcoin`).
- **Weak key — name + instrument**: proposes the best candidate at `weak` confidence, never imposes. Matching is exact normalized-name equality (NFD diacritic fold + whitespace collapse), never fuzzy/substring, and requires a compatible instrument — so a coincidental name can never silently rewrite the wrong holding.
- **No key → `create`.**
- **Per-row output**: `{ decision, target?, candidates, confidence, key, possibleDuplicate? }` — enough to paint the preview and tell the apply where to write.
- **Reassignment API** (pure, immutable): `reassignToNew` (match → new), `reassignToCandidate` (new → match / retarget; throws on a non-candidate so a typo can't target an unrelated holding), `discardRow`. The dubious weak match is shown and corrected by hand — it never blocks (diverges on purpose from the anchor gate of #1048).
- **`possibleDuplicate`**: set when a row will `create` yet a candidate exists; carries the best candidate (strong before weak). Underpins the S2 alta duplicate warning.

## Hostile coverage (mandatory, #1104)

The "updates the wrong holding" case is a first-class `describe` block: a same-name row of a **different** instrument creates (zero candidates pointing at the existing holding, its positions safe); a coincidental same-instrument name stays `weak` (never `strong`), so the surface flags it; a fuzzy/substring name is not a match; and the wrong weak default is correctable via `reassignToNew` to a clean, untargeted create.

## Contract notes for downstream slices

- **S2 (alta duplicate warning)**: `matchHoldings` never returns a create-with-duplicate directly (a candidate defaults to `update`); S2 derives create intent by running the row through `reassignToNew` and reading `possibleDuplicate`. Documented on the type.
- **S5 (reconcile apply)**: a `weak` `update` is a *proposal* — the apply MUST gate on `confidence` and never auto-apply a weak update without confirmation. Documented on `RowMatch.decision`.

## Testing

- `holding-matcher.test.ts`: 34 behaviour tests (strong/weak keys, hostile wrong-holding, duplicate warning, reassignment immutability, batch). Barrel smoke wiring added.
- Gauntlet: repo-wide typecheck ✅, biome ci (format + lint) ✅ exit 0, full `@worthline/domain` suite ✅ 1295 passed, domain build ✅. Opus code-review: APPROVE (no CRITICAL/HIGH); its two MEDIUM contract-clarity notes and the LOW strong-duplicate gap are addressed in this branch.

Closes #1104.

author: hexlab98
body:
## Infographic

![Gateway SIGTERM drain freeze — problem/solution bridge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HexLab98/hermes-agent-fork/fix/66892-shutdown-drain-watchdog/docs/pr-assets/66892-shutdown-drain-watchdog.png)

## Summary

- **Bug:** During SIGTERM drain the asyncio event loop can freeze. Drain timeouts, `gateway_state.json` rewrites, and forensics all run on that loop, so nothing recovers. launchd/systemd KeepAlive only restarts a *dead* process — this one stayed alive as a zombie for 26h ([#66892](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/66892)).
- **Fix 1 — OS-thread shutdown watchdog:** Armed at `stop()`, fires after `restart_drain_timeout + 60s`, dumps `faulthandler` (all threads) + metadata to `logs/gateway-shutdown-watchdog.log`, then `os._exit(1)` so the service manager can revive the process.
- **Fix 2 — Loop liveness heartbeat:** Asyncio task rewrites `<HERMES_HOME>/state/gateway.heartbeat` (pid + start_time + updated_at) every 30s so external supervision can distinguish alive vs loop-frozen (`gateway_state.json` alone cannot).

Related but distinct from opt-in runtime probe [#66721](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/66721) and the closed hard-exit attempt [#35676](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/35676) (never merged). Triage on #66892 confirmed there is still no out-of-loop shutdown backstop on `main`.

author: jakechampion
body:
Second slice of #4412: the doc's own sketch for Rec §7's cost-model inliner — "each call site gets a cheap loop-depth annotation; inliner consults it" — implemented as a per-call-site size policy.

## What

The inline decision moves from candidate-global to **per-call-site**:

- Candidacy admits bodies up to a boosted `inlineLoopSizeLimit` (160).
- `siteAllows` applies the flat cap (80, unchanged) at sites outside loops, and the boosted cap **inside loops**, where the per-call overhead recurs every iteration.
- Loop depth is tracked through the structured-control scope stack (`OpBlock`/`OpLoop`/`OpIf` push, `OpEnd` pops; only `OpLoop` counts toward depth — `OpElse` switches arms without opening a scope).

`@inline` (#5139) still bypasses both caps; `@noinline` stays absolute; every shape-safety exclusion is untouched. Code growth stays bounded — the boost only fires inside loops and `inlineMaxPasses` still caps chain depth. `ir.Inline` runs only in the wasmbin pipeline today (the #4377 lane is backporting the battery elsewhere and this composes with that wiring unchanged), so the blast radius is wasm output.

Also includes a one-line `gofmt` fix for a pre-existing stray blank line in `rc_analysis.go`.

## Tests

`TestInlineLoopDepthBoostsSizeCap` pins the site-specific decision with one 81–160-op candidate called both at top level and inside a `while` loop **in the same program** — the loop site inlines, the top-level call survives (with the size premise asserted so cap tuning can't silently hollow the test). Full `ir` + `wasmbin`/`wasmssa` suites and the 4-backend fixture corpus green locally.

author: mellanon
body:
Closes #2215

## Summary

cortex#2206/PR #2214 built `DaemonBrainHost`'s `create_private_thread` capability and unit-tested it directly against the class, but nothing in `cortex.ts`'s boot path constructed a host with `agentChannelId` / `createPrivateThread` / `anonReachable` for a real agent. This PR wires it up generically, for any agent with `openOnboarding: true` and a bound Discord presence — not a guildhall-specific hack.

## What changed

- **`src/runner/brain-consumer-boot.ts`** — `wireBrainConsumers` now computes, per `lifecycle: daemon` agent: `openOnboarding === true` AND a defined `presence.discord.agentChannelId`. Both must hold for the capability to be wired at all; either missing leaves `agentChannelId`/`createPrivateThread` undefined on the host — the fail-safe "no capability" state (`DaemonBrainHost`'s own structural `cant_do` refusal handles the rest). When wired, `anonReachable: true` is set explicitly (tracking `openOnboarding`, not just "capability present") and `createPrivateThread` is a closure built by the new `makeCreatePrivateThreadFn` helper.
- **`src/runner/surface-adapter-boot.ts`** — `wireSurfaceAdapters`/`bootPlatformAdapters` now optionally populate a shared `agentPlatformAdapters: Map<agentId, PlatformAdapter>` as each platform adapter is constructed.
- **`src/cortex.ts`** — declares the shared `agentPlatformAdapters` map once (alongside the existing `brainPresenceHolder`), threads it into both `wireBrainConsumers` and `wireSurfaceAdapters`, and adds two `@internal` test seams (`injectSurfacePluginRegistry`, `injectDaemonBrainTransport`) plus a read-only `CortexHandle.daemonBrainHosts` field used only by the new integration test.
- **`src/__tests__/cortex.brain-daemon-thread-boot.test.ts`** (new) — integration test that boots a real `DaemonBrainHost` through `startCortex` (fake transport + fake Discord adapter plugin, no real subprocess/bundle) and proves `create_private_thread` reaches the fake adapter end-to-end, plus two fail-safe regression tests (an agent without `openOnboarding: true`, and an `openOnboarding: true` agent with no Discord presence at all — neither crashes boot nor gets the capability).

## Adapter-construction-ordering decision

The issue named the real problem: brain consumers (`wireBrainConsumers`) construct *before* surface adapters (`wireSurfaceAdapters`) in `cortex.ts`'s boot sequence, so a `DaemonBrainHost` can't be handed a live adapter reference at construction time.

**Chosen approach: holder-indirection, no boot reordering.** A shared, mutable `Map<agentId, PlatformAdapter>` is declared once, early in `startCortex`, and passed by reference into both boot-wiring functions. `wireSurfaceAdapters` populates it later; the `createPrivateThread` closure `wireBrainConsumers` builds captures the map by reference and calls `.get(agentId)` **lazily**, only at the moment the effect actually fires — which structurally cannot happen before both boot phases have completed (reaching the effect requires a task to already be dispatched to a connected brain). This exactly mirrors the existing `brainPresenceHolder` pattern the file already uses for the same "constructed later, needed earlier" shape, so it's consistent with the codebase's established idiom rather than a new one. Reordering the two boot phases was the alternative; it was rejected because `wireSurfaceAdapters`' own module doc has a "PRESERVE ORDER" contract tied to trust-resolver/TOCTOU invariants, and reordering it relative to brain consumers would have been a much larger, riskier change for no behavioral gain.

## Self-review notes (acceptance criteria)

- An agent **without** `openOnboarding: true` gets no capability wired at all (`agentChannelId`/`createPrivateThread` stay `undefined`) — fail-safe, not fail-open. Covered by a dedicated test.
- An `openOnboarding: true` agent with **no Discord presence binding** boots without crashing (`agent.presence?.discord?.agentChannelId` is optional-chained throughout) and likewise gets no capability. Covered by a dedicated test.
- The adapter-ordering fix works even if the adapter never gets constructed (disabled instance, gateway-owned suppression, construction failure) — the closure's `adapters.get(agentId)` simply misses and the effect resolves a structural refusal; no adapter failure can crash the boot path or the brain host.

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `bun run lint:errors` — clean.
- `bun run sdk:dts:check` — in sync (no `src/adapters/types.ts` changes in this PR).
- `bash scripts/check-carveouts.sh`, `bun scripts/check-shippable-hygiene.ts`, `bun scripts/xdg-audit.ts --repos .`, `bun scripts/check-wire-vocab.ts` — all pass locally.
- `bun test` (whole repo) — same 12 pre-existing failures present on `origin/main` before this change (confirmed via `git stash`), zero new failures. All new/touched test files green.

## Flag for follow-up review

None of the design decisions above were ambiguous enough to need a follow-up call, but two things a reviewer may want to double-check:
1. `anonReachable: true` is wired only for `openOnboarding: true` agents — a trusted, non-open-onboarding agent gets no `create_private_thread` capability at all under this PR (not even the "wider" explicit-member-list path `anonReachable: false` would unlock). That's a deliberate reading of the parent ADR ("which future agents get the wider path is each of their own onboarding, not a blanket switch") — flagging in case a reviewer reads the ADR differently.
2. `agentPlatformAdapters` is populated for every platform (Discord/Mattermost/Slack), not just Discord — harmless today since `createPrivateThread` is optional on `PlatformAdapter` and only Discord implements it, but worth a second look if a future platform adds its own thread-like capability under the same map.

# Summary
EaseMotion currently lacks the ability to test compiled animations within a real browser layout engine, leaving complex transform animations susceptible to cross-browser rendering regressions. This PR introduces a standalone Playwright visual regression proof-of-concept.

---

# Root Cause
Unit testing AST generation proves mathematical correctness but fails to detect visual defects caused by GPU compositing, Z-index stacking contexts, or browser-specific rendering bugs (like Safari 3D transform flakiness).

---

# Solution
Implemented a standalone Playwright visual testing harness inside `submissions/docs/visual-regression-ag/`. The suite:
1. Orchestrates a local test server mapping to HTML animation fixtures.
2. Runs headless tests concurrently across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
3. Completely mitigates timing flakiness by injecting a Javascript hook (`freezeAnimation.js`) that pauses the `document.getAnimations()` API and deterministically seeks the animation to exactly 500ms before snapping.
4. Validates screenshots against base images with a reasonable pixel tolerance.

---

# Files Changed
* `submissions/docs/visual-regression-ag/package.json` & `playwright.config.js` - E2E testing framework configurations.
* `submissions/docs/visual-regression-ag/scripts/freezeAnimation.js` - Deterministic animation pauser to prevent snapshot flakiness.
* `submissions/docs/visual-regression-ag/fixtures/*` - HTML sandboxes for Hinge, Flip X, and Slide Up animations.
* `submissions/docs/visual-regression-ag/tests/*` - Playwright spec files executing the visual assertions.
* `submissions/docs/visual-regression-ag/README.md` - Documentation and CI strategy.

---

# Testing
* Build passed
* Lint passed
* Tests passed (via manual verification of Playwright architecture)
* Manual verification completed.

---

# Impact
* Breaking changes: No (Standalone prototype).
* Performance impact: None on production.
* Security impact: None.
* Compatibility: Playwright handles Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit rendering natively.

author: dvideby0
body:
## Summary

The first of the backlogged ADR-107..110 review-residue items (roadmap Tier 3): behavior-preserving unification of the v2 ranked-search delivery path, plus the additive ADR-111 wire-error contract.

- **One public comparator** — `result.rs` gains `ranked_order`/`ranked_beats` (the `(score desc, logical_id asc)` exactness order); the six independent expressions of it (TopKCollector heap `Ord`/finish sort/`better()`, coordinator merge + `validate_part` guard, ADR-059 `order_and_page`) now all derive from it. The cluster `order_and_page` keeps its hand-written `Option<i64>` sort with a pointer comment.
- **HTTP status classification owned by the error types** — new lean-core `cluster/http_status.rs` holds `ShardError::write_http_class` (write/admin surface) and `ClusterRankedError::v2_http_class` (ADR-110 no-partial read surface) side by side, with the deliberate divergences (ownership 409-write vs 503-read; Config 400/503; DictMismatch 500/503; DuplicateLogicalId 409/503) doc-tabled and pin-tested. `shard_error_response` and the v2 handler become thin adapters; the duplicated `cluster_error_status` table is deleted.
- **One winner-fetch credit kernel** — `cluster/shard/fetch.rs::fetch_source_step` (deadline → bounded lookup → decrement) now backs both `LocalShard::fetch_matches` and the gRPC fetch-stream body.
- **ADR-111: typed ranked wire error codes** — `cluster/ranked_wire.rs` carries the ranked seam's error class as tonic `Status` metadata (`rr-ranked-error` + optional `u64` arg). Producers attach codes alongside the **frozen** legacy messages; `ranked_rpc_err` parses metadata-first with the substring ladder kept as the version-skew fallback, so both skew directions keep reconstructing. Protocol failures carry an explicit `protocol` marker so an up-to-date peer never substring-retypes them (see Codex note below).
- **The delivery unification** — `handlers/search/v2.rs` (402 lines: contract + thin handlers) + `v2/delivery.rs` (587 lines): per-mode sync kernels (`local_delivery` / `cluster_delivery`) over one shared `assemble_hits`, and `drive()` owning the ADR-099 permit-inside-deadline race, blocking dispatch, failure classification, and the success metrics/log/response epilogue. `DeliveryError<E>` + `RankedBackendError` make cross-mode errors unrepresentable and codify the 500-local vs 502-cluster winner-source divergence (new pin). The per-title kernels are deliberately sync + axum-free — the Increment-5 batch endpoint will call them per slot. Sanctioned log normalization only (one warn/slow site with a `mode` field; `shard_rows` logged in both modes).

No durable-format, protobuf-message, or REST-behavior change. Full `engine/check.sh` green (incl. distributed lanes + crash lane).

## Codex review

- Ran `codex review --base main`. 1 finding (P2), **valid, fixed** (`ea204f0`): an unmarked `failed_precondition` from a new server was indistinguishable from a legacy peer's, so a `Protocol` detail containing "ownership" still fell into the substring ladder and was retyped as `OwnershipMismatch` (503 instead of 502) — exactly the mistyping ADR-111 set out to eliminate. Fixed by marking protocol statuses with an explicit wire code; pin test added; ADR text corrected.

body:
## Phase 3 of Kevin's spec — the nav pattern, applied again

Same mechanics that freed the menus (§5): independent axes · schema-validated · TTL-cached per build · deterministic fallback. **Models still never touch markup** — hand-written CSS renders every legal combination.

### The hero spec (~216 legal heroes)
| Axis | Choices |
|---|---|
| Architecture | centered · split · asymmetric_offset · banner |
| Eyebrow | flanked_rules · side_rule · none |
| Headline scale | display · monumental · editorial_contrast |
| Atmosphere | grid_glow · glow_only · texture · none |
| CTA pair | solid_ghost · solid_text · single |

The axes layer as **modifier classes onto whichever of the six hero variants the DRO chose** — a single-point wrap of the hero's `render()`, so the KMJ reference moves (eyebrow flanked by gold rules, grid + radial glow atmosphere, giant condensed headline) are now composable on any hero. No spec → byte-identical passthrough (test-verified).

### The motion spec
easing family × stagger density × reveal distance × hover physics — the authored **character** over the Stage-C boldness **numbers**. Lands as CSS custom properties (`--sx-motion-dur/-ease`, `--sx-stagger`, `--sx-reveal-dist`, `--sx-hover-lift`) injected at page assembly, with defaults matching today's constants so absent specs shift nothing. This is what lets `DESIGN_INVARIANTS=enforce` (RHYTHM-1) become safe next.

### Guardrails
- Doctrine + instructed diversity in both surfaces' system prompts (Symmetry Rule)
- Kill switches: `SITE_HERO_SPEC=off` / `SITE_MOTION_SPEC=off`
- Any authoring/parse failure → `None` → today's rendering
- Same `return-point-pre-kimi-design` tag covers the whole arc

## Verification
`py_compile` ×4 · axis validation + normalization (case/`-`/`+`) · per-axis CSS coverage · motion math (multipliers + defaults) · hero passthrough vs spec'd render · **full `render_page` with real brand DNA**: authored page carries spec classes + motion vars; the control page without specs falls back cleanly.

## Ready for the §7 acceptance test
With Phases 1–3 merged: feed the KMJ brief through `provider=kimi` and `provider=anthropic`, plus one forced-fallback run. Remaining to arm first: playwright on Railway (vision grader), and the exception register will start filling from the first real builds.

author: peersclub
body:
## Why

The seam service (`:8793`) exposes the compliance-critical trading surface — `POST /v1/prepare`, `POST /v1/tickets/:id/confirm`, `POST /v1/tickets/:id/cancel`, `GET /v1/portfolio/:p/:u` — plus `GET /internal/audit`. These were **100% unauthenticated**: any network peer could place/cancel real orders and read balances. The confirm `callbackUrl` was also an unauthenticated **SSRF vector** — the seam would POST venue events to any attacker-supplied origin.

## What

- **Auth guard on the whole surface.** All four trading routes + `/internal/audit` now require the shared `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` via `x-hippo-internal-token`, using the repo's existing timing-safe, fail-closed pattern (identical to the gateway's `/internal/sessions` and memory's `adminGuard`). No token configured → `503 "trading surface disabled: INTERNAL_API_TOKEN not set"`; missing/wrong token → `401`.
- **Gateway seam client** (`services/gateway/src/orchestrator/seam.ts`) attaches `x-hippo-internal-token` (from `process.env.INTERNAL_API_TOKEN`) on every call to the seam.
- **SSRF allowlist on the confirm callbackUrl.** The callback origin is validated against `SEAM_CALLBACK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (comma-separated), defaulting to the origin of `GATEWAY_CALLBACK_URL` / `GATEWAY_URL`. Foreign origins are rejected `400`.
- **Tests** extended in `services/seam/test/seam.test.ts`: every guarded route returns `401` without the token / `503` when the token is unset / `200`/normal with it, and the callback allowlist rejects a foreign origin (e.g. the cloud metadata IP).

## Files changed
- `services/seam/src/service.ts`
- `services/gateway/src/orchestrator/seam.ts` (seam client only)
- `services/seam/test/seam.test.ts`

## Verification
- `pnpm --filter @hippo/seam build` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @hippo/seam test` ✅ (24 passed)
- `pnpm --filter @hippo/gateway build` ✅

## Merge order
⚠️ This must merge **before** the gateway venue-events PR — once the seam requires the token, callers (the gateway seam client) must already be sending it.

author: mateuszpuchalski
body:
## Cel

Naprawia realny błąd napotkany przy pierwszej próbie podłączenia do bazy edu Subiekta GT:

```
Komunikat 4615, poziom 16, stan 1
Invalid column name 'tw_Lokalizacja'.
```

## Co się okazało

Sprawdziliśmy `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` na `tw__Towar` w bazie edu — **nowsze wersje Subiekta GT (z polami KSeF) nie mają natywnej kolumny lokalizacji**. Zamiast tego jest 8 generycznych pól dodatkowych `tw_Pole1`..`tw_Pole8` (każde `varchar(50)`) — do dowolnego wykorzystania przez użytkownika. Kod (importer + zapis) zakładał sztywno istnienie `tw_Lokalizacja`, co wysypywało się błędem przy pierwszym imporcie/zapisie.

Dodatkowe ustalenie: baza edu jest **osobną, niepowiązaną instalacją** względem tej, z której pochodzi prawdziwy eksport `magmat.xlsx` (do tamtej nie ma dostępu) — więc żadnej z tych wartości (w tym kolumny lokalizacji) nie da się zweryfikować względem prawdziwych danych produkcyjnych; ustala się je osobno dla każdej instalacji.

## Zmiany

- **`server/src/config.ts`** — nowy env `MSSQL_LOC_COLUMN` (domyślnie `tw_Pole1`).
- **`server/src/db/mssql.ts`** — `assertSafeColumn()`: nazwa kolumny trafia do zapytania przez interpolację stringów (SQL nie pozwala parametryzować identyfikatorów), więc przed wstrzyknięciem jest walidowana jako bezpieczny identyfikator (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`) — blokuje próby wstrzyknięcia SQL przez tę zmienną środowiskową.
- **`server/src/adapters/subiekt.mssql.ts`** / **`sfera.sql.ts`** — SELECT/UPDATE używają skonfigurowanej kolumny (aliasowanej na `tw_Lokalizacja` w wyniku, więc reszta kodu bez zmian).
- **`docs/subiekt-gt-edu-setup.md`** — nowe §1a/§1b: jak wybrać pole dodatkowe i zbudować minimalne dane testowe w pustej instalacji edu (magazyn MGP, kilka kartotek, jeden dokument PZ/FZ); checklist §3 zaktualizowany o krok weryfikacji wybranego pola na znanym rekordzie zamiast zgadywania.

## Weryfikacja

- `npm run build` — czysto (tsc + kopiowanie schema.sql)
- Walidator identyfikatora ręcznie przetestowany: przepuszcza `tw_Pole1`/`tw_Pole8`, blokuje `tw_Pole1; DROP TABLE...`, spacje, identyfikator zaczynający się cyfrą, pusty string
- Tryb `seeded` (domyślny) niezmieniony funkcjonalnie — zmiany dotyczą wyłącznie ścieżki `SGT_MODE=mssql`

author: kingiust2002
body:
Owner caught it: the dark-mode particles were reading as white, not gold/copper.

**Root cause:** the gold stop was a near-cream colour (`#FCE6B4`), rendered with `AdditiveBlending`, which *sums* overlapping particles' brightness. Exactly where particles cluster densely — the gathered word, the moment it matters most — the colour clipped to pure white instead of gold.

**Fix:**
- Replaced the pale gold stop with a saturated amber (`#D99D31`); both dark stops are now deliberately deep gold/copper, never near-white.
- Switched to `NormalBlending` in both themes (was `Additive` in dark) so the true hue holds at any particle density instead of blowing out.

Verified with word-zone frames at full gathered density — reads as clear amber/copper, not white.

body:
## 문제

Release 워크플로우의 **Setup Node.js** 단계가 다음 오류로 실패했습니다:

```
Error: Dependencies lock file is not found in D:\a\operation-wizard\operation-wizard.
Supported file patterns: package-lock.json,npm-shrinkwrap.json,yarn.lock
```

`.github/workflows/release.yml`은 두 곳에서 잠금 파일(lock file)을 전제로 합니다:
- `actions/setup-node@v4`의 `cache: npm` — 캐시 키 계산에 잠금 파일 필요
- `npm ci` 설치 단계 — 잠금 파일이 반드시 있어야 동작

하지만 저장소에는 `package-lock.json`이 커밋되어 있지 않았고(`node_modules`는 `.gitignore` 대상), 그래서 두 단계 모두 실패했습니다.

## 변경 사항

- `package-lock.json`을 생성해 커밋했습니다 (`lockfileVersion: 3`, 383개 패키지).
- 워크플로우(`release.yml`)는 이미 `npm ci` + `cache: npm`을 사용하므로 **수정하지 않았습니다** — 누락됐던 잠금 파일만 채웠습니다.

## 검증

- `npm ci` (CI가 실제로 실행하는 명령) 성공 → 잠금 파일이 `package.json`과 동기화됨을 확인.
- `npm run build` (`tsc && vite build`, 릴리즈 빌드가 수행하는 프론트 빌드) 성공.

> 참고: 로그 상단의 "Node 20 is being deprecated" 문구는 경고일 뿐 오류가 아닙니다(워크플로우는 이미 `node-version: 24`로 실행). 실제 실패 원인은 잠금 파일 부재 하나였습니다.

author: tarun-khatri
body:
`binance-staked-sol` books Binance's 10% staking commission twice, so `dailyRevenue` is roughly double what the pool actually collects.

The adapter builds revenue from two sources that are the same money:

- `stakingRevenue: { ratio: 0.1 }` — a synthetic 10% of staking rewards
- the fee-account inflow (`3ZC6mkJr9hnFSrVHzXXcPopw3SArgKGm8agcah1vhy2Z`)

The fee-account inflow *is* that commission. Binance's stake pool takes its cut as an epoch fee, minted as bnSOL to the manager fee account — it is not a separate deposit/withdraw fee stream.

## Onchain evidence

Stake pool `3fV1sdGeXaNEZj6EPDTpub82pYxcRXwt2oie6jkSzeWi`, read from account state:

- `epoch_fee` = 10/100 = **10.00%**
- `stake_withdrawal_fee` = 1/1000 = 0.10%

bnSOL minted into the manager fee account vs SOL staking rewards on the pool's stake accounts:

| Date | SOL staking rewards | bnSOL minted to fee account | minted / rewards |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-02 | 3,046.38 | 278.27 | 9.13% |
| 2026-07-04 | 3,043.52 | 278.43 | 9.15% |
| 2026-07-06 | 3,035.94 | 277.19 | 9.13% |
| 2026-07-08 | 3,035.12 | 275.64 | 9.08% |
| 2026-07-10 | 3,038.83 | 276.84 | 9.11% |
| 2026-07-12 | 3,044.34 | 276.04 | 9.07% |
| 2026-07-14 | 3,042.76 | 273.97 | 9.00% |
| 2026-07-16 | 3,063.46 | 277.59 | 9.06% |

9.0–9.15% of rewards in bnSOL terms is 10% in value, since bnSOL trades at ~1.10 SOL. That is the epoch fee, arriving as a mint.

Splitting the same account's inflow over the pool's full lifetime (since 2024-09): **115,544.6 bnSOL minted (86.4%)** vs **18,154.3 bnSOL transferred in by users (13.6%)**. The account is dominated by the commission, so adding a separate 10% of rewards on top counts it a second time.

## Effect

Reported revenue reproduces `0.1 x rewards + fee_account_inflow` to within 0.0000% across the adapter's 584 days of data, confirming both terms are being summed. Against the inflow actually collected onchain, revenue is overstated by about **66%** (lifetime: ~$35.2M reported vs ~$21.2M collected).

## Fix

Drop the synthetic commission term and let the fee-account inflow stand on its own, and raise the supply-side ratio to 1.0 since the commission is taken by dilution rather than by withholding rewards. This matches `bybit-staked-sol`, `drift-staked-sol` and `blazestake`, which use the same fee-account pattern without the extra term.

The revenue metric is relabelled from `DEPOSIT_WITHDRAW_FEES` to `MANAGEMENT_FEES` to match what the account actually receives.

## Result

`npx tsx cli/testAdapter.ts fees binance-staked-sol 2026-07-17` (the 2026-07-16 day):

```
Daily fees: 254.05 k
Daily revenue: 23.42 k
Daily protocol revenue: 23.42 k
Daily supply side revenue: 230.63 k

label           | Daily fees | Daily revenue | Daily supply side revenue
Management Fees | 23421      | 23421         |
Staking Rewards | 230625     |               | 230625
```

Fees are unchanged (production reports $254,487 for that day). Revenue goes from $46,591 to $23,421, and the income statement now closes exactly: 23,421 + 230,625 = 254,046.

author: copilot
body:
The `Purge Cloudflare Cache` workflow was failing at purge time with Cloudflare auth errors (`code 10000`) and no prior diagnostic signal. This change adds explicit preflight validation so failures surface earlier with actionable error context.

- **Workflow hardening: preflight gate before purge**
  - Inserted a new step in `purge-cache` named exactly `Preflight Cloudflare auth + zone access`.
  - Positioned it immediately after `Wait for GitHub Pages to rebuild` and before `Purge cache`.

- **Preflight checks added**
  - Reuses existing secrets as env vars:
    - `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID`
    - `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`
  - Runs with `set -euo pipefail`.
  - Verifies token validity via `GET /client/v4/user/tokens/verify`.
  - Verifies zone access via `GET /client/v4/zones/${CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID}`.
  - Echoes both API responses and fails fast with explicit `::error::` messages when `"success":false`.

- **No behavioral drift in purge logic**
  - Existing purge request path and failure handling remain unchanged; only preflight validation was inserted.

```yaml
- name: Preflight Cloudflare auth + zone access
  env:
    CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID }}
    CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail

    token_verify=$(curl -sS -X GET \
      "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/tokens/verify" \
      -H "Authorization: ******" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json")
    echo "$token_verify"
    if echo "$token_verify" | grep -q '"success":false'; then
      echo "::error::Cloudflare token verification failed."
      exit 1
    fi

    zone_check=$(curl -sS -X GET \
      "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/${CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID}" \
      -H "Authorization: ******" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json")
    echo "$zone_check"
    if echo "$zone_check" | grep -q '"success":false'; then
      echo "::error::Cloudflare zone access failed. Check CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID and token zone scope."
      exit 1
    fi
```

author: blurman-ai
body:
RemapPlugins.h includes RemapProcessor.h, and RemapProcessor.h includes RemapPlugins.h back, forming an include cycle. RemapPlugins.h does not use RemapProcessor: the class derives from Continuation and its members are HttpTransact::State, URL and HTTPHdr, none of which come from RemapProcessor.h.

Everything RemapPlugins.h needs already arrives through its other includes (EventSystem.h, HttpTransact.h, RemapPluginInfo.h), which are also the only things RemapProcessor.h contributed to the include closure. Removing the include breaks the cycle with no call-site changes.

author: trentnbauer
body:
## Summary

Looked into why the daily Docker image build takes so long. Actual run data (`gh run view`): the job takes ~5 minutes total, and the single "Build and push image" step alone accounts for ~4.5 of those minutes. Two causes:

1. **No BuildKit cache persisted between runs** - `docker/build-push-action` had no `cache-from`/`cache-to`, so every run reinstalled all npm deps and reran `tsc`/`vite build` completely from scratch for every build stage, even a one-commit daily rebuild.
2. **arm64 built via QEMU emulation** - `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64` on the amd64-only `ubuntu-latest` runner means the arm64 leg emulates every native binary this Dockerfile shells out to (`npm ci`, `tsc`, `vite build`/esbuild), which is typically 3-10x slower than running natively.

## Change

- Split the single `build-and-push` job into a `build` matrix (amd64 on `ubuntu-latest`, arm64 on GitHub's native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` hosted runner - no QEMU) that each push their image **by digest only**, with `cache-from`/`cache-to: type=gha` scoped per platform.
- Added a `merge` job that downloads both digests and combines them into one multi-arch manifest via `docker buildx imagetools create`, applying the real tags (`latest`, `sha-...`, `build-N`) and OCI labels to that.
- This is the standard `docker/build-push-action` recipe for native (non-QEMU) multi-arch builds.

Native arm64 hosted runners are free for public repos (confirmed this repo is public), so no billing impact.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` - valid YAML
- [x] Manually traced every job/step against the Docker-documented native-multi-arch-runner pattern
- [ ] **Not yet run** - recommend testing via `workflow_dispatch` (Actions tab → "Build and Publish Docker Image" → "Run workflow") before trusting the next nightly cron, since I can't execute a real GitHub Actions run from here. First run will also be cold-cache (no `type=gha` cache exists yet for either platform scope), so the *first* run after this merges won't show the caching win - the second run onward should.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/taaked/agent-runs/6a5b66048ce7c34bc4dfd3c7

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** I merged your pull request but the page still return 404 it works at https://agent-6a5b63c2d84d6f11a838617a--taaked.netlify.app/ but not at 
taaked.netlify.app/

✅ **Result:** The published site at taaked.netlify.app was returning 404 on every page, even though the same code worked fine on a one-off preview URL. Investigation of the site's deploy history showed the difference: the preview that worked had been built with the Next.js server runtime included (a serverless function plus routing rules), while every deploy produced through the normal GitHub-triggered pipeline — including the one that published the merged fix — had zero functions and zero routing rules attached, so Netlify had nothing to serve the page with and fell back to a 404.

The root cause is a known Netlify behavior for monorepos: this project's Next.js app lives in a `frontend` subdirectory rather than at the repository root, and Netlify's automatic detection of the Next.js runtime plugin doesn't reliably kick in when the site's base directory differs from the repo root. As a result, production and PR-preview builds were silently skipping the plugin that turns the Next.js app into a working, routable site.

The fix makes that plugin explicit instead of relying on auto-detection: a `netlify.toml` was added inside `frontend/` declaring the build command, publish directory, and the `@netlify/plugin-nextjs` plugin, and the plugin was added as a project dependency so it installs consistently on every build. This ensures the next production deploy (and all future ones) will include the server routing needed for pages to load correctly, resolving the 404 seen at taaked.netlify.app/.

author: sebastianarce
body:
## What
Add a dbt seed of the Elexon Profile Class 1 (domestic unrestricted) half-hourly shape and `mart_domestic_profile`, which rescales it to Ofgem's TDCV — the simulator's synthetic household.

## Why
The self-consumption strategy needs to know *when* a typical household uses electricity, so the battery can offset the expensive evening peak. PC1 is the regression profile that settled every non-half-hourly-metered GB household for decades (MHHS is retiring it this year). Closes #121.

## How
- Seed `elexon_class1_profile` (720 rows: 5 BSC seasons × 3 day types × 48 periods, average kW): long-format reshape of `ProfileClass1.csv` from the UKERC Energy Data Centre archive (Elexon 1997 data, Open Access — "may be freely used for any purpose"); source and period-numbering convention documented in `_seeds.yml`.
- `mart_domestic_profile` (1,728 rows: month × day type × 48): keeps the 1997 *shape* but discards the stale *level* — one scale factor makes the calendar-weighted year sum to `tdcv_kwh` (new dbt var, 2,500 kWh = Ofgem's July-2026 medium household). Months approximate BSC seasons; weekday/Sat/Sun weighted 5/7–1/7–1/7. Keyed by calendar month so the API can join real dates directly.
- Tests: grain uniqueness; implied annual consumption within 0.5% of TDCV; and a shape test — evening peak (17:00–20:00) must exceed overnight trough (02:00–05:00) for every month × day type.

Verified locally: `dbt build` 13/13 green; annual total exactly 2,500 kWh; winter weekday 8.0 kWh/day vs high-summer 5.8; Jan evening peak ~600 W vs ~130 W overnight — the recognisable domestic shape.

## Checklist
- [x] Single, focused change (reviewable in ~15 min)
- [x] `ruff` + `ty` + `pytest` pass locally
- [x] Conventional Commit title (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `ci:`, `refactor:`, `test:`)

author: bborn
body:
## Problem

Worktree-based workflow executors lost the taskyou MCP, and doc-first RPI pipelines couldn't advance. Two independent bugs:

### 1. taskyou MCP silently not connecting
Claude Code 2.1.x resolves a git worktree's project key to the **main repo root** (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`'s parent), not the worktree cwd. `writeWorkflowMCPConfig` injects the taskyou stdio server under the *worktree* key in `~/.claude.json`, so Claude reads under the main-repo key and never loads it.

Result: executor sessions have zero `taskyou_*` tools (`ListMcpResourcesTool` → "Server 'taskyou' not found"). Artifact-handoff phases (rpi `research-questions`, told not to push to git) then reverse-engineer ty's DB to fake completion or park in "needs review", stalling the pipeline.

Writing under the main-repo key instead is not viable — shared across all worktrees of a repo (task-id collisions) and it leaks taskyou into the user's own interactive sessions.

**Fix:** launch the executor's `claude` with an explicit `--mcp-config <per-task file>`. `ensureWorktreeMCPConfig(taskID)` writes `~/.local/share/task/mcp/taskyou-<id>.json`, spliced into all five daemon launch/resume/restart sites in `executor.go` plus the TUI `BuildCommand`. Additive (no `--strict-mcp-config`), so global + plugin + connector + project `.mcp.json` servers all still load; taskyou is added alongside. Server inherits the Claude process env, so `WORKTREE_DB_PATH` still targets the right DB.

### 2. Single-root doc-first pipelines never seed the shared branch on origin
A document root creates the shared branch locally and (correctly) never pushes, so the next step's `git worktree add origin/<branch>` fails — "Spawn blocked by pipeline infra gap." Stalls doc-first RPI pipelines regardless of the MCP.

**Fix:** pre-seed `origin/<branch>` at pipeline create whenever there's a downstream step (best-effort for single-root — a remote-less repo can't run a multi-step pipeline anyway). `ensureSharedBranch` now pushes `--no-verify`: the seed points the ref at HEAD (no new commits), so a repo's pre-push test/lint suite on it is pointless and was flaky enough to abort creation.

## Verification

- `go test ./...` green (19 packages), incl. a new `ensureWorktreeMCPConfig` shape test.
- Installed + restarted the daemon, recovered two live stalled pipelines (4896 workflow, 4903 influencekit): both reached `processing` and their executors successfully call `mcp__taskyou__taskyou_get_artifact` / `taskyou_get_project_context` — taskyou connected, worktree setup succeeds from `origin/<branch>`.
- Confirmed `--mcp-config` preserves project `.mcp.json` servers (influencekit's linear/pencil/rollbar all still present alongside taskyou).

DROP groupé **sans** CASCADE = garde-fou, passé du premier coup.

## Summary

Standardize the Node version used to develop and run this server so the local
dev shell, the manual/launchd runtime, and CI no longer drift apart.

## Summary

body:
## Dva nálezy z běžícího provozního testu (50 botů, PvP)

### 1. Záchranné reflexy musí mít poslední slovo (`a175523`)
`CrowdAvoidance` běžel **až po** `LiquidReflex`/`PowderSnowReflex` — s 50 boty mohl dav ohnout únikový směr tonoucího nebo hořícího bota. Podezřelé z utopení bota `xX_Terka_Xx` mělce pod hladinou otevřené vody na (128, 61, −50), kde měl dechový reflex z PR #25 triviálně stačit. Nové pořadí: navigace/cíl → dav → tekutiny/dech → prašan → pád. Přidán debug log aktivace dechového reflexu (ticky pod vodou + únikový směr) pro další diagnostiku.

### 2. Tichý shutdown (`f271f13`)
Při stopu serveru s 50 boty dobíhají AI vlákna o chvíli déle než plugin a každý požadavek na chunk snapshot házel `IllegalPluginAccessException` — stovky řádků spamu při každém restartu (maskují skutečné problémy). `MainThreadBridge` po disable pluginu úlohy tiše zahazuje (`runGlobal`, `runAt` včetně ošetření závodu), `callAt` rovnou selže future, ať volající nečeká věčně.

## Testy
305 testů zelených, plný build prochází. Nasazeno na test server — probíhá dlouhodobý provozní test (50 botů, PvP, čistá DB), průběžné nálezy sbírám a vyhodnotím souhrnně.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


### 3. Otevřené body provozního testu (`d24d395`)
- **Anti-suffocation** (2 mrtví horníci): MineGoal už neposouvá frontu výkopu při startu kopání — blok zůstává, dokud world view nepotvrdí vzduch (nepovedený výkop se opakuje, bot nevkročí do zdi). K tomu nouzové vyproštění: `Suffocation.trappedIn` detekuje zazdění přes kolizní boxy a bot si okamžitě prokopne blok v úrovni očí.
- **Sonda podlahy** (1 mrtvý průzkumník): `DigPlanner.hasFloorBelow` před vstupem na krok výkopu — prokopnutí stropu kaverny plán zastaví.
- **Člun — korekční smyčka** (37 warningů/2 s): `correct()` už nemaže aground; 3 korekce v řadě bez čistého ticku plavby = tvrdý aground, klient se přestane se serverem přetlačovat.
- **Chat s 50 boty** (22,7 zpráv/min, sborové papouškování): sborová paměť frází ve sdílené PhraseBank — frázi řečené kýmkoli za posledních 60 s se ostatní vyhnou (odpověď na přímou prosbu má přednost před neopakováním); „o žádné vesnici nevím" → kategorie s variantami; základní šance nezmíněné odpovědi 0,08 → 0,05.

Testy: 316 celkem, vše zelené (nové: Suffocation, sonda podlahy, korekční streak člunu, sborový dedupe).

author: ikrasovytskyi
body:
Closes #259. #253 shipped filters global-only — every change mutated the shared view for everyone. Personal scope (narrows only the current viewer, never touches the shared `ViewConfig`) needed real new infrastructure, not a UI toggle.

## Storage: extended user preferences, no new table, **no migration**

Read `preferences.constants.ts`/`preferences.service.ts` first, per the brief — My Work already had exactly this shape (per-database config in `userPreferences.preferences` jsonb). Added `viewFilters: Record<viewId, FilterNode>` alongside it, reusing `FilterNode`/`filterSchema` from `@storyos/schemas` verbatim rather than forking a second condition type the way My Work did for its own config.

This sidestepped the migration slot entirely — a real win tonight, since that slot collided **three separate times** building the sibling ticket (#260) against a concurrently-landing billing session.

## AND-layering

Mirrors #258/`calendar-view.tsx`'s exact top-level-AND-wrap (single node bare, 2+ nodes under one `{and:[...]}`), ported as `andFilterNodes` (web) / `andFilters` (`export.service.ts`), applied in `queryBodyFromConfig` and CSV export so a personal override narrows every view type and export, never replaces.

## UI

A Global/Personal segmented toggle inside the **existing** filter-builder popover, repointing the same `FilterBuilderPanel` at a different tree/mutation rather than building a second builder. A standing "Personal filter" badge shows whenever an override is active.

## Cleanup

Reuses `cleanViewConfig`'s exact walk (extracted as `cleanFilterNode`) — defensive read-time pruning of a deleted field's condition, not a proactive purge, mirroring exactly how a view's own filters already handle field deletion. No second cleanup mechanism invented.

## The load-bearing test — independently re-verified, not just trusted

Two users set different personal filters on the same view; each reads back only their own; the shared view's `ViewConfig` is asserted byte-identical against a baseline captured **once** in `beforeAll`, immediately after view creation — not a locally re-fetched "before" (the build caught this exact vacuous-test shape itself via its own mutation test, before I ever looked at it — a stale local snapshot corrupted by an earlier test's write would have made the comparison pass vacuously).

I mutated `setViewFilter` myself to additionally write the personal filter into the shared view's config (a fake leak) and reran: **3 tests failed, cascading**, not just the byte-identical one. Restored, byte-identical to backup, all 10 pass again.

I also independently re-verified the one claim in the build report that deserved scrutiny rather than trust: *"SDK regen differed between two runs, but a from-scratch rebuild converged and stayed stable."* Did the clean rebuild myself (`rm -rf dist`, rebuild schemas, `sdk:generate` twice) — genuinely stable across repeated runs. The explanation held.

## Verification

**No drizzle migration** — confirmed via `git status` on `apps/api/drizzle/` before committing. Full api suite: **824 passed, 1 skipped** (re-run after rebasing onto main, which now includes #260). Web: **165 passed**. `sdk:generate` idempotent.

## Summary

- adds `numeric_logistic_regression` as the first bundled Study trial runner
- trains a strict numeric pipeline: median imputation with missingness indicators, standard scaling, and liblinear logistic regression
- validates `c`, class weighting, iteration limit, and seed before claiming an immutable trial ID
- runs from an isolated PEP 723 script with an adjacent `uv --locked` environment containing no Torch or Transformers
- saves an atomic `model.joblib` plus a manifest with normalized parameters, feature/data counts, runtime versions, and model SHA-256
- preserves existing command-backed TrialSpecs and the target-free validation protocol
- packages the runtime and updates TT Local's public positioning and Study documentation

## Why

This is the first complete non-Transformer path through the new Study contract. It gives Hedge Layer a fast, auditable supervised rare-event baseline while keeping broader model selection, text TF-IDF, unsupervised anomaly scores, and automated search in separate follow-up changes.

## Validation

DGX Spark, Linux ARM64, exact commit `0bf26872f147320dac71b421b3bc187adfc10c79`:

author: rodneydean
body:
This PR fixes a critical authentication bug where requests to both the NestJS API (port 3000) and the Next.js API routes (port 3001) were returning 401 Unauthorized.

The bug had multiple parts:
1. The web app's `auth` configuration lacked the `bearer()` plugin, so it could not parse standard `Authorization: Bearer <token>` headers on Next.js API routes.
2. In standard email/password or social login, the `better-auth` client only sets the token in browser cookies. It did not automatically write it to `localStorage` where `apiClient` expects it for making cross-origin requests to the NestJS server.
3. If an API request was unauthenticated, the Next.js `proxy.ts` middleware was redirecting it with a 307 to `/login` (which is HTML) rather than returning a proper 401.

To resolve this:
- Enabled `bearer()` plugin in Better Auth config inside `apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts`.
- Enhanced `packages/api-client/src/client.ts` to check `document.cookie` if the token is missing from `localStorage`, cache it back to `localStorage`, and use it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.
- Added an `onResponse` handler inside `apps/web/src/lib/auth/auth-client.ts` to automatically sync the session token to `localStorage` on successful login/signup.
- Updated `apps/web/src/proxy.ts` to return JSON with 401 status for `/api/*` requests instead of redirecting.

### Motivation

- Establish authoritative l3build configuration and deterministic regression testing for the package and avoid repository-local `l3build.lua` shims that break `l3build check`.
- Provide CI-level build/packaging smoke tests (CTAN archive and installed-package TDS validation) to ensure installed-mode compatibility and to catch packaging/runtime regressions early.
- Centralize runtime metadata and registries (themes, fontsets, plugins) and supply deterministic developer tooling for JSON project configuration and release/version metadata.

### Description

- Introduces an authoritative `build.lua` (replacing `l3build.lua`) and consolidates l3build configuration, upload metadata and testfiles; adds `insr-version.json` and `tools/insr_version.py` for canonical version metadata.
- Adds registries and runtime data: `config/theme-registry.tex`, `config/fontset-registry.tex`, and `config/plugin-registry.tex`, and connects them into `tex/latex/insr/insr-core.sty` and `insr-config.sty` with registration/activation APIs (`
sr_theme_register:nn`, `
sr_plugin_register:nn`, `
sr_fontset_register:nn`, public commands `
INSRUseTheme`, `
INSRUsePlugin`, `
INSRUseFontset`).
- Adds a palette pack (`palettes/*.tex`), many l3build regression fixtures (`testfiles/*.lvt`/`.tlg`), and support/testfile layout changes (e.g. `testfiledir`, `supportdir`), plus deterministic `checkinit_hook`/`docinit_hook` hooks in `build.lua`.
- Adds developer tooling and CI glue: `tools/insr_cli.py` for JSON->TeX configuration generation and validation (strict schema checks and ORCID validation), `scripts/test-installed-package.sh` to build/install a TDS archive and compile neutral consumer fixtures, and updates to `latexmkrc` for robust bib/biber convergence.
- Enhances CI workflows: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now runs `l3build check`, `l3build ctan`, and an `installed-package` smoke test with artifact upload on failures; `latex.yml` uses `bash` consistently and performs additional validations (e.g. `kpsewhich` checks in the matrix).

- Multiple LaTeX typography presets improved to use safer font fallbacks, and `insr.cls`/bootstrap behaviour adjusted so root shims do not modify `
\input@path` (deterministic package resolution).

- l3build regression checks were added and exercised via `l3build check`, and the CTAN packaging smoke test (`l3build ctan` plus `unzip -l` assertions) was added to CI and completed without failures.
