## Summary

- add an intrinsically scoped, arity-indexed Core expression fragment with exact erasure back to Yul
- add a generic proof-carrying rule engine and migrate constant folding and neutral-element simplification to it
- remove the old raw-AST rewrite driver, its duplicate soundness theorem, and its parallel layout-resolution proof
- make unsupported built-ins and non-ANF expression shapes explicit identity cases at the Core boundary
- prove layout resolution is structurally inert on Core terms, preserving object-resolution correctness
- document the incremental architecture, migration path, and recursion boundary in the existing project documentation

## Refactoring result

The existing semantic building blocks (`pureFold`, `fold_equiv`, `neutral`, and `neutral_equiv`) are reused by the Core rules. The duplicate `simplifyBuiltinRaw` optimizer path is deleted. Successful local rewrites now run exclusively through Core; failed ingestion leaves the source built-in unchanged.

The follow-up refactoring commit is net -93 lines and removes 134 lines, primarily duplicate optimizer and resolution-proof machinery.

## Scope

This first Core slice covers flat, pure expressions. Nested, effectful, call, and recursive-call forms remain outside Core and are left unchanged at this boundary. Statement and function ingestion, lexical contexts, and SCC-based recursion support remain follow-up work.

author: andrewmclachlan
body:
Two issues with the skeleton shimmer (reported after #634):

1. **It swept right-to-left** — with `background-size: 200%` and a `-100%..100%` position sweep, the highlight (the gradient's centre) travelled backwards.
2. **It flickered on each loop** — at `100%` the highlight sat at the left edge (still visible), then snapped back to base when the animation restarted.

## Fix

Use a fixed-width highlight band (`--skeleton-band`, 220px) animated from fully off the left edge (`-band`) to fully off the right (`band + 100%`). Because the band is off-screen at both ends of the cycle, the element shows **pure base at 0% and 100%**, so the loop restarts seamlessly (no flicker), and it now sweeps **left-to-right**.

## Verification

Confirmed in the browser against the built CSS: `background-position` sweeps −220px → 700px on a 480px element (band off-left at the start, off-right at the end), and the highlight renders as a moving band. Reduced-motion (opacity pulse) fallback unchanged. Skeleton tests pass.

author: nguyencanhqk
body:
## Bối cảnh

Bắt đầu từ yêu cầu dọn menu trùng, mở rộng dần theo phản hồi khi dùng thật. Trong quá trình đó phát hiện **2 lỗi/thiếu sót thật đang ảnh hưởng người dùng** ở luồng "yêu cầu cập nhật hồ sơ".

## 1. `fix(hr)` — nút "Duyệt" trả 400, không dùng được

`POST /hr/profile-change-requests/:id/approve|reject` **luôn** trả `400 "Expected object, received string"` trước khi vào service.

**Nguyên nhân:** `@UsePipes(new ZodValidationPipe(schema))` ở method áp pipe cho **mọi tham số** của handler, mà pipe khởi tạo kèm schema thì bỏ qua `metadata.type` và validate tất cả. Handler có `@Param("id") id: string` ⇒ chuỗi id bị đem so với schema object ⇒ 400. Các handler khác chỉ có `@Req`/`@Query`/`@Body` (đều là object) nên lọt qua — đó là lý do tạo/liệt kê vẫn chạy còn approve/reject chết. Quét toàn API: **đúng 2 handler này** dính (nên nút "Từ chối" cũng đang hỏng, chỉ chưa ai bấm).

Lỗi khó lần vì `AllExceptionsFilter` **chỉ log ≥500** — 4xx không để lại dấu vết trong log.

**Vì sao test cũ không bắt được:** `profile-change-request.int-spec.ts` có hẳn khối "approve applies allowed fields" nhưng **diễn lại SQL của repository bằng tay**, không gọi HTTP ⇒ tầng controller/pipe chưa từng được test.

## 2. `feat(hr,noti)` — thông báo phê duyệt chưa từng được viết

Phần dữ liệu **đã seed đầy đủ** (3 mã trong `notification_events` + template IN_APP) nên nhìn DB tưởng có, nhưng service **không phát event** ra outbox và bridge **không đăng ký mapping**. Đợt S4-INT chỉ wiring LEAVE/ATT/AUTH (9 mã lõi `NOTI-EVENT-001..009`); 3 mã HR này thuộc phần mở rộng SPEC-08 §15 nên bị bỏ lại.

Bổ sung: producer (`outbox.enqueue` **cùng tx** với audit) + `PcrApproverAudienceReader` (người nhận lấy theo **cặp quyền thật** `approve:profile-change-request`, không hard-code role) + `HrPcrNotiBridgeRegistrar` (3 mapping, tái dùng `OutboxNotificationBridge`).

**PII (BẤT BIẾN #3):** payload event chỉ mang `requestId`/`employeeId`/actor — không kèm `newValues`/`oldValues`/`rejectionReason`.

## 3. `feat(me,hr)` — gom self-service về ME + đồng bộ giao diện hồ sơ

- Gỡ "Hồ sơ của tôi" (`/hr/me`) khỏi sidebar HR (trùng `/me/profile`); route cũ giữ nguyên cho bookmark.
- Menu avatar + các nút self-service trỏ về `/me/*`. "Bật 2FA" → route ME mới `/me/security/2fa`.
- `/me/profile` dùng lại **đúng bố cục** `/hr/employees/:id` — tách `ProfileCoverHeader` dùng chung thay vì copy markup.
- Màn mới `/me/profile/edit`: sửa trực tiếp rồi gửi duyệt, `changedFields` suy ra từ diff.
- Thanh Lưu/Hủy **dính đầu trang** ở form sửa nhân viên.

## Điểm cần người review để mắt

- **Guard ép enroll 2FA (AUTH-003)** nới từ so sánh 1 path thành allow-list 2 path. Nếu chỉ loại trừ path shell, user bị ép enroll mở `/me/security/2fa` sẽ **bị đá ngược liên tục**. Guard này trước đó **không có test nào** — đã thêm `ProtectedShell.spec.tsx` và chứng minh RED (revert guard → đúng ca đó đỏ).
- **Màn `/me/profile/edit` chỉ mở ô cho `PROFILE_CHANGE_ALLOWED_FIELDS`.** Copy đủ section như màn HR sẽ cho nhân viên sửa mã NV/phòng ban/lương rồi bị server loại **âm thầm** (HR-ERR-040).
- **Actor-exclusion:** engine loại `payload.actorUserId` ⇒ tự duyệt yêu cầu của chính mình sẽ **không** sinh thông báo cho mình. Đúng thiết kế, nhưng cần biết khi test tay.

## Test plan

- [x] `TURBO_FORCE=1 pnpm typecheck` — 10/10 task, 0 cached
- [x] `TURBO_FORCE=1 pnpm lint` — 0 error
- [x] `TURBO_FORCE=1 pnpm test` — app 163 file/1169 test · web-core 583 · console 179 · ui 66 · auth 23 · api 3742 pass
- [x] **RED-proof 2 lần:** revert guard 2FA → đúng 1 ca đỏ; revert fix controller → đúng ca approve đỏ với 400
- [x] **Kiểm chứng chạy thật trên dev-online:** approve `200` → `outbox_events` = `done` → `notifications` sinh đúng 1 dòng cho chủ hồ sơ
- [ ] Xem bằng mắt trên `cian-dev` sau khi deploy FE (`m dev-online-fast`) — phần giao diện mới **chưa được nhìn trực tiếp**, chỉ verify bằng test DOM
- [ ] Kiểm tra tay: nhân viên A gửi yêu cầu → HR B duyệt → A nhận thông báo

- `test/foundation/foundation-audit.e2e-spec.ts > 3f` — đã stash toàn bộ thay đổi và chạy lại: **vẫn đỏ** trên master.

author: bronek
body:
`choice::and_then` branches may now return *different* choice types: the result is the grade-spliced superset — every branch's alternatives, normalized and deduplicated exactly as `choice_for` produces. Previously `_typelist_select_apply_result` mandated one common result type across all applicable branches. `and_then` is the join, the one operation licensed to cross the choice boundary; with the superset collapse, the fmap-from-bind derivation `x.transform(f) == x.and_then([](auto &&v) { return choice{f(FWD(v))}; })` holds for heterogeneous branches too.

```cpp
fn::choice_for<A, B>{A{}}.and_then(fn::overload{
    [](A) { return fn::choice<U>{U{}}; },
    [](B) { return fn::choice_for<V, W>{V{}}; }});
// before: error (branches must agree); now: choice_for<U, V, W>
```

Implementation notes:

- **The join engine is a detail-layer sibling of `transform`'s collapse fold, with the opposite convention for a result of Self's own kind**: the collapse keeps it whole (fmap nests the nominal atom), the join splices its alternatives (bind flattens). It is a separate fold precisely so `transform`'s meaning cannot shift.
- **copack.hpp names no monad**: the target template is deduced from Self (`Tpl<Ts...>` pattern), the same way the collapse gate takes its `Tpl` — the fold's splice overload deduces `Tpl<Us...>` generically behind an `is_kind` gate ("all results are instances of Self's template"). The engine is thereby consumer-agnostic — the shape #350's cluster arm will reuse.
- **No new conversions**: each branch's narrower choice reaches the superset through its `copack` base and the existing `is_superset_of`-constrained widening constructors; the alternative mapping, constexpr usability, and `noexcept` pricing of that path are probe-verified and pinned in the tests.
- **Diagnostics preserved verbatim**: when the results are not all choices the trait falls back to the select machinery — a convergent non-choice result still trips `and_then`'s own `some_choice` static_assert (deliberately loud, and pinned as *viable* in the suite: a mandate, not a constraint), a divergent one still trips select's assert, and an inapplicable callback still drops `and_then` from the overload set (asking answers).
- **`noexcept`** is computed from callback applicability plus the widening arms via the existing `_is_nothrow_rts_applicable` with the superset as the result type; a throwing-move alternative in one branch's choice correctly poisons the specification (pinned, with its positive control).
- Purely additive: everything now accepted was ill-formed before; convergent callbacks keep their exact types and behaviour (pinned against the pre-change baselines).

Tests: the superset join with disjoint and overlapping (deduplicated) alternatives, runtime paths down both branches with constexpr twins, `noexcept` pins including the widening-arm fixture, and the constraint probes above.

Verified on gcc and clang across Debug/Release and both `VALIDATE_CXX23` lanes, and on MSVC (build and ctest).

Closes #349

author: yenchang265-afk
body:
## What

Two rounds of usability improvements to the hub's visual loop creator, addressing rough edges flagged in `packages/hub/README.md`.

### 1. Guided creation (commit 2ecedbe)

**Starter templates per work-source type.** The new-kind landing screen previously offered a single "+ new kind" button that always loaded one hardcoded 2-stage backlog skeleton. It now shows a "Start a new kind" card grid with four templates — Backlog loop, PR sitter, Dependency sitter, CI sitter — one per `workSource` type, each a simplified echo of the shipped kind of the same shape. Templates live in a new pure module `packages/hub/src/web/creator/templates.ts`; each factory runs `LoopManifestSchema.parse` per call so schema defaults materialize (keeping `fromFlow` round-trips exact) and no template constant can alias live editor state.

**Inline terminal creation replaces `window.prompt()`.** `+ park` / `+ done` open an inline popover (`TerminalAddForm`): backlog kinds get a dropdown of the manifest's lifecycle statuses plus "(no status move)" and a "custom…" escape; other sources get a single optional free-text field. `+ stop` adds directly (stop never carries a status). Adding a terminal that already exists **selects** it instead of duplicating — matching `terminalId`'s outcome+status dedup semantics via new pure helpers `sameTerminalSpec` / `terminalStatusOptions` in `graphmodel.ts`.

### 2. Asset pickers, scaffolds, and a gen:prompts button (commit 7f53fb0)

**Leverage existing commands/agents/skills.** New `GET /api/assets` inventories the repo's agent personas (`prompts/agents/`), opencode command wrappers (`plugins/opencode/commands/`), and skills (`skills/`) with line-parsed frontmatter descriptions (no yaml dependency). The stage form's `command`/`agent` inputs become native datalist comboboxes fed by it, with a hint when the typed name doesn't exist yet.

**Create new assets from the hub.** `POST /api/assets/{agent,command,skill}` scaffold idiomatic one-shot stubs: personas take a **builder** (edit+bash allow) or **checker** (deny-all + `{{allowlist}}` marker + `loop_verdict` tools) permission preset, and selected skills are woven into `body.md` as "Invoke the `X` skill" prose — the shipped convention. The stage form's `+ new agent` / `+ new command` panels prefill from the typed values and write the created name back into the stage; a skill can be created inline from the agent form and comes back auto-checked. All writes are slug-validated, prefix-confined, and 409 on existing targets — never overwriting. The checker preset's response notes that gen:prompts needs a manifest `bashAllowlist` first (the generator throws on an unmatched marker).

**gen:prompts from the checklist.** The post-save checklist's "run `npm run gen:prompts`" item now renders a Confirm-gated "run now" button: `POST /api/gen-prompts` execFiles the repo's `scripts/gen-prompts.mjs` (30s timeout) and reports `{ok, output}` as a domain outcome. A new non-mutating `POST /api/kinds/checklist` recomputes the checklist after scaffolds/generator runs without re-saving (`"checklist"` joins `RESERVED_KINDS`). The README safety table documents the expanded creator write authority.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck -w @agentic-loop/hub` clean; `npm run test -w @agentic-loop/hub` — 162/162 pass (template round-trips, terminal-spec dedup consistency, asset inventory, stub contents, guard rejections, generator success/failure via a fake script, checklist recompute + reserved-name)
- Playwright smoke runs against the built hub for both rounds: all four template cards open valid; both popover variants and dedup-on-re-add behave; pickers populate from the live repo (17 agents / 22 commands); unknown-name hints appear; the inline skill→agent→command scaffold chain updates the stage; the saved checklist flips scaffolded items to done; a real gen:prompts run from the hub succeeds drift-free
- QA scaffolds and the throwaway kind were removed before committing

author: hallovorld
body:
## Summary

PART B of the G1 pilot-registration prep — the v5 prereg (RenQuant#494) **§4.7 rule 4 "mechanical checkability"** counters: `n_paired_sessions` **per epoch and per role (pilot / terminal / burned)**, so the ≥40-pilot prerequisite and every hygiene exclusion are auditable at activation from recorded manifests alone. Registration itself is NOT authorized; this ships dark and safe.

**Rev 2 — implements BOTH 2026-07-18 Codex review demand sets** (my chain's review + the parallel session's restated-as-live demands): snapshot regen, telemetry_status fail-closed stamping, immutable manifest binding, branch provenance (rebuilt from current `main` as a single hallovorld-authored commit, no co-author/session trailers).

## Design

- **New `shadow_ab_epoch_telemetry.py`** (derivation-only, read-only): deduplicates session records across the printed payload + on-disk bundle copies (root + `archive/`), enumerates the epoch registry (archived `epoch<N>-freeze-*` scopes + the live root freeze as the current epoch), and attributes each record to an epoch — `freeze_fingerprint` (stamped `subrepo_pins` + `orchestrator_commit` equal a recorded freeze) or location fallbacks.
- **Safe defaults, fail-safe roles:** no registration manifest → **everything burned**; a record whose epoch is not PROVEN by a freeze-fingerprint match can never be pilot/terminal; strict postdating of `registered_at` uses the sealed `decision_snapshot.as_of`, else the conservative 00:00 UTC reading (a registration-day session without a sealed as-of burns).
- **Role boundaries from COMMITTED manifests only:** registration (`epoch_id`, `registered_at`, `burned_sessions` inline or `burned_sessions_manifest` path — format matches the PART-A `RenQuant doc/experiments/g1-pilot/burned-sessions-manifest.json`); activation (`epoch_id`, `activated_at`). Activation without registration, or a differing epoch, is rejected (§4.7 two-stage start + rule 2 no-cross-epoch-pooling). The legacy root counter demonstrably continued across the epoch-2→3 refreeze (attempted 1→2 across worlds) — exactly the pooling blindness this replaces.
- **Immutable manifest binding (review demand 3):** a filesystem path is mutable, so role boundaries bind to CONTENT and COMMITS, not paths. A supplied registration manifest must carry `source_repository` + `source_commit` (or the stamped `pilot_registration_commit`) and — when referencing the external burned-sessions manifest — a `burned_sessions_manifest_sha256` the loaded file's raw bytes must hash to. A supplied activation manifest must additionally carry `registration_manifest_sha256` binding the exact registration content it activates. Callers can pin either file's raw-byte SHA-256 (`--registration-manifest-sha256` / `--activation-manifest-sha256`; wrapper env `RENQUANT_SHADOW_AB_{REGISTRATION,ACTIVATION}_MANIFEST_SHA256`, fail-closed if set without the manifest). Every load records the actual digest in the report's `manifest_bindings` block. **Any resolve/verify failure raises — no report, all sessions stay burned, activation ineligible.** The committed evidence artifacts stay in the umbrella repo; this repo owns only the derivation.
- **telemetry_status fail-closed stamping (review demand 2):** every successful report stamps `telemetry_status: "complete"` only after the per-epoch/per-role buckets re-reconcile against the per-session role assignments (`counts_reconciled`); the runner's recorded derivation-error payload stamps `telemetry_status: "unavailable"`. Contract (in the module docstring): the activation validator MUST require `complete` + reconciled counts — **no partial/error report may support the ≥40 condition**. Conservative scoping per the review-restatement: the completeness *signal* ships here; the full activation validator belongs to the activation-commit work.
- **Existing reporting surface:** the runner attaches `epoch_role_counters` to the returned session payload (printed into `session_<date>.json` by the daily wrapper) + writes a `shadow_ab_epoch_role_counters.json` sidecar, derived AFTER the session record lands so the current session is counted; derivation failures are recorded, never raised (telemetry is not load-bearing for the session verdict) — and the module import now sits INSIDE the try, so even a broken deploy of the telemetry module cannot kill a session. New read-only audit CLI `renquant-orchestrator shadow-ab-epoch-report`; the wrapper forwards optional `RENQUANT_SHADOW_AB_{REGISTRATION,ACTIVATION}_MANIFEST` env vars (fail-closed if set but missing).

## Tests

- `tests/test_shadow_ab_epoch_telemetry.py`: **34 tests** — the original 23 (safe default; strict postdating incl. as-of-less registration-day; cross-epoch burn; burned-list precedence; activation split + two-stage/same-epoch rejections; dedup; freeze vs location attribution; runner surface; CLI) + 11 new for the review demands: telemetry_status complete+reconciled (report + runner surface), `unavailable` on recorded failure, `manifest_bindings` recorded, missing source provenance / missing burned-manifest commitment / burned-manifest digest mismatch / registration pin mismatch (+ match accepts) / pin-without-path / activation missing or stale registration binding all fail closed, CLI pinned-digest-mismatch rejection.
- **M9 baseline regenerated** via `scripts/generate_strategy_snapshot.py --update` (the new `shadow-ab-epoch-report` subcommand + `shadow_ab_epoch_telemetry` module) — `test_snapshot_not_stale` is GREEN. Correcting this PR's earlier claim: that failure was NOT pre-existing; it was this PR's own regression, as the review proved.
- Full suite (scratch clone + scratch sibling clones): **4086 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed** — including `test_live_twin_parity_manifest_current` and the full `test_shadow_ab_daily_script.py` wrapper suite.

Companion: PART A (RenQuant#504) — the burned-sessions manifest this telemetry consumes (its side carries the overwritten/log-only session completeness fix).

author: cakezcodes
body:
## Problem

The Layers screen had toggles that did nothing: **synastry hits**, **composite transits**, **beauty timing**, and **sun ingresses** had no event generator behind them, so switching them on never surfaced anything on the calendar. On top of that, layer toggle state wasn't included in the cloud snapshot, so every choice reset to defaults on reload. Separately, the journal prompt on the home (sky) page rendered in the plain sans font while the event page used the serif treatment.

## Changes (all in `public/prototype/app.js`)

- **synastry hits** — fires when the transiting moon enters a sign that holds a personal planet (sun/moon/venus/mars) in both your chart and a tracked person's chart
- **composite transits** — fires when the moon enters the sign of the shorter-arc midpoint sun between you and a person (the composite sun)
- **beauty timing** — one event at each of the four lunar quarter turns, with phase-matched hair/skin/ink guidance
- **sun ingresses** — local fallback computed from the sun's day-over-day sign change; added an `ingress` case to the `mergeCloud` dedupe guard so cloud `global_events` rows don't double it
- **toggle persistence** — `LON` is now serialized into the `app_state` cloud snapshot (`__lon`), restored on boot, and flushed on every toggle from both the Layers screen and the quick-chips row
- **serif journal prompts** — the home-page journal prompt row now uses the `.sf` serif-italic treatment with quotation marks, matching the event detail page

## Verification

- Headless simulation over Jul–Sep 2026 with a natal date and one tracked person: beauty fires 4×/month at the quarter turns, synastry/composite/ingress each fire at sensible monthly rates, and a snapshot→restore roundtrip preserves toggle state
- `node --check` passes on the modified file; `npm run build` completes with no errors

body:
## Phase 2 — Company Intelligence and measurement

### Current code audit
- **Working today:** Website and public GitHub observation, PostHog metric sync, first-party tracking, workspace-scoped observations/opportunities, authenticated runtime tick, locks, idempotency, budget limits, approval-gated publishing, and the Phase 1 Company Runtime.
- **UI or configuration-dependent:** the connection UI can only show live external data after a workspace connects the provider; external scheduling still requires a trusted service to call `POST /api/runtime/tick`.
- **Manual paths:** `Run now`, reflection, and observation scans remain available as founder-controlled fallbacks.
- **Automatic paths:** due Observation/analytics jobs, Company Runtime cycles, and publication queue processing run only when the authenticated scheduler calls the tick endpoint. Disabled, paused, or manual-mode workspaces are skipped.
- **Phase 2 minimum closure:** use existing bounded Website/GitHub/PostHog/internal metrics to produce an auditable, workspace-scoped Company Intelligence snapshot before each runtime plan.

### What changed
- Added `company_intelligence_snapshots` migration and schema.
- Added a bounded Company Intelligence loader that reads only the active goal, two most recent metric rows, and connected provider names.
- Runtime updates active-goal progress and records a daily health score, metric delta, evidence summary, and data-readiness status before planning.
- Today now shows goal progress, metric movement, and Company Intelligence health.
- Scheduler ordering now completes due analytics/observation jobs before due Company Runtime cycles consume the state.
- Added tests for health scoring, workspace scoping, bounded metric history, runtime ordering, and migration packaging.

### Security and operating boundaries
- Every read/write is scoped by `workspace_id`.
- Connection secrets and raw connector payloads do not enter the intelligence snapshot or planner.
- No new external execution permission is granted; existing Policy Engine and approval boundaries remain in force.
- Google Search Console is intentionally deferred until a dedicated OAuth application and least-privilege scopes are configured. Atlas does not present it as connected prematurely.

### Verification
- `npm run db:generate`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm test` — 95 passing tests
- `bash scripts/validate-artifact.sh`
- Agent preview of the existing Site public route

### Deployment
This is a ChatGPT Sites change. The `DB` binding is unchanged, and migration `0014_company_intelligence.sql` is required by the packaged artifact validation. No production Site version was published from this branch.

### Manual verification
1. Open Today for a workspace with an active goal and at least one metric snapshot.
2. Run Company Runtime.
3. Confirm Today shows Company Intelligence health, metric delta, and active-goal progress.
4. Connect PostHog, run the trusted tick, then confirm the next Company Runtime cycle consumes the refreshed metric state.

body:
M5 Slice 5a (gofer half) — makes session titles live end-to-end. Re-pins agent-sdk-go to **v0.8.0** (the session-title seam) and generates a title from the first prompt.

## What it adds
- **Re-pin** agent-sdk-go v0.7.0 → v0.8.0.
- **Title generation** (`internal/supervisor/managed.go`): a deterministic `snippet()` heuristic — first non-empty line → whitespace-collapse → truncate to 60 runes on a word boundary (+ `…`); whitespace-only → none. Hooked in `enqueue`, emitted once via `m.sess.Emit(event.NewSessionInfoUpdated(id, title))`, **set-once** by the existing `m.title == ""` gate (no per-turn re-emit; a blank first prompt lets a later one supply the title). The SDK projects it to `session_info_update` for peers — pass-through.
- **Lossless bridge** (`internal/daemonbridge`): `session.info` reconstructs in the gofer/event replay like every other kind.

Title *generation* is the app's job (per the SDK membership line); LLM-summary titles / a rename path are future enhancements that slot into the same seam.

## Verification
- Daemon-path test: first prompt → peer receives `session_info_update{title}`; second prompt does not re-emit. Heuristic unit tests (first-line/collapse/word-boundary/hard-cut/empty). Fidelity test proves the title round-trips losslessly through gofer/event.
- Gates green: build/vet/test/golangci-lint (0 issues), `-race` clean. Independent go-reviewer: **clean, ship it**.

author: shojuro
body:
## Summary

Second remediation wave from the 2026-07-18 audit — the Low items best cleared before external distribution. All five reviewed (opus, approved) and live-verified.

| Fix | Audit item |
|-----|-----------|
| Re-verify model sha256 before load (session-cached, fail-closed) | sec-rust #5 — TOCTOU / arbitrary GGUF into llama.cpp |
| Kill orphan `llama-server` by tracked PID, not image name | sec-rust #3 — old sweep killed every instance + other apps |
| Delete dormant one-time-payment webhook branch (`EXPECTED` gone) | sec-edge #2 — latent lifetime over-grant on amount-only validation |
| Devices table caps: length + 50 rows/user (migration 0008) | sec-db L-1 — storage/cost abuse |
| escapeHtml on all catalog `innerHTML` interpolations (+ cover `src`) | sec-client — defense-in-depth XSS |

## Live verification

- **Re-verify at load:** streams the resolved model through SHA-256, compares to the catalog's pinned hash before spawning llama-server; mismatch → refuse + `engine-failed`. Hashed once per process (watchdog respawns skip). Rust suite **115 pass**.
- **Kill-by-PID:** pid file written on spawn / removed on kill; sweep double-filters `PID eq N` AND `IMAGENAME eq llama-server.exe` (reuse-safe); absent pid → no-op. Strictly safer than the old kill-all.
- **Webhook (redeployed, live-tested):** a legacy `checkout.session.completed` event now returns `200 {received:true}` with **zero entitlements written** (no retry storm, no one-time grant); subscription `invoice.paid` still grants. Grandfathered rows untouched.
- **Devices caps (applied live):** pre-checked the populated table (7 rows, 0 violations) before the validating ALTER; 3 length constraints + cap trigger present, EXECUTE revoked; UPSERT re-registration exempt via the `(user_id, fingerprint)` key.
- **escapeHtml:** all catalog-origin `innerHTML` sites wrapped; `textContent` sinks untouched; no-op for current ASCII values (no layout change).

Details in `docs/superpowers/verification-milestone-phase1-hardening.md`. MSI rebuilt.

## Deferred
**MSI code-signing** — needs a purchased cert (Azure Trusted Signing ~\$10/mo, or OV/EV). One-step config wiring once a thumbprint exists. Plus the Phase-2 Info items.

body:
## 使用者回報的三個錯誤顯示

| 現況（錯） | 修好後 |
|---|---|
| 停車費（聯信（Times Parking股份有）） | 停車費（台灣普客二四） |
| 停車費（停車場（Times）） | 停車費（台灣普客二四） |
| 停車費（停車場（俥亭停車）） | 停車費（俥亭停車） |

## 根因（兩層疊加）

1. **規則缺口**：帳單原文是 `聯信-台灣普客二四股份有A0145 TAIPEI`、`連加*?亭停車事業股份Taipei`——
   - 「聯信-」＝聯合信用卡中心（收單方），不是店名，但金流前綴白名單漏了它 → 「聯信」被誤當主體
   - 「股份有」「事業股份」＝銀行截字殘尾，舊規則只認完整的「股份有限公司」
   - 「?亭」＝「俥」超出 Big5 的銀行缺字
2. **舊資料自我鎖死**：已寫入的 note 包著「停車費（…）」標記（巢狀括號），「店名格式整理」的規則比不到 → 怎麼跑都治不好；學習表還存有舊版時代的錯名（`停車場（Times）`），下次匯入又蓋回來

## 修法

- `cleanStore`：金流前綴加 `聯信-`、缺字修補 `?亭停車→俥亭停車`、新增 `COMPANY_TAIL` 殘尾修剪
- **台灣普客二四改回中文名**（反轉 #89 的 →Times Parking；使用者定 2026-07-18）：`BRAND_CANON` 統一中英寫法

body:
## Summary

Hardens `MagicLink` (the magnetic animated link component) per the tiger-review plan.

## Changes

- **Default `rel` for new-tab links**: external links now resolve `rel` to `noopener noreferrer` when `target="_blank"` and the caller didn't supply one. Previously `rel` was passed through verbatim, so a caller doing `<MagicLink href={ext} target="_blank" />` shipped a reverse-tabnabbing vector.
- **Prop forwarding**: the component now accepts and forwards `...rest: AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>` (e.g. `aria-label`, `id`, `data-*`, `onClick`) onto both the internal `motion.create(Link)` branch and the external `motion.a` branch. Previously arbitrary anchor attrs were silently dropped.
- **Types**: `target`/`rel` are now sourced from `AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>` instead of loose `string`, so they match the rest of the anchor prop surface. The forwarded-rest type omits motion-overlapping handlers (`onDrag`, `onDragStart`, `onDragEnd`, `onAnimationStart/End/Iteration`) whose signatures conflict with motion/react's `PanInfo`-carrying variants.
- **JSDoc accuracy**: corrected the doc comment — internal links use `motion.create(Link)` (not a plain `<a>`), and `target` is caller-supplied (not hardcoded to `_blank`).

## Verification

- `pnpm exec biome check --write` — clean.
- `cd apps/web && npx tsc --noEmit` — no errors in `magic-link.tsx`. (The 4 pre-existing errors in `src/routes/blog/$slug.tsx` are unrelated and tracked by the `blog-slug-types` PR.)

author: hafizmmoaz
body:
## Issue

zerp-pk/account#3 - the `?sort=` and `?direction=` query params were passed straight into `orderBy()` in the listing controllers. Eloquent binds *values* but not *identifiers*, so a crafted sort/direction was interpolated into the SQL text.

## Fix

Root-cause, single point: a `sortSafe` Builder macro registered in `AccountServiceProvider::boot()`.

- Column is accepted only if `Schema::hasColumn($table, $sort)` is true, else it falls back to a safe default (`created_at`).
- Direction is accepted only if it is `asc` or `desc` (case-insensitive), else the default.

The 12 listing controllers now call `->sortSafe(...)` instead of interpolating the raw request values.

## Tested

Verified locally against the running app: valid sorts still work, and crafted `?sort=`/`?direction=` payloads are ignored rather than reaching SQL.

author: theteepeenetwork
body:
First of a three-PR stack for **SJ-06 (per-class age mode)**. This is the foundation — the switch itself, asked once and stored. **Nothing child-facing consumes it yet**; that's deliberate, so this ships with zero visual risk. The register swaps + type scale come in PR B, and jar → journal in PR C.

## What this does
- **Schema:** `Class.ageMode` — `"KS1"` (younger) | `"KS2"` (older) | `NULL`. Additive, nullable, `db push`, no data migration.
- **`NULL` means KS1** — the younger, more protective default (SAFEGUARDING rule 8). It is **never** inferred from `yearGroup` (only the signup class has one, and it's free text).
- **`src/lib/ageMode.ts`** — the single place `NULL`/unknown resolves to `KS1` (`resolveAgeMode`) and the single place a form value is sanitised before storage (`normaliseAgeModeInput`). Child-facing code must go through the resolver, never read the column raw.
- **Asked once at class creation**, on both paths: `createClass` (additional classes) and the signup wizard's class step (first class).

## The Children's Code bit
The ICO Children's Code forbids **nudging** a choice that shapes a child's screen. So:
- **Nothing is pre-selected** — neither radio is defaulted.
- **Skipping is a real answer** — it stores `NULL` → younger, server-side.
- Wording is even-handed: no "recommended", no ordering that implies a preferred option.

## Safeguarding
- **Rule 9 (retention before a new field):** `RETENTION.md` gains a row for `Class.ageMode` **in this PR**. It's a teacher's per-class display setting — holds nothing about any child, never attributed/aggregated/exported, deleted with the class. (Like the rest of `RETENTION.md`, the doc still awaits DPO sign-off overall, but this field introduces no child personal data.)
- **Rule 8:** deny-by-default → the absence of a choice yields the protective register.

## Tests
`tests/e2e/age-mode-creation.spec.ts` (functional gate):
- choosing "older children" stores `KS2`;
- skipping stores `NULL`;
- **proved red** — neither option is pre-selected (temporarily default-checking the younger radio fails this test).

Stored state is asserted straight from the DB (the `PrismaClient` pattern the Stripe-webhook spec uses), since PR A has no child-facing surface to read.

## Gates
Green locally: **e2e (102)**, **security (72) + a11y (103)** (the a11y gate axe-checks the new radios), **static-security**, **motion**.

author: laurenbmoody-web
body:
## What

Adds a **Detect rooms** action to each framed deck on the deck-plan view. It reads the deck with Claude vision and proposes room outlines the crew then refine — the "bells and whistle" auto-trace: it reads the room names off the drawing and lands editable footprints.

## How

- **New edge function `deck-plan-autotrace`** (modelled on `review-supplier-cert`'s vision pattern, same `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Receives one framed-deck image (base64 JPEG) + the deck name + the crew's existing room names; returns `{ rooms: [{ name, points[], confidence }] }` — each a polygon normalized 0..1 to the image. It only reads and proposes: no DB writes, no room creation.
- **Client (`DeckPlanView`)**: the button crops that deck's band out of the GA image into base64 (same 0..1 deck-crop space the plan uses), invokes the function, and matches read labels to existing rooms (exact key, then a contained-name fallback). Matched rooms render as **dashed, labelled proposals**; a review bar shows *"AI read N rooms — M matched"* with a Curved/Straight toggle, **Apply**, and **Discard**. Apply writes the smoothed outline + centre point onto each matched room — identical to a hand trace, ready to fine-tune in the existing tracing editor.

## Notes

- No migration — `plan_shape` already shipped with the tracing editor; this is edge-function + client only.
- The model *proposes*, the human *perfects*: unmatched labels are listed (not auto-created), and every outline is editable after Apply.
- `./node_modules/.bin/vite build` passes.

author: shunsock
body:
## 概要

`configs/claude/rules/software_writing.md` の「コメント」節に、コードコメントへ issue 番号・PR 番号・チケット ID を書かない旨のルールを 1 行追記した。

Closes #344

## 背景

実案件のレビューで、除外処理の意図を `# 非稼働クライアント (issue #665) のテストは...` のようにコメントに書いた際、「コードにイシュー番号を書かないでください」との指摘を受けて削除した経緯があった。同種の判断を Claude / 人間の双方に繰り返してもらうためには、上位ルール側にも明文化しておく必要がある。

`configs/claude/skills/template/comment_markers.md` は既に issue/PR 番号を強く禁止しており (L36 / L69–72)、SEE の対象を RFC / 仕様 / ベンダー doc / ファイルパスに限定している。ただしこれは 2 スキル (`write__structured_comment` / `clean__comment_out`) の内部契約であり、汎用のライティング規範を集める `configs/claude/rules/software_writing.md` 側には同等の記述が抜けていた。

## 課題

issue 番号は**一過性の経緯**である。issue は close / リナンバリング / 移管され、参照される PR は squash-merge で番号が変わることもある。コードコメントにこれらを埋め込むと、コードが生きている間ずっと追跡不能なポインタや古い参照が蓄積していく。

一方で、除外・回避の Why (設計判断・制約・トレードオフ) はコメントに残す価値がある。両者を分離するルールが上位ルールに明文化されておらず、レビュー時の判断が個々のレビュアーの経験に依存していた。

## 目標

### 必須項目

- `configs/claude/rules/software_writing.md` の「コメント」節に「一過性の経緯 (issue 番号・PR 番号・チケット ID) はコメントに書かない。commit / PR 側に記す」旨を明示する

### 範囲外

- `comment_markers.md` の SEE 説明の追記 (issue の任意受入基準)。当該ファイルは既に issue/PR 番号を明示禁止し、SEE の対象も RFC / 仕様 / ベンダー doc / ファイルパスに限定済みのため、二重の記述を避けて今回は見送る
- 過去の bullet の並び順やインデントの変更
- コード側 (`configs/claude/skills/` など) のコメント刈り

## 採用手法

issue #344 の提案手法の差分をそのまま採用する。挿入位置は「自明な処理にコメントを付けない」の直後、「TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX 等の標準マーカーを活用し、未解決事項を明示する」の直前。禁止対象を issue 番号だけでなく PR 番号・チケット ID にも広げ、「commit メッセージや PR 説明に記す」という代替行き先までを 1 bullet で明示する。

### 検討した選択肢

| 選択肢 | 長所 | 短所 |
|--------|------|------|
| A: 該当 bullet を 1 行に流す (採用) | 周辺の bullet がすべて 1 行で、`configs/claude/rules/` 内の一貫性が保てる。文の途中で改行しないというグローバル方針とも整合 | 1 行が長くなる |
| B: issue の diff どおり 3 行折り返しで挿入 | issue のコピペで済む | L18 末尾が「恒久的に」で切れる文中ハードラップとなり、`validate__japanese` の運用方針 (文の途中で改行しない) と周辺 bullet の書式に反する |
| C: `comment_markers.md` にも SEE 補足を追加 | issue の任意受入基準を満たせる | 既に該当ファイルが同じ規範を強く明示しており、二重で書くと drift の原因になる |

### 採用理由

`configs/claude/rules/*.md` は「グローバル Claude ルール」の source of truth で、対象読者は Claude 本体と人間レビュアーの両方。他の bullet がすべて 1 行で書かれているため、A を採ることで見た目・grep しやすさ・改行方針のいずれも一貫する。textlint 実行後も指摘 0 件。

C については `comment_markers.md` が既に同じ規範を強く定義しており、そちらは 2 スキル間の契約 (writer / cleaner) の single source of truth として機能している。今回の追記でルール自体は上位側にも入るため、規範の drift を避けるためにも C は見送った。

## 変更箇所

- \`configs/claude/rules/software_writing.md\`: 「コメント」節に issue/PR/チケット番号をコメントに書かない旨の bullet を 1 項目追加

## 妥協と制限

- **既存コメントの遡及修正はしない**: 本 PR はルール文言のみを追加する。リポジトリ内の既存コメントで issue 番号を含むものがあっても、この PR では触らない。必要になった時点で別途 `clean__comment_out` や手動修正で対応する

## 検証方法

- \`git diff configs/claude/rules/software_writing.md\` が追加 1 行のみで、他節・末尾改行が変更されていないことを確認した
- \`validate__japanese\` スキル (textlint + preset-ja-technical-writing + preset-ja-spacing) を実行し、指摘 0 件で通過した
- 挿入位置が「自明な処理にコメントを付けない」の直後、「TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX」の直前であることを Read で確認した

## 確認事項

- ⚠️ issue の diff は 3 行折り返しだが、周辺 bullet の一貫性と改行方針に合わせて 1 行に連結して採用した。この改変を許容してよいかを確認したい
- ⚠️ \`comment_markers.md\` への SEE 補足 (issue の任意受入基準) は、既に同ファイル内で同等の明示禁止が存在するため見送った。追加すべきという判断であれば別 PR で対応する

## 参考文献

- [Issue #344 ルール追加: コードコメントに issue 番号を書かない](https://github.com/shunsock/dotfiles/issues/344)
- \`configs/claude/skills/template/comment_markers.md\` (L36, L69–72) — issue/PR 番号を明示禁止する既存記述

author: whyihaveyou
body:
## Problem
When a process is killed between `step.begin` and the first `content.part`/`tool.call` (terminal crash, external timeout SIGKILL, etc.), the replayed history keeps an assistant message with empty `content` and empty `toolCalls` at its tail. Providers reject empty assistant messages with `400`, so **every subsequent resume of that session fails** — the session is effectively bricked until the user hand-edits `wire.jsonl`.

Fixes #1404.

## Fix
Repair at replay time in `ContextMemory.finishResume()`: after the existing interrupted-tool-result closing, drop trailing assistant messages that have neither content nor tool calls, and clamp `tokenCountCoveredMessageCount` to the shortened history so the covered/pending split stays exact.

Deliberately does **not** touch the record write path (`step.begin` keeps recording as before): the torn records are re-dropped idempotently on every resume, which keeps the change low-risk and self-healing.

## Tests
`packages/agent-core/test/agent/finish-resume.test.ts` (4 new cases):
- drops a trailing empty assistant left by a killed turn
- drops several consecutive empty tails
- keeps a trailing assistant that has content
- keeps a trailing assistant with tool calls (exchange closes with an interrupted error result)

Also updated the generation-failure turn test to assert the repaired behavior (via an optional `expectResumeMatches` snapshot transform) — the pre-fix verbatim resume match used to require the empty tail.

Full `test/agent test/session test/services` suite: 1451 passed, 0 failed. Typecheck clean.

## Reproduction context
- kimi-code 0.26.0 (linux/x64), session resumed via `kimi -p -r session_<id> --output-format stream-json`
- process killed mid-turn by an external supervisor's per-message timeout (cc-connect)
- confirmed workaround before the fix: deleting the trailing incomplete records from `wire.jsonl` restored the session

author: dawidrylko
body:
## What

Adds a dedicated Quartz emitter (`quartz/plugins/emitters/llmstxt.ts`) that writes a Markdown `llms.txt` to the build output root, served at `https://dawid.dev/llms.txt`. Registered in `quartz.config.ts` next to the existing `Robots` emitter.

## Why

Satisfies the `agentReadiness` check shipped in `@silesiansolutions/search-quality-kit` v0.10.0 (rules replicate the Lighthouse `llms-txt` audit plus the llmstxt.org blockquote recommendation). Gives AI agents and answer engines a curated map of the site.

## Approach

`llms.txt` is a root-level, agent-facing plain-text file — a sibling of `robots.txt`. This repo already emits `robots.txt` through a committed `Robots` emitter override (upstream Quartz 4.5.2 ships none), so this mirrors that established pattern rather than:

- dropping the file into `content/`, where Quartz's Markdown pipeline could transform it, or
- placing it under `quartz/static/`, which emits to `/static/`, not the site root.

URLs are derived from `baseUrl`, exactly like `Robots`.

## Verification

Built Quartz v4.5.2 and confirmed `public/llms.txt` is emitted verbatim at the root. Ran `search-quality-kit@0.10.0 verify` in static mode against the build with `checks.agentReadiness` on:

- 50 pages crawled — **0 findings** (0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 info).
- No `agent-readiness.llms-txt-*` findings.
- Negative control (same build with `llms.txt` removed) fires `agent-readiness.llms-txt-missing`, confirming the check is active.
- No `<form>` elements in the built HTML, so WebMCP annotations are N/A.

Mirrors the showcase site added to the kit (`examples/showcase/sites/dawiddev.config.ts`, http mode); the live origin will pass once deployed.

- [x] RoundEnd に次ラウンドの手札枚数が表示される
- [x] 切り札選択者（ラウンド勝者）が表示される

author: tonytony32
body:
## The bug

The overlay drops into ambient mode (♫ glyph, 120×120 window) when
`connectionState == .connected && currentTrack == nil`.

But when a loopback source (YouTube) is the active one, `SourceArbiter` always
publishes `.connected`, and the `jellyfinIsActiveSource` gate makes
`PlayerStore.updateConnection` discard the *real* `.reconnecting` / `.error`
the Jellyfin transport is reporting. So off the home network:

- the ambient state wears an "everything's fine" face;
- tapping it (`NothingPlayingView.onTapGesture` → `ClientLauncher.openJellyfin`)
  opens the Safari web app against an unreachable URL → blank window;
- and `markAnticipating()` then holds the chrome visible for 30 s waiting on
  music that can't arrive.

## The fix

1. **`PlayerStore.jellyfinLinkHealth`** — an ungated `private(set)` signal,
   written in `updateConnection` and `ingest` *before* the gate, following the
   existing `jellyfinHasNowPlaying` pattern. A successful `ingest` means the
   server answered, so it records `.connected` there.
2. **`NothingPlayingView`** takes `linkIsDown` and renders a `wifi.slash` glyph
   instead of the notes when home is down. Same opacity / hover / snap
   treatment, so it reads as the same affordance in a different mood.
3. **Tap with the link down** shows a transient — "Can't reach Jellyfin here" —
   and does *not* launch or call `markAnticipating()`.
4. **Link live → byte-for-byte the previous behaviour.**

`OverlayView.jellyfinLinkIsDown` maps the health signal with an exhaustive
switch, so a future `ConnectionState` case can't silently fall through to
"reachable".

### On the toast copy

Worth recording, because it constrains anything added to this state later: the
ambient footprint is a fixed **120×120 for every theme**
(`OverlayWindowController.applyWindowSizeForCurrentState`), and
`TransientToastView` renders *inside that same window*. The first draft — "Can't
reach your Jellyfin server from this network." — wrapped to three lines and
covered half the square, burying the `wifi.slash` it was meant to explain. The
shorter string fits two lines, clears the glyph, and matches the phrasing of the
existing `unreachableHint` ("Can't reach the server right now.").

A badge variant ("Jellyfin unreachable" in a capsule, in place of the glyph) was
prototyped and rejected for the same reason: at 120pt it either shrinks to fit
or becomes a card filling the square, and the tap's toast then lands on top of
it. The badge and the toast also say the same sentence one tap apart, and at
rest the badge isn't legible anyway (chrome opacity 0, glyph at 0.35).

## Tests

Added `gatedUpdatesStillTrackJellyfinLinkHealth` to
`PlayerStoreSourceGatingTests`: while gated, `updateConnection(.reconnecting)`
and `.error` update `jellyfinLinkHealth` without touching the YouTube-owned
shared state, and a gated `ingest` restores it to `.connected`.

Full suite green: 106 tests, 14 suites.

## Manual test — NOT YET RUN

The SwiftUI layer has no test coverage and **these steps have not been executed**
— the layout was checked against a geometry-faithful mock at 120×120, not the
running app. Please run them before merging. Off the home network, with YouTube
playing through the bridge:

1. Play a video, confirm the overlay shows the YouTube track as usual.
2. Stop it and let the overlay collapse to ambient. **Expect:** `wifi.slash`,
   not the ♫ notes.
3. Hover it — glyph brightens to full opacity as before; glass chrome fades in.
4. Click it. **Expect:** the toast "Can't reach Jellyfin here" over a still-
   visible glyph, no Safari web app opening, and the chrome fading back out
   after the toast rather than sticking for 30 s.
5. Back on the home network: ambient shows the ♫ notes again and the tap opens
   the Jellyfin client exactly as before.

author: fabiandistler
body:
## Summary

Adds **`skills/ddd-conventions/`** — the implementation-time counterpart to `ddd-advisor`, distilled from Vlad Khononov, *Learning Domain-Driven Design* (O'Reilly, 2021). Where `ddd-advisor` guides the *design conversation* (classify subdomains, pick a pattern, map contexts), `ddd-conventions` holds the non-obvious rules that correct a coding model's likely defaults while *writing* domain code:

- **Aggregates:** exactly one instance per DB transaction; reference by ID, never by object; version field + optimistic check-and-set; root-only public API; past-tense domain events
- **Value objects:** fight primitive obsession; validate once at construction; equality-by-value, no identity field
- **Transaction scripts:** any DB write + success signal over a process boundary is a distributed transaction — make writes idempotent
- **Event sourcing:** events as the source of truth, append-only; command flow load→project→execute→append; CQRS required
- **Integration:** outbox pattern instead of dual-write `save(); bus.publish()`; never share a DB across bounded contexts
- **Boundaries:** size a bounded context by its model, start wide and decompose later; BC ≠ subdomain; one team per context

## Advisor backfills

Gaps the conventions exposed in the existing skills:

- **`ddd-advisor`:**
  - **Open-Host Service / published language** added to the context-mapping table — the upstream mirror of the ACL was missing entirely
  - **Pattern→architecture mapping table** (transaction script → minimal 3-layer, active record → layered + service layer, domain model → hexagonal, event-sourced → CQRS; CQRS whenever multiple read models are needed)
  - **Bidirectional sanity check** between tactical pattern and strategic classification
  - Cross-link to `ddd-conventions` in Related skills
- **`architecture-pattern-advisor`:** "start wide, decompose later" boundary heuristic — refactoring logical boundaries is cheap, moving physical service boundaries is expensive, so "as small as possible" is an anti-heuristic

## Wire-up

Per repo convention: plugin symlink under `plugins/architecture/skills/`, regenerated `skills.json` via `scripts/build_manifest.py`, marketplace/plugin descriptions, README/AGENTS catalogue rows. No `kb/` symlink (the skill has no `references/` dir).

## Verification

All CI sync checks pass locally: `build_manifest.py --check`, `check_docs.py`, `check_plugins.py` (35 skills), `compileall`.

body:
## Summary

- add a bounded XNYS calendar adapter with holiday, early-close, DST, and deterministic clock support
- derive fail-closed market state, entry-window policy, freshness boundaries, and pure schedule plans
- expose a read-only market-state API and responsive ET/Chicago status panel
- document the macOS Docker workflow and extend smoke verification

## Why

Milestone 2 establishes the exchange-calendar and scheduling contracts required by later market-data, scanner, risk, and paper-execution milestones. It remains paper-only and does not execute jobs, connect to providers or brokers, or expose trading controls.

## Developer impact

- market calculations use aware UTC timestamps and XNYS regular sessions
- exchange time is displayed in ET and the configured user timezone defaults to America/Chicago
- schedule planning is deterministic and returns idempotent run definitions without starting workers
- calendar initialization and invalid clock values fail closed

## Review fix

Final review found that calendar failures during FastAPI dependency construction could bypass the route-level 503 handling, and that a custom clock could supply a naive datetime. The application now handles calendar errors at the application boundary and normalizes or rejects clock values before calendar lookup.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-lab-note-pipeline-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-18-lab-note-pipeline.md`.

## What's inside

- **`Capture.title` widened `string` → `Text`** (B1 pattern, no migration): inbox payload validator accepts `string | { en?, fr? }`, admin inbox/triage render via `resolveText`, triage Name/Name (fr) prefill via strict `textPart`, live Mongo `$jsonSchema` widened (`npm run validators` already applied).
- **`scripts/lab-note/`** — self-contained mini-package (js-yaml only, own lockfile → ~2s `npm ci --prefix` in CI): pure `lib.mjs` (section extraction, contract validation, payload mapping, outcome classification; 18 unit tests) + thin CLI `post.mjs` (live PR-body fetch so editing a merged PR + re-run picks up fixes; dry-run mode; distinct exit codes 0/2/3/4/5).
- **`.github/workflows/lab-note.yml`** — reusable workflow: `workflow_call` for sibling-repo stubs (@main = always-current logic), `workflow_dispatch` rehearsal/backfill (dry-run by default), and a `pull_request: closed` self-trigger so ariko dogfoods the same file.
- **Docs** — README "Lab Note pipeline" section (contract, caller stub, secret setup, rehearsal) + ROADMAP C1a entry.

Deferred to follow-up plans (per spec rollout §9): the authoring-skill plugin + pbbls skill rewrite, sibling-repo stub fan-out, and the C1 go-live hardening items (E11000 retry, constant-time token compare, body-size guard).

body:
Previously only **script policies** could run a remediation (auto on monitor failure). This extends remediation to **every policy** — template/standard rules too — with both automatic and on-demand runs. Per the chosen behaviour: **auto on alert + manual**, remediation is **any script from the library** (standard or custom).

## Backend
- **DB:** `monitor_rules` gains `remediation_script_id` (in `CREATE TABLE` + additive migration). `create/update_monitor_rule`, `MonitorRuleRequest`, and the create/update endpoints carry it (validated via `_resolve_remediation`). New `db.raised_alert_keys(device_id)` helper.
- **Auto-remediation:** `alerts.evaluate_once()` now snapshots each device's raised alert-keys **before** and **after** evaluation and **returns** the newly-raised rules that have a remediation script (on online devices) — no change to the ~12 alert branches. `_alert_loop` executes each via the async `_exec_script_on_device` (run name `auto-remediation: <rule>`). Covers backup rules too (`backup_*` keys).

## Frontend
- **Rule form:** new optional **Remediation script** picker (any script), always shown for alerting policies; persisted on create/edit. Rows show `· fix: <script>`.
- **Manual run:** an always-available **Remediate** button on every policy row (rules *and* script policies) opens a small modal — pick an **online target device** + a **script** (defaults to the policy's configured remediation) — and runs it via the existing `POST /api/scripts/{id}/run` (which enforces device access).

## Test
- `python -m py_compile` main/alerts/database/models ✓
- `node --check app.js` ✓; all modal ids present ✓
- Auto-remediation only fires on the raise transition and only when the device is online (can't script an offline box).

Deletes the unused `cn()` helper at `apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts` and removes its now-unused direct dependencies `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` from `apps/web/package.json`.

## Why

`cn()` (the shadcn `clsx` + `tailwind-merge` combo) has **zero importers** in `apps/web/src` — grep confirmed no file imports `#/lib/utils`, `cn(`, `clsx`, or `tailwind-merge` anywhere except `utils.ts` itself. author: huynhngochuyhoang
body:
This pull request introduces enhanced diagnostics and observability for the reactive HTTP client, focusing on improved attribution of connection pool acquisition failures and expanded diagnostics reporting. The main changes include surfacing a new failure stage (`POOL_ACQUIRE`) for proven connection pool acquisition errors, updating metrics and logs to include this information, and extending diagnostics outputs (Markdown, JSON, and Actuator) to report effective connection pool configuration per client.

**Enhanced error attribution and observability:**

* `HttpClientFailureStage` and the new `failure.stage` field are introduced to clearly indicate when a failure is due to a proven connection pool acquisition problem, both in metrics and in logs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bf672eb5586e22daf308fa33fc79aa6592eaebe85c67473a9abe500d5a9e4f34R98-R103) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-726be236cc6b2081a3d13223b4d390c70e44725b7e8c1901a1601b4e86963158R29) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-726be236cc6b2081a3d13223b4d390c70e44725b7e8c1901a1601b4e86963158R285) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d654cd2b4928215e5e692b2e6395c15caf6e8d390c1692309c8ad8f6f3c040ecR51-R52) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-d654cd2b4928215e5e692b2e6395c15caf6e8d390c1692309c8ad8f6f3c040ecR72) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-d654cd2b4928215e5e692b2e6395c15caf6e8d390c1692309c8ad8f6f3c040ecR120-R122) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-2cded1fe4de2ace00d062f92d9bae01c5ee5d8d04f8b7fb4ea251efa31ded759R4) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-2cded1fe4de2ace00d062f92d9bae01c5ee5d8d04f8b7fb4ea251efa31ded759R48-R52) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-f0c00097d9798c609db15bd36b5635628312d2e28777c23e84e6a4e2ea8fd0c2R222-R245)

* Documentation is updated to explain the new failure stage, how to diagnose pool saturation, and how this information is surfaced in observability and diagnostics outputs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eeb4f3efb1db3997dea967311725710bb80eee46888185036750a9ca360f4a88R79-R98) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-580f05f15143845cbe7c93e084009bb9e5b2094df3e7b69bf11aafbab181c5a5R19)

**Diagnostics and health reporting improvements:**

* The Actuator health indicator and diagnostics provider now report the count of pool acquire failures (`poolAcquireFailureCount`), and expose the effective pool configuration (source, max connections, pending acquire timeout, metrics policy) for each client. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-580f05f15143845cbe7c93e084009bb9e5b2094df3e7b69bf11aafbab181c5a5R46-R52) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-580f05f15143845cbe7c93e084009bb9e5b2094df3e7b69bf11aafbab181c5a5L63-R65) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-580f05f15143845cbe7c93e084009bb9e5b2094df3e7b69bf11aafbab181c5a5L122-R124) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3cf9307e87fed5de3406a3162012033c5272ba1b2daa1044299246e906d8c134R12-R15) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-af528a3ce5d1274e17bc8483781667ff937ad622f444f1fce4915e0b42686598L86-R87) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-af528a3ce5d1274e17bc8483781667ff937ad622f444f1fce4915e0b42686598R124-R138) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-af528a3ce5d1274e17bc8483781667ff937ad622f444f1fce4915e0b42686598L295-R320)

* The diagnostics snapshot (Markdown, JSON) and schema are updated to include the new pool configuration fields, ensuring support and operations teams have visibility into client pool settings. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9bc113d9bb2e083e223ac355fe27c6f3cfe3f7868ffed8af773fa59a578cd1c7L78-R85) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9bc113d9bb2e083e223ac355fe27c6f3cfe3f7868ffed8af773fa59a578cd1c7R128-R131) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9bc113d9bb2e083e223ac355fe27c6f3cfe3f7868ffed8af773fa59a578cd1c7R181-R184)

These changes make it easier to diagnose connection pool issues, attribute failures to the correct stage, and audit client configuration for support and operational troubleshooting.

body:
## Problem

The decision tree under §4 **Workflow Selection Guide** (`09_Workflows_Chapter`, ko/en/ja) had three overlaps — including the rectangle↔arrow overlap reported:

1. **box↔box** — `Fan-out` and `Routing` result boxes overlapped ~80px on the right branch.
2. **arrow↔box** — `Q3 "Yes→Verify"` connector ran its horizontal (`y=155`) straight **through the Pipeline result box** (`x60–220, y135–175`).
3. **arrow↔box** *(pre-existing)* — `Q4 "No→Routing"` connector started at Q4's **center** and cut through Q4's question text along its midline; its "No" label also sat inside Q4 (unlike Q1-No, which correctly starts at the box edge).

## Fix

- Widened `viewBox` 660→780 and re-spaced Q4 / Fan-out / Routing so no boxes overlap (adopts the validated layout from PR #53).
- Rerouted **Q3 Yes→Verify** below the Pipeline box (down→left→down through the `y175–200` corridor).
- Rerouted **Q4 No→Routing** to start at Q4's right edge (`x680`) and moved its label into the gap right of Q4.

## Verification

Parsed every `<rect>`/`<line>` in the patched SVG for all three locales — **0 box-box overlaps** and **0 line-through-box intersections**. Cross-checked visually in a real browser.

## Note on PR #53

PR #53 (which only addressed the right-branch box↔box overlap) was merged into PR #51's branch *after* #51 had already merged to `main`, so it never reached `main`. This PR is the complete fix and supersedes it.

author: jumplink
body:
## What

#742 landed the GClosure IN-argument primitive **and all three of its L1 consumers** (`GLib.log_set_writer_func`, `bind_property_full`, `Gio.DBusExportedObject.wrapJSObject`) — but the README still called all three *kept-throw*, the DBus **export** half had no gjs byte-parity harness (only the client half was scenario-shared), the log writer had no conformance program, and nothing adversarially exercised the GC lifetime of closures held by long-lived registrations. This PR closes those gaps, plus one real behavior divergence it surfaced.

### `fix(node-gi): append unix-fd-list to dbus handlers`
GJS appends the invocation message's `Gio.UnixFDList` as a trailing argument to every exported DBus method handler (`null` when no fds) and as the 3rd arg of the `*Async` form — node-gi's `wrapJSObject` port dropped it. Now mirrored exactly (refs/gjs `Gio.js` `_handleMethodCall`); the `null` no-fd shape is byte-verified against gjs by the shared export scenario. Deeper fd extraction from a real fd-carrying call stays untested (documented).

### `test(node-gi): gclosure parity + gc lifetime`
- **`conformance/programs/log-writer.conf.mjs` (+ golden)** — a JS `GLogWriterFunc` receives real structured logs (level flags; fields as Uint8Array bytes incl. `GLIB_DOMAIN`/`PRIORITY`; string/Uint8Array/Variant packing), `HANDLED` stops the default writer, `log_set_writer_default()` detaches. **Byte-identical on gjs × node × bun × deno.**
- **`dbus/export-scenario.mjs`** — the object-export half as a SHARED scenario (impl surface, exported method incl. the trailing fd-list arg, property get/set via `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties`, throwing method → `org.gnome.gjs.JSError.Error`, `emit_signal`, `emit_property_changed` → proxy cache, unexport → further calls error). The gjs harness runs the SAME source; both results must equal `EXPORT_EXPECTED` — the byte-for-byte gjs cross-check the export side lacked.
- **GC/lifetime (adversarial, `--expose-gc`)** — a connected signal closure and a DBus export registration root their JS function/service via NOTHING but the marshaled closure's strong `napi_ref`: they survive a full GC with every JS reference dropped and still dispatch; `signal_handler_disconnect` / `unregister_object` release them (closure invalidate → `JsClosureFinalize` → `napi_delete_reference`), observed via `FinalizationRegistry` — a leak fails the test. `test:dbus` now runs with `--expose-gc`. (Bun's `node:test` shim ignores `skip`, so the GC test also bails imperatively off Node.)

### `docs(node-gi): un-stale gclosure kept-throw claims`
README rewritten to the true post-#742 state for all three consumers (the only remaining kept-throw in that section is the ParamSpec builder gap: `enum`/`flags`/`char`/`uchar`/`long`/`ulong`/`param` — re-verified still accurate); stale “engine cannot yet marshal a GClosure” note in `overrides/mainloop.js` and the “DEFERRED export” dbus-test header dropped. STATUS.md needs no edit — these items were never in the node-gi deferred-limitations list (the staleness lived in the README).

## Verification (local, Fedora, GLib 2.88 / gjs on PATH)

- `npm test` → **358 pass / 0 fail** (`test:gc` leg: 358/358, 0 skipped — live session bus, so the dbus + GC legs really ran)
- `npm run test:dbus` → **7/7**, incl. the gjs harness asserting BOTH `RESULT` and the new `EXPORT_RESULT` equal the shared goldens
- `npm run test:conformance` → **17 programs × gjs/node/bun/deno all green** (incl. new `log-writer`)
- `npm run test:bun` / `test:deno` → **34/34** each
- `npm run test:gimarshalling` → **369 pass / 0 fail**

## Residuals (honest)

- fd-carrying DBus calls: the trailing `UnixFDList` arrives wrapped, deeper fd extraction untested.
- `g_log_set_writer_func` is once-per-process (a 2nd install aborts inside GLib — identical under gjs; documented).
- Pre-existing README drift outside this scope (e.g. the milestone-1 intro's vfunc-chain-up note, the multi-level-subclass caveat vs `multilevel-subclass.test.mjs`) left untouched.

body:
## What

Adds a **Profile** panel to Studio so the owner can edit everything the site shows about them — display name, GitHub user, contact, role/tagline/bio per locale, avatar image, SEO title/description, social links, skill display corrections, and the advanced analysis settings (source/target languages, git identities, analytics token) — without touching `data/profile.json` by hand.

## Server

- `PUT /api/profile` — full-document write through the Zod profile schema (server-side `updatedAt`), then recomputes every project's completeness (`targetLangs` feed the translation checks).
- **Optimistic-concurrency guard**: a stale panel (file changed by another tab, `/setup`, or an `/edit` session) gets a 409 instead of silently reverting the other change.
- `POST`/`DELETE /api/profile/avatar` — sanitized, no-clobber image upload into `data/assets/`; delete removes the reference only.

## GUI

- "Profile" sidebar button, `#/profile` route, 7-card form with a deferred working copy; avatar actions apply immediately (concurrency token kept in sync).
- Pre-save checks: required fields and half-filled social/skill rows **block** the save with a friendly toast instead of being dropped silently.
- Locale columns = configured locales ∪ locales present in the data (changing `sourceLang` never hides existing text).
- Unsaved-changes guard (dirty tracking + confirm on navigation + `beforeunload`); a finishing analysis now refreshes the sidebar only, so background events can't wipe open edits.
- All strings via the en+ja i18n dictionary.

## Docs

CHANGELOG entry; GUIDE.ja.html / GUIDE.html §4 subsection (markers re-stamped).

## Verification

- `tsc`, `check:i18n` (9 pairs in sync), `validate` — green
- Playwright E2E **29/29** against a live Studio: save round-trips + reload persistence, avatar add/remove, Zod rejection of invalid input, 409 stale-write conflict (disk untouched), partial-row blocking, unsaved-changes guard (cancel keeps edits / accept leaves), orphaned-locale columns
- Adversarial review workflow (28 agents, find→refute): 8 findings confirmed, all fixed in this PR

author: kristofferc
body:
Investigation of #338: the provider already piggybacks on the REPL's completion machinery — it calls `REPLCompletions.completions` twice, once with the frame's module and once with a temporary module holding the frame's locals as globals. The headline Julia 1.10 power-ups do work through that trick today (e.g. `xs[1].<TAB>` completes fields via inference on a local array).

What actually made completions feel weak is the merge of the two passes: results were always concatenated with `range = min(range1, range2)`. When the passes return completions of *different kinds* with different replacement ranges — e.g. `d["<TAB>` where the locals pass returns dict key completions and the frame-module pass falls back to path completions inside the string — the list was polluted and the range wrong for half the entries, corrupting the inserted text.

Now the results are only merged when the ranges agree (the common identifier case); otherwise the pass whose completion consumed more context wins. Also passes the `hint` flag through and fixes the `#self#` name typo in `ignore_local`.

Before/after on a frame with locals `xs = [S(1, 2)]`, `d = Dict("key1" => 1)`:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `d["` | `"key1"]`, `.git/`, `.github/`, … (mixed ranges) | `"key1"]` |
| `xs[1].` | `field_a`, `field_b` | unchanged |
| `si` | merged identifiers | unchanged |

Stacked on #404 (uses `_completion_text`); will retarget to master when that merges.

Fixes #338

author: os-zhuang
body:
## Summary

Closes #3196. `WebhookTriggerType` declared five triggers (`create`/`update`/`delete`/`undelete`/`api`) but only the first three ever fired. The other two had no event source and silently no-op'd — the same `declared ≠ enforced` pattern as #3184 (validation `delete`-event) and #3195 (hook events).

- **`undelete`** — the engine has no soft-delete/restore capability at all: `delete` is a hard delete, there's no `deleted_at` convention, no restore operation, and `data.record.undeleted` is never emitted. The `undeleted` case in the auto-enqueuer's action mapper was dead code awaiting a producer that doesn't exist. (`restore`/`purge`/`transfer` appear only as *pre-wired* permission concepts in plugin-security, deferred to a future M2 per #1883 — nothing dispatches them.)
- **`api`** ("manually triggered") — no manual/programmatic fire path exists anywhere; the only webhook HTTP surface (`/webhooks/redeliver`) re-queues already-failed deliveries.

Per the design decision (both confirmed with the user), **trim both** rather than build out an entire restore subsystem or a manual-fire endpoint. Reintroduce `undelete` only alongside a real restore subsystem, and `api` only alongside a real manual-fire endpoint.

## Changes

- **`packages/spec/src/automation/webhook.zod.ts`** — `WebhookTriggerType` narrowed to `create`/`update`/`delete`; a "Deliberately NOT triggers" doc block records why `undelete`/`api` were removed; `object` describe no longer references manual webhooks.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/auto-enqueuer.ts`** — dropped `undelete` from the `CachedSubscription` type, the action union, and `mapActionToTrigger`. Added a **drift-guard**: `parseRow` now warns and drops any trigger it can't map to an emitted record event (e.g. a legacy `sys_webhook` row authored with `undelete`/`api`), so a dead trigger can't silently cache a subscription that matches nothing.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts`** — trigger select options → `create`/`update`/`delete`; field help updated.
- **Locale help strings** (`en`/`zh-CN`/`ja-JP`/`es-ES` `*.objects.generated.ts`) — dropped `undelete,api` from the trigger list and the "manual / API" object hint.
- **Docs** — `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx` (trigger list + action values); regenerated `content/docs/references/automation/webhook.mdx`.
- **`.changeset/`** — patch (spec + plugin-webhooks).

## Behavior change

- Authoring a webhook with `undelete`/`api` now fails at parse/validate time instead of registering a webhook that never fires. Verified zero shipped/authored webhook metadata used either — the only references were the enum, the authoring-UI options, docs, and a parse-only test.
- Legacy persisted `sys_webhook` rows with those triggers keep working for their valid triggers; the dead ones are dropped with a warning instead of sitting in the cache.

## Tests

- `webhook.test.ts` — enum rejects `undelete`/`api`; the multi-trigger case uses the 3 live triggers.
- `auto-enqueuer.test.ts` — a legacy `create,undelete,api` row still fires `create` and warns (`unknown: ['undelete','api']`); a row whose only triggers are removed values enqueues nothing.

Verified: spec 253 files / 6763 tests green, plugin-webhooks 14 tests green, `check:docs` 253 files in sync, spec + plugin-webhooks builds green, eslint clean. The `'api'` references elsewhere are the unrelated automation **flow** trigger (a live feature), not webhooks.

## Lineage

Fourth fix in the PD #10 events-enum audit line: #3160 → #3189 → #3195/#3206 → this. Remaining sibling: #3197 (schema-only event surfaces — graphql subscriptions, connector webhooks/triggers, realtime, websocket, record subscriptions).

author: marctjones
body:
Refs #332 (stays open pending click-through).

## Problem
Approval auto-open lived only on `ChatView.onChange(approvalWindowID)` — dead when the main window is closed — and the notification tap set state without opening a window or offering actions. A new approval with only the menu bar open degraded to a silent badge.

## Fix (Swift; builds + unit-tested)
- **Actionable notification**: register a `CAPDEP_APPROVAL` category with **Review** + **Deny** actions and tag approval notifications with it. The notification is now an actionable prompt with zero windows open. Approve is intentionally not a banner action (approving happens in the card with payload/labels visible); Deny is fail-closed and safe from the banner.
- **Delegate**: handles Deny (`denyApprovalByID`) and Review/tap (activate app + `presentApproval`); presents banners even when CapDep is frontmost.
- **Always-alive observer**: new `MenuBarLabel` hosts the approval/grant/override auto-open observers on the menu-bar label (the one view alive whenever the app runs), so cards surface regardless of which window is open.
- Tests: notification identifier contract (bridge↔delegate agreement).

## Verification boundary
- ✅ `swift build` clean; `swift test` 44/44.
- ✅ No Python changed — CI reruns the unchanged suite.
- ❌ Not verified: the actual behavior (close main window → trigger approval → actionable banner pops; Deny decides; Review opens card). Needs a running-app click-through; Swift isn't in CI (#344).

author: wesm
body:
Once a folder is under full audit, people should still be able to organize its documents with tags. Until now, assigning or removing a tag after enrollment was refused, even when the tag already existed.

This makes that ordinary workflow work without weakening the history. A real assignment changes the node and tag and records the same transition in the audit chain as one transaction. If recording fails, the tag change rolls back too. Backup restore and JSONL import independently check that the tag existed, the target belonged to the audit scope, the assignment really changed from absent to present (or back), and the final metadata matches the replayed history.

Repeated assignment or removal remains an idempotent no-op and does not fabricate history. Assignment outside the protected scope still fails closed.

The boundary is deliberately small: this covers assigning and removing existing tags. Creating, renaming, and deleting tag definitions remain blocked in audited vaults because those operations can affect many audited documents and need their own focused fan-out implementation. The shared mutation and chain builders stay in Go; this adds no SQL policy or new schema tables.

> **Migrates the monorepo’s default package manager and automation from npm to Bun 1.3.10**, aligning Cursor cloud images, agent rules, worktree setup, and developer docs with `packageManager` / CI.

author: nigelcopley
body:
## What

Fix the WAF serving verified search crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot) the `noindex` proof-of-work challenge on every request, which silently de-indexes any site fronted by it. Implements ADR-035.

**Root cause:** crawlers send none of the browser fingerprint headers, score into the CHALLENGED band, cannot solve the JS proof-of-work, and receive an `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` interstitial on every path. The `AllowRule` + rDNS mechanism already existed, but the package shipped no built-in seed, so `BR-CHAL-001`'s guarantee ("search engine crawlers are never challenged") only held if an operator hand-seeded a rule. Nothing did.

## Changes

**Phase A (SEO fix, MIT):**
- New setting `DJANGO_WAF_ALLOW_VERIFIED_CRAWLERS` (default `True`).
- Migration `0003` idempotently seeds rDNS-gated `AllowRule` rows for Googlebot (`.googlebot.com`/`.google.com`) and Bingbot (`.search.msn.com`) on migrate, gated on the setting, reversible. rDNS gating means a spoofed crawler UA from an unverified IP is still scored and challenged (not a UA bypass).

**Phase B (feed contract, enables Drystane curated allowlist):**
- `AllowRule` gains `source` + feed-lifecycle fields (migration `0002`).
- `sync_feed()` reads an optional `kind: "allow"` discriminator (spec 06-threat-feed-api.md section 2.8) so an operated feed can deliver curated `AllowRule` rows alongside block rules. Separate seen-key sets and absence-expiry passes per table. Backward compatible: a feed with no `kind` imports as block-only exactly as before.

## Versioning

Bumps to **1.4.0**. Behaviour change on upgrade: verified crawlers now pass by default. Per `RELEASING.md`, any behaviour change (even a safer one) is a minor. Opt out with `DJANGO_WAF_ALLOW_VERIFIED_CRAWLERS = False`.

## Tests

12 new tests (798 -> 801 total, full suite green). Cover: seed migration (create/idempotent/reverse/setting-gate), `sync_feed` allow-rule import (create/backward-compat/absence-expiry/confidence-skip/idempotent/non-interference), and rDNS gating in the rule engine (matching PTR passes, non-matching PTR falls through). Maps to AC-CHAL-001a-d and AC-FEED-004-006 in `05-verification.md`.

author: silvercrocus
body:
## Summary

- move the analytics and statistics-operations role probes into one reusable runtime boundary
- validate the scoped URL against the writer target before any scoped query: authentic shared Supavisor host, matching project ref, exact least-privilege username, port 6543, `sslmode=verify-full`, `pgbouncer=true`, reviewed parameters, role-specific connection limits, and `pool_timeout=5`
- cache successful probes for 60 seconds and failed probes for 5 seconds, deduplicate concurrent calls, invalidate when credentials change, and expose explicit invalidation
- gate every analytics repository query, statistics operation, and Ask CentrePass request on the verified boundary
- make `/api/readiness` consume the same cached probes and report routing plus privilege-contract status
- preserve disabled-feature startup without constructing scoped clients

## Root cause

Startup validation only established that the scoped environment values were syntactically valid PostgreSQL URLs. Detailed role and privilege checks existed in readiness and release tooling, but the analytics and Ask request paths could obtain scoped Prisma clients without first proving the target project, host, authenticated role, or exact privilege surface. A wrong-project or overly privileged credential could therefore serve feature requests even while readiness was degraded.

## Validation

- `npm run check`: 156 test files, 974 tests passed
- production build passed with disabled feature flags and local non-connecting build URLs
- `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`: 0 vulnerabilities
- `npm run smoke:server-startup`: production and development custom-server active-socket shutdown smokes passed
- `graphify update .` completed

Regression coverage includes wrong project, wrong host, wrong/full-privilege URL role, unsafe or unreviewed connection parameters, excess database privileges, probe failures, healthy/failure caching, explicit and configuration-driven invalidation, readiness behavior, and Ask route fail-closed behavior.

No Supabase, Render, production database, feature flag, or publication state was changed.

author: tonytony32
body:
## The problem

The overlay enters ambient mode (♫, 120×120) when `connectionState == .connected && currentTrack == nil`. But while a loopback source (YouTube) is active, `SourceArbiter` always publishes `.connected`, and the `jellyfinIsActiveSource` gate makes `PlayerStore.updateConnection` drop Jellyfin's real `.reconnecting` / `.error`.

Off the home network, the result is an ambient face that says "all good":
- tapping it (`NothingPlayingView.onTapGesture` → `ClientLauncher.openJellyfin`) opens the Safari web app against an unreachable URL → blank window;
- `markAnticipating()` then keeps the chrome visible for 30 s waiting for music that cannot arrive.

## The change

1. **`PlayerStore.jellyfinLinkHealth`** — an ungated signal of the Jellyfin link's health, written in `updateConnection` and in `ingest` *before* the gate guard, following the `jellyfinHasNowPlaying` pattern. Plus `jellyfinLinkIsDown` (`.reconnecting` / `.error`) for the view.
2. **`NothingPlayingView`** — when the home link is down, the lone note is replaced by a `wifi.slash` glyph with a "Jellyfin unreachable" caption. Hover/snap/opacity treatment is unchanged.
3. **Tap with the link down** — no web-app launch, no `markAnticipating()`; shows the transient "Can't reach your Jellyfin server from this network."
4. **Link alive** — behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was.

## Tests

`PlayerStoreSourceGatingTests.gatedWritesStillUpdateLinkHealth` covers the gated case: with YouTube driving, a gated `ingest` marks health `.connected`, a gated `updateConnection(.reconnecting)` leaves `connectionState` alone but flips `jellyfinLinkHealth`, `.error` also counts as down, and reconnecting clears it. Full suite: 106 tests pass.

### Manual test (the SwiftUI layer is not under test)

1. Configure Jellyfin, start playback on YouTube so the loopback source drives the overlay.
2. Leave the home network (or point the base URL at an unreachable host / turn off Wi-Fi) and stop the YouTube playback so the overlay falls to ambient.
3. **Expect:** the ambient window shows `wifi.slash` + "Jellyfin unreachable" instead of the note.
4. Click it. **Expect:** the transient "Can't reach your Jellyfin server from this network." appears; Safari does *not* open; the chrome does not stay expanded for 30 s.
5. Return to the home network, wait for a poll. **Expect:** the note comes back and a click opens the web app and arms the anticipating window exactly as before.
