author: ottojaa
body:
## Summary

Two video bugs in the document viewer, both stemming from `VideoViewMode` diverging from `ImageViewMode`:

1. **Videos overflow the viewer** — both flex ancestors used `items-center`, so the `<video>`'s `max-h-full` resolved against an auto-height parent (which computes to `max-height: none`). Tall/portrait videos grew straight past the viewer box.
2. **Dive transition "changes size on landing"** — the poster visibly jumped size the moment the dive overlay handed off.

## Fixes

**Overflow** — the outer container now uses `items-stretch` (giving a definite full height down the flex chain), and the video sits inside an aspect-locked hero capped with `max-h-full max-w-full`, so it contain-fits the box instead of overflowing.

**Dive size jump** — three compounding causes, all addressed by mirroring `ImageViewMode`:
- Padding mismatch: video used a uniform `p-4`, but `computeDestRect` predicts the image viewer's chrome-matched padding → now uses the same padding classes across breakpoints.
- No `[data-doc-hero]`: the FLIP settle had no target and just faded → added a `data-doc-hero` element sized by `aspectRatio` + `min(100%, Npx)` caps (contain-fit, never upscaled, matching `computeDestRect`'s `min(…, 1)` clamp). The poster is the exact `getThumbnailUrl(doc, 'lg')` URL the overlay flies in, so the settle lands pixel-exact.
- Scale-in entrance (`0.97 → 1`): the poster was still growing when the overlay dropped — the size jump itself → removed the geometry-changing entrance animation (the dive *is* the entrance). Also dropped the now-unused `motion`/`useRef`/`useState` imports.

`completeDive` now gives video the full FLIP settle (`rendersHero = image/ || video/`) instead of the 250ms give-up timeout intended for hero-less viewers (PDF/txt).

## Files
- `VideoViewMode.tsx` — rewritten to mirror the image viewer's layout + hero
- `useOpenDocumentFromCanvas.ts` — `completeDive` gives video the full settle
- `diveTransition.ts` — doc comment updated for accuracy

## Test plan
- [ ] Portrait video no longer overflows the viewer
- [ ] Landscape video contain-fits within the viewer box
- [ ] Dive from canvas → video lands seamlessly with no size pop on the poster
- [ ] PDF/txt dive still fades promptly (unchanged behavior)

author: evanbernstein
body:
Fans can now switch on a **Calibrated Track Rating** from their profile
settings, a separate opt-in alongside the existing Calibrated Show Rating.
It gives more weight to raters who use the whole 0.5-to-5 star scale, so a
track's number leans on those raters rather than accounts that rate nearly
everything 5. Tracks spread out instead of piling near 5. Everyone still sees
the plain community average by default.

The calibrated number (and its histogram) shows everywhere a track rating
appears:

- setlist gap-chart tables
- the song performance tables (song, all-timers, jam-charts, on-this-day,
  musicians pages)
- the song-title hover popup and its distribution histogram
- the song-page featured all-timer cards

An author-only compare overlay (behind the existing `ratings.compare-visible`
flag) shows the plain → calibrated delta per track. The ratings explainer at
`/show-rating-algorithm` now covers both the show and track ratings.

## How it differs from the show rating

Same family (weight raters by how much of the scale they use, drop one-note
fluffers), but it deliberately skips the two show moves that backfire on tracks:
it does not mean-center a rater's scores toward the crowd average, and it does
not shrink thin tracks toward a global anchor. Tracks are ceiling-piled from a
smaller, higher-skewing pool, so both of those just push scores back up. The
main lever is weighting (`entropy^gamma`, gamma tunable), not exclusion.

## Notes for the reviewer

- New denormalized `tracks.discriminating_rating` + `discriminating_ratings_count`
  and two tri-state `User` prefs (`track_calibrated_rating`,
  `track_rating_compare`), via migration `20260717000001`. Scores are recomputed
  in `recomputeAll` (dirty-gated hourly cron + deploy), so a new track rating
  updates within the recompute window, not on the write.
- Display gating is client-side and per-viewer: `SongPagePerformance.rating`
  stays the plain baked value from the composer, and the calibrated value is
  overlaid in the rating components via `useTrackUserRatings` /
  `resolveViewerRatingMode`. Core and the page composer stay viewer-agnostic.
- The calibrated histogram (`getCalibratedTrackDistribution`) buckets exactly the
  raters with a positive discriminating weight, so the bar total equals the
  displayed calibrated count.
- `packages/core/scripts/track-rating-calibration-spike.ts` is the throwaway
  analysis behind the design (split-half reliability, distribution shape,
  gamma sweep); kept as the retuning tool, run via `make
  track-rating-calibration-spike`.

author: rabi0424
body:
## 概要

PC版での連続生成に関する2つの不具合と、それに伴う表示崩れを修正します。

## 修正内容

### 1. 連続生成時に生成ボタンが移動して連打できない

生成中ジョブが生成ボタンの下に積まれることで、下端固定（sticky）のバーが上方向に伸びてボタンが押し上げられ、連続でクリックできなかった。

- ジョブ一覧・注記・エラーを `order: -1` で生成ボタンの**上**に通常フローで積むように変更。バー全体が下端に貼り付いているため、ジョブが増えてもバーは上へ伸び、最下段のボタンは動かない。
- （途中で試した `position: absolute` の overlay 方式は、フォームの設定項目を恒久的に覆い隠しスクロールでも到達できない問題があったため、通常フロー方式に置き換えた。）

### 2. タブ復帰時に最新の生成がギャラリーに反映されない

複数生成の完了前に他アプリへ切り替えてブラウザに戻ると、`visibilitychange` によるサーバー履歴取得（GET）と、復帰で再開したポーリングの生成完了処理（POST）が競合。新レコードをまだ含まない GET 応答が後から届いて履歴キャッシュを丸ごと上書きし、ギャラリーから消えていた（詳細表示は独立描画のため表示され、再読込するまで反映されなかった）。

- 保存中（POST 応答待ち）の ID と保存完了時刻を記録し、GET 開始以降に保存されたレコードはサーバー一覧とマージして残す。
- POST 応答時にキャッシュから消えていた場合は先頭へ戻す。
- 削除済み ID を記録し、POST 応答による削除済みレコードの復活を防ぐ。

## 変更ファイル

- `index.html` — ジョブ一覧・注記・エラーを `.job-stack` でグループ化
- `style.css` — ジョブ一覧を生成ボタンの上に通常フローで配置（PC・モバイル共通化）
- `app.js` — タブ復帰時の履歴取得と生成完了の競合対策

## 検証

Playwright で実際にページを描画して確認済み。

- **ボタン位置**: フォームが長くパネルがスクロールする状況で、ジョブ 0〜4 件を追加してもボタン座標が完全に不動。ジョブはボタンの上に表示され、最下部までスクロールすれば下部の設定項目もバーの上に出て到達可能。モバイルは従来どおり下部固定バー内でジョブがボタンの上。
- **履歴の競合**: GET 応答を遅延させた状態で生成完了（履歴追加＋POST）を発生させ、修正前は再現どおりレコード消失、修正後はキャッシュ・ギャラリーとも正しく表示（重複なし）。削除との競合で復活しないこと、通常の履歴取得が従来どおり反映されることも確認。

author: 4444j99
body:
## What

Wires the **BRANCH rung** of the closeout-reconciliation organ: `reconcile-closeouts.py --apply` now **homes** each HARD finding (`DONE_UNVERIFIED` / `PR_MISSING`) as a deduped board task on the claim's own repo, instead of only writing them to `logs/closeout-reconcile.json`. Closes the *sensor-without-effector* gap.

## Why

The organ classifies precisely (after #1229) but its real findings weren't routed to a durable owner — a sensor whose findings sit in a log is a defect. A `DONE_UNVERIFIED` ("task claims done but its PR is unmerged") is stranded work on that repo → it belongs on the board.

## How — convergence, not new plumbing

A thin **mapper** onto the existing `insight-route.py` engine (mirrors how `verify-dispatch.py` surfaces `chronic_tasks` for the `status=dispatched` half):
- `_finding_to_insight` maps a HARD finding → `{id: CLOSEOUT-<claim>, owner: <repo>, title, detail, suggested_action, source: "closeout-reconcile", severity}`.
- `_route_findings` hands each to `insight_route.route_repo_insight` → the org/repo → board-task lane (deduped vs board + keeper inbox via `pending_task_ids`, workstream auto-stamped).
- `VERIFIED` / `MISCITED` / `HOMED_ELSEWHERE` / `UNRECEIPTED` never route.

### Precedent-safe by construction
- **PREC-2026-07-10 (derived-file trap):** routes via the single-writer keeper inbox (`submit_task_upsert`), **never** the beat-regenerated `logs/censor-residual.json` sink.
- **PREC-2026-07-08 (no silent-off valve):** the mutation rides insight-route's **own** `LIMEN_INSIGHT_ROUTE_APPLY` arm — no new dark gate, nothing new for the armed-valve audit. Dry-run plan until the operator arms insight-route.

Safe to auto-home **only because #1229 made the classifier precise** — pre-fix, the 4 phantom findings would have spawned junk tasks.

## Proof
- `--doctor` green, **+2 cases**: mapper (HARD→insight, soft/no-repo→None) and router (only HARD findings home, to the claim's repo).
- **Dry-run over the live board** routes exactly the 2 genuine residuals (`AW-VALUE-REPOS`, `GOV-land-pr-1203` → `organvm/limen`), nothing for the 5 VERIFIED, **zero tickets written**.
- **Armed scratch-board proof:** one keeper ticket lands; re-run dedupes to the same ticket; real board untouched.
- `scripts/check-sensors.py` + `check-params.py` + `verify-scoped.sh` green (no registry drift; reuses an existing gate).

## Stacking
Branched on top of #1229 (the precision fix) so the effector never rides the phantom-emitting classifier. The first commit (`5aa91e06`) is #1229's; it drops out on rebase once #1229 lands. Merge #1229 first.

body:
## Summary

外部 REST API 化フェーズ（**T204〜T214・全11 Issue**）の統合ブランチを `develop` へマージする。link-hub を正準リファレンスに、日報アプリの主要リソースを API キー認証の REST API として公開し、OpenAPI 3.1 の実行時配信と Stoplight リファレンス UI（ログイン必須）まで揃えた。

**27 コミット / 60 ファイル / +3,231 −494**

## 提供する API（11 パス・18 operation）

| リソース | エンドポイント |
|---|---|
| Profile | `GET`・`PATCH /api/me`（氏名更新） |
| Reports | `GET`・`POST /api/reports`／`GET`・`PATCH`・`DELETE /api/reports/{id}` |
| Comments | `GET`・`POST /api/reports/{id}/comments`／`DELETE /api/comments/{id}` |
| Day-off | `GET`・`POST /api/day-off`／`DELETE /api/day-off/{id}` |
| Admin | `GET /api/admin/users`／`PATCH`・`DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}`／`POST /api/admin/reports`／`DELETE /api/admin/reports/{id}` |

**ドキュメント配信**（ログイン必須・外部公開なし）: `/openapi.json`（OpenAPI 3.1）・`/api-reference`（Stoplight Elements `@9`）

## 設計方針

- **ルートは薄いアダプタ**: 業務ロジック・所有者検証は `src/lib/` に置き、Server Actions（画面）と共有。UI と REST で認可が二重実装にならない
- **Zod スキーマ（`src/lib/schemas/`）を単一の正**: ルートの入力検証と OpenAPI の両方をここから導出し、手書き spec を持たない
- **エラーは型付きエラー＋`statusForError`** で HTTP へマッピング（`{ error }` 形式に統一）

## 認可モデル

| 操作 | VIEWER | MEMBER | ADMIN |
|---|---|---|---|
| 日報の作成・編集・削除 | ❌ 403 | ✅ 自分のみ | ✅ 自分のみ |
| コメントの投稿 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| コメントの削除 | ✅ 自分のみ | ✅ 自分のみ | ✅ 自分のみ |
| 休日の登録・解除 | ❌ 403 | ✅ 自分のみ | ✅ 自分のみ |
| 自分の氏名更新 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| ユーザー管理・日報バッチ | ❌ 403 | ❌ 403 | ✅ |

- 操作対象は**常に認証情報由来の `user.id`**（リクエストの識別子を信頼しない）
- 他人のリソースは **403**、存在を明かさない箇所（day-off・admin users）は **404**
- **最後の有効 ADMIN の降格・無効化・削除を禁止**（T214・UI/REST 双方に効く lib 層ガード）

## ⚠️ 契約変更（既存 API 利用者向け）

| 変更 | 対象 | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| **検証エラー 422 → 400** | `POST /api/reports`・`POST /api/admin/reports` | 全リソースで 400 に統一 |
| **403 メッセージ統一** | `GET /api/admin/users` | 「この操作には ADMIN 権限が必要です」→「このエンドポイントは ADMIN のみ使用できます」 |
| **CORS 付与** | `/api/*` | `Allow-Origin: *`（`Allow-Credentials` 不使用・Cookie 非依存のため安全）。プリフライトは 204 |

## ドキュメント

- **`docs/api.md` を削除**（api-rules 準拠）。フィールド契約・並び順・パラメータ排他は**配信 spec が唯一の正**
- `README`: API リファレンス導線（`/api-reference`・`/openapi.json`）
- `docs/architecture.md`: REST の契約（Zod→OpenAPI→配信）・APIキー認証の範囲・CORS 方針を追記

## Test plan（統合ブランチで最終確認済み）

- [x] **全体テスト: 35 files / 361 tests passed**
- [x] `npm run lint`（CI 相当・`biome lint .`）通過
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` 型エラーなし

- [x] 各 Issue で **API 動作確認を実施**（Reports 11項目 / Comments 10項目 / Day-off 10項目 / Profile 8項目 / Admin 19項目 / CORS 全名前空間）
- [x] **画面確認**: `proxy.ts` 変更（T208）時にページ側の回帰なしを確認（8項目・A/B 比較付き）／`/api-reference` の Stoplight 表示（18 operation）

## レビュー観点

- 各 Issue で個別にレビュー済み（#349・#350・#351・#352・#353・#354・#356・#359・#360・#361・#362）。本 PR は統合結果の確認が主眼

## 補足

author: tnfssc
body:
## What

Fixes several correctness, motion, and a11y issues in the `VibeFloaters` overlay (`apps/web/src/components/ui/vibe-floaters.tsx`).

## Why

- **Broken `img` src** — the `src` attribute contained a U+2026 ellipsis character (`…`) where `nothink` should have been, so the floater image never loaded. Corrected to `/nothink-vibeonly.webp` (leading slash → served from `public/`).
- **Frame-rate-dependent motion** — the original stepped position by a fixed `BASE_SPEED` px/frame, so floaters moved ~2.4× faster on 144 Hz displays than on 60 Hz. Rewrote to px/sec with delta-time integration (`BASE_SPEED = 144` px/s), using the RAF timestamp argument and a `dt` clamp (`MAX_DT = 1/30`) so a backgrounded tab's first frame doesn't teleport the floaters.
- **Reduced-motion was not reactive** — `reduced` was a one-shot `useState` initializer, so toggling the OS setting while the overlay was mounted had no effect. Now tracked via `matchMedia` + `change` listener in a `useEffect`.
- **`will-change-transform` always on** — held a compositor layer even when the overlay was inactive. Now gated on the `active` prop.
- **`(0,0)` flash on first frame** — `stateRef` started at all-zeros, so the first paint showed every floater pinned to the top-left corner before the first RAF seeded positions. `stateRef` is now lazily initialized (typed `| null`) and seeded synchronously from the fractional config in the effect (reading container size up front), with the initial transform applied before the animation loop starts.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec biome check apps/web/src/components/ui/vibe-floaters.tsx` — clean.
- `cd apps/web && npx tsc --noEmit` — no errors in `vibe-floaters.tsx`. (The 6 remaining `src/lib/blog.ts` / `src/routes/blog/$slug.tsx` errors are pre-existing on `develop` and are fixed by the `blog-slug-types` PR — not in this file's scope.)

## Scope

Single file: `apps/web/src/components/ui/vibe-floaters.tsx`. No dependency or config changes.

body:
- [x] Closes #8317 (re-created; #8302 was closed by accident)
- [x] This PR follows our [AI policy](https://github.com/RustPython/.github/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md)

## Summary

Under `QUOTE_MINIMAL`, a field containing `\r` or `\n` must be quoted regardless of the `lineterminator` — CPython quotes them unconditionally. RustPython serialized `QUOTE_MINIMAL` rows with `csv_core`, which decides quoting from the bytes it registered for the terminator, so with a terminator other than CR/LF (e.g. `'!'` or `'\0'`) embedded `\r`/`\n` were left unquoted.

`QUOTE_MINIMAL` now uses a hand-written path (like `QUOTE_NONE` / `QUOTE_STRINGS`) that decides quoting via the existing `field_needs_quotes`, which always treats `\r`/`\n` as needing quotes. `QUOTE_ALL` and `QUOTE_NONNUMERIC` still use `csv_core`.

This also fixes an empty row (`writerow([])`) emitting `""` instead of only the terminator.

```python
import csv, io
sio = io.StringIO()
csv.writer(sio, lineterminator="!").writerow(["\r", "\n"])
# before: '\r,\n!'
# after:  '"\r","\n"!'   (matches CPython)
```

Multi-character `lineterminator` (the `!@#` case in `test_write_lineterminator`) is still unsupported and left for a follow-up, so that test stays marked.

## Test plan

- Unmarks `test_write_iterable` and `test_write_empty_fields` (both `@unittest.expectedFailure` before). `cargo run --release -- -m test test_csv`: 128 run, 7 skipped, SUCCESS.
- `extra_tests/snippets/stdlib_csv.py`: passes (added writer cases for custom terminators and empty fields).
- `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy`: clean (no new warnings).
- Compared against CPython 3.14.6 on the same machine; the `QUOTE_MINIMAL` writer outputs match.

author: jcnm
body:
## Summary

The post-detail realtime room updated the comment **thread** (`PostCommentsViewModel`) for add/delete/reaction over the last three slices, but the full-screen **header** badge is owned by a **separate** VM (`PostDetailViewModel`, the post projection) that never subscribed. So a comment added or deleted **elsewhere** froze the header's comment count until a manual refresh.

iOS heals this: both the `commentAdded` and `commentDeleted` sinks do `self.post?.commentCount = data.commentCount` — resync to the **server-authoritative** count the event carries (absolute, so it heals any drift from the thread VM's optimistic ±1 arithmetic). Android's `SocketCommentAddedData` was even **missing** the `commentCount` field the gateway ships (confirmed in `packages/shared/types/post.ts` `CommentAddedEventData.commentCount` + `SocialEventsHandler.broadcastCommentAdded`).

## Changes (`apps/android` only)

- **`:core:model`** — `SocketCommentAddedData` gains `commentCount: Int = 0` (line-for-line mirror of the gateway payload + iOS `data.commentCount`; default `0` keeps every existing decode back-compatible).
- **`PostDetailViewModel`** — injects `SocialSocketManager`; a `liveCommentCount: StateFlow<Int?>` overlay (null → the fetched post's own count) folded into the `combine` (now 5-arg); `observeRealtime()` (skipped for a blank route) collects `commentAdded`/`commentDeleted` filtered to `postId` and sets the overlay to `event.commentCount`; a **successful fetch clears the overlay** so a refresh re-establishes fresh server truth over a stale live value; `project` overlays `presentation.copy(commentCount = liveCount.coerceAtLeast(0))` (clamped ≥0 for a negative authoritative payload).
- **Compose** — no new UI: the badge already reads `post.commentCount` in `PostDetailScreen`, so the resync is real, not orphan code.

## Tests (TDD red → green)

**+7 tests.** `PostDetailViewModelTest` +6 — live-add-resyncs, live-delete-resyncs, other-post-ignored, blank-route-never-subscribes, negative-clamped-to-zero, refresh-replaces-overlay-with-server-truth. `SocialSocketManagerTest` +1 — `comment:added` decode now carries the authoritative count.

**Mutation check (RED proof):** dropping the `coerceAtLeast(0)` clamp **and** flipping the `postId ==` room filter to `!=` failed **exactly** the 5 badge tests (add/delete/other-post/negative-clamp/refresh); the decode test stayed green (its path is the model field, not the filter) — behavioural, not tautological.

## Verification

- `:feature:feed:testDebugUnitTest` — `PostDetailViewModelTest` 18, 0 fail
- `:sdk-core:testDebugUnitTest` — `SocialSocketManagerTest` green (the 1 `MediaDownloadPreferencesStoreTest` DataStore timeout is pre-existing/flaky under parallel load — **passes in isolation**, unrelated to this diff which touches no DataStore)
- `:app:assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL** (the two new collectors + 5-arg combine compile, no cross-module breakage)

Reviewer **PASS**: diff `apps/android` only; SDK purity (stateless model field in `:core:model`, orchestration in the `:feature:feed` VM); SSOT (reuses the `FeedPostBuilder` projection + one overlay); Instant-App (live badge without a refresh); UDF + immutable `StateFlow`; no coverage floor lowered, no test weakened.

author: devyeony
body:
## What

Phase 4 §7-2/§7-3: the portfolio becomes an **MCP server** at `/api/mcp`, plus an **llms.txt** index for AI crawlers.

- **`/api/mcp`** (Vercel `mcp-handler`, Streamable HTTP; SSE disabled so there is no Redis dependency): six read-only tools — `get_profile`, `list_projects`, `get_project`, `list_posts`, `get_post`, `search_content` — every one served from the same content collections that render the pages. One new entry in `content/` now updates site, feeds, RAG index, **and MCP responses** with zero component changes — the architecture-reuse story §7-2 exists to tell.
- **Security defaults**: all tools are read-only over already-public content and declare `readOnlyHint`; inputs are zod-validated at the boundary (locale enum, slug/query length caps); the route sits behind a fixed-window in-memory rate limiter (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`, per-instance backstop — acceptable because the endpoint serves nothing private).
- **`search_content` is deliberately lexical**, not semantic: runtime query embedding would pull the model into the serverless function, and the AI layer stays build-time static (§7-1). Unicode-aware term scoring with title boost and Korean eojeol prefix matching ("오픈소스" hits "오픈소스에"), transparent scores in the response.
- **`/llms.txt`** (force-static): llmstxt.org-style markdown index of pages, projects, posts, and data endpoints, built from the collections — includes the one-line MCP connect instruction.
- Remaining from the §7-2 appeal set (connection GIF + colophon narrative) lands with the colophon in Phase 5.

## How verified

- `pnpm check` / `pnpm test` green — 5 new unit tests for the search scorer (title weighting, Korean prefix, snippets, limits).
- `pnpm verify` green: 162 Playwright cases (was 144) — e2e covers the JSON-RPC handshake (`serverInfo`), the exact read-only tool set incl. `readOnlyHint` on every tool, `get_profile` content, bilingual `search_content`, malformed-argument rejection, and llms.txt shape.
- Manually exercised against a dev server with curl: handshake, tools/list, profile/search calls (en+ko), invalid-locale rejection, llms.txt headers and content.
- No UI change: visual baselines, axe, and Lighthouse untouched.

## Self-review checklist

- [x] `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify` are green locally
- [x] Components reference semantic tokens only (no raw colors/px values) — no UI code in this PR
- [x] No new `"use client"` without a stated reason — none added
- [x] Device-adaptive: checked at 360 / 768 / 1280 — no layout change
- [x] i18n: en/ko messages stay symmetric; career content is not in `messages/` — tools read locale-keyed collections
- [x] Security: external input validated at the boundary; no secrets in client code
- [x] Scope: no non-goals introduced

**Stop shipping dev artefacts in production archives.** The exclude list predated the PHPStan baselines and PHPUnit caches this suite now generates, so every archive carried them. author: trozet
body:
Commit 585b72c222 ("Allow networks to start while route advertisements settle") added coverage that installs an existing network controller and verifies its advertised VRFs are preserved when a referenced RouteAdvertisements object is missing.

The fixture started the network manager before installing that existing controller and before ensuring the desired network. An initial Node event could reconcile the injected controller while no desired network was registered, stop it as stale, and let a later EnsureNetwork create a replacement with empty advertised VRFs. The assertion therefore depended on goroutine scheduling.

Install the existing controller state and call EnsureNetwork before starting the network manager. Initial sync now sees both current and desired state and exercises the intended preservation path deterministically.

author: andrebarthelmeshellmuth
body:
Correctness:
- ExplanationParser::tryAddMaxOfDistinctTermsWeight() labeled a
  synonym group's field from whichever child was iterated first
  rather than the child that actually won the max, producing a
  correct total/breakdown paired with the WRONG field name. Fixed by
  tracking the winning field alongside the winning child. Generalized
  the same method to recursively flatten nested "max of:" trees
  (dis_max-of-dis_max), not just a flat one level, so a multi-field
  query with a synonym at one position can't fall through to plain
  recursion and double-count.
- TokenHighlighter silently dropped overlapping matches from the
  rendered HTML while callers kept a separate, now-misaligned matches
  list (magnifying-glass links pointed at the wrong occurrence). Added
  filterRenderable() as the single source of truth for which matches
  survive, and TokenSourceResolver now stores THAT list, not the raw
  one.
- TokenSourceResolver::addAttributeLabel() kept only the first
  colliding attribute key for a shared value; now keeps all of them,
  same as the named-source collision handling right next to it.

Reuse:
- New Shared\SearchDebug\Utf16\Utf16CodeUnitConverter and
  Shared\SearchDebug\Format\ConfigValueScalarFormatter consolidate
  UTF-16 offset math (previously triplicated) and config-value
  scalar formatting (previously duplicated, and buggy for booleans
  inside a list) into one place each.
- Merged ExplanationParser's findChildByDescription/findChildByPrefix
  and SearchStringAnalyzer's resolveSearchAnalyzerName/
  resolveIndexAnalyzerName into shared helpers.

Efficiency:
- TokenSourceResolver no longer fetches bulk concrete storage data
  twice per request.
- New SearchStringAnalyzer::getTokenOffsetsForTexts()/
  SearchDebugClient::getTextTokenOffsetsForTexts() batch what used to
  be one Elasticsearch _analyze call per document element (10-20+ per
  token-source page view) into one call, splitting the response back
  out via Elasticsearch's live-confirmed cumulative-offset behavior
  for an array `text`, with a bounds-check fallback to per-text calls
  if that assumption ever doesn't hold.

Caught during live verification (not by any unit test): a numeric-
looking document element (e.g. "400065", a real batch number) crashed
the batched analyze call with a TypeError, because building the
pre-fetch list as `$dict[$element] = true` then `array_keys($dict)`
hit PHP's silent numeric-string-to-int array key coercion — the same
class of bug ExplanationParser::splitByQueryTokens() already
documents guarding against elsewhere in this package. Fixed with a
key-free array_unique() over a plain list, and added a regression
test.

All 168 tests green (up from 156), phpcs/phpstan clean, and every
fix verified live end-to-end against the running app.

Third mechanical seam of the **legacy seam program** (#27); implements and closes #31.

## What

All v1-model coupling in `painter/` — previously spread across three files (~90 `Node::` sites) — now lives in **one compiler module**, `painter/compile.rs`:

1. **Compiler consolidation**: `build_shape`/boolean-op paths (from `geometry.rs`) and `LayerList::{from_scene,from_node,flatten_node}`, `build_render_commands`, and the ancestor-clip walk (from `layer.rs`) move verbatim — all 1686 moved lines byte-identical to their originals. `from_scene`'s public signature is unchanged (cache/runtime call sites untouched). `layer.rs` is now a pure display-list type module; the draw loop `painter.rs` remains at zero `Node::` references.
2. **Debug separation**: `painter_debug_node.rs` → `painter/debug.rs` (git rename, 97% similarity) — the overlay is now an explicit, documented second model consumer rather than one hiding inside the painter (it has zero in-repo consumers; the path rename breaks nobody).

The lock was verified to bite (an injected violation fails with a file:line report).

Without it, the display-list types would need a `node::schema` import for one effects struct and the seam would stay leaky. author: hoelzl
body:
Implements slice 2 of the accepted ConPTY adapter design (`docs/agent/design/conpty-adapter-design.md`, #112). Closes #117.

## What

- **`termverify._conpty.is_supported()`** — explicit thin support probe alongside `spawn`, answering the same precondition `spawn` already checks, so negotiation can fail closed before any spawn is attempted.
- **`termverify.conpty`** (new public, cross-platform, fully ratcheted module):
  - `ConptyChildPort` / `ConptyBindingPort` structural protocols — the child surface shaped exactly like `ConptyChild` (verified statically and at runtime) plus the probe and spawn factory.
  - `ConptyBinding` — default binding delegating to the native module (delegation covered by monkeypatched tests, no real spawn).
  - `UnenforcedConstraintPorts` — shipped default ports reporting all six non-terminal constraints `constraint-not-enforced` with truthful per-constraint rationale; delegated terminal enforcement is refused.
  - `ConptyAdapter` — subject `argv` bound at construction (validated), injected binding + constraint ports, truthful negotiation in `CONSTRAINT_NAMES` order with receipt-binding validation identical to the direct adapter.
- **Terminal constraint owned by the adapter, never delegated:** non-empty requested capabilities → `StartUnsupported(terminal, constraint-unsupported)`; probe reports no ConPTY → `StartUnsupported(terminal, constraint-unsupported)`; a raising probe → `StartFailed`. Fake ports assert `enforce_terminal` is never called.
- **Fail-closed defaults:** with shipped ports, `start()` returns `StartUnsupported(constraint="seed")` before any child exists — the intended outcome per the design.
- **Slice boundary disclosed:** a fully negotiated start returns a structured `StartFailed` (`{"unimplemented": "epoch-machinery"}`) without spawning; tests assert the fake binding's `spawn` is never called. Epoch machinery is slice 3.
- **`termverify._negotiation`** — the receipt-validating negotiation loop extracted unchanged from `termverify.direct` and shared by both adapters (direct-adapter behavior protected by its existing test suite, which is untouched).

## Out of scope (slices 3–4)

Marker protocol, epoch loop, runtime classification matrix, watchdog abort, stop semantics, Windows integration evidence.

## Validation

- `uv --no-config run pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing` — 880 passed, 1 skipped (Windows-only skip of the off-Windows fail-closed spawn test), total coverage 95.66% ≥ 94 floor; `conpty.py` and `_negotiation.py` at 100%.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src tests scripts` (strict) — clean.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` and `--hook-stage pre-push` — all hooks pass.
- `uv --no-config build` — sdist + wheel build.

# Summary
A blur-in animation on large hero imagery provides a sense of depth and elegance, masking raw image loading blocks with a cinematic "lens focusing" effect. This PR introduces a pure HTML/CSS Blur-in Effect for a Hero Image to the EaseMotion examples library, demonstrating how to achieve this without JavaScript while handling common CSS filter rendering artifacts.

---

# Root Cause
Developers frequently implement blur effects but encounter the "edge bleeding" issue where `filter: blur()` causes the image edges to pull in transparency, exposing the container background underneath. To solve this, developers often resort to complex SVG wrappers or Canvas drawing. A much simpler, pure CSS approach involves pairing the blur with a slight `transform: scale()` to push the bleeding edges outside the viewport.

---

# Solution
Added a standalone Blur-in Hero Image example in `submissions/examples/blur-in-effect-for-a-hero-image-ag/`. 
The implementation defines a `@keyframes blurIn` animation that transitions `opacity: 0` to `opacity: 1`, and `filter: blur(20px)` to `filter: blur(0)`. Crucially, it starts the animation at `transform: scale(1.05)` and resolves to `scale(1)`. This guarantees the blurred, transparent edges are pushed outside the container's bounds, while also providing a subtle, elegant "zoom out" effect that mimics a camera lens finding focus. The implementation includes semantic HTML5 structure, responsive absolute positioning for the image under the content, and a strict `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback that bypasses the animation entirely for accessibility compliance.

---

# Files Changed
* `submissions/examples/blur-in-effect-for-a-hero-image-ag/demo.html` - Semantic markup displaying a full-width hero section, image, and foreground content.
* `submissions/examples/blur-in-effect-for-a-hero-image-ag/style.css` - Layout styling, absolute positioning for the background, `@keyframes` definitions, and the `scale()` trick for artifact prevention.
* `submissions/examples/blur-in-effect-for-a-hero-image-ag/README.md` - Documentation detailing usage, CSS filter mechanics, and accessibility benefits.

---

# Testing
* Build passed
* Lint passed
* Tests passed (via manual verification)
* Manual verification completed (Verified zero-JS execution, absence of white edge bleeding during blur, smooth zoom-out transition, and instant-load reduced-motion fallback).

---

# Impact
* Breaking changes: No (Standalone example).
* Performance impact: High. Utilizes hardware-accelerated CSS transforms and opacity, though CSS filters (`blur`) can be slightly heavy on very old mobile GPUs; testing confirms modern device smooth rendering.
* Security impact: None.
* Compatibility: Fully compatible across all modern browsers.

---

# Checklist
* [x] Issue solved
* [x] Build passes
* [x] Tests pass
* [x] Lint passes
* [x] No unrelated changes
* [x] Ready for review

author: skyphusion-rollins
body:
Local leg of vivijure-cf cf#129 phase 1 (cf PR #139). Three things, all catalog-shaped.

## 1. `GET /api/models` now serves the canonical projection (the both-hosts ruling)

The lead ruled a canonical `/api/models` on **both** hosts serving the full projected catalog. It was half-delivered: cf answered with projected planning rows + image rows, while this host still served the hardcoded image rows **alone** (`m10-chat.ts`, zero planning rows). A client reading one endpoint got a different contract depending on which host it talked to. Caught by Joan off the emitted bytes, not off a description.

Now identical on both hosts: same `{models:[...]}` envelope, same six-key row shape, projected planning rows from installed plan.enhance modules plus the image rows.

`/api/storyboard/models` is **unchanged** and remains the planner picker's endpoint here. It is a filtered view of the same projection, not a second catalog, and an agreement test pins the two together. (Worth recording why that matters: "unifying" the planner picker onto `/api/models` before this change would have made the planner go honestly-empty on local while plan.enhance modules were installed -- a self-inflicted regression that would have looked like a correct implementation of the ruling.)

## 2. Image-catalog parity: `@cf/leonardo/lucid-origin` (local#106)

cf served 11 image rows, local 10, on a surface governed by the absolute parity ruling. Delta was exactly one model. Converged **forward, by addition** -- dropping it from cf to "converge" would have deleted a live capability from users inside a cleanup.

Evidence, by strength, with the limit stated:

1. **dispatch (verified, code):** no `provider`, in neither host's bypass list, rides the generic `@cf` text-to-image path that already serves local's other ten rows;
2. **vendor catalog (verified, public docs):** listed active, text-to-image, not retired;
3. **live run on our account (NOT VERIFIED):** needs a credential I do not hold. Recorded as an open checkbox on local#106 rather than glossed.

What makes (3) acceptable rather than a gap: cf **already ships this row**, so that path is exercised in production today. This converges local to the existing status quo rather than making a new untested claim.

Both hosts now diff **byte-identical on the image id set, 11 each**.

## 3. Orphan removal: `src/planner-providers.ts` (local#107)

Local mirror of cf#133. The file had no importer in `src/`; its only consumer anywhere was the test that tested it -- the same dead weight cf cleared after cf#62 moved provider dispatch into the plan.enhance module.

The retired assertion (gateway unified billing wins over a direct BYOK key) is **documented on local#107** along with where that decision lives now (`src/platform/ai-gateway.ts`, covered by `tests/ai-gateway.test.ts`), so the coverage delta is named rather than discovered later. Recommendation on the issue: if that priority is load-bearing, assert it against the live path, not against a caller nothing invokes.

Also: `src/models.ts` becomes types-only (the four legacy Anthropic rows had zero readers), and `byok_alias` / `streaming` are dropped so `ModelEntry` stays key-identical to cf's -- `public/` is a verbatim-shared surface, and a row-shape divergence is drift the shared panel cannot absorb.

## Verification

`tsc` clean (local + chained core). **251 local + 218 core tests passing.**

- **Honest-fail guard negative-tested**, exactly as on cf: hardcoded planning backfill injected into the route, guard **watched failing**, then restored.
- **The new suite caught a bug in itself first.** The route's 60s module-discovery cache let the first no-module call poison every later module-installed case -- which reads as "the route does not project" rather than as test pollution. Fixed with a per-test cache reset and a comment saying why, so the next person does not re-diagnose it.
- **One stale assertion re-scoped rather than left to rot:** `m10-chat-image.test.ts` claimed `/api/models` "returns image catalog" and passed only because its fixture installs no modules. It now states what it actually proves.

Refs: cf#129, local#106, local#107, vivijure-cf#133, vivijure-cf#139

author: boristhoris
body:
## What changed

- add semantic audio and screen-cue contracts for trait interaction lanes and chain surges
- extend reduced-motion coverage across board, HUD, payoff, and recovery feedback surfaces
- harden renderer test setup, local-storage access, and contention-sensitive long-run tests
- avoid duplicate endless-simulation work in health-check mode
- remove unused public exports and keep generated interaction documentation current
- rebase renderer output budgets to the checked production baseline and align Vite's advisory chunk threshold
- make lint reliable on the repository's current memory footprint

## Why

The feedback surfaces had incomplete cross-modal metadata, while several repository gates were unreliable on constrained Android/Termux hardware because expensive deterministic tests and full-repository linting exceeded default runtime or heap assumptions. The bundle gate also compared current output against stale ceilings and emitted an advisory threshold that disagreed with its enforced budget.

## Impact

Trait and payoff feedback now exposes consistent visual/audio semantics, reduced-motion users avoid more residual animation paths, and local verification is repeatable without reducing simulation coverage. Production output remains within explicit checked ceilings.

## Validation

- `yarn typecheck`
- `yarn lint`
- `yarn gate:package-hygiene`
- `yarn gate:security`
- `yarn gate:desktop-build`
- `yarn gate:build-output`
- `yarn gate:long-run`
- `yarn gate:softlock-full`
- `yarn test --maxWorkers=2` (364 files, 2,734 tests)
- `node scripts/system-diagrams.mjs --check-docs`
- `git diff --check`

## Platform note

Playwright 1.57 rejects the Android/ARM64 Termux runtime with `Unsupported platform: android` before test discovery. Blueprint, renderer-layout, and renderer-3D browser gates therefore require a supported Linux, macOS, or Windows runner.

author: pguyson
body:
## Problem

The dev compose stack had two broken pieces in the MQTT plumbing:

1. **CSMS → Mosquitto**: with an empty `config.yaml`, the CSMS fell back to its default `tcp://localhost:1883`, which inside a container does not reach the sibling mosquitto service. Symptom: silent connection failure, no MQTT subscriptions, no telemetry.
2. **HA MQTT integration**: `deploy/ha/configuration.yaml` still declared `broker`, `port`, and `discovery` under `mqtt:` — keys removed in Home Assistant 2024.1+. Symptom: `Invalid config for 'mqtt' ... 'broker' is an invalid option` on HA boot.
3. **Bind-mount footgun**: if `config.yaml` was missing on first `docker compose up`, Docker auto-created it as an empty directory, sending the CSMS into a crash loop (`read /data/config.yaml: is a directory`).

## Fix

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docker-compose.yml` | Add `PANYA_MQTT_BROKER=tcp://mosquitto:1883` env override + `depends_on: mosquitto` so the CSMS uses the service name regardless of `config.yaml`. |
| `deploy/ha/configuration.yaml` | Replace deprecated `mqtt:` block with `mqtt: {}` — broker is configured via the HA UI as in production. |
| `config.yaml.example` | Replace misleading `core-mosquitto` hint with the compose service name `mosquitto`. |
| `docs/development.md` | Mark `cp config.yaml.example config.yaml` as **required** (prevents the directory-creation footgun); drop the now-unnecessary manual broker edit step. |
| `.gitignore` | Add `.omo` (agent tooling). |

## Verification

End-to-end against the compose stack:

```
panya-csms  | INFO mqtt publisher initialized broker=tcp://mosquitto:1883 base_topic=panya
panya-csms  | INFO mqtt connected broker=tcp://mosquitto:1883
panya-csms  | INFO mqtt subscriber connected broker=tcp://mosquitto:1883
panya-csms  | INFO subscribed topic=panya/charge/+/command/set_amps
panya-csms  | INFO starting ocpp csms server port=8887 path=/{ws}
```

Ran an OCPP 1.6-J simulator against `ws://localhost:8887/{ws}` → CSMS published HA discovery, charger device + entities appeared in HA, status updates flowing.

## Checklist

- [x] CSMS connects to Mosquitto by service name
- [x] HA boots without MQTT config errors
- [x] Simulator-triggered `BootNotification` produces HA entities
- [x] Status updates from simulator visible in HA
- [x] Docs updated to match new flow

author: pauldotterer
body:
## What

Flip `GatewayAuthService.EnrollGateway`'s `hostname` field from `omitempty` to **required** (keeping the `hostname_rfc1123,max=253` format constraint).

## Why

The enroll `hostname` was optional and — on the server side — stamped **verbatim** into the issued gateway certificate's DNS SAN. That DNS SAN is exactly what agents verify at the mTLS handshake, so a valid-token enrollee could mint a gateway cert bearing an arbitrary DNS name. ADR 0032 (gateway instance identity subordinate to the SPIFFE class gate) is only sound if the server name is control-authoritative.

The paired server change (spec 31 D1) stops trusting the claim: control derives the DNS SAN from its own `CONTROL_GATEWAY_URL` and refuses to enroll any gateway whose declared hostname does not exactly match that authoritative host (rejecting IP literals, mixed case, trailing dots, and unlisted names). Making the field required forces the operator to configure one canonical name (`GATEWAY_DOMAIN`) on both sides and lets control fail closed on a mismatch.

## Compatibility

Not a wire-breaking change — `buf breaking` passes (the constraint lives in an injected `validate` gotag, invisible to the wire format). The gateway client already always sends `GATEWAY_DOMAIN`, so no gateway behavior changes.

## Checks

- `buf lint` / `buf format` / `buf breaking` — green
- generated Go + TS regenerated via `make generate`

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Enhancements**
  * Gateway enrollment now requires a valid public hostname.
  * Hostnames are checked against the gateway’s configured canonical host.
  * Enrollment rejects IP addresses, unrecognized names, mixed-case hostnames, trailing dots, and mismatched values.
  * Issued gateway certificates now use the verified authoritative hostname.

author: absence0760
body:
The expanded-week editor in the plan wizard rendered every workout's weekday one day early for users in negative-UTC-offset timezones. `new Date(wo.scheduled_date)` parsed the bare `YYYY-MM-DD` as UTC midnight, and `.toLocaleDateString()` rendered that in local time — UTC midnight is the previous evening in the Americas, so a Sunday long run showed as "Sat" on every row.

Switched the parse to `parseISO()` (local-midnight construction, already the idiom in `PlanCalendar` and plan-detail), so the displayed weekday is correct in every timezone. Pure display fix; the stored `scheduled_date` payload is untouched.

Added a `TZ=America/New_York` unit test that renders a known Sunday and asserts "Sun", pinning the previous UTC-midnight behavior ("Sat") as the regression it guards.

Fixes #337

author: johnjallday
body:
## Router Refactor — G2a: workspace attachments + trash

First of **5 granular slices** of the workspace runtime family (G2). The family's dispatcher — `routeWorkspaceRuntimeRequest`, cyclomatic complexity 93, 47 handlers — is too big to migrate in one reviewable PR, so it's split by route family: **attachments (this PR)** → tasks → store-nodes → directories+folders → agents+misc (the last deletes `routeWorkspaceRuntimeRequest`).

**Net −97 lines.** Lands under the G0 golden route-table net.

### What changed
- New `workspace.RegisterRoutes(mux, *HTTPHandler)` registers the 11 attachment/trash routes as explicit Go 1.22 method+patterns (it grows one family per slice). Called from `server/routes.go`; patterns are strictly more specific than the `/api/workspaces/` subtree, so ServeMux dispatches them and leaves the rest to `routeWorkspaceRuntimeRequest` (until migrated).
- Handlers read `{workspaceID}` / `{attachmentId}` via `r.PathValue` — matching the existing workspace convention (runs, triggers), not `{id}`.
- Removed `TrimPrefix`+`Split` extraction from 11 handlers (across `http_handlers_attachment.go` and `http_handlers_folder.go`), the shared `attachmentRouteParts` helper's path parsing, and every per-handler method guard (the mux owns method dispatch).

### Behavior changes (all intended; real routes unchanged)
The golden records changes only on wrong-method / nonsensical requests:
- Wrong methods on sub-actions (`relink`/`trash`/`restore`/`locate`/`move`) now return **405** instead of an accidental 404/400.
- `GET` on attachment paths (not a real endpoint) falls through to the workspace handler; cleanly 405ing it needs the workspace-CRUD routes migrated too.

### Verification
- workspace + server tests green; vet + staticcheck clean.
- Golden re-proven env-stable (external tools present vs hidden → identical table).
- Real-server smoke of the full lifecycle: create→201, move-to-trash→200, list-trash→count 1, restore→200, bulk-trash→200, delete→200, and wrong-method `DELETE .../relink`→405.

### Next
Once merged, **G2b (tasks)** branches from the updated `origin/dev`.

author: gaoflow
body:
`FBig`/`DBig` → float conversion rounds the source to a fixed 53/24-bit intermediate and then lets `f{32,64}::encode` round again into the format's exponent-dependent subnormal grid. That second rounding is wrong in two ways. This is the subnormal counterpart of the normal-range double-rounding that was recently addressed.

**Subnormal double-rounding (1 ULP).** A subnormal has fewer than 53/24 significant bits — its spacing is fixed at `2^-1074` / `2^-149` — so the fixed intermediate keeps bits below the subnormal grid. For a value just past a subnormal halfway, the intermediate rounds *to* the halfway (dropping the excess that lifts it above) and `encode` then rounds half-to-even *down*, one ULP below the correctly-rounded value:

```rust
// value = (2m+1)·2^-1075 + 2^-1135, just above the halfway between subnormals m and m+1
let sig = (IBig::from(2 * m + 1) << 60) + IBig::ONE;
let v = FBig::<HalfEven, 2>::from_parts(sig, -1135);
v.to_f64(); // returned m·2^-1074 (rounded to even); correct is (m+1)·2^-1074
```

**Debug panic / release double-round on high-precision inputs.** `to_f64`/`to_f32` feed the *unrounded* source significand into the base-changing division, whose `debug_assert!(lhs.digits() <= self.precision + rhs.digits())` fires whenever the significand is wider than the target precision:

```rust
DBig::from_str("123456789012345678.9012345678901")?.to_f64(); // panics in debug builds
```

In release the assert is compiled out and the oversized quotient is re-rounded downstream — a silent double rounding.

**Fix.** Round the source *once*, straight to the target's precision at its own magnitude (`min(53, e + 1075)` bits for f64 at binary exponent `e`, analogously for f32), so `encode` re-rounds nothing. To keep that single rounding correct without an exact arbitrary-precision conversion, the source is first taken to a fixed, generous width with round-to-odd; rounding that down to the final width then reproduces the correctly-rounded result for every rounding mode. The division now rounds an over-wide quotient down to the requested precision instead of assuming the caller pre-bounded the dividend, so the assertion is removed and high-precision inputs convert without panicking (and without the release double-round).

Correctness holds to within the base conversion's working precision; a value closer to a boundary than the conversion resolves stays a pre-existing limitation of finite-precision base changing (shared with `with_base`). The base-2 / `Repr` paths are exact for all inputs.

Tests cover subnormal halfways nudged just past the boundary across the exponent range, in both base 2 and base 10, for f64 (oracle: `float()`) and f32 (oracle: exact `Fraction` → nearest `2^-149`, not `numpy.float32`, which itself double-rounds), plus the high-precision decimals that previously panicked. `cargo test --workspace --exclude dashu-python`, `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets --workspace --exclude dashu-python -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` all pass.

author: mysteraitch
body: ## Summary Convention change (#826): a value position that renders an em dash for an **absent** value (no value at all — a NULL column, an unset field, an undefined denominator) now renders a **middle dot `·`** with an accessible label, instead. Blank-but-present values keep their existing `(blank)`-style humanised handling untouched. Prose em dashes (sentence punctuation) are unaffected — only value-position markers changed. Rationale (from the issue): the em dash doubles as prose separator throughout the site, so `—` in a cell is ambiguous, and a bare glyph carries no accessible name. `·` in a value position reads unambiguously as "nothing here", and both surfaces now carry `title`/`aria-label` = "not recorded" (or a more specific label where one is warranted). ## Helper design (constant + helper first, per the issue's implementation-shape comment) - **Build-side** — `src/ci/render/format.ts`: `absentMarker(label = ABSENT_LABEL)` returns `·`. Exported constants: `ABSENT_MARKER` (`'·'`), `ABSENT_CLASS` (`'absent'`), `ABSENT_LABEL` (`'not recorded'`). Re-exported through `site-render.ts`'s barrel like every other render helper. - **Client-side** — `site/field-wrappers.js`: `absentMarker(el, label = ABSENT_LABEL)`, same shape, using the shared `ElementFactory` pattern the other field wrappers (`licenceField`, `statusField`, …) already use. - Same class name, same default label, same glyph on both sides, so an absent value looks and behaves identically wherever it appears. - CSS: `.absent{color:var(--muted)}` added to both `site/style.css` and the generated pages' shared affordance CSS block (`src/ci/render/page.ts`), matching the existing `.zero` de-emphasis convention. The accessible name lives in the element's own attributes, never in colour alone. ## Adoption table | Site | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `site/app.js` — FOI-history vintage cell | bare `—` | `absentMarker(el)` | | `site/app.js` — register-history vintage cell | *(see note below — no marker actually exists here)* | unchanged | | `site/compare.js` — match-percentage cell | bare `—`, inline in `renderCounts` | extracted to exported `matchPercentCell(total, matching)` for testability; uses `absentMarker(el)` | | `src/ci/build-dataset-pages.ts` — sheet rows/cols/class (×3) | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-dataset-pages.ts` — FOI entry meta.json "data vintage" row | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-dataset-pages.ts` — requested/responded (×2) | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-dataset-pages.ts` — open-data meta.json "declared coverage" row | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-dataset-pages.ts` — per-series issuing status | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-dataset-pages.ts` — FOI index vintage column | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-forbidden-section.ts` — suffix lists (×2: `suffixCodes`/`suffixLinks`) | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-forbidden-section.ts` — per-callsign table "original start" cell *(found via grep, adopted)* | `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-home-aggregates.ts` — zero-total `sharePct` fallback | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` (4 table columns switched to `raw: true` so the HTML fragment renders instead of being escaped) | | `src/ci/build-home-aggregates.ts` — zero-hit detector's example column *(found via grep, adopted)* | `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-interdataset-stats.ts` — declared-coverage column | bare `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `src/ci/build-interdataset-stats.ts` — flag-absent-from-a-publication cell *(found via grep, adopted)* | `—` | `absentMarker()` | | `site/table-sort.js` `BLANK_SORT_TOKENS` | `—`/`–` only | `·` added; `—`/`–` kept for backwards compatibility with previously rendered content | ### Deliberately left (with reasons) - **`site/app.js` register-history vintage cell** — the issue's scope list names this, but on inspection the register-history table's "publication" column always has a value (it iterates every known dataset, never a NULL join); there is no em-dash branch there to adopt. Only the FOI-history table's vintage cell (added in #825/#811) actually has one. - **`build-forbidden-section.ts`'s "in current register" cell (`regCell`)** — renders `✓`/`—` for a present boolean fact ("is this callsign in the current register: yes/no"), not an absent *value*. Left as the existing dash so as not to conflate "known false" with "no value recorded"; flagged here for visibility. - **Markdown-only report generators** (`cross-dataset-invariants.ts`, `dataset-status.ts`, `value-catalogue.ts`, `forbidden-suffix-history.ts`, `report-sweep.ts`) — these emit `.md` files, not HTML; there is no DOM element to carry `title`/`aria-label`, and the issue's measured scope names only the HTML/JS render surfaces. Left as `—`. - **`build-publisher-pages.ts` / `site/home.css` decorative `::before` glyphs** — CSS `content: "—"` on an empty hold-map cell's pseudo-element, not a text/value DOM node; no accessible-name attachment point exists there. Left unchanged. ## Tests - `src/ci/render/format.test.ts` / `site/field-wrappers.test.ts`: new `absentMarker`/`AbsentMarker` coverage — default label, custom label, HTML-escaping, glyph identity (never an em dash), always carries `title`+`aria-label`. - `site/table-sort.test.ts` / `site/table-controls.test.ts`: `·` added to the blank-token fixtures; new dedicated tests that `·` is recognised as blank and sinks to the end of a sort like the dash placeholders it replaced. - `site/app.test.ts`: `FoiHistoryTable_WhenAVintageIsAbsent_...` updated to assert the marker element (class/glyph/title/aria-label) instead of the literal em dash. - `site/compare-match-percent.test.ts` (new): unit tests for the extracted `matchPercentCell`. - `src/ci/build-home-aggregates.test.ts` / `src/ci/build-interdataset-stats.test.ts`: the two existing tests that pinned a literal em dash (found via a repo-wide grep, not in the issue's original list) updated to assert `absentMarker()`. - Full real-archive builds (`build-dataset-pages.test.ts`, `build-forbidden-section.test.ts`, `build-home-aggregates.test.ts`, `build-interdataset-stats.test.ts`) pass unchanged otherwise — no golden fixtures needed regenerating beyond the two literal-string test assertions above. ## Verification - `npm run test:unit`: **2050 passed, 278 skipped, 0 failed** (139 files passed, 18 skipped). - `npm run typecheck`: clean. - `npm run lint`: clean. ## Visual evidence (headless Playwright, light + dark) Client surface — FOI-history table, a callsign with an absent observation vintage: - Before: [light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterAitch/amateur-callsigns-file-watch/f1f90bd00cdb723ab5960fd19c9c18759b6335d7/826/client-before-light.png) · [dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterAitch/amateur-callsigns-file-watch/f1f90bd00cdb723ab5960fd19c9c18759b6335d7/826/client-before-dark.png) - After: [light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterAitch/amateur-callsigns-file-watch/f1f90bd00cdb723ab5960fd19c9c18759b6335d7/826/client-after-light.png) · [dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterAitch/amateur-callsigns-file-watch/f1f90bd00cdb723ab5960fd19c9c18759b6335d7/826/client-after-dark.png) Build surface — a real FOI dataset page with absent meta fields (`archive/foi/ofcom-299351--available-list-referral`: undated request, unrecorded data vintage): - Before: [full page, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterAitch/amateur-callsigns-file-watch/f1f90bd00cdb723ab5960fd19c9c18759b6335d7/826/build-before-light.png) · [dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterAitch/amateur-callsigns-file-watch/f1f90bd00cdb723ab5960fd19c9c18759b6335d7/826/build-before-dark.png) · [focused crop, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterAitch/amateur-callsigns-file-watch/f1f90bd00cdb723ab5960fd19c9c18759b6335d7/826/build-cr

Applies the surviving findings from the post-land review of #11 (adversarially verified; 4 candidates refuted and dropped).

**Behaviour fixes (`preview.js`)**
- Stale-alt restore: a broken embed edited to a different working image kept the old image's alt until a full re-render - the rewire path now only falls back to the stash when the DOM diff left alt blank.
- Alt resurrection: the observer now watches `alt` and re-blanks a broken image whose alt the diff re-synced, preventing the native fallback rendering jammed against the CSS placeholder.
- `role="img"` + `aria-label` keeps the placeholder in the accessibility tree despite `alt=""`.

**Cleanups**
- Shared masked-icon base rule for the two placeholder pseudos (copies had already drifted).
- `--mps-gutter-font` generalised to `--mps-mono-font`, consumed by the broken-image label instead of a duplicated stack; dead `var()` fallbacks dropped.
- Harness: `<base href>` replaces the regex font-URL rewrite (also un-masks the attachments/ retry fidelity gap - that image now loads in the harness as live); heading assertion covers h2 family/weight (mutation-verified).
- Stale `extension.js` comment updated; the find-in-page/selection loss of generated-content filenames is documented as accepted.

Tests: 160/160 unit, 20/20 visual assertions.

body:
Two commits.

**Stop shipping dev artefacts in production archives.** The exclude list predated the PHPStan baselines and PHPUnit caches this suite now generates, so every archive carried them. Trumpet's build script had already been updated; the other sixteen had not, which is why its zip was the only clean one. author: ogprotege
body:
# Vigil foundation (milestones M0–M3)

Everything below the app UI for a reliable, on-device AI usage monitor. The full product plan, verified provider research, and decision records ship inside this PR under `docs/`.

## What's in here

**`protocol/` — the cross-language contract (the crown jewels)**
- `providers.json`: Claude + Codex usage endpoints, exact headers (including the load-bearing `claude-code/x.y.z` User-Agent), poll policy (≥5 min, jitter, 429 backoff 15→60 min), and data-driven response mappings.
- `fixtures/`: captured-shape provider responses paired with expected normalized outputs. Both the TypeScript CLI and Swift core are tested against the *same files* — mapper drift fails CI, not users.
- `qr-vectors/`: deterministic payload ⇄ QR-chunk pairs. CLI asserts the encode direction, VigilKit the decode direction.

**`cli/` — `vigil-link` (npx-runnable, stateless, one runtime dependency)**
- `vigil-link` — discovers credentials (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, macOS Keychain) or mints Vigil its own Claude token pair via browser OAuth + PKCE (ADR-0005: never fights Claude Code over refresh tokens), live-verifies each account, renders chunked `vigil1` QR codes with a consent gate + terminal auto-clear.
- `vigil-link status` — your session/weekly windows in the terminal.
- `vigil-link doctor` — credential discovery diagnosis.
- 57 tests: fixture parity, fixture-server E2E (429/401-refresh paths), OAuth mint flow incl. state-mismatch guard and manual-paste fallback, property-tested chunking, token redaction, golden outputs.

**`packages/VigilKit/` — Swift core for the iOS/macOS app**
- Normalized models, data-driven `UsageMapper`, `FetchScheduler` actor with a file-backed 429 ledger shared across app/widget processes (the anti-stale-data mechanism), `SnapshotStore`, `ThresholdEngine` (80/95% crossings), Keychain vault (`AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`), and the `vigil1` QR decoder (raw-DEFLATE via Compression).
- XCTests mirror every CLI parity suite plus scheduler-ledger math and threshold semantics.

**`docs/`** — architecture, provider spec (with the verified endpoint research), QR protocol, privacy stance ("Data Not Collected", truthfully), Mac build checklist, six ADRs.

## Verification

- `cd cli && npm ci && npm run build && npm test` → 57/57 green locally (Linux).
- CI: `cli.yml` (ubuntu) + `apple.yml` (macOS, `swift test` on VigilKit — the compile-check for Swift authored off-Mac).
- First real-credential smoke lives in `docs/mac-checklist.md` (run `vigil-link status` on your machine, camera-scan a QR, exercise the mint flow).

## Notes for the reviewer

- macOS CI minutes are free only on public repos (10× billing on private) — see checklist notes.
- `vigil-link` npm name reservation needs your npm login (checklist step 4).
- Codex token refresh endpoint is unverified → v1 surfaces expiry as a re-link prompt.
- Next milestone (M4): SwiftUI app onboarding + dashboard on top of this core.

author: ubugeeei
body: ## Why PR #21 (`ci/pr-previews`) was squash-merged, but the `musea-preview` CI job it added fails on every PR: ``` vize musea: could not find Vite. Install vite and @vizejs/vite-plugin-musea, then run from your project root. ``` `vize musea serve --build` resolves `vite` from the project root's `node_modules`. `vite@8.1.5` was only present transitively (via `vite-plus` and the `@vizejs/*` plugins), so pnpm never symlinked it into the top-level `node_modules`, and the lookup failed. `@vizejs/vite-plugin-musea` was already a direct dep; `vite` was the missing half of what the error asks for. ## Fix Declare `vite` as a direct devDependency. The lockfile already resolved `vite@8.1.5`, so this only registers the existing version as a direct import (no version churn) and lets pnpm surface `node_modules/vite`. ```jsonc "typescript": "^7.0.2", "vite": "^8.1.5", "vite-plus": "^0.2.5", ``` Verified locally: after `pnpm install`, `pnpm exec vp run musea:build` succeeds and emits `dist-musea/` with the `__musea__/` gallery entry. This is a follow-up to the already-merged #21. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is enabled.

## What this is

The real, working A2A protocol feature from #316, extracted and re-implemented cleanly. #316's branch (misleadingly named `fix/action-versions`) had accumulated a large amount of unrelated content on top of the genuine A2A work:

- A stray junk file (`so`, containing leaked shell/scratch output) committed inside the main feature commit.
- A stale, buggy copy of `include/q4nx_reader.h` that would have **regressed** an already-fixed correctness bug on `main` (it splits GGUF architecture tags on digits as well as `-`/`_`, which mangles names like `qwen3` → loses the version digit; `main`'s current copy deliberately doesn't do that).
- Stale copies of `include/common.h`, `include/backend_manager.h`, `src/backend_manager.cpp`, `src/backend_npu.cpp`, `src/gguf_loader.cpp`, `src/model_discovery.cpp` — all older than what's currently on `main` (predates this session's model-agnostic router work) and would have wiped out real, already-merged functionality if merged as-is.
- Unrelated gitnexus skill docs, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` tweaks, and CI Actions version-pin fixes bundled in from the branch's actual original purpose (`fix/action-versions`).

This PR contains **only** the A2A protocol code, re-targeted at current `main`.

## Why a fresh reimplementation, not a cherry-pick

#316's branch predates a migration in this repo from a raw-socket HTTP loop to `cpp-httplib` in `tests/zaya_server.cpp`. The original A2A endpoint code (`write(cl, ...)`, manual `accept()`/`read()` loop) doesn't apply to the current `httplib::Server`-based file at all — the endpoints were re-implemented against `svr.Get`/`svr.Post`, with the SSE streaming endpoint using `res.set_chunked_content_provider(...)` in place of raw socket writes. The logic (Agent Card structure, task lifecycle states, peer routing) is preserved as originally designed.

## New endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` | Agent Card — skills: `text-generation`, `model-discovery` |
| `POST /a2a/v1/message:send` | Task-based inference (sync) |
| `POST /a2a/v1/message:sendStream` | SSE streaming with `taskStatus`/`taskArtifact` events |
| `POST /a2a/v1/tasks:route` | Delegate inference to a peer agent by skill match |

New CLI flag: `--a2a-peer <url>` (repeatable) — registers and discovers remote A2A peers at startup.

New file: `tests/a2a_client.h` (unmodified from the source branch — self-contained, no dependency on any of the stale infra above).

## Verification

- ✅ Builds clean: `cmake --build build --target zaya_server -j$(nproc)`.
- ✅ Smoke-tested against a running server: fetched `/.well-known/agent-card.json`, confirmed `/` health now includes an `agentCard` pointer, confirmed `POST /a2a/v1/message:send` returns a well-formed `TASK_STATE_FAILED` response when no model is loaded (rather than crashing or hanging).
- Not yet tested: multi-peer `tasks:route` delegation (needs two running instances) and the SSE `sendStream` path end-to-end with a real streaming client — both use the same underlying `a2a_handle_message`/`A2AClient` logic already exercised above, but haven't been separately verified.

## Related

Supersedes the A2A portion of #316. Recommend closing #316 once this merges (I'll leave that decision to you rather than closing it in this PR, since #316 still nominally intersects with the also-legitimate `fix/action-versions` CI work it started as — worth checking whether that part is still needed separately).

author: julianam-w
body:
## What

`generate_metric_definitions_macro()` in `scripts/build_reporting_assets.py`
ran unconditionally, for every deployment. Gates it to
`DEPLOYMENT == "standard"`, mirroring the existing survey-model generation
gate (`DEPLOYMENT != "standard"`) immediately below it.

## Why

For non-standard (deployment repo) builds, the generator:
1. regenerates a local `macros/metric_definitions.sql` from
   `csv/metric_definitions.csv` + any deployment-specific
   `csv/metric_definitions_{deployment}.csv`, and
2. **deletes the package's own `metric_definitions.sql`** if one exists on disk.

If that regenerated local file is ever committed in a deployment repo, it
duplicates the `get_metric_definitions` macro name against the package's copy
(both live on `macro-paths`) — a hard `dbt` compilation error on the
deployment's next `dbt deps`. This is exactly what happened in
`tamanu-dbt-msf-kule`: a tracked local `macros/metric_definitions.sql`
collided with the package's canonical copy on a fresh `dbt deps`. Resolved
there by removing the local macro (the package's canonical registry already
carried every one of Kule's 29 metric definitions — verified identical
`metric_id` sets before deleting). This PR fixes the root cause so the build
script doesn't regenerate a colliding local copy for any deployment going
forward.

## Scope check

Confirmed no deployment repo currently ships a
`csv/metric_definitions_{deployment}.csv` localised-extension file that this
change would silently stop merging (checked `tamanu-dbt-msf-kule`, which has
none). If a deployment repo *does* introduce localised metric-definition
extensions later, this call site would need revisiting — worth flagging in
review if anyone knows of a repo already relying on that merge behaviour.

## Verified

- `python -m ast` syntax check passes.
- Existing unit tests (`scripts/tests/test_generate_metric_definitions_macro.py`,
  14 tests, covering the pure helper functions) pass unchanged — this fix
  only touches the orchestration call site, not the generator itself.

author: niksedk
body:
Follow-up to #12605 — fixes the remaining bugs found in the code audit.

## OCR window

1. **Forced-filter regression from #12604:** the unknown-words orphan sweep in `DeleteSelectedLines` checked membership against `OcrSubtitleItems`, which can be filtered to forced-only — deleting a visible row then permanently wiped the unknown-word entries of every hidden (non-forced, not deleted) row. Now checks the full `_allOcrSubtitleItems` list.
2. **Delete during a running OCR corrupted the run:** all OCR loops capture indices into `OcrSubtitleItems` at start, but the Delete key/context menu stayed active while OCR ran — deleting a row shifted every later index (text landing on the wrong row) and eventually threw out of the background task, leaving `IsOcrRunning` stuck true with the window in a dead "running" state. `DeleteSelectedLines` now no-ops while OCR is running (matching the other controls, which are already disabled during a run).
3. **VobSub color chooser previewed the wrong image:** it passed the item's position in the (possibly filtered or delete-mutated) grid collection into the source-indexed `GetSubPicture`. `OcrSubtitleItem` now exposes its stable `SourceIndex` and the color chooser uses it.

## Other

4. **MicroDVD:** the empty-time-code repair only fixed the first `{}`, so a `{}{}Text` line was half-repaired and then discarded as a parse error. Both codes are now repaired (unit tests added for both the single- and double-empty cases).
5. **Burn-in with cut enabled burned the wrong lines:** the `-ss` before `-i` makes ffmpeg restart timestamps at zero, but the generated ASSA kept absolute times — a 10:00→12:00 cut showed the 00:00–02:00 dialogue (or nothing). The subtitle is now limited to the cut window and shifted by −cutStart, exactly like `TransparentSubtitlesViewModel.GetSubtitleBasedOnCut` already does. The live preview is unaffected (it builds its own ASSA and passes no seek).
6. **TTS Review Speech lockup:** the play commands disable every row before awaiting `PlayAudio`, and only the playback timer re-enables them — so an mpv init/load failure threw out of the async command and left all play/regenerate buttons dead until the window was reopened (and an exception escaping an async command can tear down the Avalonia dispatcher). `PlayAudio` now catches the failure, resets the playback UI state, and shows the error, mirroring its existing missing-file handling.

Tests: 2 new MicroDVD tests; full libse (558), seconv (242), and libuilogic (14) suites pass; UI builds with zero warnings. The UI fixes (2, 3, 5, 6) were verified by inspection, not exercised in the running app.

author: averagejoematt
body:
## What & why

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (header "Verified: 2026-07-10") carried **six false operational claims** that the prose-class `scripts/check_doc_facts.py` did not police. All six reproduced verbatim; an incident responder using the cron table would misdiagnose a stale-brief incident. Each is corrected to ground truth **read from the cited CDK/lambda source** (not guessed), and the highest-stakes claim — the compute cron table — is now a synced fact via a new self-contained gate rule.

### The six corrections (old → new · source)

| # | Claim | Old | New | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Compute cron table | computes at `cron(20–35 17 …)` (10:20–10:35 UTC, **AFTER** the 17:00 brief) | character `cron(30 16 …)` / adaptive `cron(35 16 …)` / metrics `cron(40 16 …)` / insight `cron(45 16 …)` — 09:30–09:45 PT, **BEFORE** the brief | `cdk/stacks/compute_stack.py:192/205/282/295` (Phase 3.1 "…completes BEFORE daily-brief at 17:00") |
| 2 | site-api Stack | `LifePlatformOperational` | `LifePlatformServe` (#793) | `cdk/stacks/serve_stack.py` |
| 3 | Concurrency quota | **10** (default) | **100** | `aws lambda get-account-settings` → `ConcurrentExecutions=100` |
| 4 | Rate limiting | "In-memory sliding window (module-level dicts)" | DDB-backed `lambdas/rate_limiter.py`; the dicts are the fail-open fallback only | `rate_limiter.py:1-25`, `site_api_ai_lambda.py:143-144` ("legacy, only used if DDB rate_limiter fails") |
| 5 | Cost profile | "~$13/month … Anthropic API $8-12 … Total ~$18-23" | ~$80/month all-in against the $85 Bedrock/budget ceiling; Bedrock (ADR-062/049) is the dominant driver | `core_stack.py` `amount=85`; ARCHITECTURE.md:89 states $85 correctly |
| 6 | "three doors" | Cockpit `/now/`, Story, Evidence | live five-door v5 IA: `/cockpit/`, `/data/`, `/coaching/`, `/protocols/`, `/story/` (fixed in header prose **and** the ASCII diagram) | CLAUDE.md v5 IA / live site |

The header **Verified** date is bumped `2026-07-10 → 2026-07-18`. Scope was held to exactly these six claims — no unrelated prose was rewritten.

## Regression guard (`scripts/check_doc_facts.py`)

Self-contained addition (new functions + wiring, no refactor of existing rules):

- `_cdk_cron_map()` parses `function_name → schedule` cron **per function block** from `cdk/stacks/*.py` (drops templated `cron(0 {INGEST_HOURLY} …)`).
- `_cron_hits(files, cdk_map)` flags any live doc line that quotes **exactly one** `cron(…)` next to **exactly one** known CDK function whose value disagrees.
- Precision guards: hyphen-aware name matching (`wednesday-chronicle` ≠ `wednesday-chronicle-schedule`), `HISTORICAL`-exempt lines, and frozen snapshots (`docs/reviews/`, `docs/archive/`, `CHANGELOG`) already out of scope via the existing `EXEMPT_DIRS`/`EXEMPT_FILES`. This is why the many stale cron tables in `docs/reviews/REVIEW_BUNDLE_*.md` do not trip it.

This would have caught the 2-month-stale table the day `compute_stack.py` changed.

### Non-vacuity proof

Live plant-and-restore in the doc:

```
$ # reintroduce the stale cron for character-sheet-compute, then run the gate
❌ 1 live doc/source line(s) state a stale platform number as current fact:
   docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:138: cron for `character-sheet-compute` claims cron(35 17 * * ? *), CDK schedules cron(30 16 * * ? *) (#1205)
EXIT=1
$ # restore
restored EXIT=0
```

Plus unit tests in `tests/test_wiki_checkers.py`: `test_cron_gate_is_not_vacuous` (catches a stale cron, passes the correct one, exempts history / hyphen-suffixed rule names / ambiguous multi-cron lines), `test_cdk_cron_map_discovers_from_source` (ground truth is live-discovered, not pinned), `test_cron_gate_clean_on_current_tree`.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/check_doc_facts.py` → **exit 0** (87 docs + 227 source files scanned).
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_wiki_checkers.py -q` → **12 passed**.
- `black lambdas/ mcp/ cdk/ tests/ scripts/ deploy/ --check` → all 730 files unchanged.
- `flake8 scripts/check_doc_facts.py tests/test_wiki_checkers.py` → clean (exit 0).

## Post-merge ops

**None.** Docs-only change + a `scripts/` CI-gate rule. No Lambda, no site, no CDK, no AWS mutation — nothing to deploy. The new gate runs in the existing docs-CI (`test_doc_facts_clean` / `test_wiki_checkers.py`).

Fixes #1205

## Summary

- upgrade campaign reports to schema v8 with typed target-runtime and target-catalog receipts
- require one explicit portable providers config and pass it unchanged to every target Harn subprocess
- resolve `--catalog-routes` from the target catalog, so planning and execution use the same provider/model aliases
- fail closed on missing, unreadable, malformed, or target-rejected catalog input before any live dispatch
- remove Burin/home-directory credential fallback and use exact `assert_eq` contracts in the touched tests

## Why

A campaign must attribute both the binary and catalog that produced its evidence. The prior head planned routes from the caller VM but executed provider probes through a separate target Harn process, allowing aliases and pins to diverge. The repaired boundary accepts a generic providers TOML path, validates it once, forwards it as `HARN_PROVIDERS_CONFIG`, and records the target catalog status, path, SHA-256, counts, and command environment. No Burin path or machine-specific fallback is embedded in Harn.

## Summary
- **#535 (P0)**: `BACnetClient::stop()` in the vendored client now stops the network layer + transport so the UDP socket fd is actually released. Previously every per-operation client leaked one socket (~180 fds/h measured on the OT bench), hitting EMFILE at ~5 h uptime — HTTP/health died and weather fell back permanently ("frozen fallback weather" in Workbench). Regression test asserts stable `/proc/self/fd` count across 50 client start/stop cycles.
- **Weather stale-hold**: on a transient fetch error the service now holds the last good reading (marked stale, `app-fault` BV active) instead of replacing the cache with the canned 70.0/50.0 fallback.
- **#537**: hosted server is built via the generic builder so `vendor_id 999` reaches I-Am responses (BIP builder has no `vendor_id` setter; default 0 is ASHRAE reserved).
- **#539**: `/bacnet/whois` filters the device-table snapshot by the requested `low`/`high` instance range instead of returning all seeded/out-of-range devices.

Evidence: nightly OT bench report 2026-07-18 round 2 (§3 fd instrumentation 52→142 fds/30 min; §4 I-Am hex `…2100`; §10 #539 whois snapshot).

body:
## 概要

常時注入される CLAUDE.md + `rules/*.md` を **66577 バイト → 23293 バイト**（約 22.75 KiB / 23.29 十進 KB）に削減し、あわせてツール結果の捏造を防ぐ検証ゲートを常時ルールへ組み込み、軽微な陳腐化（ターミナル記述）を修正した。親 Issue #66 の対策 P3 / P6 / P7 に対応する。

削減は「削除」ではなく「統合・圧縮・docs/ への退避」を基本とし、規範の情報自体は失っていない（reference 系は `~/.claude/docs/` へ移動、改訂ログはスキルへ移設）。

### 主な変更

- **reference 系を docs/ へ退避**: `codex-config.md` / `mermaid-conventions.md` を `rules/` から `docs/` へ移動（常時注入から外す）。CLAUDE.md の chezmoi 運用詳細も `docs/chezmoi-workflow.md` へ退避し、コア規範のみ CLAUDE.md に残した

- **ポインタのみの rule を削除**: `task-delegation.md`（改訂ログは task-delegation スキルへ移設）
- **tool-call-hygiene を縮約**: 8.8KB → 4.0KB。Case A/B 分岐 + 必須ルール要点のみ残し、詳細は `tool-call-parse-recovery` スキルに委譲
- **検証ゲートを組み込み（#72）**: 実在確認 / 不確実性の明示 / 根拠の引用の 3 点を tool-call-hygiene に追加（`postcompact-reinject.py` の GUARDRAIL と用語・トーンを整合）

参照元（`doc-polish` / `task-delegation` / `peer-review` スキル・CLAUDE.md）のリンクは全件、新パスへ張り替え済み。

### 受け入れ条件のステータス
