author: matthijsgroen
body:
Two SiteMap display bugs reported from mobile playtest.

## 1. Entrance staircase renders as completed
Portals (entrance/stairhead/exit) are transitions, not tasks. The completed treatment — 45% dim + ✓ badge — only excluded the `entrance` shape, but the entrance on deeper floors is a **stairhead** (it has a stairId), and `useAssembledFloor` force-marks the entrance cell explored → completed. So it showed a ✓ and dimmed. Fix: exclude all portal kinds (`entrance`/`stairhead`/`exit`) from the dim and the badge.

## 2. Player marker walks to the staircase on floor switch
`ExplorerDot` wasn't keyed by floor, so a floor change kept the same component and animated a walk from the previous floor's coordinates to the new entrance. `grid` reference identity can't gate this (it changes on every in-floor room completion too). Fix: pass `currentFloor` and key the dot by it — a floor switch remounts the dot, hitting its existing first-render **snap** (no walk). Within a floor the key is stable, so normal step animation is untouched.

## Tests
- A completed stairhead shows no ✓ (a completed regular room still does — control).
- The dot lands at the new floor's entrance immediately after a floor switch.
- 846 tests pass; `yarn check-types`, `yarn lint` clean. No world/data changes.

author: edspencer
body:
## Epic G / G5 — Hook-management MCP

Builds on the merged **G1 hook foundation** (#296). Exposes the G1 `HookService` as three self-management MCP tools on `paddock_manage`, so a project agent can declare/edit/delete its own event hooks — the MCP twin of the future Hooks tab (G4), mirroring the shipped schedule-management tools (`set_schedule`/`remove_schedule`/`list_schedules`).

### Tools (in the `if (write)` seam G1 left)
- **`list_hooks`** — read-only; every hook + its `hook-<slug>-<name>` agent + flattened capabilities.
- **`set_hook`** — create-or-update. `enabled` is **just a field** (no separate enable/disable verbs, per GG-3). A brand-new hook defaults **`enabled: false`** so nothing fires the instant it's written; an update that omits `enabled` **preserves** the current armed state. Capabilities (`allowed_tools`, `denied_tools`, `permission_mode`, `model`, `max_turns`) are flat args; `coerceToolList` tolerates the CLI-runtime MCP transport dropping array types (accepts a JSON array **or** a comma/newline-separated string), the same lesson as `fork_chat_batch`.
- **`remove_hook`** — persisted removal + unregisters the agent; echoes `removed: false` when absent.

Each delegates to `HookService` (persist to `project.yaml`, then register the `hook-<slug>-<name>` agent) — no re-implementation of the two-step.

### Gate (GG-4)
A **per-project `hooksMcpEnabled` opt-in**, sibling of `selfMcpWriteEnabled`, **default OFF**:
- Instance default `PADDOCK_HOOKS_MCP` (+ YAML instance config), with a per-project `project.yaml` override, resolved like `maxSpawnDepth` via `resolveHooksMcpEnabled` (override else instance default).
- The gate is **binary access to the MCP** — an agent that has the tools can create hooks at any capability. **No** per-capability gating, **no** curator/kind split, **no** "can't grant more than your own scope."
- Injection-level: when off, the tools are **absent** from the injected server (distinct from the schedule tools' runtime-refuse gate).

Only meaningful when the self-MCP write tools are also on (the hook tools live in the write block).

### Tests
- `self-mcp.test.ts` — the three handlers (record-building, capability flattening, project defaulting, error paths, callback-throw surfacing), `coerceToolList`, and the **present-when-on / absent-when-off** gate (12 tools without hooks → 15 with).
- `hook-config.test.ts` — `resolveHooksMcpEnabled`.
- `config.test.ts` — the `PADDOCK_HOOKS_MCP` flag + YAML file loader.
- `hooks.test.ts` — the `HookService` surface (persist + arm + read + remove) G5 consumes.
- Full server suite green (**671** tests); server typecheck clean.

### Live E2E
Deployed the built server and drove **real-`claude` turns**:
- In a project **opted in** (`hooksMcpEnabled: true` via PATCH → persisted to `project.yaml`): the agent called `list_hooks` → `set_hook` → `list_hooks`; the hook persisted to `project.yaml` and the fleet registered the `hook-<slug>-<name>` agent.
- In a **non-opted** project on the **same instance**: the agent listed the full `paddock_manage` write toolset **minus** the three hook tools and reported them absent.

### Out of scope
Hooks tab UI (G4) and chat-list badge/banner (G3). Zero herdctl changes.

author: wgpatrick
body:
## What

Owner-agreed taste-loop priority: remove the loudness confound from batch ratings (docs/taste-loop-design.md "Confounds" — the learned taste model carried **+0.57 on samplePeakDb**, i.e. "louder wins"). After `renderVaryBatch` renders a batch, every variant is now gain-matched to a common integrated LUFS **by default**, so all future picks (and the score-time feature vectors, which measure the normalized files) rate sound rather than level.

## How

- **Where**: `renderVaryBatch` in `src/vary/batch.ts` — the shared module both `beat vary` (CLI) and `beat_vary` (MCP) import, so both surfaces inherit it identically. `beat render` song renders are untouched.
- **Measurement**: reuses the metrics layer's BS.1770 `integratedLufs` (`src/metrics/loudness.ts`) and the same 4x-oversampled true-peak estimator `beat metrics` reports (`truePeak`, newly exported from `src/metrics/analyze.ts`).
- **Target**: the batch **median** variant's own LUFS (lower-middle for even counts) — relative, small gains, never an absolute genre target. Pure gain only; no limiting.
- **True-peak safety**: upward gain is capped so estimated true peak never crosses **-1 dBTP** (never capped below 0 — an already-hot render isn't attenuated for it), recorded as `capped`.
- **Silence**: immeasurable variants (-Infinity LUFS, missing/undecodable render) are left byte-identical and noted (`measuredLufs: null`).
- **Audition**: `--audition` stitching runs after normalization in every caller, so `audition.wav` is built from the normalized renders.
- **Opt-out**: `--no-normalize` (CLI, all three vary rungs) / `normalize: false` (MCP). Help text and the `beat_vary` tool description updated.

## Manifest fields added (D21 additive)

Batch-level:
```json
"normalization": { "targetLufs": -13.14, "truePeakCeilingDbtp": -1 }
```
Per-variant:
```json
"loudness": { "measuredLufs": -12.59, "gainDb": -0.55, "capped": false }
```

## Verification

- 5 known-answer synthetic-WAV tests (`test/vary-normalize.test.ts`): median-target gain math, -1 dBTP cap, silence handling, float32 path, manifest fields.
- Full suite: **895 pass, 0 fail** (`npm test`, ~16s).
- End-to-end on a real offline-rendered 3-variant batch: v1 pulled -0.55 dB to land at the median exactly; a variant that rendered at +0.4 dBTP was correctly cap-held at 0 gain and flagged; audition stitched from the normalized wavs.
- Roadmap: new done row under "Taste loop" in `scripts/roadmap-data.mjs`; `docs/product-roadmap.md` regenerated.

author: ethan0905
body:
### What I found

`save_token` in `login/src/kimi_code.rs` persists the Kimi credential file
(`kimi-code.json`), which contains the **plaintext access and refresh tokens**,
using the default umask:

```rust
fs::create_dir_all(credentials_dir(codex_home))?;   // dir: default perms
...
fs::write(&temp_path, &contents)?;                  // file: default perms
fs::rename(temp_path, path)?;
```

With a typical `022` umask the file lands at `0o644` (world-readable) and the
`credentials/` directory at `0o755`. This is inconsistent with the OpenAI
`auth.json` store in the same crate, which deliberately writes `0o600`
(`login/src/auth/storage.rs:211-214`). `CODEX_HOME` itself is created with a
plain `create_dir_all` (so `0o755` under a default umask), so the parent
directory does not protect these files either.

### What can happen if it's not fixed

On a shared or multi-user host — or any setup where `$HOME`/`$CODEX_HOME` is
group- or world-traversable (e.g. the `0o755` home default on Debian/Ubuntu) —
another local user can read `$CODEX_HOME/credentials/kimi-code.json` and lift the
long-lived **refresh token**, which is enough to mint new access tokens and take
over the user's Kimi provider account. Unlike the OpenAI path, these tokens are
neither encrypted nor keyring-backed, so file permissions are their only
protection. (On single-user machines or `0o700`-home distros this isn't
exploitable, so realistically it's a shared-host issue — but a real one there.)

### How I fixed it

Restrict the credential file to `0o600` and the directory to `0o700` on Unix,
mirroring the `auth.json` idiom — and make the guarantee actually hold rather
than best-effort:

- **Directory**: create it `0o700`, and explicitly tighten it if it already
  exists (an earlier version may have left it `0o755`; `DirBuilder` won't change
  an existing directory).
- **File**: remove any stale or pre-planted temp file first, then create it with
  `create_new` + mode `0o600`. This means a leftover temp can't keep its old
  loose mode, a planted **symlink can't be followed** (avoiding a
  truncate-through-symlink write), and a race between the remove and create
  **fails closed** instead of writing through whatever appeared. The mode is also
  set explicitly after open so it's exact regardless of umask.

Non-Unix behavior is unchanged.

### Scope

Focused on the credential file and its directory, which hold the actual secret. I
left the `device_id` file untouched: it's a randomly generated device identifier
sent as a request header, not a credential. Happy to harden it too if maintainers
prefer.

### Tests I ran

Two Unix tests: one asserts a clean `save_token` produces a `0o600` file and
`0o700` directory; the other pre-creates a **world-readable directory and a stale
world-readable temp file** and asserts the result is still `0o600`/`0o700`, i.e.
existing loose permissions are repaired rather than preserved.

```
cargo test  -p codex-login --lib kimi_code                 # 4 passed, 0 failed
cargo clippy -p codex-login --all-targets --no-deps        # clean
cargo fmt   -p codex-login -- --check                      # no diffs
```

(Note: a full `cargo clippy -p codex-login` also lints a pre-existing warning in
the unrelated `codex-core-plugins` dependency, which this change does not touch.)

author: lmmoreira
body:
## Summary
- S18 sets the backend to `--no-allow-unauthenticated` (Cloud Run IAM), but the BFF only authenticated at the app layer (`X-Internal-Key`). Without a Google-signed ID token, every BFF→backend call would be rejected by Cloud Run before `InternalApiGuard` ever runs.
- New `IIdentityTokenProvider` port + a `google-auth-library` adapter (`getIdTokenClient`, one client cached per audience so the library's own token refresh/caching is reused, evicted on rejection so a transient failure doesn't permanently poison that audience)
- Wired in via a **single axios request interceptor**, registered once against the shared `HttpService` — verified against the actual `@nestjs/axios` source that a plain `imports: [HttpModule]` (no `.register()`) always resolves to the same underlying axios instance, so this one registration covers all three patterns that currently reach the backend: `BackendHttpService`'s `headers()`-based methods, its `*ForPublic` methods (previously built headers inline, bypassing `headers()`), and `HealthController`'s separately-injected `HttpService` for the readiness ping
- The interceptor guards against `BACKEND_INTERNAL_URL` (the actual connection target every caller builds its URL from) before attaching the token — a future third-party integration on the same shared axios instance won't silently leak this token to an external host
- `BACKEND_AUTH_MODE=none|iam` (default `none`); a startup guard requires `iam` whenever `NODE_ENV=production` (both staging and prod cloud builds set this — unlike the staging/prod-specific `ENABLE_DEV_AUTH` pattern, this guard has no staging/prod distinction)
- `X-Internal-Key` and actor headers are untouched — this adds the IAM leg on top, not instead of

author: chris-obtuseai
body:
## What

The first live pass on the Wave-26 runtime hit `OperationalError("database is locked")`. The autonomy ledger is a single-writer, non-WAL SQLite file the brain writes every cycle; a read-only settlement/held-out read that lands mid-write is refused.

## Why it's a soft skip, not a failure

Completion is **deferrable by design** — pending episodes persist and the next pass retries, inside a 48h expiry window. So a busy ledger is an expected transient. The read now:

- lives in `_read_ledger_state`, which sets an explicit `busy_timeout` and classifies a lock/busy `OperationalError` as a soft `"busy"` note;
- is recorded by `run_shadow_pass` as `summary["ledger_busy"]` (surfaced to the dashboard/planner) instead of a hard error;
- **still ISSUES** from the board artifact, which touches no database — issuing never depends on the ledger.

## Tests

- `test_locked_ledger_reads_as_busy` — a real concurrent `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` writer makes the ro read raise; the helper classifies it `"busy"` (low busy_timeout so it's fast).
- `test_busy_ledger_defers_completion_but_still_issues` — a busy ledger defers completion yet still issues 1, with `errors == []` and `ledger_busy is True`.

Full suite CLEAN (5834 passed; 13 known canonical-path only), ruff clean.

author: m-jerez
body:
Promotes `main` (v0.10.0) into `prod` to cut the **0.10.0** release. Version bump and
curated changelog already landed on `main` (#245).

Merging this runs the full release gate again (`publish.yml`), then **stages** every
`@ts-runtypes/*` package to npm, **tags `v0.10.0` on the prod commit**, and creates the
GitHub Release. Packages go live only after the maintainer 2FA approval
(`pnpm rtx release stage-approve`, leaves-first), then the website deploy is dispatched
manually.

## Release 0.10.0

This release rebuilds unknown-key handling around a non-mutating clone and makes the
circular-reference guard pay-for-use. **Minor bump — this batch is breaking:**

- **unknown-keys (breaking):** `createCloneExactShape` replaces the mutating strip
  family (`createStripUnknownKeys`, `createUnknownKeysToUndefined`, their override
  twins and Fn types are removed) — non-mutating declared-shape clone, unknown keys
  dropped by construction, class prototypes and runtime types preserved.
- **unknown-keys (breaking):** `createHasUnknownKeys` gains the compile-time
  `{runsAfterValidation: true}` count fast path (~3x at 7 props, ~44x at 30 flat
  props); its plain fn-hash prefix moved (`trR` → `lRN`).
- **core (breaking):** `rejectCircularRefs` becomes a compile-time option on the four
  guarded families; the global `setRejectCircularRefs` / `isRejectCircularRefsEnabled`
  toggles are removed. Armed factories inline a baked path-skeleton guard; a plain
  cyclable type ships neither the walker nor its RunType bundle.
- **core:** Built-in `rt::` / `rtFormats::` pure fns delivered on demand (disk cache
  v15); the pure-fn cache honors `emitMode` (`code` | `functions` | `both`).
- **pure-fn:** Symmetric factory/direct registration + a wrappable anonymous
  registration lane for wrapper frameworks.
- **config+lint:** One `genDir` convention, per-family lint rules, zero-config linting.

Full notes: [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/MionKit/ts-run-types/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

Note for the rebase-merge: the PR range also spans the 8 commits already released in
v0.9.3 (prod carries them as rebase-merged copies with different SHAs). They are

author: akromicc
body:
## Qué

Cierra en el kernel la **familia de nullability** — los hermanos latentes del bug del `uuid` nullable ya arreglado. Igual que un `*uuid.UUID`, una columna escalar OPCIONAL cuyo tipo Go es un valor no-puntero escribe su zero value verbatim en vez de NULL, indistinguible de "no seteado":

- `timestamp`/`timestamptz`/`datetime`/`date` → `time.Time` zero = `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`
- `numeric`/`decimal`/`float`/`double` (incl. `numeric(p,s)` parametrizado) → `float64` zero = `0`
- `boolean`/`bool` → `bool` zero = `false`

## Regla de contrato (respetada exacto)

- OPCIONAL (`!Required`) **sin** Default declarado → tipo **PUNTERO** (`*T`) → unset persiste NULL.
- OPCIONAL **con** Default declarado (`manifest.DefaultLiteral` no vacío) → se mantiene el tipo **VALOR**; el DEFAULT de la columna cubre el unset, preservando la semántica del addon.
- `Required` → siempre valor (NOT NULL), como hoy.

## Cambios

- `dynamic/model.go` — `columnToField`: tras el bloque uuid ya existente, pointer-iza `time.Time`/`float64`/`bool` bajo la regla. Reusa `manifest.DefaultLiteral(c.Default)`.
- `dynamic/coerce.go` — `coerceInputToStruct`: el switch ahora corre sobre `baseFt.Kind()` (deref) para que las formas puntero de bool/numeric parseen su valor y dropeen vacíos/inválidos → puntero nil → NULL. `*time.Time` cae al branch `default` (dropea vacío, preserva RFC3339). Vars `timeType`/`float64Type`/`boolType`.
- Tests nuevos `dynamic/model_nullable_scalar_test.go`: por tipo (opcional-sin-default→puntero, opcional-con-default→valor, requerido→valor), no-punteros intactos, y coerce de `*float64`/`*time.Time`/`*bool` (vacío→drop, poblado→parse, inválido→drop).

## Fuera de alcance (a propósito)

`string`/`text`/`json`/`jsonb`/`int`/`bigint`/`vector` NO se tocan: el string vacío es un valor legítimo, jsonb tiene su propio manejo, y los enteros no tienen la ambigüedad NULL-vs-zero aquí. `uuid` ya estaba.

## Verificación

`GOWORK=off go build ./...`, `go vet ./dynamic/`, `go test ./dynamic/` y la **suite completa `go test ./...`** todo verde — ningún reflector de otro paquete (options/facets/search/compute) rompió, no hizo falta ningún deref adicional fuera de coerce.

Second implementation slice (first of three for Slice B). Adds the consumption tooling's foundation: `materialize.sh`, its tests, and the deny-path collector skeleton. No behavior change to the repo — pure additions under `tools/consume/`.

**`materialize.sh <checkout> <sha> <out-dir>`** (REQ-3, REQ-4a): produces a read-only, fidelity-verified export of a commit — `git archive` then `tar -x` as **two exit-checked steps** (POSIX has no `pipefail`), **per-file blob-hash fidelity** (a truncated/corrupt extract fails loud; `MISSING`/`PARTIAL` only compare dir names), a frozen **machine-derived `.skillset`**, `chmod -R a-w`, and an **atomic publish** via `mv`. Fails loud, leaves no partial dir, refuses to overwrite.

- `t_readonly_export` (AC-2) — no `.git`, writes denied, content stable, `.skillset` present.

body:
Cierra #204. Continuación acotada de #54 y #150.

## Qué hace
El GM pulsa **Add asteroid** / **Add nebula** en el editor de contenido (tipo Mapa); eso arma una colocación **de un solo uso** y activa la edición en radar. El **siguiente clic izquierdo** en el radar GM añade un objeto nuevo del tipo elegido en esa coordenada, sobre el `MapDocument` **staged** — sin crear ni modificar entidades ECS.

- **ID determinista y único por tipo**: `asteroid-N` / `nebula-N`, primer sufijo libre desde 1 (salta huecos), sin texto libre.
- **Valores por defecto cerrados**: rotación 0 y tamaño válido por defecto para asteroides; las nebulosas no serializan propiedades.
- **Atómico**: cada colocación es exactamente una entrada de undo (vía `MapEditSession::addObject`) y limpia el redo; una edición posterior invalida el redo.
- **Cancelación antes de mutar**: Escape o clic derecho cancelan la colocación armada; el gesto se **consume antes** de la selección/arrastre ECS del GM.
- Preview y dirty state reflejan el objeto nuevo de inmediato (reusa el preview de #54/#96).

## Diseño
- Núcleo **puro y testeable** en `src/content/mapDocument.{h,cpp}`: `nextMapObjectId(document, kind)` y `makeMapObject(kind, x, y)`.
- Cableado de UI en `contentEditor` (`armMapPlacement`/`placeMapObjectAt`/`cancelMapPlacement`, dos botones, estado) y el gesto en `gameMasterScreen::onMouseDown`.
- Reutiliza toda la maquinaria existente de sesión/undo/redo/preview; no cambia el contrato del documento ni la validación.

## Archivos
- `src/content/mapDocument.{h,cpp}` — helpers puros.
- `src/screens/gm/contentEditor.{h,cpp}`, `src/screens/gm/gameMasterScreen.cpp` — UI y gesto.
- `tests/mapDocumentTests.cpp`, `tests/mapEditSessionTests.cpp` — ID/valores/atomicidad.
- `resources/locale/main.{es,en}.po`, `docs/CONTENT_EDITOR.md` — i18n y doc.

## Verificación
- `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DBUILD_CONTENT_RESOURCE_TESTS=ON` + `ninja EmptyEpsilon`: **binario completo compila y enlaza** (incluye contentEditor y gameMasterScreen).
- `ctest -R 'map_|content_'`: **8/8 verde** (nuevos casos de ID/valores/atomicidad incluidos).

## Pendiente (verificación humana)
Smoke GUI 800×600 (acceptance 7): activar cada herramienta, colocar, observar preview y deshacer. La interacción con `<canvas>`/radar no es testeable sin GUI.

## Alcance / límites
Sin mutación ECS ni Apply automático; sin borrado, multiselección ni panel avanzado (siguientes cortes de #54); sin IDs/Lua/coordenadas de clientes externos.

author: dbrucknr
body:
## Summary

Two independent RFC-mandated duplicate-capability policies, both previously handled by a `find_map()`/`.find()` that implicitly took whichever instance came first — the same bug shape found earlier in this audit (see `RFC_AUDIT.md`).

- **RFC 4724 §3 (Graceful Restart)**: "the receiver of the advertisement MUST ignore all but the **last** instance of the Graceful Restart Capability." The previous code searched for the first *non-zero* `restart_time`, which happened to agree with "last instance" in every case the old tests covered, but diverges once a later, zero-`restart_time` instance follows a non-zero one. Fixed via a new `extract_gr_capability()` (`pathvectord/src/daemon/peer.rs`) that finds the true last `GracefulRestart` instance first, then interprets its `restart_time`/flags/families together, all from that one instance.
- **RFC 9234 §4.2 (BGP Role)**: identical duplicate Role capabilities must collapse into one; *differing* values must reject the connection with a Role Mismatch notification (code 2, subcode 11). The previous code took the first Role capability and silently ignored any conflicting ones. Fixed in `validate_open()` (`pathvector-session/src/fsm/mod.rs`).
- Checked whether the same gap applies to RFC 6793's `FourByteAsn` capability. It doesn't: RFC 5492 explicitly defers duplicate-value semantics to the capability-introducing RFC, and RFC 6793's text says nothing about repeated instances, so `resolve_as()`'s first-match extraction is correct as-is.

## Verification

- Unit-level real-teeth verification for both fixes: reverted each fix, confirmed the corresponding test failed for the specific reason under test (not a generic panic), restored the fix, confirmed green.
- Wire-level e2e proof (`pathvector-e2e`) against a real TCP peer and Docker-hosted `pathvectord`, also real-teeth verified: `gr_duplicate_capabilities_last_instance_wins` and `role_differing_duplicates_are_rejected`.
- `pathvector-session`, `pathvectord`, `pathvector-e2e`: full test suites, clippy (`-D warnings`), fmt, and rustdoc all clean.

## Where I'd like a second look

While proving the Role e2e scenario, my first version of the mock peer had a **false-pass bug**: it only read one message after sending its OPEN and never replied to a `Keepalive`, so the handshake stalled regardless of whether the real fix was present. When I deliberately reverted the production fix to confirm the test would fail (the real-teeth step), it *still passed* — for the wrong reason. I caught this only by inspecting the mock's live container logs mid-test and seeing it had received an unanswered `Keepalive`. Fixed by making the mock echo `Keepalive` back when no `Notification` arrives, so a broken fix now genuinely completes the handshake and the test fails as it should.

I'm confident in the fix logic itself (verified the GR tuple's `restart_time`/flags/families all come from the *same* last-matched instance, not mixed across instances; verified the `RoleMismatch` subcode-11 wire encoding is pre-existing, fuzzed, correct). Where I'd appreciate Codex's eyes: whether there's a comparable false-pass risk anywhere else in `pathvector-e2e`'s existing scenarios that hasn't been caught yet — this was the first time in the audit series a test passed despite testing nothing, and I only found it by accident (checking logs out of suspicion, not because anything looked wrong on the surface).

author: jeremydmiller
body:
## What this does

Pulsar has true broker-native, arbitrary-timestamp delayed delivery (`DeliverAt` / `DeliverAfter`), but Wolverine's Pulsar sender never stamped it: the sender *claimed* `SupportsNativeScheduledSend => true`, yet scheduled/delayed sends were published immediately and only worked because the scheduled time round-trips as an envelope header and the **receiving** Wolverine node held the message locally (in memory for buffered listeners — lost on restart, and useless for non-Wolverine consumers).

This PR makes Pulsar a first-class native scheduling transport:

- **`PulsarSender.SendAsync` now maps `Envelope.ScheduledTime` onto DotPulsar's `DeliverAtTime` message metadata**, so the broker itself parks the message until it is due. The stamp is applied *after* the envelope mapper runs, so it uniformly covers the default mapper, CloudEvents, and custom interop mappers — and a custom mapper that stamps its own deliver-at metadata is respected (never overwritten).
- **Capability gating** (the same shape as the NATS transport's server-version gate): Pulsar brokers have shipped delayed delivery enabled by default since 2.4, so it is on by default, but `UsePulsar(...).DisableNativeScheduledSend()` opts out for brokers running `delayedDeliveryEnabled=false`. The sender then reports `SupportsNativeScheduledSend => false` and Wolverine falls back to its durable scheduled-message scheduler. Broker-per-tenant child transports inherit the flag (`PulsarTenant.Compile`).

## Subscription-type caveat

Pulsar only dispatches delayed messages on **Shared / KeyShared** subscriptions — `Exclusive` / `Failover` consumers (Wolverine's Pulsar listener default) receive them immediately. That is handled gracefully and documented:

- Wolverine-to-Wolverine stays correct under any subscription type: the scheduled time still round-trips as a header, so a listener that receives a not-yet-due envelope holds it locally until it is due (durable inbox for durable listeners, in-memory for buffered) — the pre-existing fallback, unchanged.
- To have the message parked **on the broker** (or consumed by non-Wolverine apps), the listening subscription must be `Shared`/`KeyShared`. The new *Scheduled Delivery* section in `docs/guide/messaging/transports/pulsar.md` spells this out, mirroring the identical constraint already documented for the retry-letter topics.

## Retry-letter interaction

None: `MoveToPulsarRetryTopic` / retry-letter redelivery builds its own `MessageMetadata` (including its own tiered `DeliverAtTimeAsDateTimeOffset`) on a separate producer inside `PulsarListener` and never flows through `PulsarSender`, so delays are not double-applied. Verified by reading the path and by the retry/redelivery test suites.

## Test coverage

New `native_scheduled_delivery.cs` in `Wolverine.Pulsar.Tests` — **9 tests, all passing**:

- Unit: deliver-at stamped from `ScheduledTime` (incl. UTC conversion), metadata untouched without a scheduled time, custom-mapper deliver-at respected, config flag default/`DisableNativeScheduledSend()`/tenant inheritance.
- Integration (Testcontainers Pulsar): a **raw DotPulsar `Shared` consumer** proves the *broker* holds a scheduled message — nothing receivable in the early window, delivered only after deliver-at (this consumer knows nothing about Wolverine headers, so the receiver-side fallback cannot mask a missing stamp).
- Integration end-to-end over two Wolverine hosts on a `Shared` subscription: a message scheduled 5s out is handled no earlier than its deliver-at time; a plain send on the same endpoint is delivered promptly.

Also: `dotnet build wolverine.slnx -c Release` succeeds with 0 warnings/0 errors, and the compliance `schedule_send` tests pass.

**Local environmental note:** on the (heavily loaded, multi-suite) dev box, the three pre-existing `can_schedule_retry` compliance variants failed with tracked-session timeouts — they fail **identically on an unmodified main checkout** on the same machine (baselined via `git stash` + rebuild), so they are environmental, not caused by this diff. CI is the real signal for those.

Closes #3470

author: menno420
body:
## What

Builds the D4 observability design's P1 item: **arm the four outbox metric families that are declared in code but never registered** on the live registry, and add the missing emitter for the one gauge that has no emitter anywhere in the tree.

## Before

- The composition root builds the registry with the default `METRICS` tuple only (`build_registry()` at `sb/app/main.py`), so `OUTBOX_METRICS` — `outbox_pending_age_seconds`, `outbox_delivered_total`, `outbox_dead_letter_total`, `outbox_claims_total` — is **never instantiated**. The relay's guarded counter bumps (`_inc`) call `registry.counter(name)`, which raises `KeyError` for an unregistered family; the guard's bare `except` discards it. The outbox is the durability spine, yet its health was invisible on `/metrics`.
- `outbox_pending_age_seconds` (the backpressure gauge) had **no emitter at all** anywhere in the tree — only the spec declaration and a docstring referenced it.

## After

- The composition root builds `build_registry(METRICS + OUTBOX_METRICS)` — the same union the cardinality gate already validates — so all four outbox families are live handles on the registry and land on `/metrics`.
- A guarded gauge `_set` twin (mirroring the existing `_inc`) plus a bounded `pending_age_seconds` read on the store emit `outbox_pending_age_seconds` on each relay tick. Observability never blocks delivery: both the store read and the emit are inside the guard.
- Unit tests prove the four families now emit at the outbox seam (counters increment into a real registry and appear in `render()`; the gauge value renders), plus a render smoke asserting a non-empty `/metrics` body carrying an outbox family.

## Scope

Pure wiring of already-declared families. **No new metric semantics, no backend/auth/threshold decisions** — those remain owner questions in the D4 doc's Open Questions and land with the later slices (scrape path, `/readyz` outbox-depth gate, structured logs). The gauge's semantics are already fixed by its declared spec docstring.

Layer rules respected: kernel work stays in `sb/kernel/outbox/*` (imports spec/namespace only); the registry union is at the composition root (`sb/app`).

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway domain for session dashboards (design: `docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md`): sessions get a persistent "board" face that agents compose. This PR delivers the whole server side — protocol schemas and validators, `board.get/update/widget.put/widget.grant/event` RPCs, `board.changed`/`board.command` events, HMAC-ticketed widget serving, the `dashboard` agent tool, tier-1 state-event session notices, and SQLite persistence in the per-agent DB. UI wiring (already landed as #110644/#110728/#110740) connects in the follow-up stitch PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Boards are session state owned by the agent, so storage is the per-agent DB: STRICT `board_tabs`/`board_widgets` with FK cascade and layout/grant checks. Per the new additive-surface rule in AGENTS.md, the schema version stays at 13: tables are declared canonically for fresh DBs and lazily ensured once per DB handle on existing DBs (idempotent DDL, folds into the next natural bump). Downgraded builds keep working — boards are simply absent. Widget iframes authenticate via 2-minute HMAC view tickets bound to session+name+revision+persisted view-generation (no operator token ever reaches sandboxed content); reconstruction-safe (delete/recreate with identical bytes invalidates old tickets). Session reset preserves boards; session deletion removes them. Tool-call parity: the `dashboard` tool covers everything the UI can do, including `focus_tab`/`set_chat_dock` via `board.command`.

## User Impact

No visible surface yet (agent tool + RPCs; UI stitch follows). No config surface added. No schema version bump.

## Evidence

- Store parity suite (in-memory vs SQLite): 10/10; persistence/ticket suite 84 passed; session-deletion lifecycle, agent-DB bootstrap/migration, v13-with-tables open and v13-without-tables lazy-create paths all covered.
- `generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify` clean; `check-changed` green remotely (16m43s full gate); autoreview clean across rounds (review found the original operator-auth serving design unusable from sandboxed iframes — replaced with the ticket scheme).
- Contract: matches the frozen board contract + amendments (`frameUrl`, `declaredSummary`).

author: hy4ri
body:
## Plugin

- **Id:** `Hy4ri/ds4-color`
- [x] New plugin
- [ ] Update to an existing plugin (version bumped in `plugin.toml`)

## What it does

Sets the DualShock 4 lightbar color from a Noctalia bar button and a color panel. Left-click the bar button applies the last saved color directly; right-click opens a panel with a native color picker, a hex field, and 9 presets. **Save** persists the chosen color (so left-click reapplies it later) without touching the controller; **Apply** sets the lightbar immediately and also saves it.

The entire DualShock 4 HID output-report protocol is implemented in **pure Lua** — no external binary or library. The plugin detects controllers by scanning `/sys/class/hidraw/*/device/uevent` for Sony VID `054c` / PIDs `05c4` `09cc` `0ba0`, builds the USB report (`0x05`, 32 B) and Bluetooth report (`0x11`, 78 B with CRC32), and writes them to `/dev/hidrawN`.

## External dependencies

None. `dependencies = []` in `plugin.toml`. The final byte write uses Noctalia's `writeFile`, with a `python3` `O_WRONLY` fallback for the char device (only `python3` is used, no downloaded/remote code).

## Testing

- [ ] Tested on Niri
- [x] Tested on Hyprland
- [ ] Tested on Sway
- [ ] Tested on another compositor:
- **Noctalia version tested against:** current main (plugin_api 3)
- **Plugin API level:** 3

Manually exercised: bar widget left-click applies saved color; right-click opens panel; preset click + Apply sets the lightbar on a connected DS4 (USB and Bluetooth); Save persists without writing; IPC `noctalia msg plugin Hy4ri/ds4-color:service all apply <hex>` confirmed.

## Screenshots / Videos

`thumbnail.webp` is included (panel screenshot).

## Checklist

- [x] The directory name matches the part of `id` after the `/` in `plugin.toml` exactly (`ds4-color/`).
- [x] It ships `plugin.toml`, `README.md`, `thumbnail.webp`, and `translations/en.json`.
- [x] `README.md` follows the README template, documents every entry id and dependency, and includes exact panel IPC commands.
- [x] I created `thumbnail.webp` with the thumbnail generator (used a screenshot conversion instead — see note above).
- [x] `version` follows semver (`0.1.0`) and is bumped in this PR; `plugin_api` is the oldest API level this plugin requires (3).
- [x] Every non-English translation in this PR uses a locale supported by Noctalia core (only `en.json` shipped; no machine translations).
- [x] I did not edit `catalog.toml`; CI generates it.
- [x] This PR touches exactly one plugin directory (`ds4-color/`).

## Code review attestation

Plugins run as trusted, unsandboxed Luau in the user's session. Confirm:

- [x] The code is readable and not obfuscated, minified, or generated.
- [x] It does not download and execute remote code.
- [x] Every network call, filesystem write, and spawned process is something the description above accounts for (only `python3` spawned for the raw hidraw write; no network calls).
- [x] I have the right to publish this code under the `license` declared in `plugin.toml` (MIT).

body:
## What

The sheet for a book you already own only offered **+ another copy** of that exact edition — there was no way to say "I also have the hardback." Now both sheets (the catalog/scan sheet and the manage sheet opened from the library list) carry an **"own a different edition too? pick its format"** control: choose a format and file it to **+ library**, **+ digital**, or **+ wishlist**.

![different edition controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ReadableCode/Book-Bot/claude/shelf-view-first-person-5d4qtq/docs/screenshots/different-edition.png)

## How

`POST /api/books` gains a `new_edition` flag. When set, the server files the add as a **sibling edition of the same work**:
- reuses an existing same-format sibling if the work already has one (double-taps don't duplicate)
- otherwise mints a fresh edition **without** the source edition's ISBN, Google volume id, or OpenLibrary key — those identify the *other* format, and inheriting them would corrupt exact-ownership matching
- requires a format (400 without one); the client guards with a toast too

After adding, scanning the original barcode shows both: "✓ this exact edition is in … (paperback)" plus "other editions you have: hardcover — in library".

## Verification

- API: paperback (with ISBN) + hardcover via `new_edition` → two distinct editions, hardcover with no borrowed ISBN; repeat add is idempotent; lookup of the paperback ISBN reports exact + related; missing format → 400
- Browser: controls render on both sheets; picking audiobook → digital adds and toasts "audiobook edition added — owned digitally ✓"; clicking add without a format toasts the guard
- `uv run pytest`: 36 passed

Second code-review follow-up (the item I flagged in #89 but didn't auto-fix).

## The bug
The intervention Add/Edit forms submitted the `datetime-local` input's raw, **zone-less** `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` string. The repository parsed it with `new Date(...)`, which JS interprets in the **runtime's** (server's) timezone. On a UTC server, a French user's 09:30 was stored as 09:30 UTC (= 11:30 Paris) and displayed back shifted by the UTC offset.

## The fix
- Convert the value to a full ISO-8601 instant **on the client** — where the user's timezone is actually known — via a hidden `scheduledAt` field; the visible input is now controlled. The server's `new Date(...)` is then unambiguous regardless of server timezone.
- Extracted `toDatetimeLocal` (was inline in the edit form) plus the new `datetimeLocalToIso` into `lib/datetimeLocal.ts`.
- Hardened `schemas/intervention.ts` to reject a non-parseable date rather than relying on the DB to error on `Invalid Date`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 237/237 passing
- [x] Verified in-browser (browser at UTC+2): entering 09:30 now submits the hidden field `2026-08-01T07:30:00.000Z` and the created intervention round-trips back to 9:30 AM. Create + delete flow clean, no console errors.

author: 10ne1
body:
glibc 2.43 implements strchr(3), strrchr(3) and strstr(3) as C23-style _Generic macros which propagate the const qualifier of the input string to the return type.

For example, a 'const char *' input now produces 'const char *' output types and vice-versa (non-const -> non-const).

Building with clang and -Werror=incompatible-pointer-types fails:

  src/lxc/confile.c:2690:4: error: assigning to 'char *' from
      'const char *' discards qualifiers
      [-Werror,-Wincompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers]

Constify the result pointers where they are only read and cast the result back to char* where the code intentionally writes through it into caller-owned writable storage.

This is just a build fix, the runtime behavior is unchanged.

Fixes: #4710

author: danielbdyer
body:
## Problem

`check environments` / `check estate` (and its sibling `check shape`) read each cloud environment's **whole** OSSYS estate via bare `Source.read (Source.ofOssys …)`, ignoring the configured `model.modules` scope. Every other model-bearing verb routes its read through the shared scoped seam (`Compose.applyModuleFilter` → `ModuleFilterBinding.fromConfig` → `ModuleFilter.apply`); these two bypassed it.

The concrete consequence is the **clone collision**: reading the whole estate pulls in clone / deleted / test / system eSpaces, and a cloned module carries the *same* entity SS_Keys as its original. `Catalog.create` refuses duplicate Kind SS_Keys (`catalog.kinds.duplicateKey`), so the estate read **fails loud** (exit 6) on any estate containing clones.

## Why matching is unchanged

SS_Key **is** stable across environments (module SS_Key equal everywhere; entity SS_Key stable per LifeTime lineage; only *clones* share keys). So the fix is **scope-only** — the existing SS_Key-based matching (`CatalogDiff.between`) is correct once clones are scoped out. Re-keying by logical name would be the weaker/unsafe path the codebase explicitly warns against in `NameAlignment.fs` (by-name is A1-bounded, "never auto-detected" — it can silently align a mis-wired pair).

## Changes

- **New `ScopedRead.fs`** — the one sanctioned scoped OSSYS read: `SnapshotScopeBinding.fromModel` query-time pushdown + `ModuleFilter.apply` semantic backstop (the same composition full-export and `PeerTransfer.acquireContractsWith` already use, named once).
- Thread the `model.modules` scope (`Config.ModelSection`) into `CheckEstateArgs` and `PlanAction.CheckShape`; validate at plan construction so a bad module name refuses by name (exit 2) before any read.
- Route **every** estate/shape read through the seam: the agreed-env target, the `--against model` authored target (`ModelResolution.resolveCatalog` did not filter itself, so it was unscoped too), and each confirm env. The scoped `Source` also carries the data-plane profile, so profiling stays in scope.
- **Governance:** `EstateScopeGovernanceTests` source-scans `src/Projection.Cli/Faces/*.fs` for `Source.ofOssys` (not `…With`) so no future face can silently re-introduce a whole-estate read, plus pure scope canaries (narrows to `model.modules`; empty selection is the byte-identical identity; an unknown module refuses).

`check shape` gets the same scope fix. `diff` / `compare` are general two-ref tools (not the configured-model surface) and are intentionally left as-is.

## Verification

- Build 0/0 (Cli + Tests).
- **944 + 166 focused pure tests pass, 0 failed** — planning/CLI/config, estate, readiness, and the (unchanged) peer-transfer / name-alignment suites.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`check shape` is largely superseded by `check environments`. Worth a separate decision on whether to keep maintaining it or steer users to the newer instrument.

author: darthjee
body:
## Summary
Reorganize `frontend/assets/js/components/common/` (and its mirrored spec tree) from a flat, file-type-split layout into themed subfolders, each carrying its own component(s) together with their controller/helper.

## Problem
Related files for a single component were scattered across three different locations: the component itself lived directly in `common/`, its controller (if any) lived in `common/controllers/`, and its helper (if any) lived in `common/helpers/`. This made it harder to see, at a glance, which files belonged together, and increased the effort needed to navigate or refactor a single component.

## Solution
Grouped the ~50 components (plus their controllers, helpers, and the existing `listTypes/` folder) into themed subfolders: `base/`, `buttons/`, `modals/`, `cards/`, `badges/`, `forms/`, `header/`, `pagination/`, `list_page/`, `list_types/`, and `misc/` — each with its own `controllers/`/`helpers/` sub-subfolders only where it actually has files for those. Every relative import path across `frontend/assets/js/` and `frontend/specs/assets/js/` was updated to match the new locations, and spec files were moved into the mirrored themed structure. Root-level docs (`docs/agents/frontend.md`, `docs/agents/pagination.md`, `docs/agents/i18n.md`) were updated to reflect the new paths.

## Details
- All moves used `git mv` to preserve history.
- One deviation from the plan: `PhotoCard.jsx` / `PhotoCardHelper.jsx` (not explicitly listed in the plan's `cards/` table, likely a naming mix-up with `CardPhoto.jsx`) were placed in `cards/` since they're clearly a card component.

author: aguilanegra
body:
## Summary

Closes the last code group of Tier 3 — **Group R** (event registration/enrollment). Members can now be enrolled into events from the event detail page, with an optional saved-card charge and a managed registrants list.

**Group S (#280 profile photo, #281 2FA backup codes)** was investigated and confirmed to be **Clerk Dashboard instance-config only — no code change**. Those issues should be closed as Clerk config (enable avatar upload under User profile settings; enable the Backup Codes MFA strategy), not via this PR.

## What was missing

The `event_registration` table, `event_billing` tiers, the saved-card charge path (`payment.process` with `paymentMethodSource: 'saved'`), and the audit constants all already existed — but there was **no write/read/cancel path** and no enrollment UI. The event detail page's `currentRegistrations` was hardcoded to `0`.

## Changes

### Backend
- **`EventsService.ts`** — new `registerMemberForEvent`, `getEventRegistrations`, `cancelEventRegistration` (+ `MemberAlreadyRegisteredError` / `EventNotFoundError` / `MemberNotFoundError`). Registration rows carry no `organizationId`, so all three are org-scoped via the parent event. Register dedupes on non-cancelled event+member, resolves the tier price, inserts the row, and back-links an optional charge `transactionId`. Cancel is a soft-cancel (`status='cancelled'`, `cancelledAt` set).
- **`Events.ts`** router — `register` / `registrations` / `cancelRegistration`, all `FRONT_DESK`, audited (`EVENT_REGISTRATION_CREATE` / `EVENT_REGISTRATION_CANCEL`), with `MemberAlreadyRegisteredError` → 409 and event/member-not-found → 404. Wired into `routers/index.ts` under `events.*`.
- **`EventsValidation.ts`** — `RegisterForEventValidation`, `EventRegistrationsValidation`, `CancelEventRegistrationValidation`.

### UI
- **`EnrollMemberModal.tsx`** — searchable member picker (`client.members.list`), optional billing-tier select, and a "charge saved card" toggle (enabled only when the member has a saved card and the tier price > 0). On submit: if charging, calls `payment.process` (`paymentMethodSource: 'saved'`, `billingType: 'one-time'`, `isTaxable: true`), then registers with the returned `transactionId`; a decline surfaces in the modal and does **not** create the registration.
- **Event detail page** — "Enroll Member" button, a **Registrants card** (member, tier, amount, per-row cancel), and the real `currentRegistrations` count wired in (was hardcoded to `0`).
- i18n keys added to `en.json` + `fr.json`.

## Tests
44 new tests, all passing:
- `EventsService.test.ts` — 12 (register incl. tier price resolution, dedupe, transaction back-link, org scoping, not-found paths; registrants join; soft-cancel)
- `Events.test.ts` — 6 (guard role, input forwarding, audit, 409/404 mapping)
- `EventsValidation.test.ts` — 21 (schema accept/reject cases)
- `EnrollMemberModal.test.tsx` — 5 (list/search, enroll without charge, charge-then-enroll, decline handling)

Residual risk is limited to prose accuracy if upstream zfb behavior changes before this warning is removed. No visual impact is expected because this is description text only. ## Draft upstream zfb issue body (do not file automatically) Suggested title: `Dev server drops island-root data-* attributes retained by production build` ### Summary The zfb dev server drops author-declared `data-*` attributes from the root element of a client island during SSR, while `zfb build` preserves the same attributes. This dev/build discrepancy makes selectors anchored to island-root `data-*` attributes silently fail only during development. This was observed in `zudo-doc` with the mobile chrome-font tokens `--zdc-sidebar-font` and `--zdc-toc-font`. Their mobile rules target `aside[data-zd-mobile-sidebar]` and `div[data-zd-mobile-toc]`; granular mobile overrides appear broken under `pnpm dev`, but work in built and previewed output. ### Minimal reproduction 1. In a zfb docs project with a client island whose root renders an author-declared `data-*` attribute, clear both the zfb graph cache and Vite cache, then restart the dev server: ```sh rm -f .zfb/graph.bin rm -rf node_modules/.vite pnpm dev ``` 2. On a doc route, render a mobile island root and a granular font rule such as: ```tsx
Mobile navigation
``` ```css :root { --zdc-sidebar-font: "Courier New", monospace; } aside[data-zd-mobile-sidebar] { font-family: var(--zdc-sidebar-font); } ``` The rule is intentionally anchored to the island-root attribute, matching how the mobile surface is distinguished from other chrome. 3. Inspect the dev server's SSR HTML for the route. The island root is present, but `data-zd-mobile-sidebar` is absent, so the selector does not match. 4. Run `zfb build` for the same project and inspect the generated SSR HTML for the same route. The built HTML retains `data-zd-mobile-sidebar`, and the selector matches. The same discrepancy is reproducible with `data-zd-mobile-toc` on a `
` island root. Previewing the production build also shows the expected font. ### Expected behavior Development SSR and production-build SSR should emit the same author-declared island-root `data-*` attributes. Selectors anchored to those attributes should therefore behave consistently in dev, build, and preview. ### Actual behavior The dev server strips the island-root `data-*` attributes, while `zfb build` preserves them. As a result, per-surface mobile chrome-font overrides silently no-op only in dev. Production output is correct. ### Impact This is a developer-experience and dev/prod consistency issue. Authors can incorrectly conclude that granular mobile chrome fonts are unsupported because `--zdc-sidebar-font` and `--zdc-toc-font` do not reach their mobile surfaces under the dev server, even though the same configuration works after build. Until fixed, these mobile overrides must be verified with `zfb build` and preview rather than `pnpm dev`. ### Tracking note The original downstream report, zudolab/zudo-doc#2898, was superseded-closed after the work was incorporated into zudolab/zudo-doc#2961. author: lostpointer
body:
Closes LOS-226 — https://linear.app/lostpointer/issue/LOS-226

## Проблема

При разборе LOS-214 в `test_runs/telemetry_log_auto_forward_2.csv` не было видно **ни одного** `TestStart` при четырёх запусках `start_test` и лишь **один** `TestDone` из четырёх. Это маскировало реальный баг и заметно замедлило разбор.

Причин оказалось **две**, и вторая в задаче не описана — нашлась при планировании.

### 1. Метки времени

События старта и остановки писались с жёстко зашитым `ts_ms = 0`: точка входа — WS-поток, где времени тика нет. Реальную метку получали только события завершения, которые пушатся из `Update()`.

### 2. Сшивка по точному совпадению меток

Экспортёр CSV искал событие через `eventByTs.get(ts)` — точный поиск по `Map`, хотя комментарий рядом обещал «join by closest timestamp». При этом кадр пишется раз в `kLogIntervalMs = 10`, а метка события — это тик control loop (2 мс).

Проверено на реальном логе: шаг между кадрами 10–12 мс, 3225 кадров. Совпадение метки события с меткой кадра — примерно **1 случай из 5**.

Это и объясняет три пропавших `TestDone`: метки у них были **корректные**, события потеряла сшивка. Наблюдаемые 1 из 4 (25%) сходятся с расчётом.

## Изменения

* **`AutoDriveCoordinator`** — кэширует `ts_ms` последнего тика (по образцу `last_rc_active_` из LOS-214) и проставляет во все восемь пушей `Start*`/`StopAll`.
* **`CalibrationManager`** — берёт время напрямую из `platform_.GetTimeMs()`.
* **`app.js`** — вместо точного поиска `assignEventsToFrames()`: события раскладываются по интервалам `(метка предыдущего кадра, метка текущего]`, края прижимаются к первому/последнему кадру, чтобы ничего не пропало. Склейка нескольких событий через `'|'` сохранена.
* **`StopAutoForward()`** — пишет `ImuCalibFailed(stage=2)`. До сих пор обрыв auto-forward не оставлял в логе следа вообще, хотя после LOS-214 это штатный путь (аборт по перехвату пультом). Новый тип события не заводился — `ImuCalibFailed` с `param = stage` уже есть в протоколе и уже назван в `EVENT_TYPE_NAMES`.

  Событие пишется только если сбор реально шёл: `ProcessCompletion()` зовёт `StopAutoForward()` и при **успешном** завершении, где такое событие было бы ложным.

## Проверка

864 юнит-теста + 70 SIL зелёные, clang-format прогнан командой из workflow.

**Новые тесты — все пять проверены откатом правки, краснеют:** метки у `Start*`/`StopAll`, метка у события старта auto-forward, событие обрыва, отсутствие ложного события обрыва после успеха.

**Функция раскладки** проверена ad-hoc скриптом на `node` (JS-тестов в прошивочной веб-части нет, инфраструктуру в рамках задачи не заводил) на синтетике с сеткой кадров 10–12 мс:

```
  ok  все 38 события разложены (получено 38)
  ok  событие сразу после кадра 3 → кадр 4
  ok  точное совпадение → тот же кадр 5
  ok  событие до первого кадра → кадр 0
  ok  событие после последнего → последний кадр
  ok  склейка '|' по возрастанию времени
  ok  пустые входы

старая сшивка по точному совпадению: 0 из 38
```

## Проверить на железе

Скачать лог кнопкой «CSV» и убедиться, что для каждого прогона видна пара `TestStart → TestDone` с ненулевыми возрастающими метками, а прерывание калибровки пультом даёт `ImuCalibFailed`.

body:
## Summary
Replaces the docs pipeline's two unmaintained npm packages — `electron-pdf` (HTML→PDF) and `markdown-styles` (MD→HTML) — which pin ancient transitive deps (`marked ^0.3.5`, `uuid ^2.0.1`, `@sentry/electron 1.5.2`, `highlight.js ^9`, `cookie <0.7.0`, `form-data 2.5.1`, plus Electron itself) that keep tripping GitHub's security scanner with no auto-fix path. See DRV-45 through DRV-51.

**POC on tplink** to validate before rolling into `control4-driver-template`.

New pipeline:
- **MD → HTML:** `tools/render-md.mjs` — markdown-it + markdown-it highlight + github-markdown-css + highlight.js github theme. Clean, maintained deps; `npm audit` = **0 vulnerabilities**.
- **HTML → PDF:** `tools/render-pdf.py` — WeasyPrint, a CSS Paged Media engine (no browser/Chromium). Installed into the existing project `.venv`, so the same `make init` provisions it locally and in CI.

## Why not puppeteer
Evaluated first (closed PR #8). Its post-install Chromium fetch corrupts on macOS (`dlopen` framework errors) and drags a ~300MB browser download — worse dev/CI ergonomics than what it replaces.

## Pagination
Manual `<div style="page-break-after: always">` markers in source landed at odd spots as content shifted. Replaced with automatic, content-aware CSS Paged Media rules (WeasyPrint honors these properly, unlike Chromium):
- neutralize legacy markers
- keep headings attached to following content (`break-after: avoid`)
- never split tables / code blocks / figures across a page (`break-inside: avoid`)
- avoid orphan/widow lines

No per-driver marker maintenance; pagination is automatic.

## Local + CI
- **Local (macOS):** WeasyPrint needs the Pango stack (`brew install pango`, one time). The Makefile auto-sets `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH` on Darwin so `make docs-pdf` just works — no manual env.
- **CI (`build.yml`):** removes the entire Electron/Chromium shared-lib stack (libnss3, libatk*, libcups2, libgbm1, libasound2, …), `xvfb`, `xvfb-run`, and `ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX`; adds WeasyPrint's lighter deps (libpangocairo, libgdk-pixbuf, libffi). Net **fewer** system packages than before.

## Verification
- Full `make build` passes end-to-end (preprocess → gen-squishy → update-xml → docs → fmt → package → zip); both driver PDFs render with correct margins, automatic pagination, tables, code spans, and logo sizing.
- `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities (was several open Dependabot advisories).

## Closes
Part of DRV-45 … DRV-51 (fully closed once rolled out via the template to all driver repos).

## Test plan
- [ ] CI build is green on this PR (validates the reworked workflow + weasyprint in a clean Ubuntu runner)
- [ ] Review rendered PDFs (attached in chat) for layout/pagination
- [ ] After merge: port to `control4-driver-template`, tag, `copier update` across driver repos

author: accuser
body:
Resolves #734.

The checker did quadratic and clone-heavy work on the common path of **every** call. This removes it with targeted guards and borrows — no behavioural change.

## Changes

**`type_of` / `ExprKind::Call` (`checker.rs`)**
- Counted user sum-variant owners (`O(types × variants)`) *before* the cheap `http_variant` keyword check — so every ordinary function call paid for it. The scan now sits behind the `http_variant` guard, and further behind `http_implied` (since the owner count only matters when the surrounding type doesn't already imply `HttpResult`). Uses `.any(...)` instead of `.count()` to short-circuit on the first owner.
- An ordinary call now does zero type/variant scanning: `http_variant` (miss) → `queue_variant` (miss) → `check_call` → `fns` hashmap hit.

**`check_call` (`calls.rs`)**
- Removed the deep `FnDecl` clone (whole body) done for every known-function call — borrow it out of the immutable `input` instead.
- The bare-variant-constructor probe cloned every matching `TypeDecl`; it now collects references (`Vec<&TypeDecl>`), which the ambiguity check below reuses.

**`check_static_call` (`calls.rs`)**
- Was cloning the type's entire `MethodTable` and the matched static `FnDecl` per static-shaped call. Both are now borrowed.

**`check_binop` / `collect_is_bindings` (`expressions.rs`)**
- Re-walked the whole lhs subtree at every `&&`/`implies` node to gather `is`-bindings — `O(N²)` for an N-term chain. The collector is a pure read of the `expr_types` side-table (populated before it runs), so it's now memoised by span (`Ctx::is_binding_cache`), collapsing the chain to a single pass.

## Why it's safe
- The decls outlive the `&mut Ctx` borrow: `Ctx.input` is a `&'a ResolvedCommons`, so references into it are `'a`-bound and independent of the mutable borrow.
- The owner-scan restructure is semantically identical — `http_variant` and `queue_variant` name sets are disjoint (`Ok`/`Created`/… vs `Ack`/`Retry`), so falling straight to `check_call` when the HTTP condition fails matches the old else-if ladder.
- `collect_is_bindings` has no side effects (no diagnostics, no ref recording), so memoising it changes only cost, not output.

## Testing
- `cargo test --workspace` — all 60 suites pass, 0 failures.
- `cargo clippy -p bynk-check -p bynk-emit` — clean.

## Follow-up (out of scope)
A precomputed `name → variant/type/fn` index on `ResolvedCommons` (as the issue suggests) would also make the *remaining* off-hot-path scans (variant-constructor disambiguation) constant-time. Not needed to remove the per-call quadratic cost, so left for a future change.

## Summary

Adds the first playable Succession Foundation, allowing Frontier to continue after a character’s completed life while preserving the civilization and its history.

- Added typed civilization-owned archives for completed character lives.

  - Civilization inventory
  - Personal inventory
  - Kept-item settings
  - Equipped tool
  - Knowledge
  - Discoveries

  - Current location
  - Current time
  - Completed world events

### Motivation
- Reduce the monolithic `ast-graph-extractor` implementation by extracting language-specific traversal/emitters so each grammar can evolve independently. 
- Centralize common traversal, path resolution, and edge-emitter utilities to avoid duplication and make behavior consistent across languages. 
- Keep the public extractor API stable so callers (e.g. `graph-extractor.ts`) continue to work unchanged. 

### Description
- Added a shared utilities module at `src/core/ast-graph/shared.ts` that contains `Ctx`/types, `walk`, path resolution helpers, and edge emitters (`pushImport`, `pushExport`, `pushCall`, etc.).
- Split the large language handlers out of the original file into `src/core/ast-graph/typescript.ts`, `src/core/ast-graph/python.ts`, `src/core/ast-graph/go.ts`, and `src/core/ast-graph/other-languages.ts` (remaining languages), each exporting a `*Spec()` factory.
- Converted `src/core/ast-graph-extractor.ts` into a small dispatcher that imports per-language specs, preserves `extractEdgesFromTree` and `ExtractionResult`, and delegates traversal to `shared.walk`.
- Moved language-focused tests into `src/core/ast-graph/` with a shared test helper `test-utils.ts` to reuse a single `ParserPool` and to keep tests colocated with their implementations.

body:
## Summary

- fix collision tunneling, brick lifecycle, resize state, and scoring consistency
- add scoring v2 with legacy score migration and the `neon-drift-v2` leaderboard mode
- add configurable ball trails, stronger impacts, readable brick HP, and High/Low/Off effects
- make menus, score filters, and level selection fully navigable with arrow keys and Enter
- add level thumbnails, locks, and selectable unlocked starting levels
- add Perfect Drift, visible combo, Overdrive, and rebalanced multiball/laser/shield power-ups
- give levels 2–9 distinct brick mechanics
- rebuild level 10 as the three-phase Neon God final boss with boss HUD, victory screen, and Endless Mode
- add focused rule, migration, level, physics, power-up, effects, and scoring tests

## Why

Breakout had several correctness and progression issues: fast balls could tunnel through bricks, destroyed bricks could remain collidable during their fade, resize handling disturbed active state, and multiball multiplied scoring and power-up generation too aggressively. The menu also depended on numeric shortcuts and the later levels did not have enough mechanical identity or a real conclusion.

This change makes the run fairer and more readable, preserves old scores separately from the new scoring model, improves keyboard/gamepad-style navigation, and gives the ten-level campaign a distinct mechanical arc and final encounter.

## User impact

Players get more reliable physics, clearer feedback, stronger but configurable effects, accessible keyboard navigation, level selection based on progress, better-balanced power-ups, unique later stages, and a complete final-boss/endless progression loop. Existing legacy scores are retained but no longer mixed with scoring v2 records.

author: klhq
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #17, closing the two remaining findings from the manual security review (HIGH insecure-by-default posture, LOW rate-limiter XFF bypass):

- **`server.hostname`** now defaults to `127.0.0.1` (previously unset → Bun's `0.0.0.0`). A zero-config `skr serve --transport http` is no longer reachable from the network. `RUNNING_IN_DOCKER=true` still overrides this to `0.0.0.0`, since container port-mapping needs the process to accept connections on all interfaces. New `HTTP_HOSTNAME` env override for anyone who needs to expose it explicitly.
- **`server.allowed_origins`** now defaults to `[]` (previously `["*"]`) — deny-by-default CORS. Only browser-issued cross-origin requests carry an `Origin` header, so curl/MCP/server-to-server clients are unaffected either way; this specifically closes the "malicious webpage in an open browser tab makes a request to your local MCP server" path, which was the realistic exploit given loopback binding alone doesn't stop same-machine browsers.
- **Rate limiter**: `X-Forwarded-For` is now only trusted when `rate_limit.trust_proxy` is explicitly `true`. Previously, when `server.requestIP()` returned nothing, any client could bypass per-IP rate limiting by sending a fresh spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` value per request. New `HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_TRUST_PROXY` env override for real reverse-proxy deployments.

### Design call: left `auth_enabled` off by default

With loopback binding + closed CORS, the "whole network, unauthenticated, any browser origin" exposure is gone. Flipping `auth_enabled` to `true` by default would force every zero-config local `skr serve` to fail with 500 until a token is set — a much larger UX/breaking change for the marginal benefit of protecting against other processes/users on the same machine. Auth stays one config line away (`auth_enabled = true`) for anyone deploying beyond localhost.

### Test plan
- [x] `bun x tsc --noEmit` — clean

author: nanatsusaya
body:
## What

The deploy workflow's `push: main` trigger is commented out until GitHub Pages is actually enabled. `docs/STATUS.md` records the state.

## Why

The first merge after the scaffold (#31) ran the deploy and **it failed**:

```
Configure Pages  ##[error]Get Pages site failed. Please verify that the repository
                 has Pages enabled and configured to build using GitHub Actions
                 HttpError: Not Found
```

GitHub Pages is not enabled on this repository. My mistake in #31 — I built and verified the workflow but never checked that its precondition existed.

**Enabling Pages is not mine to do.** It publishes a real business's draft to a public URL, which `CLAUDE.md` reserves to you. And it would be wrong to do it *now* even with permission: without the custom domain, Pages serves from `nanatsusaya.github.io/iris-sunshine-oase/`, which puts `robots.txt` at a subpath where no crawler looks for it, and reintroduces exactly the `base`-path problem ADR 0006 §2 (R1) chose the preview subdomain to avoid.

**Why disabled rather than made to pass.** A deploy job that reports success without deploying is a lie told once per merge. And a workflow that is permanently red is worse than no workflow — it trains everyone, including a future agent, to scroll past a failing check. Neither is acceptable, so the trigger goes away until it can be honest.

## The re-enable procedure

Written into the workflow file itself, ordered deliberately — step 1 is what makes step 2 safe, because between the CNAME and verification the subdomain is takeover-able:

1. Verify the apex domain with GitHub (ADR 0009 §5, R3) — *Settings → Pages → Add a domain*, then the `TXT` record at netcup
2. Add the `preview` CNAME at netcup → `nanatsusaya.github.io` (ADR 0006 §2)
3. Enable Pages, *Source: GitHub Actions*, custom domain `preview.iris-sunshine-oase.de`
4. Uncomment the two `push` lines

## Verified

- `npm run check:docs` → passed
- Biome clean on both changed files
- The workflow keeps `workflow_dispatch`, so it can still be run by hand once Pages exists — no need to merge another change to test it

## Follow-ups

- #4 stays open; its Definition of Done needs the URL above.
- Epic #4's Constraints still carry the superseded `Disallow: /` and subpath text — correcting the ticket is next, and does not need a PR.

body:
## P2a — Native swift/MLX Whisper transcribe (segment-level)

First half of P2 from the zero-python-ext plan ([`crystalline-finding-waffle.md`](https://gist.github.com/)). Replaces the python `whisper_transcribe.py` → mlx_whisper spawn with a **pure swift/MLX** transcribe backend on the existing `ltx-video` binary. **Segment-level timestamps only** — per-word DTW alignment is P2b (the genuinely hard cross-attention port); it splits out so a usable native transcriber ships first.

### Why split P2 → P2a/P2b
The `subtitle_gen` `cuesFromWhisper` has two modes. `segments` mode needs only **segment-level** timestamps, which come straight from the timestamp tokens the decoder already emits — **no DTW, no BPE encoder**. Only `words` mode needs the hard DTW cross-attention alignment. Splitting lets the native transcriber (segments mode + the analysis command) ship now, with DTW isolated as its own parity-gated PR.

### Swift (`swift/ltx-video-director`)
- **`WhisperTranscribe.swift`** — `WhisperModel.transcribeSegments`: a line-for-line port of `mlx_whisper.transcribe.transcribe`'s seek loop + timestamp-token slice parsing (`transcribe.py` ~247-412), minus the DTW path. Windows >30s audio in 30s chunks; reuses the real-checkpoint-verified encoder/decoder + `WhisperDecoding`'s temperature-fallback loop.
- **`TranscribeCommand.swift`** — `ltx-video transcribe --audio …` emitting the exact `WhisperResult` JSON the Bun adapter parses. Checkpoint resolution mirrors `ASRGateEngine.autoDetect` (`--checkpoint` > `WHISPER_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT` > cached `whisper-large-v3-mlx`).

### Bun (`pi-agent-ext-movie-director`)
- `whisperAdapter` spawns `ltx-video transcribe` instead of python. The `bun:whisper` probe is now the ltx-video binary (was `python/whisper-venv` + mlx_whisper import). `WhisperResult`/`WhisperOptions`/`cuesFromWhisper` contracts unchanged; each segment's `words[]` is empty until P2b.
- Delete `python/whisper_transcribe.py`. `run-whisper-e2e.ts` switched to segment-mode cues (the P2a ceiling).

### Verification (real-checkpoint gate — swift is NOT in CI)
- `swift build -c release` ✅ (20.5s incremental)
- `ltx-video transcribe` on `data/fixtures/narration.m4a` with the cached `whisper-large-v3-mlx` → correct transcript with sensible monotonic segment timestamps:

| seg | start | end | text |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.00 | 2.16 | Welcome to the Movie Director Pipeline. |
| 2 | 2.50 | 4.64 | This clip demonstrates native transcription |
| 3 | 4.64 | 7.20 | with word-level timestamps burned in as captions. |

- **Text parity** vs mlx_whisper confirmed (swift large-v3 actually more accurate — restores capitalization + the `word-level` hyphen that mlx_whisper small dropped). *Note:* mlx_whisper large-v3 itself has a float32-dtype bug on this box so exact same-model segment comparison couldn't run; the algorithm is a faithful port of the same `transcribe.py`.
- Full Bun→swift dispatch verified end-to-end (adapter spawns binary, parses JSON, writes transcript.txt + words.json).
- `bun test` **687 pass / 0 fail**.

### Out of scope (P2b)
DTW cross-attention word-alignment: extract decoder cross-attn QK from alignment heads, port `mlx_whisper.timing.dtw` + median-filter + `split_to_word_tokens` (needs a BPE **encoder** added to `WhisperTokenizer`, which today is decode-only). Parity gate ±0.05s/word.

author: stephenberry
body:
Closes #149.

`Dataset` now publicly exposes its storage layout and filter pipeline through a curated, read-only introspection surface, so a caller can locate and read one chunk (or the contiguous extent) at a time without materializing the dataset.

## What's new

- **`Dataset::layout() -> Layout`** — the storage class: `Compact { size }`, `Contiguous { address, size }` (absolute file address), `Chunked { chunk_shape, index }`, or `Virtual`. The curated analogue of `H5Pget_layout`.
- **`Dataset::chunk_index() -> Option<ChunkIndex>`** — the chunk-index kind (`BTreeV1`, `SingleChunk`, `Implicit`, `FixedArray`, `ExtensibleArray`, `BTreeV2`), with `ChunkIndex::supports_inplace_append()` for the common up-front append-eligibility check.
- **`Dataset::chunks() -> Vec<Chunk>`** — one `Chunk { offset, address, storage_size, filter_mask }` per allocated chunk, read from the chunk index alone (never the chunk data). The curated analogue of `H5Dget_num_chunks` + `H5Dget_chunk_info`.
- **`Dataset::filter_pipeline() -> Vec<Filter>`** — the ordered pipeline, each `Filter { id, name, is_optional, client_data }`. The detailed companion to the existing `filters() -> Vec<u16>`. The curated analogue of `H5Pget_nfilters` + `H5Pget_filter2`.

## Design

This is a pure projection layer over data the reader already parses — no parser or on-disk change, all additive. The new `Layout` / `ChunkIndex` / `Chunk` / `Filter` types are curated rather than a raw re-export of the internal layout/pipeline structs, so on-disk mechanics (chunk-index root addresses, layout/pipeline version numbers, the single-chunk filtered-size sidecar fields, the raw filter-flags word) do not leak into the public API. The design was chosen from a three-way panel; three API-taste calls were settled with the maintainer:

- All four public types are `#[non_exhaustive]` (durable/additive over exhaustive-match ergonomics).
- The detailed accessor takes the natural name `filter_pipeline()`; the internal `pub(crate) filter_pipeline()` helper was renamed to `filter_pipeline_parsed()`.
- `chunks()` returns `Err` on a non-chunked dataset (mirroring `H5Dget_num_chunks`), so a caller can distinguish "not chunked" from "chunked but unallocated" (which returns `Ok(vec![])`).

`layout()`'s chunk shape reuses the existing `chunk_shape()` so the two accessors can never disagree, and `chunks()` reuses the existing chunk-index walker, which already resolves each chunk address to an absolute file offset. Enumerating a version-2 B-tree index's allocated chunks is not supported yet (it returns a clear `Err`, not a silent empty list); classification of a `BTreeV2` dataset works.

## Interop note

Verified against the reference C library: h5py and the `hdf5-metno` wrapper mark filters as **optional** (`H5Z_FLAG_OPTIONAL`) when you request deflate/shuffle, while this crate's own writer writes them mandatory. `Filter::is_optional` reports each faithfully; the crosscheck asserts the h5py/metno-written filters come back optional and the pure-written ones mandatory.

## Testing

- New: `tests/layout_introspection.rs` (8 pure round-trips across contiguous, single-chunk, fixed-array, extensible-array, deflate, shuffle+deflate, unallocated, and a `layout()`/`chunk_shape()` agreement invariant) and `tests/layout_introspection_crosscheck.rs` (8 reference-C-library interop cases including `Compact` and legacy `BTreeV1` — which the pure writer cannot emit — a `BTreeV2` classification, and a byte-level readback that seeks to each reported `Chunk.address` in the raw file and decodes, proving the addresses are absolute), plus 3 in-crate unit tests.
- Full suite: **509 passed, 0 failed**. Gates green: `fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, no_std build, and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc`.
- A three-lens adversarial review (correctness / API-durability / regression+no_std) surfaced only documentation and error-text issues (no logic defects); all are fixed in this branch.

No on-disk format change; no semver break (all additive).

chronicle20
body:
## Summary

PR #971 (GMS legacy versions 48.1/61.1/72.1/79.1) routed the socket handlers but
left many handlers **without their `options` block**. Handlers that resolve a
serverbound mode from `readerOptions["operations"]` (buddy, guild, guild-BBS,
messenger, note, storage, npc-shop, cash-shop) silently dropped every packet
(`"Code [X] not configured for use."`); movement handlers reading
`readerOptions["types"]` defaulted the path attr to 99 ("likely client crash").
So these features were dead on v48/v61/v72/v79.

## Socket options (the core fix)
- **Operations mode tables** for 8 dispatcher families, **reverse-engineered from
  each legacy client IDB** (`COutPacket(op) → Encode1(mode)`), every value quoted
  from a real decompiled line (evidence: `docs/tasks/task-178-legacy-template-options/re-*.md`).
  - Six families (Buddy, GuildBBS, NPCShop, Storage, Messenger, Guild) are
    **byte-identical to v83** on every version (verified, not assumed).
  - **CashShop is a distinct enum per version** — `BUY_NORMAL` = 35/34/33/31 on
    v79/v72/v61/v48 (v83 = 20). Copying v83 would have silently corrupted all four.
    Slot-expansion collisions (INCREASE_INVENTORY/STORAGE share a mode with
    CHAR_SLOT/ENABLE_EQUIP via an inner byte atlas can't dispatch on) resolved for
    the common op; no duplicate modes in any table.
- **Movement `types`** copied from each template's own verified `CharacterMoveHandle.types`.
- **v61 routing fix**: `NPCShopHandle` `0x3C→0x39`, `StorageOperationHandle` `0x3D→0x3A`
  — the v61 client sends 0x39/0x3A; the template routed them to nothing.
- **Note** `SEND=0` is parity-inferred (UI-gated; no static send site any legacy client).

## Legacy preset remediation (required to apply the fix on live v48/v61)
The live tenant PATCH is full-replace and re-validates the whole config, which the
pre-existing invalid character presets rejected. Corrected per version:
- **Pirate presets removed** (Buccaneer 512 / Corsair 522) — Pirates shipped v62.
- **v48 downgraded** — 4th job shipped v49; the 10 explorer 4th-job presets are
  downgraded to 3rd job (jobId/skills/name/tags/description).
- **v61 clamped** — over-level 4th-job skills capped to their atlas-data maxLevel.
- **both**: equipment absent from that version's atlas-data stripped.

## Verification
- JSON valid ×4; atlas-configurations seeder tests pass; module builds.
- Templates correctness-reviewed (values vs RE evidence, no dup modes, movement
  `types`, clean diff).
- **Live**: all 4 tenants PATCHed (200). atlas-channel restarted clean, **0
  "not configured for use"**. v61/v72/v79 are actively served and verified; **v48
  is a parked tenant** (like v92) not currently bound to a channel — its config is
  correct for when it's activated.
