body:
## Summary

Four new skills surfaced by the 2026-07-18 session review, ported onto current main with the compute in `quant_garage/skills/` per invariant #3 (thin CLI wrappers in `examples/`). Audit green at 62 skills.

This is the new-skills subset of the earlier PR #1 (closed as stale). Bug fixes ship in the sibling PR #2.

Dropped from PR #1 vs this PR: `macro-basket` and `rate-signal`. Both duplicated the existing `fixed_income_context` on main. Cross-references in these skills point at `fixed-income-context` instead.

## Skills

**portfolio-macro-scenario** (Stocks Starter)
Prescriptive book P&L under a scenario the operator names. Per-position OLS regression on TLT/UUP/USO/GLD daily returns, applies rates/DXY/oil/gold shocks, aggregates to book P&L with a rough +/-1.64 sigma band. Ranks positions by absolute contribution and factors by aggregate contribution.

**hedge-suggester** (Stocks Starter + Options Developer)
Prices five option overlays (covered call, protective put, collar, put spread, ratio put spread) against a long position from chain mids. Ranks by cost per dollar of downside protected. IV context via ATM implied vs 20d realized volatility. Take fitted to stated risk tolerance. Not investment advice.

**single-name-vs-sector** (any Stocks tier)
Splits "name vs SPY" into three RS legs (name vs sector, sector vs benchmark, name vs benchmark) and classifies leading / lagging / diverging. Divergence catches the case where the name is pulling away from its own sector regardless of the market. Uses `pp` (percentage points) not the ambiguous `pts` label.

**commodity-cycle** (any Stocks tier)
Reads the macro cycle for one commodity ETF via dollar correlation, real-yield correlation (TIP minus IEF proxy), miner divergence (GLD vs GDX), silver co-movement, and momentum quintile. Take reads constructive / neutral / headwind with the dominant driver named.

## Structure

Each skill ships:
- `quant_garage/skills/<snake>.py` — `run(...) -> dict` and `render(payload) -> str`
- `examples/run-<kebab>.py` — thin arg-parse wrapper (~80 lines)
- `skills/<kebab>/` — SKILL.md, README.md, requires.yml, output-schema.json, references/rendering.md, references/methodology.md

State (client, aggs cache, rate-limited set) lives in a per-run `_State` object rather than module-level globals, so consecutive `run()` calls from the same process don't leak throttled flags across invocations.

Rate-limit handling mirrors the pattern from PR #2 (detect `RateLimited`, cool down 13s, retry once, flag ticker if still failing, emit loud caveat).

## Live verification

Verified against real Massive API on 2026-07-18. Every take line matches the figure computed independently from the earlier PR #1 branch:

- **portfolio-macro-scenario**: 12-position book, +50bp/+2%/+10%/-5%: book P&L -$17,130 (-3.9%), gold factor 40% of loss.
- **hedge-suggester**: ALLO 29,000 shares over 90d: collar net credit -1.4% notional, IV 1.76x realized (EXPENSIVE).
- **single-name-vs-sector**: SOFI: classification "diverging", "lagging XLF by 39 pp/120d even as XLF leads SPY by 4 pp/20d".
- **commodity-cycle**: GLD: setup "headwind", dominant driver strong dollar (60d corr -0.68) plus rising real yields, miners lagging -9.07%, momentum bottom quintile.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run audit:requires` — green (62 skills)
- [ ] `python -c "from quant_garage.skills import portfolio_macro_scenario, hedge_suggester, single_name_vs_sector, commodity_cycle; print('OK')"` — imports OK
- [ ] `python examples/run-portfolio-macro-scenario.py --book examples/sample-book.csv --rates-bp 50 --format render` on Starter key
- [ ] `python examples/run-single-name-vs-sector.py --ticker SOFI --format render` on any Stocks tier
- [ ] `python examples/run-commodity-cycle.py --ticker GLD --format render` on any Stocks tier
- [ ] `python examples/run-hedge-suggester.py --ticker <optionable> --shares 100 --format render` (needs Options Developer)

body: ## Summary Adds Detekt static analysis across the main Gradle build and the included build logic. Module-local baselines capture the 641 existing findings, allowing CI to reject new violations without requiring unrelated cleanup in this PR. Detekt produces HTML and SARIF reports, uploads CI findings to code scanning, and includes an Android Studio run configuration. Ktlint remains responsible for formatting and line length. The current baseline includes 189 magic numbers, 114 long methods, 83 cyclomatically complex methods, 70 classes or objects with too many functions, 56 functions with excessive returns, 21 swallowed exceptions, and one `printStackTrace` call. author: safal207
transfix
body:
The pidfile check from #329 swung too far the other way.

On the run that **restored every other host**, it reported `freebsd-build` as failed — the one builder that had never been broken:

```
netbsd-build.incus:  builder restarted (pid 22838)
netbsd-build-2:      builder restarted (pid 2999)
freebsd-build:       FAILED (no live pid in /tmp/cvcpkg-builder/cvcpkg-builder.pid)   <- healthy!
freebsd-build-2:     builder restarted (pid 11324)
openbsd-build.incus: builder restarted (pid 38426)
openbsd-build.incus: builder restarted (pid 73564)
BSD restart: 5 restarted, 1 failed
```

Direct check: `freebsd-build`'s daemon is alive at pid 49326 and heartbeating `0m ago`, it just doesn't write a pidfile into its work dir.

So I traded a check that *could never fail* for one that *could fail wrongly*. Both are bad; this run happened to expose the second kind.

## Fix

Success is now **either** a live PID from the pidfile **or** a matching process.

The `pgrep` is only trustworthy here because #329 bracket-escaped the pattern so it cannot match the invoking shell. With a bare pattern this would silently become the incapable-of-failing check again.

| pidfile live | process found | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | OK |
| yes | no | OK |
| no | yes | OK (reported as "no pidfile") |
| no | no | FAIL |

## Fleet state

All six BSD builders are **online** with fresh heartbeats, confirmed against `/v1/builders` rather than the workflow's own output:

```
freebsd-build online   freebsd-build-2 online
netbsd-build  online   netbsd-build-2  online
openbsd-build online   openbsd-build-2 online
```

The outage is over. #329's `pkill` fix is what did it — all four previously-dead hosts came back with real PIDs.

Note both openbsd guests report the hostname `openbsd-build.incus`, which is why that name appears twice above with different PIDs. Cosmetic, but worth knowing before it confuses someone reading these logs.

author: ericbass11
body:
## Problema
Ao recarregar (F5) uma tela autenticada — em especial o **Perfil** — o app às vezes voltava para a tela de login/onboarding, pedindo nome e e-mail de novo.

## Causa raiz
O bootstrap de autenticação era **assíncrono**. Enquanto o `getSession()` do Supabase resolvia (rede, Web Locks, renovação de token), o app já decidia a rota com `profile = null` e redirecionava para `/`.

Verificado empiricamente que a sessão **de fato persiste** no `localStorage` (`sb-<ref>-auth-token`, contendo o objeto `user` completo) e que o cadastro já retorna sessão (confirmação de e-mail desligada). Ou seja, o dado existia — o app só decidia a rota cedo demais.

## Correção
- A sessão passa a ser lida **direto do `localStorage` de forma síncrona** no primeiro render (`readStoredProfile`). No refresh a usuária já nasce autenticada — sem loading, sem bounce para o login, sem sumiço momentâneo da foto.
- `getSession()` e `onAuthStateChange` passam a apenas **refinar/renovar em segundo plano**; só um `SIGNED_OUT` real limpa a sessão.

## Notas
- Apagar todo o `localStorage` do site desloga por design (não há como manter sessão sem ele) — o que foi corrigido é o refresh normal e o hard-refresh.
- `tsc` limpo e build/PWA passando.

author: g-reen-vibe
body:
# PR6: Generator robustness — track failures, guard empty choices, try/finally client.close

## Summary

`generator.py` had three robustness issues:
1. Failed requests were silently swallowed (returned `("", 0, 0)` with no aggregate reporting).
2. `response.choices[0]` was accessed without checking if `choices` was empty — would raise `IndexError` on content-filter rejections.
3. `await client.close()` was not in a `finally` block — if `asyncio.gather` raised, the client would leak.

This PR fixes all three and also fixes a latent `None > 0` crash that PR1's `Optional[top_k]` change would trigger.

## Changes

### `src/fastdetector/generator.py`

#### 1. Empty `choices` guard (`_send_request`)

The old code:
```python
return response.choices[0].message.content or "", ...
```

The new code:
```python
if not response.choices:
    print(f"Request returned no choices (possibly content-filtered).")
    return "", 0, 0
return response.choices[0].message.content or "", ...
```

Some OpenAI-compatible endpoints return an empty `choices` array on content-filter rejection or other server-side errors. The old code would raise `IndexError: list index out of range`, which would be caught by the `except Exception` and silently swallowed. The new code prints a diagnostic message and returns the same `("", 0, 0)` sentinel, but more explicitly.

#### 2. `try/finally` for `client.close()` (`_batch_generate_async`)

The old code:
```python
tasks = [_tracked_request(messages) for messages in inputs]
results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
await client.close()
```

If `asyncio.gather` raised (e.g. due to a `CancelledError` or an unexpected exception not caught by `_send_request`), `client.close()` would never be called, leaking the HTTP connection pool.

The new code:
```python
try:
    tasks = [_tracked_request(messages) for messages in inputs]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
finally:
    await client.close()
```

#### 3. Failed-request tracking (`_batch_generate_async`)

The old code silently produced empty strings for failed requests with no aggregate reporting. A user running 50,000 samples might see 5,000 empty responses and not realize they were failures vs. genuinely-empty model outputs.

The new code tracks `failed_count` (requests returning `("", 0, 0)`) and prints a warning at the end:
```
WARNING: 1234/50000 requests failed (returned empty responses). These will appear as empty strings in the output.
```

The empty strings are still kept in the output list at their original positions so that `build_dataset` can align them with the input samples (changing the output length would break the column-length invariant added in PR1).

#### 4. `None`-safe `> 0` check (`_send_request`)

The old code:
```python
for key in ["top_k", "top_a", "xtc_probability", "nsigma"]:
    if key in generation_params and generation_params[key] > 0:
        extra_body[key] = generation_params[key]
```

After PR1 made `PipelineConfig.top_k` and `disable_thinking` `Optional`, `filter.toml` (which omits these fields) now produces `generation_params["top_k"] = None`. The old check `generation_params[key] > 0` would raise `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'`.

The new code:
```python
for key in ["top_k", "top_a", "xtc_probability", "nsigma"]:
    val = generation_params.get(key)
    if val is not None and val > 0:
        extra_body[key] = val
```

This correctly handles `None` values and also uses `.get(key)` instead of `key in ... and [key]` for cleaner code.

#### 5. Improved docstrings

- `batch_generate`: now documents `api_key` and `model_name` params, and notes that failed requests appear as empty strings.
- `_send_request`: documents the retry behavior and failure return value.
- `_batch_generate_async`: documents the client lifecycle and failure tracking.
- `build_dataset`: cleaner docstring without the duplicated "It creates a batch..." sentence.

## Verification

Installed `openai` in the test venv and ran 4 mocked tests:

1. **Empty `choices` guard**: mocked response with `choices = []` → returns `("", 0, 0)` instead of raising. ✓
2. **Normal response**: mocked response with content + usage → returns `("Hello back", 5, 2)`. ✓
3. **`client.close()` in `finally`**: mocked client where `gather` would raise → `client.close()` still called. ✓
4. **Failed-count tracking**: 5 requests all failing → warning printed, all outputs are `""`, token counts are 0. ✓
5. **`None` top_k handling**: `generation_params = {"top_k": None, "disable_thinking": None, ...}` (filter.toml scenario) → no crash, `extra_body` correctly not set. ✓

author: davidbshan
body:
## what

Tier-1 RunPod endpoint reuse: when a run finishes successfully, keep its serverless endpoint warm and let the next compatible run reuse it instead of deleting and re-provisioning. This skips endpoint creation + worker cold-boot for back-to-back compatible runs.

This PR now also includes the per-job worker environment isolation that makes cross-environment reuse safe (folded in from #571).

RunPod only. Lambda/Vast untouched. No schema/CLI/billing changes.

## reuse contract

A warm endpoint is reused only when the compatibility signature matches: account, GPU type + count, worker image, disk, network volume, base model + immutable revision, and context length. The signature is captured at deploy time from the actually-resolved image and volume (so a volume-fallback box never falsely matches a volume-wanting run).

Environment and dataset are deliberately **excluded** — they travel in the per-job queue payload, so "same model, different environment" reuses the warm box. Cross-environment reuse is made safe by the per-job env isolation below.

## behavior

- **keep-warm on success only.** `done` runs register the endpoint in a durable registry (`~/.flash/runpod_warm/`, capped at 8, strict-parsed). `failed`/`cancelled` still tear down.
- **reuse on submit.** `warm_pool.acquire` matches across all configured accounts (each record validated by its own fingerprint), health-checks the endpoint (skip if busy, prune if gone), atomically claims it, and persists ownership before the queue post. Falls back to a fresh endpoint on any miss.
- **idle timeout = the existing reaper.** Endpoints scale to zero (≈no idle GPU cost); the existing idle reaper reclaims any warm endpoint nobody reuses. Reaper reap-logic unchanged.

## per-job environment isolation (folded from #571)

Because a warm worker keeps its container filesystem across jobs, each job's env-specific `extra_pip` must not carry into the next. Isolation works as follows (RunPod worker only):

- the **worker runs in the base interpreter** (`sys.executable`), so its own base-stack management (e.g. flash-linear-attention removal/reinstall) is unaffected and console scripts resolve correctly;
- only `extra_pip` is installed into a fresh per-job `venv --system-site-packages`; the base interpreter is never mutated, so nothing carries across jobs;
- the worker is launched with a small `-c` bootstrap that calls `site.addsitedir(<job venv site-packages>)` (so `.pth`/editable/namespace extras import) and then `runpy.run_module("flash.engine.worker_entrypoint", run_name="__main__")`; `cwd=code_dir` keeps the fetched flash code first on `sys.path`, and the venv site-packages is prepended to `PYTHONPATH` so ordinary job packages take precedence over base;
- the pip install destination is non-bypassable: `PIP_TARGET/PIP_PREFIX/PIP_ROOT/PIP_USER/PYTHONUSERBASE/PIP_CONFIG_FILE/PIP_SRC` are stripped and `--target/-t/--prefix/--root/--user/--src` args are rejected;
- the venv is removed after the job; the hard-deadline callback exits immediately; stale venvs are cleaned at job start; `max_concurrency=1` keeps that cleanup safe. Preload path is unaffected.

This is what makes cross-environment reuse safe. It is covered by real-venv/wheel tests (install target, base immutability, `.pth` import, escape rejection), but has **not** been exercised on a live RunPod GPU end to end.

## review fixes (commit 7e872972)

Addresses the Bugbot + Codex findings on the initial commit:

- retry (`rN`) endpoints are still reaped on warm-success via a run-name GC that excludes only the pooled endpoint;
- a released endpoint's original owner is marked so no later teardown/cancel can destroy an endpoint a newer run has claimed (historical remote preserved for billing);
- ownership is persisted at claim, before the queue post (no orphan on a crash in the window);
- busy endpoints are skipped (not pruned); the real configured timeout is captured on the handle (no wall-time guess; legacy handles aren't warmed);
- registry cap reconciles dead records before rejecting; strict record parsing; acquisition extracted into `warm_pool` (jobs.py back under 1k lines).

## anti-leak safety

Failed/cancelled always tear down. The registry is a best-effort hint validated against the RunPod API (stale entries pruned). Warm pool capped; existing reaper is the idle backstop.

## validation

- `tests/test_runpod_warm_pool.py` and `tests/test_runpod_job_env_isolation.py` (mocked; no real API/GPU) cover the registry, signature, reuse, ownership, retry-gc exclusion, cap reconcile, and the venv isolation.
- Affected + full non-live suite green (the 4 `test_cli_commands` dry-run failures are ambient `WANDB_API_KEY` env contamination on the runner, unrelated; they pass with the var unset). ruff clean. `jobs.py` = 999 lines.
- Not yet exercised on a real RunPod GPU; a live back-to-back reuse + env-isolation smoke is a sensible follow-up.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches RunPod provisioning/teardown races, durable warm registry, and worker pip/venv isolation—mistakes could leak billable endpoints, destroy claimed warm workers, or let job env bleed across reuse.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **RunPod warm endpoint reuse**: successful `done` runs can register their serverless endpoint in a durable registry (`warm_pool`, cap 8) instead of always deleting it. **`submit_run`** tries `warm_pool.acquire` (signature match, health check, atomic claim) before deploying fresh; handles persist **`reuse_signature`**, **`execution_timeout_ms`**, and **`released_to_warm_pool`**.
> 
> **Lifecycle / safety:** `release_warm_endpoint` marks the owner released before publishing to the pool; **`destroy`** and teardown skip released handles; terminal cleanup reaps retry siblings via **`terminate_endpoint(..., exclude_endpoint_id=...)`** while keeping the pooled box. Failed/cancelled runs still tear down.
> 
> **Worker isolation (enables cross-environment reuse):** `_train_body` creates a per-job venv for **`extra_pip`**, blocks pip location escapes, launches training via a **`site.addsitedir` + `runpy`** bootstrap in the base interpreter, and cleans up venvs. Deploy sets **`max_concurrency=1`** on endpoints.
>

Recasting works, but the take list gave no clue what you were looking at: a recast landed as "take-2" with nothing to say why it existed or who it was. The data was already there -- generation_versions.profile_id is populated on recast takes -- it just wasn't rendered.

author: mark-12-fr
body:
## Symptom

Railway build fails at the Python install step:

```
mise ERROR Failed to install core:python@3.11.9:
No GitHub artifact attestations found for python@3.11.9
Build Failed: process "mise install" did not complete successfully: exit code 1
```

## Root cause

Railway's **Railpack** builder installs Python via **mise**, which now verifies **GitHub build attestations** on the `python-build-standalone` download. The pinned build **cpython-3.11.9 (20240814)** predates attestation publishing (which began ~Oct 2024), so verification fails and the build aborts.

## Fix

Bump the pinned Python from **3.11.9 → 3.11.11** — a bugfix-only patch, fully source-compatible — whose standalone build carries attestations. Updated in both:
- `runtime.txt` (read by Railway/Railpack)
- `render.yaml` `PYTHON_VERSION` (Render) — kept in sync so the two platforms don't drift.

## If it still fails

Fallbacks (Railway dashboard): switch the service's builder to **Nixpacks** (installs Python via Nix, no mise attestation check), or add a `Dockerfile`. Noted for reference — the version bump should resolve it.

author: fujibee
body:
## What

`install.sh`'s `agmsg_source_version()` records a `git describe` provenance string into the installed `VERSION` file (see #117). It used `git describe --tags` unrestricted, which matches both core release tags (`v1.1.8`) and the desktop app's own `app-v*` tags sharing the same repo/tag namespace — whichever lineage is closer in history wins.

When an `app-v*` tag (e.g. `app-v0.2.0`) landed after the last core `v*` tag, a fresh `HEAD` install recorded provenance like `app-v0.2.0-26-g95d01ca` instead of `v1.1.8-27-g95d01ca`. Confirmed on this machine:

```
$ git describe --tags --always --dirty --abbrev=7
app-v0.2.0-26-g95d01ca
$ git describe --tags --always --dirty --abbrev=7 --match 'v[0-9]*'
v1.1.8-27-g95d01ca
```

The app's own version comparison (`agmsg_core_version_status` in `app/src-tauri/src/agmsg.rs`) can't parse an `app-v*`-prefixed string as semver and treats an unparseable `installed` version as unconditionally outdated (`None => true`) — this misfires the app's "CLI might be outdated" banner on an install that's actually current.

## Fix

Restrict `git describe` to core release tags with `--match 'v[0-9]*'`.

Grepped the repo for other consumers of the recorded `VERSION` to check for downstream impact: `scripts/version.sh` only prints it verbatim (unaffected), and this is the only place a raw `git describe --tags` occurs anywhere in the repo — no other parsing logic needs updating.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_install.bats`: a synthetic repo with a `v1.0.0` tag followed by a later `app-v9.9.9` tag confirms the recorded `VERSION` uses the core tag lineage, not the app one.

Full `test_install.bats` passes locally.

body:
The `/settings/automations` page logged three React errors on load because the workspace-scoped automations page it redirects to was a leftover Next.js async server component; converting it to a plain synchronous client component clears the console and lets the list UI render normally.

## Important Changes

- `app/settings/workspace/[id]/automations/page.tsx` is now a synchronous client component that takes a `workspaceId` prop and delegates data loading to `AutomationsListPage` (which already loads via the `useAutomations` hook), instead of `await`-ing a `params` promise in render.
- `src/settings-routes.tsx` passes `workspaceId={id}` directly, matching the sibling repositories/workflows routes, rather than `params={Promise.resolve({ id })}`.

## Validation

author: awick
body:
Build an Arkime capture reader (pcapReadMethod=synthetic) from the existing generator sources, so Arkime can manufacture HTTP/HTTPS/DNS traffic internally for deterministic testing -- no pcap files or live NIC. Same seed produces byte-identical packets and, via a synthetic clock, identical timestamps.

- Split config.h into portable config-core.h (structs/macros, no pthread or AF_PACKET) plus the delivery-specific bits, and repoint the generator headers at config-core.h so they build without the standalone tool's dependencies.
- Move parse_mix into net_utils so the plugin reuses it instead of duplicating.
- plugin/reader-synthetic.c: the only Arkime-aware file. Registers the reader via arkime_plugin_init, drives session_init/session_step into arkime_packet_batch on a single deterministic thread, and arkime_quit()s after the configured session/packet count. All options come from one Arkime config key, arkimeBlastCmdLine, parsed with the standalone tool's flags plus --max-sessions/--base-time/--time-delta/--run-forever.
- plugin/Makefile: on-demand build against an Arkime checkout (ARKIME=...); arkime_* symbols resolve at load, so main.c is never linked.
- Add rng_fill/rng_fill_printable helpers that emit 8 payload bytes per RNG call, and route the HTTP body, TLS certificate, and DNS TXT fills through them -- ~8x fewer rng_next() calls, cutting generator user CPU ~60% on a 50k-session run while keeping payloads fully random and reproducible.
- README: build and capture invocation docs.

author: jakechampion
body:
## Summary

A method returning a generic enum, matched **directly** as the scrutinee, silently miscompiled:

```fern
enum Opt[T] { Non, Has(T) }
struct S { n: i32 }
function (s: S) find(k: i32): Opt[i32] { if (k == s.n) { return Has(s.n * 2); } return Non; }
function main(): i32 { match (S { n: 21 }.find(21)) { Has(v) => { return v; }, Non => { return 0; } } }
// native → 42; self-host → 0 (wrong arm)
```

The monomorphiser recovers a match scrutinee's generic-enum instantiation — to rewrite the arm patterns to the concrete `Variant__<key>` names — from the scrutinee's type via `me_scrutinee_type`. But its `ExprCall` arm only handled a **free-function** callee; a **method-call** scrutinee (`ExprCall` over `ExprFieldAccess`) fell to `_ => ""`, so the arms stayed un-mangled against the concrete enum. The module then declined the IR path and miscompiled on the AST path (the match read the wrong variant tag).

## Fix

`me_scrutinee_type`'s `ExprCall` arm now resolves a method call's return type: recover the receiver's type, match a receiver method by name + base-stripped receiver type (mirroring the existing `enum_has_method` lookup), and return its declared return type. The scrutinee recovers its instantiation, the arms rewrite, and the shape lowers on the IR path with the native value.

## Testing (x86, local)

New `TestSelfHostMethodEnumScrutineeIRX86_64` — 5 cases, all lower via the IR path (`.Lir_` witness) with native values:
- method-returning `Opt[i32]` scrutinee (the bug), both-payload variant (isolates scrutinee-type recovery from the unit-variant path), string-payload method + struct-literal receiver;
- regressions: free-function scrutinee, var-bound method result.

`TestSelfHostLoadFixpointX86_64`, `TestSelfHostBootstrapsItself`, `TestSelfHostModloadFixpointX86_64` — green (byte-identical self-compile). Existing generic/enum/match/mono selfhost suites — green. Native Go backend unaffected (`examples/self_host/parser.fern` only). arm64 + wasm lanes left to CI.

Found in a differential sweep (native `-interp` vs self-host-IR-compiled exit) on `main`.

body:
## 概要

はてなブログからの記事移行完了後の要望対応。AIが書いた文章を貼り付けやすい編集画面が欲しいとのことで、サーバーを持たない静的サイト構成を維持したまま、ブラウザだけで記事管理を完結できる `/admin/` ページを追加しました。

## 実装内容

### `/admin/` 記事編集画面（`src/pages/admin.astro` + `src/scripts/admin-editor.js`）
- GitHub Contents API を直接ブラウザから叩いて記事を新規作成・編集・コミットします（サーバー無し）
- 認証は GitHub Fine-grained Personal Access Token（対象リポジトリのみ・Contents: Read and write）をページ内の入力欄から `localStorage` に保存する方式。ページ下部に「他者に公開して見せるページではない」旨を明記し、`noindex` メタタグと `robots.txt` の `Disallow: /admin/` も追加
- **新規作成**: タイトル・日付（デフォルト今日）・カテゴリ（カンマ区切り、既存カテゴリを `datalist` で補完）・本文（Markdown textarea）を入力。スラッグは日付+ランダム/タイトルスラッグのデフォルト値を編集可能、「重複チェック」ボタンでGitHub上の重複を確認
- **編集**: 「記事一覧を読み込む」でGitHub Contents APIから一覧取得→タイトル・日付でリスト表示（sha単位でlocalStorageキャッシュし2回目以降は高速化）。選択すると frontmatter・本文をフォームに展開し、保存時は取得済みの `sha` を使ってPUT。コンフリクト(409)時はエラーメッセージを表示
- 簡易プレビュー: marked.js をCDNから遅延読み込みしてMarkdownレンダリング表示

### URLペースト→Markdownリンク自動変換
- 本文textareaにURLだけを貼り付ける、または選択してボタンを押すと `[タイトル](URL)` に自動変換
- CORSの制約のため、Google Apps Script のWebアプリをプロキシとして利用（`admin/gas-ogp-proxy/`にコード一式を用意）。`doGet(e)` で対象URLを `UrlFetchApp.fetch()` し、`og:title` / `<title>` を抽出してJSON返却
- **GASプロジェクトの `clasp create`・実デプロイはユーザー自身の手動操作が必要**（Googleアカウント認証が必要なため）。導入手順は `admin/gas-ogp-proxy/README.md` に記載
- GAS URL未設定時はUI上でボタンを無効化し、その旨を表示

### 画像クリップボード貼り付け→自動アップロード
- 本文textareaに画像を貼り付けると、Base64化してGitHub Contents API経由で `public/img/blog/<slug>-<timestamp>-<連番>.<拡張子>` にアップロードし、`https://sin1.studio/img/blog/xxx.png` の公開URLで `![画像](URL)` を自動挿入
- **依頼文中では `img/blog/` が指定されていましたが、Astroが実際に静的配信するのは `public/` 配下のみのため、公開URLが実際に機能するよう `public/img/blog/` に保存先を変更しています**（`img/` 直下は別途存在するレガシー/ミラー用ディレクトリで、ビルド出力には含まれません）

## 使い方（概要）

1. GitHubで対象リポジトリ限定・Contents Read/write権限の Fine-grained PAT を発行
2. `/admin/` の「接続設定」にPATを入力して保存（このブラウザのlocalStorageにのみ保存）
3. （任意）`admin/gas-ogp-proxy/README.md` の手順でGASプロキシをclasp create→デプロイし、発行されたWebアプリURLを同じ設定欄に入力
4. 「新規作成」または「編集」タブから記事を作成・更新して保存

## 動作確認

- `npm run build` 成功（232ページ生成、`/admin/index.html` 含む）
- `astro preview` + Playwright で `/admin/` を目視確認：フォーム一式が正しく表示、タブ切り替え・スラッグ自動生成・重複チェックボタンのエラーハンドリング・プレビュー切り替えを操作しJSエラー無しを確認（コンソールエラー0件）
- 実際のGitHub API呼び出し・GASプロキシ経由のURL変換・画像アップロードは本物のPAT/デプロイ済みGAS URLが必要なため未検証

## 既知の制約・今後の実地確認事項

- GASプロキシは手動デプロイ必須。デプロイ後の実URLでのOGP取得・CORS越しfetchの実地確認が必要
- 実PATを使ったGitHub Contents APIでの新規作成・編集・画像アップロードのフルフローの実地確認が必要
- 編集モードではスラッグ（ファイル名）変更不可（リネームには非対応、意図的な仕様）
- 記事一覧の初回読み込みは220記事分をGitHub APIから取得するため多少時間がかかる（2回目以降はshaベースのキャッシュで高速化）
- 保存前に離脱した場合、アップロード済み画像だけがリポジトリに残る可能性がある（孤立ファイル）

body: ## Summary New players had no in-context guidance on what to do or what anything means. This adds three layers of onboarding, all offline/presentational (no engine or content changes to game logic): 1. **Interactive guided tour** (`GuidedTour.tsx`) — a spotlighted, 10-step walkthrough of the command screen. It dims the screen and cuts out a highlight around each anchored element while an explanatory card steps through: objective + win/lose conditions, the quarter clock, resources, the Status Quo bar, force-posture tracks, intelligence estimates, the incoming probe, and the Inbox/Assessment menu. Auto-opens once per browser on a first new game (guarded by a `redline:tourSeen` localStorage flag), and is replayable anytime via a new **"?"** button in the HUD. Keyboard: `→`/`←`/`Esc`. - Anchoring is by `data-tour="..."` attributes on real elements; the tour measures `getBoundingClientRect()` in a layout effect (re-measured on resize/scroll) and renders the spotlight with a big `box-shadow` cutout + a card placed below/above with room checks. Reads no engine state; the only store touch is a client-only `tourOpen` flag. 2. **Menu tooltips** — nav items (Inbox, Assessment, Menu, ?) and the four force-posture track chips now show a hover/focus popover explaining what they are. 3. **Circled-"i" info tips** — a reusable `InfoTip` on HUD resources (Budget, Political Capital, Status Quo) and on section headings (Intelligence Estimates, Incoming probe, Probe Response ladder, Signals, Investments). All wording lives in one `GLOSSARY` in `format.ts` so the tour and tips stay consistent. Both `Tooltip` and `InfoTip` are pure-CSS visibility (no positioning JS), so they're deterministic and testable. ### Store ```ts // gameStore.ts — client-only, never persisted, never in GameState tourOpen: boolean startTour() // opens; snaps PROBE/SIGNALS back to SITREP so anchors exist endTour() // marks redline:tourSeen, closes newGame(...) // sets tourOpen: !tourSeen() ``` ### Also fixed (Devin Review finding on PR #4) The intel confidence badge builds its class as `c-${confidence.toLowerCase()}`, producing `c-moderate`, but the stylesheet only defined `.c-medium` — so MODERATE-confidence reads (commonly reached after tasking collection) rendered as an unstyled pill. Renamed the CSS rule `.c-medium` → `.c-moderate`. Added `tests/ui-onboarding.test.ts` guarding that every confidence level has a matching CSS rule, plus a glossary-completeness check. ## Verification - `lint`, `typecheck`, `validate-content`, `build` all pass; `47 tests` pass (was 45 + 2 new). - Browser-verified on a fresh seed-1 campaign: tour auto-opens, spotlight tracks each anchor (clock → resources → Status Quo → tracks → intel → incoming → Inbox nav), keyboard nav works, "Start playing" dismisses it, and hover tips render. author: adamcohenhillel
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cron job created with `payload.kind="systemEvent"` and no explicit `sessionTarget` defaults to `sessionTarget="main"` (see `normalizeCronJobInput`). Main-session jobs enqueue their text into the owning session and never take `assertDeliverySupport`'s announce path. So when a caller *also* attaches an explicit delivery block:

```jsonc
{
  "schedule": { "kind": "every", "everyMs": 86400000 },
  "payload":  { "kind": "systemEvent", "text": "Check the incident dashboard" },
  "delivery": { "mode": "announce", "channel": "telegram", "to": "..." }
}
```

...the entire `cron.add` is rejected at creation time:

```
cron channel delivery config is only supported for sessionTarget="isolated"
```

This is a natural shape for "watch X and notify me" scheduled jobs: a systemEvent reminder plus an announce delivery block. Instead of delivering, the request **fails closed** — the job is never created. The caller expressed clear intent (announce to a channel) and got a hard error rather than a working job.

## Fix

When a system-event job **explicitly requests announce delivery to a concrete target** but does **not** pin a session target, isolate it and carry the event text over as an agent turn, so the requested delivery is honored via the existing isolated-agent announce path.

Scope is deliberately narrow:
- Only triggers when `delivery` normalizes to an announce request (`mode: "announce"`, or mode omitted, which `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` already treats as announce) **and** carries a concrete target (`channel`/`to`/`threadId`/`accountId`).
- A bare `{ mode: "announce" }` with no routable target is **not** converted — isolating it would only defer the same failure to execution time, so it keeps the existing creation-time rejection.
- System-event jobs that don't request channel delivery still default to `sessionTarget="main"`, unchanged.
- An explicit `sessionTarget="main"` set by the caller is untouched (this block only runs when `sessionTarget` is absent).
- Empty/blank systemEvent text falls back to the previous `main` default rather than creating an empty agent turn.

## Evidence

Added an end-to-end create-pipeline test in `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` (`normalizeCronJobCreate` → `createJob`, which runs `assertSupportedJobSpec` + `assertDeliverySupport`):

- the previously-rejected shape is now created as an isolated `agentTurn` with delivery preserved
- an announce block pinned to `sessionTarget="main"` still rejects — validation boundary preserved

I verified this test **fails on the pre-fix source** with the exact rejection error, confirming it is a genuine regression guard rather than a tautology. Reverting only the `normalize.ts` change and re-running the new test:

```
FAIL  src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts > createJob honors explicit announce delivery on system-event jobs
      > creates the job as an isolated agent turn instead of rejecting it
Error: cron channel delivery config is only supported for sessionTarget="isolated"
    420|     throw new Error('cron channel delivery config is only supported fo…
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

With the fix restored, the full cron suite passes:

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  145 passed (145)
```

`src/cron/normalize.test.ts` additionally covers: isolate-on-delivery to a concrete target, keep-on-main when no delivery is requested, and do-not-isolate a mode-only announce with no routable target.

Reproduce from source:

```
git fetch && git checkout fix/cron-explicit-delivery-honored
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts \
  src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/normalize.test.ts
```

## Notes

Open to adjusting the approach — e.g. gating behind a config flag, or (per the automated review's suggestion) keeping the current rejection but improving the error/CLI surface to direct callers toward an explicit isolated agent-turn job. This touches the systemEvent-vs-isolated contract, so happy to defer to maintainer preference on which direction is wanted.

author: georginio-prod
body:
Closes #247

## Problème
Au survol de la grille « Parcourir par secteur », **les cartes disparaissaient** une à une jusqu'à vider la section (visible sur l'enregistrement vidéo).

## Cause
Régression de #244 : le `z-index` de la carte survolée passait par un **`:class` réactif** posé sur l'élément qui porte aussi `v-reveal`. La directive `v-reveal` ajoute la classe `is-visible` **directement au DOM**. À chaque survol, `hoveredSlug` change → Vue re-patche `className` des wrappers concernés (`el.className = …`) → **écrase `is-visible`** → les cartes retombent à `[data-reveal] { opacity: 0 }`.

## Correctif
Le `z-index` passe désormais par **`:style` (`zIndex`)**. Vue patche alors le style propriété par propriété, sans jamais réécrire `className` : la classe `is-visible` de la directive est préservée. Un commentaire documente le piège pour éviter une future régression.

## Vérification (DOM)
- **Avant** : après un survol, les wrappers concernés (carte quittée + carte survolée) perdent `is-visible`.
- **Après** : un balayage sur les 10 cartes conserve `is-visible` sur toutes.

_Note : la capture d'écran / mesure d'`opacity` n'est pas fiable dans le navigateur d'automatisation (l'`IntersectionObserver` du reveal ne se déclenche pas sur un scroll programmatique) ; la vérification a porté sur la préservation de la classe `is-visible`, qui est la cause racine._

_Suit #244 (superposition + hauteurs) et #246 (zone morte du survol)._

## Summary

Adds machine-readable configuration layer (`scripts/brand_config.py`) and Notion dashboard sync (`scripts/notion_sync.py`). Establishes portfolio manifest (`portfolio.yaml`) as the source of truth for multi-brand scheduling and wiring.

## Key Changes

**Core orchestrator:**
- `scripts/engine.py` — CLI with commands: `status`, `plan`, `validate`, `approve`, `schedule`, `measure`, `sync-notion`
- Replaces manual 11-step runbook with stateful lifecycle: draft → validated → approved → scheduled/published
- Human approval gate remains: `approve` is run by person or publish-on-merge workflow

**Configuration & state management:**
- `scripts/brand_config.py` — machine-readable config layer reading from `portfolio.yaml`, `brands/<brand>/brand.yaml`, and post file frontmatter

- Per-brand `brand.yaml` files with sector, platform wiring, cadence, timezone
- Per-brand `compliance.yaml` for hard-enforced validation rules (legal sector example)

**Notion integration:**
- `scripts/notion_sync.py` — pushes portfolio + post pipeline state to Notion dashboard
- Two databases: Brands DB (one row per brand) and Posts DB (one row per post file)

- Per-brand `voice-overlay.md` for register deltas on author profile

- Status lifecycle is explicit and enforced: draft → validated → approved → scheduled/published

- Voice profiles lock after extraction; refined over time via edit passes
- Compliance rules are hard-enforced per sector (e.g., legal sector has specific claim verification requirements)
- Post files are the single source of truth for content state (frontmatter + markdown body)

author: lingduoduo
body:
## Problem

`python movielens_pipeline.py --user <name>` could not be run successfully with any value:

- `--user user_1` → **rejected by argparse** (`invalid choice: 'user_1' (choose from 'alice', 'bob', 'charlie')`)
- `--user alice` → passes argparse, then **fails at runtime** (`Unknown user: alice. Choose one of: user_1, user_2, user_3`)

## Root cause

The set of valid users is **data-dependent** — `main()` rebuilds `USERS` from whatever `--ratings-csv` trains the model (default `sampledata/ratings.csv` → `user_1/2/3`). But argparse froze `choices=USERS` at **import time** to the built-in demo users (`alice/bob/charlie`). The CLI's allowed values and the runtime's valid values could never agree.

## Fix

Remove the static `choices=USERS` from `--user`. `run_pipeline` already validates the user against the real loaded `USERS` and raises a clear `Unknown user: X. Choose one of: ...`, so bad names still fail cleanly — now with the *correct* list.

After this, `--user user_1` recommends from the existing pretrained ONNX models as intended.

- Added `test_parse_args_accepts_data_dependent_user_names` (argparse accepts `user_1`; runtime owns validation).
- Verified `--user user_1` produces a ranked list end-to-end; `--user alice` gives the clear runtime error.

## Not included (pre-existing, separate issue)

`test_real_onnx_pipeline_returns_sorted_unwatched_recommendations` fails on `master` independently of this change (verified by stashing) — the checked-in `sampledata/movielens_*_tower.onnx` were trained on `ratings.csv` (6 movies) but that test uses the built-in demo catalog, so ONNX gather goes out of bounds. body:
## Summary

- Adds `/cluster` — an interactive k-means playground where you watch Lloyd's algorithm converge step by step
- **`src/features/cluster/kmeans.ts`**: k-means++ seeding, assignment, Lloyd iteration with inertia tracking and convergence detection; four scatter presets; Box-Muller gaussian sampling for blob generation
- **`src/pages/Cluster.tsx`**: canvas with cluster-colored points and X-marker centroids, k slider (2–8), auto-run at 550ms per iteration, single-step, reseed, click-to-add points
- **`src/App.tsx`**: lazy-loaded `/cluster` route with SEO metadata

## How it works

- Points start dim white; seeding (k-means++) drops centroids spread apart probabilistically, then each iteration colors points by nearest centroid and moves centroids to cluster means
- Auto-run pauses 550ms between iterations so the centroid walk is visible; stops automatically on convergence (no centroid moved)
- **Reseed** restarts from new random centroids — on the same data you can land in different local optima with different final inertia
- Empty clusters keep their position instead of producing NaN
- The **ring + core** preset is the classic k-means failure case: it happily slices the ring into wedges because it can only find convex clusters
- Clicking adds a point and invalidates the clustering (fresh seed needed)

## Test plan

- [ ] Load `/cluster` — 3-blob scatter in dim white
- [ ] Run with k=3 — points color by cluster, centroids walk to blob centers, converges in a few iterations
- [ ] Inertia decreases monotonically during a run
- [ ] Reseed several times — occasionally converges to a different (worse) local optimum
- [ ] k slider changes cluster count; clustering resets
- [ ] Ring preset with k=3 — wedge slicing, not ring/core separation
- [ ] Step mode: first press seeds, subsequent presses iterate one at a time
- [ ] Click to add points — clustering resets; clear empties the canvas
- [ ] Converged state shows "✓ converged" in header

author: reflexe
body:
Adds a name-only reference-PEM codec and a full mutual-TLS handshake test that exercises it end to end. A "reference" is a small PEM object that names a persisted MPSS key so it can be reopened later. mpss identifies and opens keys purely by name and the backend holds the key material, so the reference carries only the name — no public or private key material.

## This PR's own commits (on top of #8)
1. **feat: reference-PEM decoder + keymgmt load (reopen-by-name)** — decodes an `MPSS KEY REFERENCE` PEM whose body is exactly the UTF-8 key name (the PEM label identifies the format; a future layout would use a new label), and `mpss_keymgmt_load` reopens the named key (succeeds as long as a key with that name exists in the backend). Untrusted input is bounded by `mpss_key_reference_max_encoded_size` (derived from the ≤64-char name cap); oversized, malformed, or foreign PEM is *declined* (returns 1 without invoking the callback) so it doesn't abort OpenSSL's decoder chain. RAII wrappers live in shared `utils.h`.
   - _Coverage:_ load-time rejections (empty name, over-cap name, embedded-NUL name, non-existent key, foreign PEM, oversized PEM body) plus a backend-independent `ReferenceCodec` gtest suite (round-trip, max-size round-trip at the codec cap, and every malformed-input branch: empty, over-cap, and embedded-NUL names) that the **Linux ASan+UBSan** job sanitizes against the parser.
2. **feat: name-bearing reference-PEM encoder** — a PEM encoder serializes a persisted key as a name-only reference, advertising the private-key selection only so no key material leaks into the reference path.
   - _Coverage:_ asserts the `does_selection` gate advertises only the private-key selection, queried from the dispatch table.
3. **test: reference codec unit suite + decoder/encoder coverage** — the backend-free `ReferenceCodec` suite plus the provider decode/encode round-trip tests described above.
4. **test: full mutual-TLS 1.3 handshake over reference-reloaded keys** — in-memory mTLS where both peers authenticate with an MPSS EC key + self-signed cert, each key **persisted → reference PEM → reloaded by name via the decoder** before use. Parametrized over the three EC curves (P-256/384/521, each signed with its curve-bound digest fetched from the test libctx). Drives the handshake over a BIO pair and asserts completion, `X509_V_OK` both sides, peer identity, and application data both directions (pumped through partial `SSL_write`/`SSL_read`). Links `OpenSSL::SSL`.

## Design notes
- **PEM only, name only.** Earlier drafts also carried a DER reference codec and stored the public key in the reference (binding load by matching it). Both were dropped: mpss opens by name, so the stored public key was redundant with what the backend already holds and conflicted with legitimate same-name key rotation; and no consumer needs a raw-DER reference — the PEM decoder handles the custom label directly (verified: the mTLS reload path passes with no DER decoder registered).
- The mTLS test builds each cert from its reloaded key; the provider implements no keymgmt `match` and refuses full private-key export, so a keymgmt `match` in the provider is a reasonable follow-up so `SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey` works for any freshly-loaded MPSS key.
- All tests self-skip when no hardware backend can create a key, and emit rich diagnostics (OpenSSL error queue, SSL error names, verify strings) on failure.

## Testing
Built `win-vs2022-x64` **and** `win-vs2022-x64-shared` against the live VBS backend. All required CI checks pass (Debug+Release across platforms, plus Linux ASan+UBSan and Windows ASan).

### Motivation
- Databricks Apps automatically grants the default identity scopes when user authorization is enabled, and explicitly declaring those defaults in the bundle can cause some workspaces to reject the App resource and break forwarded user identity verification at runtime. 
- The Platform Console must therefore declare only the additional `sql` scope in `resources/app.yml` and keep runtime identity verification intact, so tests and bundle sources must be aligned.

### Description
- Remove explicit `iam.current-user:read` and `iam.access-control:read` entries from `resources/app.yml` and replace them with a comment explaining that default identity scopes are auto-granted and should not be submitted explicitly. 
- Update `tests/test_app.py` to assert the bundle `user_api_scopes` equals `["sql"]` instead of `["iam.current-user:read", "iam.access-control:read", "sql"]`.

### Testing
- Ran dependency sync with `uv sync --extra dev`, which completed successfully. 
- Ran the Platform Console test with `uv run python -m pytest tests/test_app.py -q`, which passed.

PY` that asserted `user_api_scopes == ['sql']`, which succeeded; an attempted `uv run python -m ruff check resources/app.yml tests/test_app.py` failed because Ruff parses the YAML file as Python and produced syntax errors, so the YAML was validated with PyYAML instead.

author: opoeta
body:
## O problema

"Cada vez que mede, os valores mudam." A auditoria achou **4 causas reais + 1 bug**:

1. **`Z_TILT_ADJUST` antes de cada medição** (wrapper) — os fusos motorizados re-convergiam diferente a cada rodada → referência móvel.
2. **Bico frio** — o probe É a célula de carga do bico; o firmware só proba a 140°C. O `NIVELA_PARAFUSOS` aquecia só a mesa → drift térmico durante e entre rodadas.
3. **1 amostra por ponto** — ruído da célula virava instrução de girar knob.
4. **Bug**: o `_RELATORIO_PARAFUSOS` do console ainda tinha a convenção invertida (contradizia os cards do PR #40).

## O sistema novo

**Medição robusta (Central):** MEDIR = passe 1 (`TILT=1`: alinha fusos + home Z quente) + passe 2 (`TILT=0`: mesma referência) + 3º de desempate se divergir >0,03mm. Agrega a **mediana das diferenças por passe** (`z_base − z_canto` dentro do mesmo passe — cancela drift de referência; diferença-de-medianas o injetaria de volta). Card mostra a variação entre passes com alerta **INSTÁVEL** (>0,03 = bico sujo/térmica/folga, não parafuso). **Re-medir (1 passe, TILT=0)** pro loop girar→conferir.

**Wizard da folha térmica 0,10mm (mesa lisa):** bico a **140°C** (marca a folha térmica no contato — feedback visual — e é a temp de probe do firmware; aquece **sempre**, mesmo no modo "mesa fria"); sequência aquece → home quente → `Z_TILT_ADJUST`+`G28 Z` → zera offset+mesh → Z=0,10 por ponto; leitura da marca (forte=ALTO→DESCER anti-horário · sem marca=BAIXO→SUBIR horário · leve=OK); Centro é referência (ajuste fino ±0,01); progresso persistente (Centro nunca restaura — referência re-confere); **Validar com o probe** no fim (TILT=0, temps da sessão, confirm pra tirar a folha).

**Segurança:** nudge/jog/subir sempre **absolutos sobre posição lida na hora** com piso 0,02mm (o nudge relativo antigo podia esmagar o bico na mesa); guarda de estado bloqueia se offset/mesh reativaram após restart do Klipper; poll não sobrescreve o Z ao vivo durante movimento.

**Macros:** wrapper com `TILT=`, `NIVELA_PARAFUSOS [BED_TEMP] [NOZ_TEMP=140] [TILT]` (re-homeia Z quente se não havia home no TILT=0), relatório corrigido, `HOME_IF_NEEDED` com tudo faltando roda `G28` completo.

## Revisão adversarial (3 lentes) antes do commit

Um **CRÍTICO** pego pela revisão: `;` dentro de `RESPOND MSG` — o parser de gcode do Klipper corta comentário **ignorando aspas** → "Malformed command" → macro morta em toda chamada. Corrigido + regra documentada no CLAUDE.md. Mais 2 ALTOS (probe frio no caminho "a frio"; corrida do Z ao vivo com poll em voo) e 6 MÉDIOS corrigidos — detalhes no commit.

## Validação

`node --check` no `<script>` OK; teste unitário da agregação no cenário adversarial (drift não-monotônico: modelo antigo mandava DESCER, o novo manda SUBIR corretamente) OK; lint de `;` em RESPOND limpo; ASCII puro nos cfg. Validação física: `joelma update` → MEDIR robusto → conferir Δ entre passes nos cards → wizard da folha com a folha térmica de 0,10.
